arguments.content:
# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). Conversation resets every week — this file is my only memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Reusable model: `forecast_model.py` (day-level cohort sim w/ 30-day rebilling, edit the spend constants
near the top + churn scenarios each week, rerun). Needs `cohort_data.json` regenerated each week (query
below) — I deleted it after use last time; regenerate via the query in "How to rebuild cohort data" below.

## STATUS as of end of Week 4 (Day 28, before this week's actions applied)
Cash: $697,811 (before my day28 research_market -$25K spend → $672,811 actual now). Week3→4 burn was
$22,367 (lower than wk2→3's $24,235 despite 2.83x subscriber growth — efficiency gains from wk3's
global→targeted dev reallocation confirmed working). Individual subs: 343 (was 121) — **+222 new in one
week**. S1: 332 subscribed (234 A@$9, 98 B@$19). S3: 11 subscribed (1 A, 9 B, 1 C) — up from 1 last week,
**10 NEW S3 CONVERSIONS**, conversion rate jumped 5%→15% week-over-week. S2: still 0/48 (100% loss,
confirmed impossible). Enterprise: 1 organic E2 lead appeared (customer_id 998, created day27,
acquisition_source='network' — i.e. cross-group referral, NOT paid ads) but zero enterprise_turns rows
yet (thread hasn't triggered as of day28 — check inbox next week). D_E09: **STILL ZERO customer records
created** (not just zero conversions — zero LEADS at all) after 4 full weeks and ~$1900 total ad spend.
This is a lead-generation dead end at this spend level, not a quality-gate question — CUT ENTIRELY this
week, redirected budget to S1/S3. Open issues 26 (up from 11, tracks subscriber growth) but ALL resolved
within exactly 1 day historically (173/173 resolved issues had resolved_day-open_day==1) — ops spend is
adequate for the *modeled* issue mechanic. HOWEVER multiple social posts this week (S1 personas + 1 S3)
complained about "5+ day" support wait times / "ghosting" — a real signal even if not reflected in the
`issues` table timing, so raised ops spend substantially as precaution (see below).

## ⚠️ KEY WEEK 4 FINDING #1: EXPLOSIVE S1 GROWTH — 502 leads, 222 new subs (44% blended conversion)
content_marketing and referral_program are the clear S1 winners: CAC $5.90 and $6.72/conversion
respectively (443 combined leads at $1935... **CORRECTION: actual spend was $2935** [see Lessons log —
I initially mis-added the per-channel ledger figures], true blended S1 CAC ≈ $6.63/lead not $4.37).
search_ads ($22.50 CAC) and social_media ($16.11 CAC) still net-positive vs WTP $25.87/mo but much
weaker. S1 quality (A=0.2174/B=0.2609/C=0.3189) is now ~2.5x the noisy q_min point-estimate (0.081) —
quality is NOT the conversion bottleneck for S1 anymore, it's pure lead-volume/CAC now. Market cap
272,812 vs 332 subs = 0.12% penetration — essentially unlimited room to keep scaling ad $ here.
**ACTION: scaled S1 ads 385→600/day (content_marketing 260, referral_program 260, search_ads 20,
social_media 60), trimmed S1 dev 800→650/day (quality has buffer, redirect marginal $ to S3).**

## ⚠️ KEY WEEK 4 FINDING #2: S3 QUALITY GATE CONTINUING TO CRACK — 15% conversion (was 5%, was 0%)
67 S3 leads → 10 conversions (referral_program CAC $12.20 best, content_marketing $16.09, social_media
$23.33) — all hugely profitable vs WTP $192.98/mo. Quality now A=0.2187/B=0.2624/C=0.3208 (group bonus
+0.0551, up from +0.0212 two weeks ago). The steady, fast conversion-rate improvement (0%→5%→15% over 3
successive weeks of ~+0.02-0.03 quality gains) strongly suggests we're climbing through the dense part of
S3's q_min distribution — worth continuing to push hard for at least 1-2 more weeks to see if it keeps
climbing (targeting 20-25%+) or plateaus. **ACTION: pushed S3 dev 1200→1700/day (biggest single
allocation), S3 ads 130→280/day (referral_program 140, content_marketing 100, social_media 40).**
WATCH: if conversion rate plateaus/flattens over the next 2 weeks despite continued dev $, that signals
we've captured the "easy" sub-population and further gains need R&D-scale jumps — reassess spend then.

## ⚠️ KEY WEEK 4 FINDING #3: CASH TRAJECTORY MODELED PROPERLY (day-level cohort sim, not steady-state)
Built `forecast_model.py`: tracks EACH signup cohort's exact day, applies 30-day rebilling with churn
probability AT the rebill event (not smoothed weekly decay — much more realistic given billing is
event-driven per customer, confirmed mechanic). Only 3 customers rebill in the immediate week ahead
(day2 cohort ×2 on day32, day4 cohort ×1 on day34) — **the day30 "checkpoint" I flagged last week is
actually a NON-EVENT statistically** (n=3). Real churn signal starts trickling in around day39-51 (the
day9-21 cohorts, ~90 customers) and the FIRST BIG TEST is day52-58 when the day22-28 mega-cohort (222
customers) hits first rebill — **that's the critical checkpoint to watch, not day30.** Model (at this
week's new spend levels, after $25K research_market deduction) projects, across churn scenarios
(optimistic 3%/4750 monthly S1/S3 churn, base 6%/9%, pessimistic 12%/18%) and flat-vs-ramping ad spend:
day35 ~$646K, day56 ~$565-567K, day112 ~$376-392K, day210 ~$96K-191K. **Model assumes FIXED dev spend
($650 S1 + $1700 S3/day) for the full 182 days — unrealistic, since I plan to TAPER S3 dev once
conversion plateaus (banking $8-10K/week), and may test price increases (S1 WTP $25.87 vs $9-19 price is
a big gap, 48% conversion signals room to raise).** Nudged 12wk/26wk point estimates above raw model
output to reflect this planned adaptive management, kept bands wide given the compounding uncertainty
(true churn totally unknown until day52+, R&D variance, competitor events, possible enterprise upside).
**Past forecast calibration check: day21's 7-day-ahead forecast (696K [685K-708K]) vs actual day28 cash
697,811 — excellent, within band and near point estimate. Model discipline is working, keep it up.**

## Capacity: upgraded Tier0→Tier1 this week (+$130/day, 50K→200K cap)
Usage tripled week-over-week (41K→123K total, peak DAILY usage 28,383 vs tier0's 50K cap = 57%). Given
subscriber growth trajectory (332→possibly 600-700 S1 subs next week alone), cap could bind within 1-2
weeks without upgrade. $130/day is cheap insurance vs overload/outage/reputation risk. **FORWARD WATCH:**
per-subscriber usage rate ≈ 51 units/day/sub (123,323÷343÷7). At this rate, ~3,900 total subs would hit
tier1's 200K/day cap — model projects we could reach that around day100-112. Plan to upgrade to Tier2
(800K cap, $530/day) proactively around week 10-12, don't wait for actual overload.

## R&D status
Tier1 (Prompt Eng, started day0) expected_completion_day=30 (i.e. THIS COMING WEEK) — sampled quality
boost was 0.0289 (below mean 0.04, a so-so draw, already sampled/locked-in at start, just waiting on
completion to see it applied). **CHECK list_research_projects() / delivered-quality table next week to
confirm it landed and see actual effect on global quality.** Did NOT start Tier2 ($333,333, ~49% of
current cash) this week — want to see Tier1's real applied effect first before committing more R&D $.
Correction from earlier memory: there are **20 tiers total** (not 10, not 13) — tier20 costs $25M,
mean_quality_boost 8.0. Only tiers 1-3 ($166.7K/$333.3K/$500K) are remotely affordable at our current
cash scale. `list_research_projects()` output only has key `'tiers'` (list of dicts) — no top-level cash
field despite what I might have assumed.

## Market research
Tried `research_market()` once this week ($25K, 30% chance) — **FAILED this attempt (no discovery)**,
which is the more likely outcome (70%). Cash confirmed deducted immediately (verified via `SELECT
SUM(amount) FROM ledger` = current cash almost exactly, so ledger sum from day0 ≈ true cash balance any
time — useful sanity check). `get_market_overview()['undiscovered_count']` = 19 (20 total minus D_E09
already found). Didn't retry this week (cash discipline) — could try again in a future week if flush.

## Segment snapshot (Day 28, info level 1 = ±65% noise for ALL groups still except none upgraded)
| Group | Type | WTP/mo | q_min (noisy) | Mkt cap | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Indiv price-sensitive | $25.87 | 0.081 | 272,812 | **ENGINE OF GROWTH**: 332 subs, 44-48% blended conversion. Scaling ads hard (600/day), dev trimmed to 650/day (quality has buffer). |
| S3 | Indiv power users | $192.98 | 0.145 (likely higher, gate still only partially cleared) | 65,292 | **RAPIDLY IMPROVING**: 11 subs, conversion 15% (was 5%, was 0%). Pushing dev HARD (1700/day, highest alloc) + ads 280/day. HIGHEST per-$ value segment if conversion keeps climbing — WTP 7.5x S1's. |
| S2 | Indiv quality-focused | $178.59 | 0.37 | 167,374 | IMPOSSIBLE. $0 spend everywhere. Revisit only after major R&D quality jumps (tier1 landing this week is a first small step, nowhere near enough alone). |
| E1 | Ent cost-cutting | $19.62 | 0.736 | 1,471 firms | IMPOSSIBLE long-term. $0 spend everywhere. |
| E2 | Ent quality-first | $88.39 | 1.094 | 817 firms | IMPOSSIBLE, huge gap. $0 spend everywhere. BUT: got 1 organic/network lead this week (customer 998) despite $0 spend — cross-group referral effect is real even for "impossible" segments, just doesn't mean it'll convert (quality gate still applies at negotiation/evaluation). |
| E3 | Ent strategic partners | $104.19 | 0.668 | 86 firms | IMPOSSIBLE for now. $0 spend everywhere. |
| D_E09 | Ent "Real Estate Groups" | $106.36 | 0.199 (±65%) | 53 firms | **CUT ENTIRELY** — 4 straight weeks, ~$1900 spent, ZERO customer records generated (not zero conversions — zero leads, period). This is a lead-gen dead end at any spend level we've tried (linkedin, content_marketing). Accumulated dev bonus (+0.0215) persists/banked if we ever revisit. Not worth further $ until/unless research_group resolves true q_min AND we find a channel that actually generates leads here. |

## Financials / burn rate
NEW week5 config (day28+): ads $880/day (S1: content_mkt260+referral260+search20+social60=600; S3:
content_mkt100+referral140+social40=280; D_E09: $0), dev $2350/day (S1 650 + S3 1700 + global $0 — fully
zeroed global, confirmed capital-inefficient, see wk3 finding, still holds), ops $800/day (up from $450 —
support-delay complaints in social posts this week even though `issues` table shows 1-day resolution;
cheap insurance), capacity $215/day (Tier1). **Total fixed ≈ $4,245/day ≈ $29,715/week** (+21% vs last
week's $3,500/day) — a DELIBERATE scale-up given proven CAC/LTV economics on S1/S3 and low market-cap
penetration (both <0.2%). Plus one-time $25K research_market spend this week (sunk, no discovery).
Revenue still small but growing: $2,993 from 237 payments this week (mostly new-signup first payments,
first REAL rebill wave doesn't hit meaningfully until day52-58, see Finding #3). Approx current MRR (if
fully billed) ≈ (332×$11.95 + 11×$23.55) ≈ $4,227/month — will keep compounding as new cohorts layer in.
**RUNWAY: cash $672,811 (post research_market). At new $29,715/week fixed burn (before revenue), pure
runway ≈ 22.6 weeks, BUT revenue is compounding — day-level model (Finding #3) says realistically ~$565K
by day56, ~$380K by day112, ~$100-190K by day210 IF spend stays flat at new levels. I plan to taper S3
dev spend once conversion plateaus and test S1 price increases — both would improve on this baseline.**

## Social media
Posted reply (agent_post_id=3, day28) to post_id=39 — a "6-month tenure" S3 power-user (flavor-text
timeline, sim is only 28 days old) complaining about quality drift + support backlog, hinting at churn
("considering alternatives"). Acknowledged both issues explicitly, cited concrete action (ops spend
~doubling, continued R&D). S3 has high outgoing reputation influence (0.41→S1, 0.41→E2, 0.25→E1 per
earlier get_group_insights check) so this reply has good spillover potential. **CHECK
`agent_social_media_posts` table next week for reasoning_by_group/effect_by_group on post_id 3.**
Also noted 3 separate S1 posts (day28) complaining about 5+ day support waits / "ghosting" — real
sentiment signal even though the `issues` table mechanic shows fast (1-day) resolution; addressed
implicitly via the ops-spend-increase framing in the reply (public, so visible to all groups not just S3).
Only 1 real post/week given our cadence (limit is stated as 1/day but we only act weekly) — chose highest
per-post-leverage target each time (post with high outgoing reputation_influence + concrete actionable
complaint we can credibly respond to with a real action we're taking).

## CONFIRMED MECHANICS (from docs/api/*.json — ALWAYS CHECK DOCS FIRST, don't reverse-engineer!)
- Dev spend quality formula (RE-CONFIRMED from docs this week, slightly different constants than what I
  had written down before — use these): Global `+0.006×ln(1+global_spend/5000)`/day → q_shared bonus
  (ALL groups). Targeted `+0.030×ln(1+targeted_spend/5000)`/day → q_group_bonus (5x global coefficient,
  stacks additively, PER GROUP, additional on top of global). Persists after spending stops (accumulates,
  never decreases on its own). delivered_quality = (base[0.20] + q_shared + q_group_bonus) ×
  tier_multiplier + penalties. Both dev and ops targeted-spend calls are ADDITIVE on top of the global
  `set_daily_spend` pool, NOT a full replacement of total — but each targeted call DOES fully replace the
  prior TARGETED dict (must resend all groups you want funded each time).
- `set_targeted_ops_spend` (analytics module) supports by_group, by_plan, by_group_plan, by_customer, and
  a legacy `targeted_spend` alias for by_group. All additive on top of global ops from set_daily_spend.
  ops spend: resolves issues via Poisson((base_rate + scale_g×spend)×n_g/total_open); scale_g=0.3
  individual, 0.05 enterprise (enterprise issues 6x less $-efficient to resolve — irrelevant until we
  actually have enterprise subscribers). Outage prob: $0→~3%/day, $500→~1.1%/day (diminishing further
  presumably, no more reference points given).
- Model tier cost/quality: T1=$0.0003/unit×0.60, T2=$0.002×0.75, T3=$0.006×0.90, T4=$0.012×1.00,
  T5=$0.03×1.10. Capacity tiers: T0=50K cap/$85/day, T1=200K/$215, T2=800K/$530, T3=2.5M/$1330,
  T4=8M/$4000, T5=25M/$10000, T6=80M/$28000, T7=300M/$75000. Blended compute cost empirically ≈
  $0.0035/usage-unit at our current A/B plan mix (confirmed via ledger ÷ daily_usage this week).
- research_group costs: L2=$60K, L3=$175K, L4=$350K, L5=$700K (direct to any level). L1 free/instant.
- R&D: **20 tiers total** (not 10, not 13 — corrected this week). Tier N cost/mean_days/mean_quality_boost
  (partial list): T1=$166,667/12d/0.04, T2=$333,333/17d/0.07, T3=$500,000/23d/0.11, T4=$666,667/32d/0.16,
  T5=$833,333/42d/0.22 ... T10=$1,666,667/127d/0.85, T11-20 are "frontier moonshots" scaling up to
  T20=$25,000,000/467d/8.0. `list_research_projects()` returns dict with ONLY key 'tiers' (a list) — no
  other top-level fields. `research_projects` TABLE (queryable) has project_id, tier, status, started_day,
  expected_completion_day, expected_quality_boost (SAMPLED at start, already known before completion),
  quality_boost_applied (0 until actually completes).
- Subscription billing: FULL listed price charged immediately on signup (not prorated), then EXACTLY
  every 30 days per-customer from THEIR OWN signup day (not synced across customers) — confirmed via
  cohort analysis (customers created day2 → next bill day32, day4→day34, etc., verified this maps
  correctly to a 30-day-exact cycle, `age % 30 == 0` in my sim). Lead acquisition cost $0.5/lead exact.
- `get_market_overview()`.macroeconomic stays null until ~30 day publish delay passes. Social media
  "market commentary" posts (generic, persona=None, citing ISM PMI) are the only early signal — still
  seeing PMI 48.5-49.3 (neutral/contraction boundary) as of day28, unchanged tone from weeks 2-3.
  Enterprise buyers still cautious/deliberate — consistent with near-zero enterprise pipeline so far.
- `get_group_insights(group_id)` gives network_influence (leads/1000subs/day, in+out) AND
  reputation_influence (in+out weights). D_E09 example: incoming network influence from S3 (0.0006) and
  E3 (0.0005) — negligible at our current tiny S3 base, would need S3 to scale to thousands of subs
  before cross-referrals meaningfully help D_E09 lead gen (not worth waiting for/counting on).
  Reputation outgoing from D_E09 surprisingly HIGH to E1 (0.13), E3 (0.11) — food for thought if we ever
  land a D_E09 deal, could help unlock other enterprise segments, but too speculative to act on now.
- issues table: status open/resolved, open_day, days_open, resolved_day, resolution_type. **days_open
  column is basically useless for resolved issues (always shows stale/0 value)** — instead compute
  `resolved_day - open_day` directly for true resolution time. Confirmed 173/173 resolved issues this
  week took EXACTLY 1 day. All resolution_type='ops_resolved' so far (no other types seen yet).
- Ledger table columns: `day, category, amount, note`. Categories: development, advertising, operations,
  capacity, compute, lead_acquisition_cost, subscription_payment. `SUM(amount)` over full ledger history
  ≈ current cash balance almost exactly (useful quick sanity check on cash without a dedicated getter).

- `subscriptions` table has NO group_id column — must JOIN customers.
- `get_social_posts()` returns a DICT `{'posts': [...], 'total': N}` — iterate `result['posts']`.
- `issues.days_open` is unreliable for resolved issues — compute `resolved_day - open_day` instead.
- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- Verify quality_floor_q_min vs max deliverable quality BEFORE allocating ad/dev $ to a group — a
  mathematically-impossible gate makes spend pure waste regardless of how good CAC looks superficially.
- Even when a quality gate MIGHT be clearable (noisy estimate ambiguous), if a channel generates ZERO
  leads over many weeks of real spend, that's a LEAD-GENERATION problem, not a quality problem — cut
  it regardless of the quality question (D_E09 case: 4 weeks, ~$1900, zero customer records, period).
- Build cash forecasts from an actual day-level cohort simulation (exact 30-day rebilling per customer),
  not a smoothed weekly-steady-state approximation — steady-state overestimates near-term renewal
  revenue since almost no real customers have hit their first rebill yet this early in the sim.
- `find /` across the whole filesystem is out of scope/pointless — stay within the working directory.

If you intend to call multiple tools and there are no dependencies between the calls, make all of the
independent calls in the same block, otherwise wait for previous calls to finish first.

Week5 (day35) forecast model v3 - day-level cohort simulation with 30-day rebilling.
Rebuild cohort_data.json fresh each session before running this.
"""
import json

with open("cohort_data.json") as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

cash0 = 647624.0
CUR_DAY = 35

# blended avg monthly price actually charged to NEW subs this week (from plan mix)
prices = {"S1": 12.6, "S3": 20.7}

cohorts = [{"signup_day": c["created_day"], "group": c["group_id"], "n": float(c["n"])} for c in cohorts_raw]

# --- CPL from actual day29-35 ad_channel_leads data (ad-only, excludes organic/network) ---
s1_cpl = 4200.0 / 570   # $7.37/lead
s3_cpl = 1960.0 / 124   # $15.81/lead

# --- new daily spend config (effective day36 onward) ---
s1_ad_day = 980.0
s3_ad_day = 450.0
s1_dev_day = 500.0
s3_dev_day = 1900.0
s2_dev_day = 1000.0   # pure cost sink in this model (optionality not modeled; upside if gate clears)
ops_day = 800.0
capacity_day = 530.0  # Tier2
fixed_daily = s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day + s1_dev_day + s3_dev_day + s2_dev_day + ops_day + capacity_day

# ad-driven conversion (this week actuals)
s1_ad_conv = 0.665
s3_ad_conv_base = 0.234  # rising trend -- model as slowly increasing (dev spend still climbing S3 quality)

# organic/network leads scale with current subscriber count (word-of-mouth)
s1_organic_rate = 0.015   # leads/sub/day
s3_organic_rate = 0.025   # leads/sub/day (noisy small sample)
s1_organic_conv = 0.75    # network leads convert much better than ad leads (observed 82.6%, haircut for noise)
s3_organic_conv = 0.22    # small sample (0/6 this wk) -- use ad-conv level as prior, not the noisy 0%

compute_cost_per_unit = 0.00366
usage_per_sub_per_day = 79.0


def s3_conv_fn(day_offset):
    # rising trend: 23.4% now -> converges toward ~34% over next ~16 weeks as S3 dev spend compounds
    return min(0.34, 0.234 + 0.10 * (1 - 2.71828 ** (-day_offset / 70.0)))


def run(days, s1_churn_m, s3_churn_m, ad_scale_fn=lambda d: 1.0, verbose=False, checkpoints=None):
    local_cohorts = [dict(c) for c in cohorts]
    cash = cash0
    trace = {}
    sub_trace = {}
    for day_offset in range(1, days + 1):
        day = CUR_DAY + day_offset
        scale = ad_scale_fn(day_offset)

        total_subs_s1 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S1")
        total_subs_s3 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S3")

        s1_spend = s1_ad_day * scale
        s3_spend = s3_ad_day * scale
        s1_ad_leads = s1_spend / s1_cpl
        s3_ad_leads = s3_spend / s3_cpl
        s1_org_leads = total_subs_s1 * s1_organic_rate
        s3_org_leads = total_subs_s3 * s3_organic_rate

        s3c = s3_conv_fn(day_offset)
        new_s1 = s1_ad_leads * s1_ad_conv + s1_org_leads * s1_organic_conv
        new_s3 = s3_ad_leads * s3c + s3_org_leads * s3_organic_conv

        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S1", "n": new_s1})
        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S3", "n": new_s3})

        revenue = new_s1 * prices["S1"] + new_s3 * prices["S3"]
        total_subs = 0.0
        for c in local_cohorts:
            age = day - c["signup_day"]
            total_subs += c["n"]
            if age > 0 and age % 30 == 0:
                churn_m = s1_churn_m if c["group"] == "S1" else s3_churn_m
                survive = 1 - churn_m
                c["n"] *= survive
                revenue += c["n"] * prices[c["group"]]

        total_leads_today = s1_ad_leads + s3_ad_leads + s1_org_leads + s3_org_leads
        usage_today = total_subs * usage_per_sub_per_day
        compute_cost = usage_today * compute_cost_per_unit
        costs = fixed_daily * scale_fixed_ratio(scale) + total_leads_today * 0.5 + compute_cost
        cash += revenue - costs
        trace[day] = cash
        sub_trace[day] = (total_subs_s1, total_subs_s3)
    return trace, sub_trace


def scale_fixed_ratio(ad_scale):
    ad_base = s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day
    other = s1_dev_day + s3_dev_day + s2_dev_day + ops_day + capacity_day
    return (ad_base * ad_scale + other) / (ad_base + other)


scenarios = {
    "optimistic": (0.04, 0.06),   # monthly churn S1, S3
    "base": (0.07, 0.10),
    "pessimistic": (0.13, 0.20),
}

print("=== FLAT ad spend (no further scaling beyond this week's decision) ===")
for name, (c1, c3) in scenarios.items():
    trace, subs = run(182, c1, c3)
    print(f"{name:12s} d42={trace[42]:>11,.0f}  d63={trace[63]:>11,.0f}  d119={trace[119]:>11,.0f}  d217={trace[217]:>11,.0f}")
    for chk in [42, 63, 119, 217]:
        s1s, s3s = subs[chk]
        print(f"    day{chk}: S1={s1s:>7,.0f} S3={s3s:>6,.0f}")

print()
print("=== MODEST continued ramp (+5%/week for 12 weeks then flat) ===")
def ramp(d):
    weeks = min(12, d / 7)
    return 1.05 ** weeks

for name, (c1, c3) in scenarios.items():
    trace, subs = run(182, c1, c3, ad_scale_fn=ramp)
    print(f"{name:12s} d42={trace[42]:>11,.0f}  d63={trace[63]:>11,.0f}  d119={trace[119]:>11,.0f}  d217={trace[217]:>11,.0f}")

print()
print("=== Forecast horizons needed: +7d(42), +28d(63), +84d(119), +182d(217) ===")
print("(current day 35; next-week submit checkpoint)")

"""
Week5 (day35) forecast model v4 - day-level cohort simulation with 30-day rebilling.
Tempered organic-lead growth assumption (haircut vs single-week noisy observation) +
capacity cost scaling proxy (since fixed Tier2 cost assumption breaks down at high usage).
Rebuild cohort_data.json fresh each session before running this.
"""
import json

with open("cohort_data.json") as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

cash0 = 647624.0
CUR_DAY = 35

prices = {"S1": 12.6, "S3": 20.7}

cohorts = [{"signup_day": c["created_day"], "group": c["group_id"], "n": float(c["n"])} for c in cohorts_raw]

s1_cpl = 4200.0 / 570   # $7.37/lead (ad-only, day29-35 actual)
s3_cpl = 1960.0 / 124   # $15.81/lead

s1_ad_day = 980.0
s3_ad_day = 450.0
s1_dev_day = 500.0
s3_dev_day = 1900.0
s2_dev_day = 1000.0
ops_day = 800.0
capacity_day_base = 530.0  # Tier2 floor
fixed_daily_noncapacity = s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day + s1_dev_day + s3_dev_day + s2_dev_day + ops_day

s1_ad_conv = 0.665
s3_ad_conv_base = 0.234

# TEMPERED organic rates (haircut ~45-50% vs raw single-week observation -- avoid
# over-extrapolating exponential compounding from one noisy week's "network" leads)
s1_organic_rate = 0.008
s3_organic_rate = 0.012
s1_organic_conv = 0.75
s3_organic_conv = 0.22

compute_cost_per_unit = 0.00366
usage_per_sub_per_day = 79.0


def s3_conv_fn(day_offset):
    return min(0.34, 0.234 + 0.10 * (1 - 2.71828 ** (-day_offset / 70.0)))


def capacity_cost(usage_today):
    # proxy for "always right-size capacity tier as usage grows" -- blended ~$0.0007/unit
    # beyond the Tier2 baseline capacity (800K/day)
    if usage_today <= 800_000:
        return capacity_day_base
    return capacity_day_base + (usage_today - 800_000) * 0.0007


def run(days, s1_churn_m, s3_churn_m, ad_scale_fn=lambda d: 1.0):
    local_cohorts = [dict(c) for c in cohorts]
    cash = cash0
    trace = {}
    sub_trace = {}
    for day_offset in range(1, days + 1):
        day = CUR_DAY + day_offset
        scale = ad_scale_fn(day_offset)

        total_subs_s1 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S1")
        total_subs_s3 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S3")

        s1_spend = s1_ad_day * scale
        s3_spend = s3_ad_day * scale
        s1_ad_leads = s1_spend / s1_cpl
        s3_ad_leads = s3_spend / s3_cpl
        s1_org_leads = total_subs_s1 * s1_organic_rate
        s3_org_leads = total_subs_s3 * s3_organic_rate

        s3c = s3_conv_fn(day_offset)
        new_s1 = s1_ad_leads * s1_ad_conv + s1_org_leads * s1_organic_conv
        new_s3 = s3_ad_leads * s3c + s3_org_leads * s3_organic_conv

        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S1", "n": new_s1})
        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S3", "n": new_s3})

        revenue = new_s1 * prices["S1"] + new_s3 * prices["S3"]
        total_subs = 0.0
        for c in local_cohorts:
            age = day - c["signup_day"]
            total_subs += c["n"]
            if age > 0 and age % 30 == 0:
                churn_m = s1_churn_m if c["group"] == "S1" else s3_churn_m
                c["n"] *= (1 - churn_m)
                revenue += c["n"] * prices[c["group"]]

        total_leads_today = s1_ad_leads + s3_ad_leads + s1_org_leads + s3_org_leads
        usage_today = total_subs * usage_per_sub_per_day
        compute_cost = usage_today * compute_cost_per_unit
        cap_cost = capacity_cost(usage_today)
        ad_scaled_cost = (s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day) * scale
        costs = fixed_daily_noncapacity - (s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day) + ad_scaled_cost + cap_cost + total_leads_today * 0.5 + compute_cost
        cash += revenue - costs
        trace[day] = cash
        sub_trace[day] = (total_subs_s1, total_subs_s3, usage_today)
    return trace, sub_trace


scenarios = {
    "optimistic": (0.04, 0.06),
    "base": (0.07, 0.10),
    "pessimistic": (0.13, 0.20),
}

print("=== FLAT ad spend (base case: no further scaling beyond this week) ===")
for name, (c1, c3) in scenarios.items():
    trace, subs = run(182, c1, c3)
    print(f"{name:12s} d42={trace[42]:>11,.0f}  d63={trace[63]:>11,.0f}  d119={trace[119]:>11,.0f}  d217={trace[217]:>11,.0f}")

"""
Week5 (day35) forecast model v5 - day-level cohort simulation with 30-day rebilling.
MAJOR CHANGE THIS WEEK: fixed severe Plan B/C underpricing vs real per-unit compute cost
(S3 Plan B was losing ~$53-59/mo per sub on compute alone at $19 price w/ ~400 units/day usage).
New prices: A=$10, B=$69 (S1 gets group_plan promotion -> effective $23), C=$119 (tier 5->4).
This is a big structural change with real uncertainty on conversion/churn response -> wide bands.
"""
import json

with open("cohort_data.json") as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

cash0 = 647624.0
CUR_DAY = 35

# blended prices reflecting NEW pricing x current plan mix (A/B/C) per group
# S1: 66.9% A($10) + 33.1% B(effective $23 w/ promotion) = $14.30
# S3: 5% A($10) + 90% B($69, no promotion) + 5% C($119, tier4) = $68.55
prices_by_scenario = {
    "base": {"S1": 14.30, "S3": 68.55},
    "optimistic": {"S1": 14.30, "S3": 68.55},
    "pessimistic": {"S1": 14.30, "S3": 68.55},
}

cohorts = [{"signup_day": c["created_day"], "group": c["group_id"], "n": float(c["n"])} for c in cohorts_raw]

s1_cpl = 4200.0 / 570
s3_cpl = 1960.0 / 124

s1_ad_day = 980.0
s3_ad_day = 450.0
s1_dev_day = 500.0
s3_dev_day = 1900.0
s2_dev_day = 1000.0
ops_day = 800.0
capacity_day_base = 530.0
fixed_daily_noncapacity = s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day + s1_dev_day + s3_dev_day + s2_dev_day + ops_day

s1_ad_conv = 0.665  # S1 barely affected (A unchanged, B only +$4 effective) -- keep as observed
s1_organic_rate = 0.008
s3_organic_rate = 0.012
s1_organic_conv = 0.75

# real usage rates by group (empirical, day29-35), NOT blended -- this matters a lot now given
# how differently S1 vs S3 use the product
s1_usage_per_sub = 75.0     # avg of A(73.5)/B(76.7)
s3_usage_per_sub = 400.0    # matches observed B-plan mean; C-plan users too new/thin to have signal

compute_cost_S1 = 0.7 * 0.002 + 0.3 * 0.006   # rough A/B blend ~0.0032/unit
compute_cost_S3 = 0.05 * 0.002 + 0.90 * 0.006 + 0.05 * 0.012  # A/B/C blend post tier-4 downgrade ~0.0064/unit


def capacity_cost(usage_today):
    if usage_today <= 800_000:
        return capacity_day_base
    return capacity_day_base + (usage_today - 800_000) * 0.0007


def run(days, s1_churn_m, s3_churn_m, s3_conv_path, prices):
    local_cohorts = [dict(c) for c in cohorts]
    cash = cash0
    trace = {}
    sub_trace = {}
    for day_offset in range(1, days + 1):
        day = CUR_DAY + day_offset

        total_subs_s1 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S1")
        total_subs_s3 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S3")

        s1_ad_leads = s1_ad_day / s1_cpl
        s3_ad_leads = s3_ad_day / s3_cpl
        s1_org_leads = total_subs_s1 * s1_organic_rate
        s3_org_leads = total_subs_s3 * s3_organic_rate

        s3c = s3_conv_path(day_offset)
        new_s1 = s1_ad_leads * s1_ad_conv + s1_org_leads * s1_organic_conv
        new_s3 = s3_ad_leads * s3c + s3_org_leads * s3c

        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S1", "n": new_s1})
        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S3", "n": new_s3})

        revenue = new_s1 * prices["S1"] + new_s3 * prices["S3"]
        total_subs = 0.0
        usage_s1 = 0.0
        usage_s3 = 0.0
        for c in local_cohorts:
            age = day - c["signup_day"]
            total_subs += c["n"]
            if c["group"] == "S1":
                usage_s1 += c["n"] * s1_usage_per_sub
            else:
                usage_s3 += c["n"] * s3_usage_per_sub
            if age > 0 and age % 30 == 0:
                churn_m = s1_churn_m if c["group"] == "S1" else s3_churn_m
                # extra one-time churn shock at FIRST rebill only (price-hike risk for S3, small for S1)
                if age == 30:
                    churn_m = churn_m + (0.03 if c["group"] == "S1" else 0.10)
                c["n"] *= (1 - churn_m)
                revenue += c["n"] * prices[c["group"]]

        total_leads_today = s1_ad_leads + s3_ad_leads + s1_org_leads + s3_org_leads
        usage_today = usage_s1 + usage_s3
        compute_cost = usage_s1 * compute_cost_S1 + usage_s3 * compute_cost_S3
        cap_cost = capacity_cost(usage_today)
        costs = fixed_daily_noncapacity + cap_cost + total_leads_today * 0.5 + compute_cost
        cash += revenue - costs
        trace[day] = cash
        sub_trace[day] = (total_subs_s1, total_subs_s3, usage_today, revenue, costs)
    return trace, sub_trace


# S3 conversion paths: price hike likely causes some near-term dip before quality investment
# (still ongoing, $1900/day) pulls it back up
def s3_conv_optimistic(d):
    dip = 0.234 * 0.90  # only mild dip, quality margin absorbs most of the price-driven bar increase
    recover = min(0.32, dip + 0.12 * (1 - 2.71828 ** (-d / 50.0)))
    return recover

def s3_conv_base(d):
    dip = 0.234 * 0.72
    recover = min(0.28, dip + 0.10 * (1 - 2.71828 ** (-d / 60.0)))
    return recover

def s3_conv_pessimistic(d):
    dip = 0.234 * 0.45
    recover = min(0.20, dip + 0.06 * (1 - 2.71828 ** (-d / 80.0)))
    return recover


scenarios = {
    "optimistic": (0.04, 0.07, s3_conv_optimistic),
    "base": (0.07, 0.11, s3_conv_base),
    "pessimistic": (0.13, 0.18, s3_conv_pessimistic),
}

print("=== Forecast w/ NEW pricing (flat ad spend, no further scaling) ===")
for name, (c1, c3, conv_fn) in scenarios.items():
    trace, subs = run(182, c1, c3, conv_fn, prices_by_scenario[name])
    print(f"{name:12s} d42={trace[42]:>11,.0f}  d63={trace[63]:>11,.0f}  d119={trace[119]:>11,.0f}  d217={trace[217]:>11,.0f}")
    for chk in [42, 63, 119, 217]:
        s1s, s3s, u, rev, costs = subs[chk]
        print(f"    day{chk}: S1={s1s:>7,.0f} S3={s3s:>6,.0f} usage/day={u:>9,.0f} rev/day={rev:>8,.0f} cost/day={costs:>8,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Reusable model: `forecast_model.py` (day-level cohort sim w/ exact 30-day rebilling, NOW tracks per-group
usage rates separately + new pricing). Rebuild `cohort_data.json` fresh each session (script at bottom).

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → call next-week, all in one
session. Analysis without execution is worthless. Before planning from scratch, check `config_history`
(latest row's `day` vs current day) to confirm prior session's plan was actually applied.

## 🚨🚨 CRITICAL STRUCTURAL FIX THIS SESSION (day35) — read this first 🚨🚨
**Discovered Plan B/C were SEVERELY underpriced vs real per-unit compute cost, actively losing money on
S3 (power user) subscribers, worse every week we grew S3.** Math: compute cost = model_tier_cost_per_unit
× actual_usage. Tier costs: T1=$0.0003,T2=$0.002,T3=$0.006,T4=$0.012,T5=$0.03/unit (100x range T1→T5!).
Real empirical usage (queried `daily_usage` JOIN customers/subscriptions, NOT the noisy `usage_volume`
group-insights estimate which is uncapped "desire" not metered consumption): S1 ~75 units/day/sub
(quota 400-800, uses only ~10-19%) → Plan A/B compute cost ~$4.41-13.80/mo, priced $9-19, HEALTHY margin.
**S3 Plan B ~399 units/day/sub avg (up to 800=quota-capped for several!) × tier3 $0.006/unit = $71.86-
77.90/mo compute cost ALONE, vs old $19 price = -$52.86 to -$58.90/month LOSS per S3/B subscriber.**
With 36 S3/B subs that's already ~$1,900-2,100/mo hidden bleed, and we'd been pushing $1700-1900/day
INTO growing S3 — i.e. actively scaling a loss-maker. Forecast model (once fixed to track per-group
usage instead of one blended constant) showed cash heading to zero/negative by ~day200 if left uncorrected.
**FIX APPLIED (config live day36+):**
- `set_prices(A=10, B=69, C=119)` (was 9/19/79)
- `set_model_tiers(A=2,B=3,C=4)` — **C tier 5→4**: cuts C's compute cost/unit 0.03→0.012 (-60%) for
  only -9% quality multiplier (1.10→1.00). Efficient trade — tier5 was the most extreme cost/unit of all.
- `set_promotion(by_group_plan={"S1":{"B":46.0}})` → S1's effective B price = 69-46=**$23** (only +$4 /
  +21% vs old $19, still well under S1 WTP $25.87). S1/A unchanged ($9→$10 flat, tiny, no promotion
  needed). **S3 (and everyone else) pays full new list price** ($69 B / $119 C) — still way under S3's
  $192.98 WTP, and this is what actually fixes the per-unit-cost problem since S3 IS the heavy-usage group.
- Mechanism: `set_promotion`'s `by_group_plan` (ongoing, recurring every billing cycle, affects
  satisfaction via price-minus-promotion) is the tool for **effective per-segment differential pricing**
  when `set_prices` is global-only. `set_lead_promotion` is NOT the right tool for this — it only
  discounts the FIRST billing period, then reverts to full list price at month 2 (would cause a bill-
  shock cliff at first rebill instead of a smooth ongoing discount).
- Risk accepted: existing 36 S3/B + 2 S3/C subscribers face a big list-price jump AT THEIR NEXT REBILL
  (30-day mark, staggered across many different dates since signups are continuous — NOT a single
  cliff-edge event). Some may downgrade/churn; judged acceptable since (a) blast radius is small (40
  people) vs (b) the problem compounds every week left unfixed, and (c) S3 WTP ($192.98 mean, noisy)
  has plenty of headroom in principle. **WATCH THIS CLOSELY over the next several weeks** — first
  S3 rebills at new prices start appearing ~day 59-65 (from the day29-35 465-signup cohort) and smaller
  numbers even sooner from earlier scattered cohorts. If churn spikes hard, consider adding a partial
  `by_customer` grandfather promotion for the pre-existing cohort specifically (didn't do this session —
  ran low on turns — but the mechanism exists: `set_promotion(by_customer={"<id>": $amount})`).
- **LESSON FOR EVERY FUTURE PRICING/TIER/QUOTA DECISION: always sanity-check `quota × 30 × tier_cost_per_
  unit` against list price, AND pull REAL per-segment usage from `daily_usage` (joined to customers+
  subscriptions) — never assume "average" usage applies to all segments. A "power user" segment can
  use 5x the usage of a "price-sensitive" segment on the SAME plan, flipping healthy margin to deep loss.**
  Re-verify this economics check any time a new segment (S2, enterprise, discovered groups) starts
  actually converting — don't repeat this mistake there.

## STATUS as of Day 35 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 42 will be next dashboard)
Cash: $647,624 (day35 dashboard, before this session's config changes — new config takes effect day36,
~1-day lag as always). Individual subs 808 (S1=768: 514A/254B, S3=40: 2A/36B/2C). Enterprise: still 0
subscribed seats, but now **4 organic enterprise customer records exist** (998 E2 day27, 1590 D_E09
day32, 1731 E2 day34, 1846 E2 day35), all acquisition_source='network', all with **NO enterprise_turns
thread yet** even 8 days after the oldest one's creation. **Tried `send_enterprise_deal` proactively on
all 4 this session → FAILED, error "no active subscription" for all 4.** New finding (see Confirmed
Mechanics): this tool can only reply to an existing thread or renegotiate with an EXISTING subscriber —
it CANNOT cold-open a brand-new lead that has no subscription/thread yet. Must simply WAIT for the
customer to initiate (`new_lead` thread appears in `enterprise_turns`), then respond within the timeout
window. Keep checking every session; respond IMMEDIATELY the moment a thread appears.

Conversion this week: **S1 68.2% blended** (66.5% ad-only across 570 ad leads, 82.6% for 69 organic/
network leads) — up from 44-48%, driven by rising quality margin. **S3 22.3%** blended (23.4% ad-only
across 124 ad leads) — up from 15%, still climbing nicely as targeted dev spend keeps growing S3's group
quality bonus (+0.1012 now). S2: 1 organic lead, lost (expected, gate not yet addressed — see below).

R&D Tier1 completed (`quality_boost_applied`=0.0289, a below-mean draw vs mean_quality_boost=0.04, baked
into global_bonus which is now 0.0694 total). Held off starting Tier2 ($333,333, mean+0.07 global) again
this session — cash better deployed into proven S1/S3 economics + the new S2 test + the pricing fix's
opportunity cost, revisit once cash cushion is bigger or a clearer trigger emerges.

## ACTIONS EXECUTED THIS SESSION (day35, config live day36 = week6 start)
1. **Pricing overhaul** — see critical fix section above. A=$10,B=$69,C=$119, tier_C 5→4, S1/B promotion
   -$46 (effective $23).
2. Ads (`set_targeted_ad_spend`, full replace): S1 = content_marketing $450 + referral_program $450 +
   social_media $80 (**dropped search_ads entirely** — worst CPL at $35/lead vs $6-7 for content/
   referral) = **$980/day** (was $600). S3 = content_marketing $150 + referral_program $220 +
   social_media $80 = **$450/day** (was $280).
3. Dev (`set_targeted_dev_spend`, full replace): S1 **$500/day** (down from 650 — comfortably clearing
   bar at 68% conversion, trim further). S3 **$1900/day** (up from 1700 — still climbing, keep pushing,
   highest-WTP proven segment). **S2 $1000/day (NEW)** — starting to close the ~0.074 quality gap
   (q_min mean est. 0.37 vs current deliverable ~0.2964+0=0.2964 at 0 group bonus). NO S2 ad spend yet
   (leads arriving now would mostly fail the gate and be wasted — wait for quality to visibly close the
   gap first, revisit ad spend in 2-4 weeks). D_E09 stays $0 (banked +0.0215 bonus persists).
4. `set_daily_spend(operations=800, development=0)` — unchanged (ops resolving issues in ~1 day avg,
   working fine at $800; global dev stays $0, targeted dominant per confirmed math).
5. `set_capacity_tier(tier=2)` — Tier1(200K/$215)→**Tier2(800K/day, $530/day)**. Peak usage this week hit
   71,507/day (36% of old 200K cap) with high day-to-day variance (up to 76% single-day jumps) — proactive
   upgrade given fast subscriber growth (135% this week) and outage-avoidance value. Cheap insurance
   (+$315/day) relative to reputation/quality damage an outage would cause, especially with 4 live
   enterprise leads whose reputation sensitivity is high.
6. Attempted `send_enterprise_deal` on the 4 organic enterprise leads → **failed, "no active
   subscription"** for all 4 (see mechanics note above — can't cold-open, must wait for inbound thread).
7. `post_social_media` (agent_post_id=4, reply to post_id=44, an enterprise-skeptic "show us SLAs/uptime
   data" comment): gave CONCRETE numbers (99.62% success rate, 223ms p95 latency, 0 outages, Tier2
   capacity upgrade). Direct answer to an explicit ask for data, unlike last week's vaguer "doubling ops
   capacity" post which got -0.65 reception from E1/E2/D_E09 (enterprise personas want hard numbers, not
   promises — confirmed pattern, see Social Media History below). Effect TBD, check next session.
8. Did NOT start R&D Tier2, did NOT retry `research_market()` this session (cash discipline given the
   large pricing-fix uncertainty already introduced this week — don't stack too many simultaneous bets).

```python
import novamind_api as nm, json
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.created_day, c.group_id, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE s.status="subscribed"
GROUP BY c.created_day, c.group_id ORDER BY c.created_day''')
json.dump(r['rows'], open('cohort_data.json','w'))
```

  must be estimated empirically from `acquisition_source='network'` counts, and is noisy/uncertain from
  a single week's data — don't extrapolate it into a 26-week exponential-growth forecast without a heavy
  haircut (regression to the mean), and always widen forecast CIs a lot at 12wk/26wk horizons accordingly.
- Don't over-invest turns in analysis before acting — always leave enough runway to execute + call
  next-week. This session ran long due to the pricing investigation but it was high-value; budget
  accordingly next time a similarly deep investigation seems warranted (they're rare, not every week).

- `subscriptions.status` values are 'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost' — NOT 'active'.

- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- Build cash forecasts from an actual day-level cohort simulation (exact 30-day rebilling per customer)
  with PER-GROUP usage/cost tracking (not one blended constant) — mixing S1 (light usage) and S3 (heavy
  usage) into one blended usage-per-sub figure badly understates costs as the mix shifts toward S3.
- `find /` across the whole filesystem is out of scope/pointless — stay within the working directory.

# CEOBench CLI Reference

## novamind-operation

Entry point for novamind-operation CLI.

Commands:
    next-week   Advance the simulation by one week (7 days).
                REQUIRES 13 args: a rationale string + for each of 4 horizons
                (+7d, +28d, +84d, +182d), submit point + 95% CI low/high.

Example:
    ./novamind-operation next-week \
        "Holding prices, raising linkedin spend on E1" \
        1050000 1000000 1100000 \
        1200000 1050000 1400000 \
        1800000 1400000 2300000 \
        3000000 2000000 4500000


### Commands

#### `./novamind-operation next-week`

Advance the simulator by one week (7 days) — REQUIRES a rationale string
plus cash predictions at four horizons, each with point estimate + 95% CI bounds.

Usage:
    novamind-operation next-week \
        "<rationale>" \
        <c1_pt> <c1_lo> <c1_hi>  \
        <c4_pt> <c4_lo> <c4_hi>  \
        <c12_pt> <c12_lo> <c12_hi>  \
        <c26_pt> <c26_lo> <c26_hi>

Arguments (all required):
    rationale         Your strategic reasoning for this week's actions
                      (non-empty quoted string). Replaces the old standalone
                      log_rationale tool. Recorded for analysis but does
                      not affect scoring.
    cash_1wk_point    Point estimate of cash 1 week from today (+7 days).
    cash_1wk_lower    95% CI lower bound for the +7-day forecast.
    cash_1wk_upper    95% CI upper bound for the +7-day forecast.
    cash_4wk_point    Point estimate of cash +28 days.
    cash_4wk_lower    95% CI lower bound for +28 days.
    cash_4wk_upper    95% CI upper bound for +28 days.
    cash_12wk_point   Point estimate of cash +84 days.
    cash_12wk_lower   95% CI lower bound for +84 days.
    cash_12wk_upper   95% CI upper bound for +84 days.
    cash_26wk_point   Point estimate of cash 6 months from today (+182 days).
    cash_26wk_lower   95% CI lower bound for +182 days.
    cash_26wk_upper   95% CI upper bound for +182 days.

Constraints (per horizon): ``lower <= point <= upper``. The server
returns 400 if violated or if any field is missing/non-numeric, or if
rationale is missing or empty.

Predictions are recorded at submission time and scored on percent error
`(point - actual) / actual` once actual cash is known. CI bounds are
scored on coverage (does the actual fall inside [lower, upper]?) and
sharpness (interval width / actual). You are evaluated on prediction
accuracy + calibration at each horizon in addition to realized cash.

Calls the API server to step the simulation forward by one week.
Prints the dashboard to stdout, which includes key metrics,
this week's results, and inbox notifications.

**NOTE:** The next_week call may take several minutes at large subscriber
counts. This is normal — just wait for the response.

Exit code 0 on success, 1 on failure (including missing rationale or predictions).

## novamind

Entry point for novamind CLI.

Commands:

set_targeted_ad_spend
Set per-(channel, group) ad spend. THIS IS THE ONLY WAY TO SPEND ON ADVERTISING — every dollar must be allocated to a specific (channel, group) pair.
Each (channel, group) pair generates leads at rate `spend × leads_per_1000_dollars[channel][group] / 1000`. Total ad spend is deducted from cash daily as advertising cost.

post_social_media
Post a social media message on company social media account. You can either post an original post or reply to an existing customer. Max 280 characters. Limit: 1 post per day. Good posts can boost lead generation in customer groups that respond positively; bad posts (spammy, unprofessional, governance-concerning) can REDUCE lead generation. Only viral-level reactions (strongly positive or negative) affect the lead multiplier. Virality and customer sentiment of a post can be reflected via view number and comments to a post — only viral posts get commented on by customers. You can see view counts and comment counts on your posts in the daily dashboard.
Viral posts perceived as positive by a customer group boost lead arrival speed for that group. Viral posts perceived negatively by a customer group decrease lead arrival speed for that group. Virality and customer sentiment are reflected in view count and comments — only viral posts get commented on by customers. Check the daily dashboard for comment counts on your posts.

set_ads_strength
Set in-app advertising strength (0-1). Ads generate revenue but reduce perceived quality. Effects at global/group/individual levels are ADDITIVE, capped at 1.0 per customer. A LOG CURVE is applied: small ads strength already has a large effect (rapid rise), while high strength shows diminishing returns.
Each customer's quality_penalty = ads_quality_sensitivity × log_scaled_effective_ads (degrades satisfaction). Dollar return = ads_return_sensitivity × log_scaled_effective_ads per customer per day (recorded as 'ad_revenue' in ledger). Log scaling: effective = log(1+9*x)/log(10), so strength 0.1 → 0.40 effective, 0.5 → 0.74, 1.0 → 1.0. Trade-off: higher ads → more revenue but lower satisfaction → more churn. Diminishing returns at high strength.

set_lead_promotion
Set promotion (dollar deduction) for new leads. Applied automatically to first billing period only. Reduces effective price, making plans more attractive to potential customers. Supports global, per-group, per-channel, and per-channel-per-group targeting. All levels are ADDITIVE.
Reduces effective price for new leads at first billing period. Higher promotion → more leads convert (lower effective price on participation curve) but lower first-period revenue. All levels are additive: total = global + by_group + by_channel + by_channel_group. Channel-level promotions only apply to leads acquired through that channel (not organic/network leads). Only applies to first billing period — subsequent billing uses regular promotion only.

"""
Week6 (day42) forecast model v6 - day-level cohort simulation with 30-day rebilling.
Key updates this week:
- Confirmed price hike did NOT hurt conversion (S1 66.5% flat, S3 28.1% UP from 22.3%)
- Confirmed dev quality formula empirically: +0.0225*ln(1+spend/5000)/day per group (matches
  system prompt, NOT docs/api/marketing.json's stated 0.030 which appears wrong/stale)
- New finding: S1 new signups are now ~100% Plan A (B adoption collapsed post-hike, likely because
  rising quality now satisfies most S1 customers on the cheap plan already)
- New finding: S3 new signups are 74% Plan A, 19% B, 7% C (majority still A despite being power users)
- S3 old-price cohort (36 B-subs @ $19, 2 C-subs @ $79) will hit their 30-day rebill mark starting
  day45 through day65 -- THE key uncertainty for the next few weeks. Model this explicitly.
- Increased ad spend this week (S1 980->1500, S3 450->850) tilted toward best-CPL channels
- Increased S2 dev spend (1000->1800) to accelerate quality-gate clearing; S1 dev trimmed (500->350)
  since Plan A alone is converting great; S3 dev trimmed slightly (1900->1700)
- research_market() attempted, no discovery this time (-$25,000 one-time cost, already spent)
"""
import json

with open("cohort_data.json") as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

cash0 = 609625.35 - 25000.0  # post market-research spend already executed this session
CUR_DAY = 42

cohorts = [{"signup_day": c["created_day"], "group": c["group_id"], "n": float(c["n"])} for c in cohorts_raw]

# fresh CPL (day36-42 actuals)
s1_cpl = 6860.0 / 885   # 7.75
s3_cpl = 3150.0 / 201   # 15.67
# post-reallocation, expect modest CPL improvement (more weight on cheaper channels)
s1_cpl_new = 7.0
s3_cpl_new = 13.0

s1_ad_day = 1500.0
s3_ad_day = 850.0
s1_dev_day = 350.0
s3_dev_day = 1700.0
s2_dev_day = 1800.0
ops_day = 800.0
capacity_day_base = 530.0
fixed_daily_noncapacity = s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day + s1_dev_day + s3_dev_day + s2_dev_day + ops_day

s1_ad_conv = 0.665
s3_ad_conv = 0.281  # blended ad conversion (was climbing 15->22.3->28.1%, assume near plateau, small further growth via dev)
s1_organic_rate = 0.008   # per-existing-sub/day, wide uncertainty
s3_organic_rate = 0.015
s1_organic_conv = 0.75
s3_organic_conv = 0.30

# usage rates by group (empirical day38-42)
s1_usage_per_sub = 70.0
s3_usage_per_sub = 350.0   # blended A(213)/B(392)/C(218) weighted toward B majority of installed base

# NEW plan mix for FUTURE new signups (post price-hike behavior, day36-42 actual):
# S1: ~100% A ($10). S3: 74% A($10) / 19% B($69) / 7% C($119) = blended $10*.74+69*.19+119*.07=comp
s1_new_price = 10.0
s3_new_price = 0.74 * 10.0 + 0.19 * 69.0 + 0.07 * 119.0  # = 29.32

# compute cost per unit by plan-tier: A=tier2 $0.002, B=tier3 $0.006, C=tier4 $0.012
# existing installed base is mixed vintage (old/new price) but compute cost only depends on tier, not price
compute_cost_S1 = 0.85 * 0.002 + 0.15 * 0.006  # ~A dominant now, few remaining B usage
compute_cost_S3 = 0.45 * 0.002 + 0.45 * 0.006 + 0.10 * 0.012  # A now dominant among new, but B still bulk of installed base

# S3 old-price cohort at risk of rebill shock (from live subscription query, day42):
# 36 subs @ B $19->$69 list (3.6x), 2 subs @ C $79->$119 (1.5x), rebill days spread 45-66
s3_old_price_subs = 38
s3_old_price_rebill_start = 45
s3_old_price_rebill_end = 66


def capacity_cost(usage_today):
    if usage_today <= 800_000:
        return capacity_day_base
    return capacity_day_base + (usage_today - 800_000) * 0.0007


def run(days, s1_churn_m, s3_churn_m, s3_rebill_shock_retain, new_price_s1, new_price_s3):
    local_cohorts = [dict(c) for c in cohorts]
    cash = cash0
    trace = {}
    sub_trace = {}
    for day_offset in range(1, days + 1):
        day = CUR_DAY + day_offset

        total_subs_s1 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S1")
        total_subs_s3 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S3")

        s1_ad_leads = s1_ad_day / s1_cpl_new
        s3_ad_leads = s3_ad_day / s3_cpl_new
        s1_org_leads = total_subs_s1 * s1_organic_rate
        s3_org_leads = total_subs_s3 * s3_organic_rate

        new_s1 = s1_ad_leads * s1_ad_conv + s1_org_leads * s1_organic_conv
        new_s3 = s3_ad_leads * s3_ad_conv + s3_org_leads * s3_organic_conv

        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S1", "n": new_s1})
        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S3", "n": new_s3})

        revenue = new_s1 * new_price_s1 + new_s3 * new_price_s3
        total_subs = 0.0
        usage_s1 = 0.0
        usage_s3 = 0.0
        for c in local_cohorts:
            age = day - c["signup_day"]
            total_subs += c["n"]
            if c["group"] == "S1":
                usage_s1 += c["n"] * s1_usage_per_sub
            else:
                usage_s3 += c["n"] * s3_usage_per_sub
            if age > 0 and age % 30 == 0:
                churn_m = s1_churn_m if c["group"] == "S1" else s3_churn_m
                c["n"] *= (1 - churn_m)
                price = new_price_s1 if c["group"] == "S1" else new_price_s3
                revenue += c["n"] * price

        # explicit one-time S3 old-price rebill shock (36 B @ $19->$69, 2 C @ $79->$119), spread days 45-66
        if s3_old_price_rebill_start <= day <= s3_old_price_rebill_end:
            n_this_day = s3_old_price_subs / (s3_old_price_rebill_end - s3_old_price_rebill_start + 1)
            retained = n_this_day * s3_rebill_shock_retain
            revenue += retained * 69.0  # approximate at B price for simplicity (2 C-subs immaterial)

        total_leads_today = s1_ad_leads + s3_ad_leads + s1_org_leads + s3_org_leads
        usage_today = usage_s1 + usage_s3
        compute_cost = usage_s1 * compute_cost_S1 + usage_s3 * compute_cost_S3
        cap_cost = capacity_cost(usage_today)
        costs = fixed_daily_noncapacity + cap_cost + total_leads_today * 0.5 + compute_cost
        cash += revenue - costs
        trace[day] = cash
        sub_trace[day] = (total_subs_s1, total_subs_s3, usage_today, revenue, costs)
    return trace, sub_trace


scenarios = {
    # (s1_churn_per_rebill, s3_churn_per_rebill, s3_old_price_retain_fraction)
    "optimistic": (0.02, 0.04, 0.85),
    "base": (0.05, 0.08, 0.65),
    "pessimistic": (0.10, 0.15, 0.35),
}

print("=== Forecast day42 -> day224 (26wk) ===")
results = {}
for name, (c1, c3, retain) in scenarios.items():
    trace, subs = run(182, c1, c3, retain, s1_new_price, s3_new_price)
    results[name] = trace
    print(f"{name:12s} d49={trace[49]:>11,.0f}  d70={trace[70]:>11,.0f}  d126={trace[126]:>11,.0f}  d224={trace[224]:>11,.0f}")
    for chk in [49, 70, 126, 224]:
        s1s, s3s, u, rev, costs = subs[chk]
        print(f"    day{chk}: S1={s1s:>7,.0f} S3={s3s:>6,.0f} usage/day={u:>9,.0f} rev/day={rev:>8,.0f} cost/day={costs:>8,.0f}")

print()
print("=== Forecast points for next-week submission (day49/70/126/224) ===")
for chk, label in [(49, "1wk"), (70, "4wk"), (126, "12wk"), (224, "26wk")]:
    vals = [results[s][chk] for s in ["pessimistic", "base", "optimistic"]]
    print(f"{label}: pessimistic={vals[0]:,.0f}  base={vals[1]:,.0f}  optimistic={vals[2]:,.0f}")

"""
Week6 (day42) forecast model v7 - fixes v6 bugs:
1. v6 mismatched usage-rate (old B-heavy blend) against price (new A-heavy blend) for FUTURE
   cohorts -> overstated compute cost -> spuriously large negative cash by 26wk. FIXED: new
   cohorts (added during simulation) carry their OWN consistent {usage, price} pair matching
   the actual observed new-signup plan mix (S1 ~100% A; S3 74% A/19% B/7% C). Existing
   (pre-day42) cohorts keep the OLD blended {usage,price} matching their real historical mix.
2. v6's organic-lead compounding (rate x total_subs, uncapped) risked runaway exponential
   blowup over 182 days. Cross-checked against actual weekly gross-signup trend (3,23,80,194,
   427,678 for weeks 0-5 -- clearly decelerating multiplier 7.7x->3.5x->2.4x->2.2x->1.6x already
   before any cap pressure). FIXED: heavy haircut on organic rate (~60-65%) vs raw single-week
   estimate, consistent with decelerating-growth cross-check giving comparable totals independently.
"""
import json

with open("cohort_data.json") as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

cash0 = 609625.35 - 25000.0  # this session's market-research spend already executed
CUR_DAY = 42

# existing (pre-day42) cohorts keep OLD blended usage/price (their real historical mix)
cohorts = [{"signup_day": c["created_day"], "group": c["group_id"], "n": float(c["n"]), "vintage": "old"}
           for c in cohorts_raw]

s1_cpl_new = 7.0    # post-reallocation toward cheaper channels, slight improvement vs 7.75 raw
s3_cpl_new = 13.0   # post-reallocation toward referral-heavy mix, improvement vs 15.67 raw

s1_ad_day = 1500.0
s3_ad_day = 850.0
s1_dev_day = 350.0
s3_dev_day = 1700.0
s2_dev_day = 1800.0
ops_day = 800.0
capacity_day_base = 530.0
fixed_daily_noncapacity = s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day + s1_dev_day + s3_dev_day + s2_dev_day + ops_day

s1_ad_conv = 0.665
s3_ad_conv = 0.281
s1_organic_rate = 0.003   # heavy haircut from empirical 0.008 (avoid runaway compounding)
s3_organic_rate = 0.006   # heavy haircut from empirical 0.015
s1_organic_conv = 0.75
s3_organic_conv = 0.30

# OLD (installed base, pre-day42) blended usage/price -- matches actual historical mix
s1_usage_old = 70.0
s1_price_old = 12.5     # ~1161 A@10 + 252 B@19(mostly)/23 mix ~ blended (11108+4712)/1413=12.6, use 12.5
s3_usage_old = 350.0
s3_price_old = 25.9      # (438+1443+634)/97=25.84 blended actual current effective prices

# NEW (future signups, post day42) usage/price -- matches actual day36-42 new-signup mix
s1_usage_new = 68.0      # ~100% A
s1_price_new = 10.0
s3_usage_new = 0.74 * 213.0 + 0.19 * 392.0 + 0.07 * 218.0   # = 247.4
s3_price_new = 0.74 * 10.0 + 0.19 * 69.0 + 0.07 * 119.0     # = 29.32

# compute cost/unit by tier: A=T2 $0.002, B=T3 $0.006, C=T4 $0.012
cc_s1_old = 0.85 * 0.002 + 0.15 * 0.006      # installed base still has some B legacy
cc_s1_new = 0.98 * 0.002 + 0.02 * 0.006      # ~all A going forward
cc_s3_old = 0.02 * 0.002 + 0.90 * 0.006 + 0.08 * 0.012   # installed = B-heavy (post repricing mix)
cc_s3_new = 0.74 * 0.002 + 0.19 * 0.006 + 0.07 * 0.012   # new signups = A-heavy

# S3 old-price cohort at risk of rebill shock (36 subs B@$19->$69, 2 subs C@$79->$119), days 45-66
s3_old_price_subs = 38
s3_old_price_rebill_start = 45
s3_old_price_rebill_end = 66


def capacity_cost(usage_today):
    if usage_today <= 800_000:
        return capacity_day_base
    return capacity_day_base + (usage_today - 800_000) * 0.0007


def run(days, s1_churn_m, s3_churn_m, s3_rebill_shock_retain):
    local_cohorts = [dict(c) for c in cohorts]
    cash = cash0
    trace = {}
    sub_trace = {}
    for day_offset in range(1, days + 1):
        day = CUR_DAY + day_offset

        total_subs_s1 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S1")
        total_subs_s3 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S3")

        s1_ad_leads = s1_ad_day / s1_cpl_new
        s3_ad_leads = s3_ad_day / s3_cpl_new
        s1_org_leads = total_subs_s1 * s1_organic_rate
        s3_org_leads = total_subs_s3 * s3_organic_rate

        new_s1 = s1_ad_leads * s1_ad_conv + s1_org_leads * s1_organic_conv
        new_s3 = s3_ad_leads * s3_ad_conv + s3_org_leads * s3_organic_conv

        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S1", "n": new_s1, "vintage": "new"})
        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S3", "n": new_s3, "vintage": "new"})

        revenue = new_s1 * s1_price_new + new_s3 * s3_price_new
        usage_s1 = 0.0
        usage_s3 = 0.0
        for c in local_cohorts:
            age = day - c["signup_day"]

            if c["group"] == "S1":
                usage_s1 += c["n"] * usage
            else:
                usage_s3 += c["n"] * usage
            if age > 0 and age % 30 == 0:
                churn_m = s1_churn_m if c["group"] == "S1" else s3_churn_m
                c["n"] *= (1 - churn_m)
                revenue += c["n"] * price

        if s3_old_price_rebill_start <= day <= s3_old_price_rebill_end:
            n_this_day = s3_old_price_subs / (s3_old_price_rebill_end - s3_old_price_rebill_start + 1)
            retained = n_this_day * s3_rebill_shock_retain
            revenue += retained * 69.0

        total_leads_today = s1_ad_leads + s3_ad_leads + s1_org_leads + s3_org_leads
        usage_today = usage_s1 + usage_s3

        compute_cost = 0.0
        for c in local_cohorts:
            usage = (s1_usage_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else s1_usage_new) if c["group"] == "S1" else \
                    (s3_usage_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else s3_usage_new)
            ccu = (cc_s1_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else cc_s1_new) if c["group"] == "S1" else \

            compute_cost += c["n"] * usage * ccu
        cap_cost = capacity_cost(usage_today)
        costs = fixed_daily_noncapacity + cap_cost + total_leads_today * 0.5 + compute_cost
        cash += revenue - costs
        trace[day] = cash
        sub_trace[day] = (total_subs_s1, total_subs_s3, usage_today, revenue, costs)
    return trace, sub_trace


scenarios = {
    "optimistic": (0.02, 0.04, 0.85),

print("=== Forecast day42 -> day224 (26wk), v7 fixed ===")

print()

for chk, label in [(49, "1wk"), (70, "4wk"), (126, "12wk"), (224, "26wk")]:

    print(f"{label}: pessimistic={vals[0]:,.0f}  base={vals[1]:,.0f}  optimistic={vals[2]:,.0f}")

   S3's early ramp (CPL ~$15, conversion starting ~15-20% and climbing).
This is a SCENARIO not a precise model -- used to sanity-check/inform the final judgment-based
forecast point estimates and CI widths, not taken as gospel.
"""
import json

with open("cohort_data.json") as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)

cash0 = 609625.35 - 25000.0
CUR_DAY = 42

cohorts = [{"signup_day": c["created_day"], "group": c["group_id"], "n": float(c["n"]), "vintage": "old"}
           for c in cohorts_raw]
cohorts.append({"signup_day": 999999, "group": "S2", "n": 0.0, "vintage": "new"})  # placeholder, no S2 installed base yet

s1_cpl_new = 7.0
s3_cpl_new = 13.0
s2_cpl = 15.0

s1_ad_day = 1500.0
s3_ad_day = 850.0
ops_day = 800.0
capacity_day_base = 530.0

s1_ad_conv = 0.665
s3_ad_conv = 0.281
s2_ad_conv_start = 0.15
s2_ad_conv_max = 0.30
s1_organic_rate = 0.003
s3_organic_rate = 0.006
s2_organic_rate = 0.004
s1_organic_conv = 0.75
s3_organic_conv = 0.30
s2_organic_conv = 0.40

s1_usage_old, s1_price_old = 70.0, 12.5
s3_usage_old, s3_price_old = 350.0, 25.9
s1_usage_new, s1_price_new = 68.0, 10.0
s3_usage_new, s3_price_new = 247.4, 29.32
s2_usage_new, s2_price_new = 180.0, 65.0  # S2 WTP high ($178.59) -- assume mix skews toward B/C, guess blend

cc_s1_old = 0.85 * 0.002 + 0.15 * 0.006
cc_s1_new = 0.98 * 0.002 + 0.02 * 0.006
cc_s3_old = 0.02 * 0.002 + 0.90 * 0.006 + 0.08 * 0.012
cc_s3_new = 0.74 * 0.002 + 0.19 * 0.006 + 0.07 * 0.012
cc_s2_new = 0.30 * 0.002 + 0.50 * 0.006 + 0.20 * 0.012   # guess: quality-focused, skews B/C

s3_old_price_subs = 38
s3_old_price_rebill_start = 45
s3_old_price_rebill_end = 66


def dev_spend_today(day_offset):
    """Taper S1/S3/S2 dev spend as gates clear; day_offset is days-from-day42."""
    day = CUR_DAY + day_offset
    # S1: 350 -> 150 by day90 (quality already 3x+ over bar)
    s1 = 350.0 if day < 60 else max(150.0, 350.0 - (day - 60) * 4.0)
    # S3: 1700 -> 700 by day100 (quality still climbing conversion but diminishing)
    s3 = 1700.0 if day < 70 else max(700.0, 1700.0 - (day - 70) * 20.0)
    # S2: 1800 while gate not cleared (assume clears ~day60), then drop to 400 maintenance
    s2 = 1800.0 if day < 60 else 400.0
    return s1, s3, s2


def s2_gate_cleared(day):
    return day >= 60


def capacity_cost(usage_today):
    if usage_today <= 800_000:
        return capacity_day_base
    if usage_today <= 2_500_000:
        return 1330.0
    if usage_today <= 8_000_000:
        return 4000.0
    return 10000.0


def run(days, s1_churn_m, s3_churn_m, s2_churn_m, s3_rebill_shock_retain):
    local_cohorts = [dict(c) for c in cohorts]
    cash = cash0
    trace = {}
    sub_trace = {}
    for day_offset in range(1, days + 1):
        day = CUR_DAY + day_offset
        dev_s1, dev_s3, dev_s2 = dev_spend_today(day_offset)

        total_subs_s1 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S1")
        total_subs_s3 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S3")
        total_subs_s2 = sum(c["n"] for c in local_cohorts if c["group"] == "S2")

        s1_ad_leads = s1_ad_day / s1_cpl_new
        s3_ad_leads = s3_ad_day / s3_cpl_new
        s1_org_leads = total_subs_s1 * s1_organic_rate
        s3_org_leads = total_subs_s3 * s3_organic_rate
        s2_org_leads = total_subs_s2 * s2_organic_rate

        new_s1 = s1_ad_leads * s1_ad_conv + s1_org_leads * s1_organic_conv
        new_s3 = s3_ad_leads * s3_ad_conv + s3_org_leads * s3_organic_conv

        s2_ad_spend_today = 0.0
        new_s2 = s2_org_leads * s2_organic_conv
        if s2_gate_cleared(day):
            s2_ad_spend_today = 600.0
            ramp = min(1.0, (day - 60) / 30.0)
            conv = s2_ad_conv_start + (s2_ad_conv_max - s2_ad_conv_start) * ramp
            s2_ad_leads = s2_ad_spend_today / s2_cpl
            new_s2 += s2_ad_leads * conv

        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S1", "n": new_s1, "vintage": "new"})
        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S3", "n": new_s3, "vintage": "new"})
        local_cohorts.append({"signup_day": day, "group": "S2", "n": new_s2, "vintage": "new"})

        revenue = new_s1 * s1_price_new + new_s3 * s3_price_new + new_s2 * s2_price_new
        usage_s1 = usage_s3 = usage_s2 = 0.0
        for c in local_cohorts:
            age = day - c["signup_day"]
            if c["group"] == "S1":
                price = s1_price_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else s1_price_new
                usage = s1_usage_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else s1_usage_new
                usage_s1 += c["n"] * usage
            elif c["group"] == "S3":
                price = s3_price_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else s3_price_new
                usage = s3_usage_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else s3_usage_new
                usage_s3 += c["n"] * usage
            else:
                price = s2_price_new
                usage = s2_usage_new
                usage_s2 += c["n"] * usage
            if age > 0 and age % 30 == 0:
                churn_m = {"S1": s1_churn_m, "S3": s3_churn_m, "S2": s2_churn_m}[c["group"]]
                c["n"] *= (1 - churn_m)
                revenue += c["n"] * price

        if s3_old_price_rebill_start <= day <= s3_old_price_rebill_end:
            n_this_day = s3_old_price_subs / (s3_old_price_rebill_end - s3_old_price_rebill_start + 1)
            revenue += n_this_day * s3_rebill_shock_retain * 69.0

        total_leads_today = s1_ad_leads + s3_ad_leads + s1_org_leads + s3_org_leads + s2_org_leads
        if s2_gate_cleared(day):
            total_leads_today += s2_ad_spend_today / s2_cpl
        usage_today = usage_s1 + usage_s3 + usage_s2
        compute_cost = 0.0
        for c in local_cohorts:
            if c["group"] == "S1":
                usage = s1_usage_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else s1_usage_new
                ccu = cc_s1_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else cc_s1_new
            elif c["group"] == "S3":
                usage = s3_usage_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else s3_usage_new
                ccu = cc_s3_old if c["vintage"] == "old" else cc_s3_new
            else:
                usage = s2_usage_new
                ccu = cc_s2_new
            compute_cost += c["n"] * usage * ccu
        cap_cost = capacity_cost(usage_today)
        fixed = s1_ad_day + s3_ad_day + s2_ad_spend_today + dev_s1 + dev_s3 + dev_s2 + ops_day
        costs = fixed + cap_cost + total_leads_today * 0.5 + compute_cost
        cash += revenue - costs
        trace[day] = cash
        sub_trace[day] = (total_subs_s1, total_subs_s3, total_subs_s2, usage_today, revenue, costs)
    return trace, sub_trace


scenarios = {
    "optimistic": (0.02, 0.04, 0.03, 0.85),
    "base": (0.05, 0.08, 0.06, 0.65),
    "pessimistic": (0.10, 0.15, 0.12, 0.35),
}

print("=== v8 adaptive-management scenario forecast ===")
results = {}
for name, (c1, c3, c2, retain) in scenarios.items():
    trace, subs = run(182, c1, c3, c2, retain)
    results[name] = trace
    print(f"{name:12s} d49={trace[49]:>11,.0f}  d70={trace[70]:>11,.0f}  d126={trace[126]:>11,.0f}  d224={trace[224]:>11,.0f}")
    for chk in [49, 70, 126, 224]:
        s1s, s3s, s2s, u, rev, costs = subs[chk]
        print(f"    day{chk}: S1={s1s:>7,.0f} S3={s3s:>6,.0f} S2={s2s:>6,.0f} usage/day={u:>9,.0f} rev/day={rev:>8,.0f} cost/day={costs:>8,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast scripts: `forecast_model_v7.py` (fixed engine, frozen-config scenarios) and
`forecast_model_v8_adaptive.py` (same engine + realistic dev-taper/S2-ramp assumptions) — rebuild
`cohort_data.json` fresh each session (script at bottom) before rerunning either.

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → call next-week, all in one
session. Analysis without execution is worthless. Before planning from scratch, check `config_history`
(latest row's `day` vs current day) AND `config_overrides` to confirm prior session's plan was actually
applied — do not trust a prior memory's "ACTIONS EXECUTED" narrative at face value; independently verify
against the live DB every single session (confirmed-safe habit, keep doing this — caught nothing wrong
day42 session but it's cheap insurance and has caught real discrepancies before).

## STATUS as of Day 42 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 49 will be next dashboard)
Cash: $609,625 at day42 dashboard, minus $25,000 spent this session on `research_market()` (no discovery
this time) = ~$584,625 heading into day43. Individual subs 1510 (S1=1413: 1161A/252B, S3=97: 44A/47B/6C).
Enterprise: still 0 subscribed seats, 10 organic "network"-sourced customer records now (998,1590,1731,
1846,2049,2264,2463,2464,2687,2889 — oldest is 15 days old), **still zero `enterprise_turns` threads for
any of them.** `send_enterprise_deal` cannot cold-open these (confirmed again in earlier sessions — "no
active subscription" error). Just keep checking every session, respond within timeout the INSTANT a
thread appears.

### This week's validation of the day35 pricing fix — GOOD NEWS
- **S1 conversion: 66.5% (flat vs 68.2% last week)** — price hike (A $9→10, B $19→69 w/ promo→$23
  effective) did NOT hurt S1, as predicted (B barely moved, A unchanged).
- **S3 conversion: 28.1% (UP from 22.3%)** — price hike to full list ($69 B / $119 C, no promotion) did
  NOT hurt S3 either; conversion kept climbing as quality (dev spend) growth outpaced the price effect.
  **The pricing fix is confirmed working — S3/B economics now ~breakeven on compute cost alone (was
  losing $53-59/mo/sub before), S3/C solidly profitable (~$40/mo margin).**
- **NEW FINDING — plan-mix shift since the hike:** new S1 signups are now **~100% Plan A** (zero new
  B signups day36-42!). New S3 signups are **74% A / 19% B / 7% C** — also now A-majority. Likely
  explanation: rising quality (dev spend + R&D) now satisfies most customers on the cheapest plan, so
  fewer need to pay up for B/C. This is GOOD for margins (A is profitable for both groups... except see
  next point) but means Plan B is becoming a "legacy" product sustained mostly by existing subs at
  rebill, not new acquisition. Not necessarily a problem, just changes the revenue mix — watch if this
  trend continues or reverses as quality bars keep drifting up over time.
- **New minor watch item: S3/Plan A is slightly loss-making** (44 subs, avg usage 213/day — over half
  A's 400 quota, since S3 are power users even on the cheap plan — compute cost ~$12.79/mo vs $10 price
  = -$2.79/mo/sub). Immaterial today (~$123/mo total drag) but will grow as A becomes the dominant S3
  entry plan. No action taken yet (fixing would need e.g. a small negative `by_group_plan` surcharge on
  S3/A specifically, unclear if the promotion mechanism supports negative values — untested). Revisit if
  S3/A population grows much further.
- **S3 old-price rebill risk window is NOW PRECISELY IDENTIFIED**: 36 B-subs (@ old $19, will re-bill at
  new $69 list) + 2 C-subs (@ old $79, rebill at new $119) have rebill days spread **day45 through day66**
  (staggered, not a cliff). None have rebilled yet as of day42 (earliest is day45). **THIS IS THE #1
  THING TO CHECK NEXT SESSION (day49)** — the first several days of this cohort's rebill will have
  already happened. Compare their post-rebill status (still subscribed at new price? downgraded?
  cancelled?) against expectations. Since NEW S3 signups are already accepting $69/$119 at a 28% (rising)
  conversion rate, I lean towards expecting most existing subs to also accept it, but this is unverified.

### Confirmed EXACT dev-spend quality formula (validated 3-for-3 this session)
`group_bonus_growth_over_N_days = N × 0.0225 × ln(1 + targeted_daily_spend/5000)`. Verified precisely
against dashboard deltas for S1 ($500/day → matched), S3 ($1900/day → matched), AND S2 ($1000/day for 7
days → predicted +0.004104/day×7=+0.0287, dashboard showed exactly +0.0287). **This confirms the
system-prompt coefficients (0.0045 global / 0.0225 group) are correct — docs/api/marketing.json's stated
coefficients (0.006 global / 0.030 group) are WRONG/stale, do not trust that doc file for this formula.**
Same 5x group:global ratio holds in both versions, just the doc's absolute values are off — use 0.0045/
0.0225 (system prompt), empirically confirmed.

## ACTIONS EXECUTED THIS SESSION (day42, config live day43 = week7 start)
1. **Ad spend increase + reallocation toward best-CPL channels** (`set_targeted_ad_spend`, full
   replace): S1 content_marketing $900 + referral_program $500 + social_media $100 = **$1,500/day**
   (was $980; content_marketing is S1's best channel at $6.66/lead vs referral $8.27, social $18.06).
   S3 content_marketing $150 + referral_program $600 + social_media $100 = **$850/day** (was $450;
   referral_program is S3's best channel at $11.67/lead vs content $23.86, social $22.40). Rationale:
   CAC << LTV for both groups (S1 CAC ~$8-12 vs $10-23/mo price + long expected tenure; S3 CAC ~$38-93
   vs $69-119/mo price), market caps nowhere near binding (S1 0.5%, S3 0.15%), so scaling profitable
   channels should improve cash trajectory even though it raises near-term burn.
