   alone now converts at 66.5%, quality no longer remotely the bottleneck, 100% of new signups take the
   cheap plan). S3 **$1700/day** (was $1900 — quality already 2-3x above mean q_min, still helping
   conversion at the margin but likely diminishing returns starting). S2 **$1800/day** (was $1000 — to
   ACCELERATE closing the ~0.0685 mean-case quality gap; at $1800/day, growth is +0.00692/day vs +0.0041
   at $1000/day, closing the gap in ~10 days instead of ~17). D_E09 stays $0 (banked bonus persists).
3. `research_market()` — **no discovery this time** (30% chance, missed), -$25,000 spent. 19 undiscovered
   groups remain (1 of 20 found so far: D_E09).
4. `post_social_media` (agent_post_id=5, reply to post_id=63, an S1 support-response-time complaint):
   cited concrete stat (avg ticket resolution 1.0 days across 948 tickets closed this month). Continues
   the confirmed-working "concrete numbers > vague reassurance" pattern (day35's post_id=4 reply got
   +0.3 to +0.72 across EVERY group including all 4 enterprise segments — the best all-around reception
   yet). Effect TBD, check `agent_social_media_posts` next session.
5. Did NOT start R&D Tier2 ($333,333) — holding cash discipline given already-large spend increases this
   week (ads +$920/day, dev +$450/day) plus the $25K research spend. Revisit next week.
6. Did NOT change capacity tier (Tier2, 800K/day cap) — peak usage this week only 137,261 (17%
   utilization), still lots of headroom.
7. Did NOT touch enterprise ad spend — **confirmed all-time enterprise linkedin/content spend ($2,520+
   across E1/E2/E3/D_E09) has generated ZERO attributed leads** (all 10 enterprise customer records are
   'network'-sourced, not ad-attributed). Enterprise ad spend appears genuinely ineffective — stop
   considering it unless new evidence emerges; pure wait-and-monitor strategy for enterprise now.

New fixed daily spend baseline (day43+): ads $2,350 (was $1,430) + dev $3,850 (was $3,400) + ops $800 +
capacity $530 = **$7,530/day fixed ≈ $52,710/week**, plus lead acq (~$150-250/day, scales with lead
volume) + compute (~$400-700/day, scales with usage). Total run-rate ≈ **$8,200-8,600/day**. Revenue
currently ~$1,200-1,600/day (growing as rebills + new signups accumulate) — net burn roughly
-$6,600-7,000/day right now, expected to shrink over coming weeks as subscriber base (and thus rebill
revenue) keeps compounding.

## Forecast modeling — key structural insight from this session
Built two cohort-simulation scenarios (`forecast_model_v7.py` frozen-config, `forecast_model_v8_adaptive.py`
with dev-taper + S2 ramp-up assumptions). **Critical finding: with FIXED ads+dev spend of ~$7,530/day
held constant for the full 182-day horizon, cash trajectory goes NEGATIVE by ~day200-224** because
per-subscriber margins are thin (~$0.11-0.17/day net of compute cost) and it takes a very large
subscriber base (~60K+) to amortize that fixed cost via thin unit margins alone. **However, if dev spend
is TAPERED as quality gates clear (S1/S3 already 2-3x above their mean q_min; no reason to keep spending
$2,050/day combined there indefinitely) and S2's large untapped market (WTP $178.59, cap 167K) gets
captured once its gate clears (~day60 estimate), cash stabilizes and stays positive (~$180-260K by
day224)**. **TAKEAWAY FOR FUTURE SESSIONS: don't leave dev spend frozen for months once a group's
quality is comfortably clear of its bar — keep tapering it down as conversion growth plateaus, and watch
for the S2 gate clearing to start ad spend there.** Real outcome is likely between these two scenarios;
used judgment-blended figures (not raw model output) for this week's submitted forecast — see rationale.

## ⚠️ NEXT SESSION TODO (day49) — check these first
1. **S3 old-price rebill cohort outcome** — subs 346(day15→day45), 594(day22→52), 768/769/770(day24→54),
   920/921/922(day26→56), 975(day27→57), 1039[C](day28→58), 1143/1144(day29→59), 1258/1259/1260(day30→60)
   will have rebilled by day49 (using new $69/$119 list price, no promotion). Query their status — still

   28% conversion at same price, but UNVERIFIED for existing relationship-based customers specifically).
2. Check S2 quality bonus — should be ≈0.0287 (day42) + 7×0.00692 ≈ **0.0771** by day49 if $1800/day dev
   spend continued uninterrupted. Compare actual. Gap to mean q_min (0.37) was 0.0685 at day42; should be
   nearly closed by day49-52 if on pace.
3. Check enterprise_turns again (10 pending leads, oldest 998 now 22 days old with no thread — still
   nothing we can do but wait/monitor).
4. Check ad spend reallocation results: did S1/S3 CPL improve as expected from the channel shift? Did
   conversion rates hold (66.5% S1 / 28.1% S3 targets)?
5. Reconsider R&D Tier2 ($333,333, mean +0.07 global quality, mean 17 days) — revisit given cash
   position after this week's spend increases settle.
6. Reconsider further S3 dev taper if conversion growth shows diminishing returns (compare this week's
   28.1% to next week's actual — if roughly flat, that's the cue to cut S3 dev further per the "taper as
   gates clear" strategy validated by the forecast model this session).
7. Rebuild `cohort_data.json`, rerun `forecast_model_v7.py`/`v8_adaptive.py` with fresh actuals, compare
   day49 actual cash to this session's forecast (point $541,500, band $525K-$556K) — first calibration
   check of the new modeling approach.
8. If S2 gate looks close to clearing (bonus approaching the ~0.0685 threshold), consider starting a
   SMALL S2 ad spend test (~$300-600/day) to begin the learning process, similar to how S3 ramped.

## Capacity forward watch
Tier2 (800K/day cap, $530/day). Peak this week 137,261/day (17% of cap) — plenty of headroom. Revisit
if peak usage starts exceeding ~400K/day (50% of cap) consistently.

## R&D status (20 tiers total, not 10 — corrected this session, docs/api confirms 20)
Tier1 (Prompt Eng) COMPLETED day30, quality_boost_applied=0.0289 (below mean 0.04), baked into
global_bonus (0.0728 as of day42, includes historical global dev spend which is now $0 ongoing).
Tier1 cost was $166,667 (12 mean days, +0.04 mean boost) — confirmed via `research_projects` table.
Tier2=$333,333/17d/+0.07, T3=$500,000/23d/+0.11, T4=$666,667/32d/+0.16, T5=$833,333/42d/+0.22,
T6=$1M/53d/+0.30, T7=$1,166,667/67d/+0.40, T8=$1,333,333/83d/+0.52, T9=$1.5M/103d/+0.67,
T10=$1,666,667/127d/+0.85. T11-20 frontier moonshots up to T20=$25M+/467d/+8.0 (not affordable for a
long while). Only T1-3 remotely affordable now; none in progress. `list_research_projects()` →
`{'tiers':[...]}` with cost/mean_days/mean_quality_boost/in_progress/completed/total_quality_boost.

## Segment snapshot (Day 42, info level 1 = ±65% noise except D_E09)
| Group | Type | WTP/mo | q_min (noisy) | Mkt cap | Status |

  simple decelerating trend-extrapolation of actual weekly gross-signup counts as a sanity bound.**

  cohort/vintage** — mixing an old (high-usage) cohort's usage rate with a new (cheap-plan-majority)
  cohort's price will spuriously understate margin. Track "vintage" (old installed base vs new future
  signups) separately when plan-mix shifts materially (as it did here post price-hike).

  the frozen one and blend judgmentally for medium/long-horizon forecasts, with wide CIs reflecting the

"""
v9 (day49 session): fresh cohort simulation post price-hike#2 (A13/B95/C139) + capacity Tier3 +
R&D Tier1 rerun + S2 ad test start. Simplified vs v7/v8 (less over-engineered) but grounded in
this week's ACTUAL measured conversion/CPL/usage numbers. Two scenarios (frozen spend vs adaptive
reinvestment) blended for final judgment call -- see bottom.

Key facts baked in:
- Existing subscribers are PERMANENTLY GRANDFATHERED at their signup listed_price (confirmed
  empirically day49: cust 375 signed at S3/B $19 day15, still paying exactly $19 at day45 rebill,
  well after the day35 hike to $69). Only NEW signups get current list price. So a price hike is
  low-risk (doesn't touch existing revenue/satisfaction), it only affects future conversion+ARPU.
- promotion floors at 0 and is NON-NEGATIVE only (can't use as a surcharge). by_group_plan promo
  applies to ALL vintages of that group+plan, not just new -- caused a bug this session (S1/B $46
  promo vs $19 old list = -$27 floored to $0 for 13 existing customers). FIXED (set to 0) this
  session, but 1 lesson: never set a group_plan promo bigger than the OLD listed price if any
  legacy cohort might still be on it.
"""
import json

cash0 = 354085.47   # day49 cash AFTER this week's actions (R&D Tier1 -166,667, research_market -25,000)
CUR_DAY = 49

with open("cohort_data.json") as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)
# cohorts_raw: list of {created_day, group_id, n} -- current installed base by cohort (vintage)

# current blended locked-in avg effective price by group (from day49 query)
avg_locked_price = {"S1": 12.66 * (2925/2925), "S3": None, "S2": 10.0}
# recompute precisely below instead of hardcoding blend; use group-level totals from live query output (day49):
# S1: 2412 A@9.79 + 242 B@18.00 -> total mrr 23620+4355=27975, n=2654 -> avg 10.54
# S3: 155 A@9.99 + 86 B@48.07 + 29 C@116.24 -> total 1548+4134+3371=9053, n=270 -> avg 33.53
# S2: 1 A@10 -> avg 10.0
avg_locked_price = {"S1": 27975/2654, "S3": 9053/270, "S2": 10.0}
n0 = {"S1": 2654, "S3": 270, "S2": 1}

# plan mix for NEW signups (this week actual) & new list prices (post-hike, day49+)
plan_mix = {"S1": {"A": 0.999, "B": 0.001, "C": 0.0},
            "S3": {"A": 0.642, "B": 0.225, "C": 0.133},
            "S2": {"A": 0.9, "B": 0.1, "C": 0.0}}  # guess for S2, tiny sample so far
price = {"A": 13.0, "B": 95.0, "C": 139.0}
new_avg_price = {g: sum(plan_mix[g][p]*price[p] for p in "ABC") for g in plan_mix}
# S1 ~13.08, S3 ~48.25(ish, recompute), S2 ~22.6

# compute cost per unit by tier; plan->tier A=2,B=3,C=4
tier_cost = {"A": 0.002, "B": 0.006, "C": 0.012}
# avg daily usage per group/plan (day46-49 actuals)
usage = {"S1": {"A": 64.9, "B": 68.0, "C": 68.0}, "S3": {"A": 217.1, "B": 406.6, "C": 322.6},
         "S2": {"A": 46.5, "B": 150.0, "C": 250.0}}  # S2 B/C guesses, no data yet
def compute_cost_per_sub_month(g):
    return sum(plan_mix[g][p] * usage[g][p] * 30 * tier_cost[p] for p in "ABC")
cc_new = {g: compute_cost_per_sub_month(g) for g in plan_mix}
# blended cost per INSTALLED (mixed vintage) sub -- approximate using same plan-mix as current actual stock
installed_plan_mix = {"S1": {"A": 2412/2654, "B": 242/2654, "C": 0.0},
                       "S3": {"A": 155/270, "B": 86/270, "C": 29/270},
                       "S2": {"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0, "C": 0.0}}
def installed_cc(g):
    return sum(installed_plan_mix[g][p] * usage[g][p] * 30 * tier_cost[p] for p in "ABC")
cc_installed = {g: installed_cc(g) for g in plan_mix}

# ad spend, CPL (blended, this week actual for S1/S3; guess for S2), conversion rate (post-hike estimate)
ad_spend = {"S1": 2100.0, "S3": 900.0, "S2": 400.0}
cpl = {"S1": 6.92, "S3": 14.69, "S2": 15.0}
conv_rate_start = {"S1": 0.65, "S3": 0.35, "S2": 0.13}   # post price-hike estimate (down a bit from 71.7/40.7/9.1 pre-hike, S2 ramping)
conv_rate_max   = {"S1": 0.70, "S3": 0.42, "S2": 0.30}   # ceiling as quality keeps compounding
conv_improve_wk = {"S1": 0.003, "S3": 0.004, "S2": 0.015}  # S2 climbs fastest (gate still clearing)

organic_leads_wk0 = {"S1": 230.0, "S3": 22.0, "S2": 12.0}  # this-week estimate, scales with installed base growth (haircut applied)

ops_day = 1000.0
capacity_day = 1330.0
dev_day_total = 250 + 1700 + 1900  # 3850

def run(weeks=26, ad_growth_per_wk=0.0, dev_taper=False, extra_rd_every_n_wk=None, rd_cost=166667, verbose=False):
    cash = cash0
    n = dict(n0)
    avg_price = dict(avg_locked_price)   # blended avg locked price of INSTALLED base, drifts up as new higher-priced cohorts join
    conv = dict(conv_rate_start)
    ads = dict(ad_spend)
    dev_total = dev_day_total
    weekly_cash = []
    for wk in range(1, weeks+1):
        week_revenue = 0.0
        week_cost = 0.0
        for g in ["S1", "S3", "S2"]:
            leads_ad = ads[g] * 7 / cpl[g]
            leads_org = organic_leads_wk0[g] * (n[g]/n0[g])**0.5   # sublinear growth in organic w/ base (haircut vs naive linear)
            leads = leads_ad + leads_org
            conv[g] = min(conv_rate_max[g], conv[g] + conv_improve_wk[g])
            new_subs = leads * conv[g]
            new_rev = new_subs * new_avg_price[g]
            # rebills: n[g]/30 per day * 7 days, at blended avg_price (installed base, drifting toward new_avg_price slowly)
            rebill_subs = n[g] / 30.0 * 7
            rebill_rev = rebill_subs * avg_price[g]
            week_revenue += new_rev + rebill_rev
            # update avg_price: weighted blend as new subs join
            avg_price[g] = (avg_price[g]*n[g] + new_avg_price[g]*new_subs) / (n[g] + new_subs)
            # compute cost: existing installed base at cc_installed, new subs at cc_new, blend similarly
            cc_blend = (cc_installed[g]*n[g] + cc_new[g]*new_subs) / (n[g] + new_subs) if (n[g]+new_subs) > 0 else cc_installed[g]
            week_cost += (n[g] + new_subs) * cc_blend / 30 * 7   # monthly cost prorated to a week
            week_cost += leads * 0.5   # lead acquisition cost
            n[g] += new_subs
            if ad_growth_per_wk:
                ads[g] *= (1 + ad_growth_per_wk)
        if dev_taper and wk == 8:
            dev_total = 2200   # taper down once S2 gate clears & S1/S3 plateau further
        week_cost += ads["S1"] + ads["S3"] + ads["S2"]
        # already added leads*0.5 above per group before ads updated; ads already reflects this week's rate (fine, approx)
        week_cost += dev_total + ops_day*7 + capacity_day*7
        cash += (week_revenue - week_cost)
        if extra_rd_every_n_wk and wk % extra_rd_every_n_wk == 0 and cash > rd_cost*1.8:
            cash -= rd_cost
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{wk} day{CUR_DAY+wk*7} cash={cash:,.0f} n={ {k:round(v) for k,v in n.items()} } rev={week_revenue:,.0f} cost={week_cost:,.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, n

print("=== SCENARIO A: frozen spend (no further ad/dev increases) ===")
wc_a, n_a = run(weeks=26, ad_growth_per_wk=0.0, dev_taper=True, extra_rd_every_n_wk=None, verbose=True)

print()
print("=== SCENARIO B: adaptive (modest ongoing ad growth + periodic R&D) ===")
wc_b, n_b = run(weeks=26, ad_growth_per_wk=0.02, dev_taper=True, extra_rd_every_n_wk=10, verbose=True)

def pick(wc, wk):
    return wc[wk-1]

print()
print("Point estimates (blend A/B):")
for wk, label in [(1,"1wk"), (4,"4wk"), (12,"12wk"), (26,"26wk")]:
    a = pick(wc_a, wk); b = pick(wc_b, wk)
    print(f"{label}: A={a:,.0f}  B={b:,.0f}  blend={0.5*(a+b):,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: `forecast_model_v9.py` (fixed a critical bug in v7/v8: forgot to ×7 the ads/dev daily
spend when accumulating WEEKLY cost — understated costs ~7x! Always sanity check model cost/revenue
per-week against a manual hand-calc before trusting output). Rebuild `cohort_data.json` fresh each
session (script at bottom) before rerunning.

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → call next-week, all in one
session. Before planning from scratch, check `config_overrides` (settings_json is a FULL SNAPSHOT after
each call, confirming targeted ad/dev spend calls **fully REPLACE** the prior dict — any group you don't
include reverts to $0, no exceptions) to confirm prior session's plan was actually applied — verify
against the live DB every session, don't trust prior narrative at face value.
**Always sanity-check a new forecast model's per-week cost/revenue against a manual hand-calc** — a 7x
unit error (day-rate vs week-total) is an easy, high-impact mistake (caught and fixed this session).

## STATUS as of Day 49 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 56 will be next dashboard)
Cash: $354,085 heading into day50 (after $166,667 R&D Tier1-rerun + $25,000 research_market this
session, both spent day49). Individual subs 2925 (S1 2654: 2412A/242B: S3 270: 155A/86B/29C; S2 1: 1A —
**FIRST S2 CONVERSION, gate is opening!**). Enterprise: still 0 subscribed seats, 22 organic customer
records now (was 10), **still ZERO `enterprise_turns` threads ever** — confirmed re-tested cold-open on
newest customer (5234), still "no active subscription" error. Pure wait/monitor, no action possible.

## 🔑 BIG STRUCTURAL DISCOVERY THIS SESSION: PRICE GRANDFATHERING IS PERMANENT
**Existing subscribers keep their signup-day `listed_price` FOREVER — `set_prices` changes ONLY affect
NEW signups from that day forward, existing subs are NEVER repriced, even across many 30-day rebill
cycles.** Confirmed empirically: customer 375 (S3/B) signed day15 @ $19 (list price at the time), price
was hiked to $69 on day35, customer rebilled on day45 (30 days after signup) — **paid exactly $19, not
$69.** Checked broadly: as of day49, S1 still has 510 subs @ old $9 A-price + 241 subs @ old $19 B-price
sitting alongside the 1900 @ new $10 / 1 @ new $69; S3 has 36 @ old $19 B alongside 50 @ new $69 B, etc.
**Implication: price increases are LOW RISK — they never touch existing revenue/satisfaction, only
shape future conversion+ARPU.** This flips the earlier (wrong) assumption that hiking prices threatens
an "old cohort rebill shock" — there IS no such shock, ever, for individual (non-enterprise) subs. Use
this: keep raising prices for new cohorts whenever margin analysis or conversion resilience supports it,
with much less fear than before.

### 🐛 BUG FOUND + FIXED: by_group_plan promotion applies to ALL vintages, not just new signups
Day35 I set `by_group_plan: {S1: {B: 46.0}}` intending to discount NEW S1/B signups (listed $69) down to
an effective $23. Side effect: this promotion applies to EVERY S1/B sub regardless of vintage — old S1/B
subs (listed $19) got effective_price = 19-46 = **-27, floored to $0** at their next rebill! Found 13
customers already paying $0/month due to this (228 more would have hit it as they rebilled over the
next ~30 days). **FIXED this session**: `set_promotion(by_group_plan={"S1":{"B":0.0}})`. Lesson: **never
set a group_plan promotion ≥ the OLD listed price if ANY legacy cohort might still be on that plan** —
promotions are vintage-blind, always check `SELECT listed_price, effective_price, promotion, COUNT(*)
FROM subscriptions GROUP BY ...` after any promotion change to confirm no unintended $0/negative-margin
subs appear. The 13 affected customers self-heal (promotion=0 now) at THEIR next rebill (~30 days after
their last one) — no way to fix retroactively, just stops future damage.

## Margin analysis that triggered this week's 2nd price hike (A10/B69/C119 → A13/B95/C139)

## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **A cohort-forecast model's per-week cost accumulation must multiply EVERY daily $/day rate by 7 —
  mixing daily and weekly units in the same accumulator understated total costs by ~7x this session for
  the ads+dev components (only ops/capacity had the ×7 in the original code). Always hand-verify week-1
  against an independent manual calc before trusting the model for longer horizons.**
- **Price increases are LOW RISK to existing revenue** — grandfathering means existing subs are never
  repriced. Don't be overly conservative about testing higher prices for new cohorts.
- **`by_group_plan` promotions apply to ALL vintages** — can accidentally floor old customers' price to
  $0 if the promotion exceeds their (lower, legacy) listed price. Always re-check after setting one.
- Forecast models with organic-lead compounding (rate × total_subs) can blow up into implausible growth
  over a 26-week horizon if the rate isn't heavily haircut — cross-check against simple decelerating
  trend-extrapolation of actual weekly gross-signup counts as a sanity bound. (Less of an issue when
  growth is mostly AD-DRIVEN/linear-in-spend rather than organic-compounding — check which dominates.)
- When modeling cohort economics, keep usage-rate and price assumptions CONSISTENT for the same
  cohort/vintage — mixing an old (high-usage) cohort's usage rate with a new cohort's price understates
  margin. Track "vintage" separately when plan-mix shifts materially.
- Always sanity-check `quota × 30 × tier_cost_per_unit` (or better, REAL measured usage × 30 × tier
  cost) against list price using ACTUAL per-segment usage whenever a new segment/plan-mix starts
  converting in volume — confirmed AGAIN this session (S3 A and B were quietly loss-making even after a
  huge price hike, because S3 usage is 3-6x S1's on the same plan).

- `customers.customer_type` valid values are 'small'/'large', not 'enterprise'/'individual'.

v9 (day49 session): fresh cohort simulation post price-hike#2 (A13/B95/C139) + capacity Tier3 +
R&D Tier1 rerun + S2 ad test start. Simplified vs v7/v8 (less over-engineered) but grounded in
this week's ACTUAL measured conversion/CPL/usage numbers. Two scenarios (frozen spend vs adaptive
reinvestment) blended for final judgment call -- see bottom.

Key facts baked in:
- Existing subscribers are PERMANENTLY GRANDFATHERED at their signup listed_price (confirmed
  empirically day49: cust 375 signed at S3/B $19 day15, still paying exactly $19 at day45 rebill,
  well after the day35 hike to $69). Only NEW signups get current list price. So a price hike is
  low-risk (doesn't touch existing revenue/satisfaction), it only affects future conversion+ARPU.
- promotion floors at 0 and is NON-NEGATIVE only (can't use as a surcharge). by_group_plan promo
  applies to ALL vintages of that group+plan, not just new -- caused a bug this session (S1/B $46
  promo vs $19 old list = -$27 floored to $0 for 13 existing customers). FIXED (set to 0) this
  session, but 1 lesson: never set a group_plan promo bigger than the OLD listed price if any
  legacy cohort might still be on it.
"""
import json

cash0 = 354085.47   # day49 cash AFTER this week's actions (R&D Tier1 -166,667, research_market -25,000)
CUR_DAY = 49

with open("cohort_data.json") as f:
    cohorts_raw = json.load(f)
# cohorts_raw: list of {created_day, group_id, n} -- current installed base by cohort (vintage)

# current blended locked-in avg effective price by group (from day49 query)
avg_locked_price = {"S1": 12.66 * (2925/2925), "S3": None, "S2": 10.0}
# recompute precisely below instead of hardcoding blend; use group-level totals from live query output (day49):
# S1: 2412 A@9.79 + 242 B@18.00 -> total mrr 23620+4355=27975, n=2654 -> avg 10.54
# S3: 155 A@9.99 + 86 B@48.07 + 29 C@116.24 -> total 1548+4134+3371=9053, n=270 -> avg 33.53
# S2: 1 A@10 -> avg 10.0
avg_locked_price = {"S1": 27975/2654, "S3": 9053/270, "S2": 10.0}
n0 = {"S1": 2654, "S3": 270, "S2": 1}

# plan mix for NEW signups (this week actual) & new list prices (post-hike, day49+)
plan_mix = {"S1": {"A": 0.999, "B": 0.001, "C": 0.0},
            "S3": {"A": 0.642, "B": 0.225, "C": 0.133},
            "S2": {"A": 0.9, "B": 0.1, "C": 0.0}}  # guess for S2, tiny sample so far
price = {"A": 13.0, "B": 95.0, "C": 139.0}
new_avg_price = {g: sum(plan_mix[g][p]*price[p] for p in "ABC") for g in plan_mix}
# S1 ~13.08, S3 ~48.25(ish, recompute), S2 ~22.6

# compute cost per unit by tier; plan->tier A=2,B=3,C=4
tier_cost = {"A": 0.002, "B": 0.006, "C": 0.012}
# avg daily usage per group/plan (day46-49 actuals)
usage = {"S1": {"A": 64.9, "B": 68.0, "C": 68.0}, "S3": {"A": 217.1, "B": 406.6, "C": 322.6},
         "S2": {"A": 46.5, "B": 150.0, "C": 250.0}}  # S2 B/C guesses, no data yet
def compute_cost_per_sub_month(g):
    return sum(plan_mix[g][p] * usage[g][p] * 30 * tier_cost[p] for p in "ABC")
cc_new = {g: compute_cost_per_sub_month(g) for g in plan_mix}
# blended cost per INSTALLED (mixed vintage) sub -- approximate using same plan-mix as current actual stock
installed_plan_mix = {"S1": {"A": 2412/2654, "B": 242/2654, "C": 0.0},
                       "S3": {"A": 155/270, "B": 86/270, "C": 29/270},
                       "S2": {"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0, "C": 0.0}}
def installed_cc(g):
    return sum(installed_plan_mix[g][p] * usage[g][p] * 30 * tier_cost[p] for p in "ABC")
cc_installed = {g: installed_cc(g) for g in plan_mix}

# ad spend, CPL (blended, this week actual for S1/S3; guess for S2), conversion rate (post-hike estimate)
ad_spend = {"S1": 2100.0, "S3": 900.0, "S2": 400.0}
cpl = {"S1": 6.92, "S3": 14.69, "S2": 15.0}
conv_rate_start = {"S1": 0.65, "S3": 0.35, "S2": 0.13}   # post price-hike estimate (down a bit from 71.7/40.7/9.1 pre-hike, S2 ramping)
conv_rate_max   = {"S1": 0.70, "S3": 0.42, "S2": 0.30}   # ceiling as quality keeps compounding
conv_improve_wk = {"S1": 0.003, "S3": 0.004, "S2": 0.015}  # S2 climbs fastest (gate still clearing)

organic_leads_wk0 = {"S1": 230.0, "S3": 22.0, "S2": 12.0}  # this-week estimate, scales with installed base growth (haircut applied)

ops_day = 1000.0
capacity_day = 1330.0
dev_day_total = 250 + 1700 + 1900  # 3850

def run(weeks=26, ad_growth_per_wk=0.0, dev_taper=False, extra_rd_every_n_wk=None, rd_cost=166667, verbose=False):
    cash = cash0
    n = dict(n0)
    avg_price = dict(avg_locked_price)   # blended avg locked price of INSTALLED base, drifts up as new higher-priced cohorts join
    conv = dict(conv_rate_start)
    ads = dict(ad_spend)
    dev_total = dev_day_total
    weekly_cash = []
    for wk in range(1, weeks+1):
        week_revenue = 0.0
        week_cost = 0.0
        for g in ["S1", "S3", "S2"]:
            leads_ad = ads[g] * 7 / cpl[g]
            leads_org = organic_leads_wk0[g] * (n[g]/n0[g])**0.5   # sublinear growth in organic w/ base (haircut vs naive linear)
            leads = leads_ad + leads_org
            conv[g] = min(conv_rate_max[g], conv[g] + conv_improve_wk[g])
            new_subs = leads * conv[g]
            new_rev = new_subs * new_avg_price[g]
            # rebills: n[g]/30 per day * 7 days, at blended avg_price (installed base, drifting toward new_avg_price slowly)
            rebill_subs = n[g] / 30.0 * 7
            rebill_rev = rebill_subs * avg_price[g]
            week_revenue += new_rev + rebill_rev
            # update avg_price: weighted blend as new subs join
            avg_price[g] = (avg_price[g]*n[g] + new_avg_price[g]*new_subs) / (n[g] + new_subs)
            # compute cost: existing installed base at cc_installed, new subs at cc_new, blend similarly
            cc_blend = (cc_installed[g]*n[g] + cc_new[g]*new_subs) / (n[g] + new_subs) if (n[g]+new_subs) > 0 else cc_installed[g]
            week_cost += (n[g] + new_subs) * cc_blend / 30 * 7   # monthly cost prorated to a week
            week_cost += leads * 0.5   # lead acquisition cost
            n[g] += new_subs
            if ad_growth_per_wk:
                ads[g] *= (1 + ad_growth_per_wk)
        if dev_taper and wk == 8:
            dev_total = 2200   # taper down once S2 gate clears & S1/S3 plateau further
        week_cost += (ads["S1"] + ads["S3"] + ads["S2"]) * 7
        # already added leads*0.5 above per group before ads updated; ads already reflects this week's rate (fine, approx)
        week_cost += dev_total * 7 + ops_day*7 + capacity_day*7
        cash += (week_revenue - week_cost)
        if extra_rd_every_n_wk and wk % extra_rd_every_n_wk == 0 and cash > rd_cost*1.8:
            cash -= rd_cost
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{wk} day{CUR_DAY+wk*7} cash={cash:,.0f} n={ {k:round(v) for k,v in n.items()} } rev={week_revenue:,.0f} cost={week_cost:,.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, n

print("=== SCENARIO A: frozen spend (no further ad/dev increases) ===")
wc_a, n_a = run(weeks=26, ad_growth_per_wk=0.0, dev_taper=True, extra_rd_every_n_wk=None, verbose=True)

print()
print("=== SCENARIO B: adaptive (modest ongoing ad growth + periodic R&D) ===")
wc_b, n_b = run(weeks=26, ad_growth_per_wk=0.02, dev_taper=True, extra_rd_every_n_wk=10, verbose=True)

def pick(wc, wk):
    return wc[wk-1]

print()
print("Point estimates (blend A/B):")
for wk, label in [(1,"1wk"), (4,"4wk"), (12,"12wk"), (26,"26wk")]:
    a = pick(wc_a, wk); b = pick(wc_b, wk)
    print(f"{label}: A={a:,.0f}  B={b:,.0f}  blend={0.5*(a+b):,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: `forecast_model_v10.py` (cohort sim, hand-verified internally consistent — reproduce
manual week1 rev/cost calc before trusting any future version). Rebuild `cohort_data.json` fresh each
session if needed (script at bottom), and ALWAYS refresh CPL/usage/conversion/plan-mix inputs from
live queries (see "How to rebuild" section) — stale inputs = garbage forecast.

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → build/refresh forecast model →
call next-week, all in one session. Before planning from scratch, check `config_overrides` (day-filtered)
+ `config_history` (day-filtered) to confirm prior session's plan actually landed — verify against the
live DB every session, don't trust prior narrative at face value.
**Always sanity-check a forecast model's per-week cost/revenue against a manual hand-calc** — unit
errors (daily vs weekly rates) are easy, high-impact mistakes. v10 was hand-verified this session (see
script docstring) — reuse its structure, don't regress.

## STATUS as of Day 56 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 63 will be next dashboard)
Cash: $307,910 (down from $354,085 day49, net -$46,176 last week — but revenue is ACCELERATING fast,
see burn analysis below). Individual subs 4,775 (S1 4,227: 4037A/190B; S2 45: all A; S3 503: 347A/108B/
48C). Enterprise: still 0 subscribed seats, 0 `enterprise_turns` threads EVER (60 organic customer
records across 5 groups: E1 17, E2 22, E3 10, D_E09 8, D_E02 3). Pure wait/monitor, no action possible.

## 🔑 KEY FINDING THIS SESSION: S3 usage keeps RISING — margins went NEGATIVE across ALL 3 plans
Measured actual usage (day50-56) for S3: A=232.3/day (was 217.1 last wk), B=481.8/day (was 406.6),
C=412.0/day (was 322.6). **Usage per customer appears to grow over time even within existing cohorts**
(not just a new-vintage effect) — watch this pattern every session, it erodes margins silently.
At LAST week's prices (A13/B95/C139), recomputed real margins: S3-A blended install = **-$0.94/mo**,
S3-B blended (mixing legacy $19/$69 cohorts with new $95) = **deeply negative** (-$25.57/mo avg, driven
by grandfathered legacy cohorts whose usage grew after they signed up), S3-C blended similarly negative.
**Whole S3 segment gross margin (revenue − compute, installed base, BEFORE any ads/dev spend) = -$4,662/
month** this week. This triggered another price hike (see Actions below) — B/C especially, since legacy
grandfathering means only NEW signups get fixed pricing (existing underwater cohorts stay underwater
until they churn — small $ impact, ~-$1,076/wk, not worth chasing further, just re-verify occasionally).

## 🔑 KEY FINDING: AD SPEND IS ALREADY NET CASH-POSITIVE WITHIN THE SAME WEEK — burn comes from elsewhere
Checked this explicitly: S1 ad spend $14,700/wk (at old alloc) → ~1,394 new subs → ~$18,122 IMMEDIATE
signup revenue same week, before any rebills. **Ad spend pays for itself same-week given high conversion
(60-70%) and price >> CPL.** The weekly cash burn is NOT from ads — it's from DEV+OPS+CAPACITY (fixed,
$1000s-$1000s/day, no immediate revenue offset) plus compute cost on the thin/negative-margin S3 base.
**Implication: ad spend increases on good-CPL channels are low-risk and should be scaled aggressively
(market caps have huge headroom everywhere — S1 1.5%, S2 0.03%, S3 0.8% utilized). Dev/ops/capacity
increases are the real burn-risk levers — be more careful/incremental with those, especially while cash
is working through the reinvestment trough.**

## 🔑 KEY FINDING: Social posts emphasizing LOW PRICE backfire for quality-focused/enterprise segments
Day49 post (reply to PMI-anxiety complaint, framed around "$13/mo, pays for itself during budget
freezes") scored **+0.65 for S1/E1 (price-sensitive/cost-cutting) but -0.65 for S2, S3, E2, E3, D_E02,
D_E09** (quality-focused/enterprise — every other group). Comments explicitly said "$13/mo positioning
contradicts B2B SaaS platform claim", "signals consumer-grade product misaligned with procurement
standards", "commodity SMB tool ... lacks infrastructure for complex long-term engagements." **CONTRAST
with posts 4 & 5 (day35, day42) which cited RELIABILITY/SUPPORT metrics (99.62% uptime, 223ms p95, 1.0-
day avg resolution) with NO price mention and scored +0.3 to +0.72 ACROSS every single group, best-yet
both times.** Lesson: **concrete uptime/support/reliability metrics = universal positive. Concrete PRICE/
affordability framing = sharply segments the audience, alienating higher-WTP/enterprise groups.** Only
lead with price/affordability if TARGETING an S1/E1-only audience specifically (not possible currently —
posts appear to reach/affect all groups that see them). Default to reliability/quality framing.
Posted day56 reply (post 7, replying to a "radio silence on bug reports" complaint cluster — 2 near-
identical posts same day, both S1) using concrete ticket numbers (2,432 tickets/1.0-day avg), explicitly
NO price mention — testing whether this reliability-only framing repeats the universal-positive pattern.
**Check `agent_social_media_posts` next session for post_id=7's effect_by_group.**

## ACTIONS EXECUTED THIS SESSION (day56, config live day57 = week9 start)
1. **Price hike #3**: `set_prices(A=15, B=145, C=195)` (was A13/B95/C139). A: +15% (moderate, S1 is bulk
   of volume, don't want to shock it too much 2 weeks in a row). B: +53%, C: +40% (aggressive — fixes
   the negative S3 margins decisively for new signups; S3 has proven strongly inelastic demand across
   2 prior hikes — conversion kept RISING 28.1%→40.7%→50.5% through both). New-signup margins now:
   A +$1-11/mo (positive across S1/S2/S3), B +$58/mo, C +$47/mo (all healthy cushions vs current usage).
2. **Ad spend reallocation** (`set_targeted_ad_spend`, full replace, $3,900/day total, was $3,400):
   Moved money from worst-CPL to best-CPL channels within each group. S1: content $1600(+300)/referral
   $850(+150)/social $0(-100, was worst CPL at $20/lead). S3: content $150(-150, was worst at $22/lead)/
   referral $750(+250, best at $12.54/lead)/social $50(-50). S2: content $350(+150, cheaper at $9.52/
   lead)/referral $150(-50, pricier at $17.07/lead). Rationale: ads are self-funding same-week (see
   finding above) — reallocating toward efficiency + modest net increase is low-risk.
3. **Dev spend rebalance** (`set_targeted_dev_spend`, full replace, $4,100/day total, was $3,850): S1
   $300(+50, small bump to offset the new price hike raising the quality-at-price bar). S3 $1700
   (unchanged — still clearly working, conversion rising, no plateau). S2 $2100(+200, push harder — gate
   is opening, conversion 9.1%→18.1% over 2 weeks, biggest incremental opportunity).
4. **Ops bump**: $1000→$1200/day. Issue volume nearly DOUBLED wk/wk (2,606 opened day50-56 vs ~1,415
   prior period) while avg resolution held at 1.0 days — get ahead of it before resolution time slips.
5. **Social media post** (agent_post_id=7, reply to post_id=95, a "filed a bug report, radio silence"
   complaint — see finding above for framing rationale).
6. **Skipped R&D and research_market this session** — preserving cash through the projected reinvestment
   trough (model shows trough ~week5-6/day91-98 at ~$188-195K under frozen spend). Revisit once cash
   trend is confirmed stabilizing/recovering, or if actuals run meaningfully ahead of the v10 model.

New fixed daily spend baseline (day57+): ads $3,900 (was $3,400) + dev $4,100 (was $3,850) + ops $1,200
(was $1,000) + capacity $1,330 (unchanged, Tier3) = **$10,530/day fixed**, plus lead acq (~$1,800-2,000/
wk, scales w/ leads) + compute (~$1,200-1,900/day, scales w/ usage, S3 driving a disproportionate share).

## Conversion rates day50-56 (prices A13/B95/C139 — the price hike BEFORE this session's, i.e. hike #2)
- **S1: 64.3%** (down from 71.7% pre-hike#2 — a ~10% relative decline from the +30% price jump A10→13).
  Still net revenue-per-lead POSITIVE vs pre-hike (0.643×13=8.36 vs 0.717×10=7.17, +16.6%).
- **S3: 50.5%** (UP from 40.7% — again rising THROUGH a price hike, demand proven inelastic). Plan mix
  shifted toward A (80.1%A/11.7%B/8.2%C, was 64.2/22.5/13.3) — cheaper-plan preference growing as B/C
  got pricier, but overall conversion still climbing. Revenue/lead: 0.505×32.92=16.63 vs 0.407×37.77=
  15.37 pre-hike (+8.2%, smaller gain than S1 because of the A-ward mix shift diluting ARPU).
- **S2: 18.1%** (UP hugely from 9.1%, n=243 leads now, gate clearly opening). Dev $1900/d + new $400/d
  ad spend (from day49) both clearly working — reinforced further this session (dev→2100, ads reallocated).
**NEXT SESSION: this week's actual conversion will be at the NEW A15/B145/C195 prices — the #1 thing to
check.** Given inelastic demand pattern holding for S3 through 2 hikes and only-moderate S1 hike this
time, expect S1 conversion to partially recover (~61-65%) and S3 to dip only slightly if at all (~45-50%)
— but the B/C jump (+53%/+40%) is much bigger than any single prior hike, so there's real risk of a
bigger-than-usual mix shift toward A or a real conversion dip. WATCH CLOSELY, don't over-extrapolate the
"S3 is infinitely inelastic" pattern — this is the biggest single-plan price jump yet.

## Cash burn trajectory (clean weekly windows, EXCLUDING one-time R&D/research_market spend)
Revenue (subscription_payment) by week (day1-7 ... day50-56): 60, 305, 1068, 2818, 6118, 8266, 19552,
30603 — **accelerating fast** (recent w/w growth: +137%, +57%). Operational net (rev − recurring opex,
excl. one-time): -16575,-22013,-24567,-22368,-25187,-37998,-38873,-46176 — burn growing in $ terms as we
scaled ads/dev/ops/capacity, but revenue growth RATE has consistently outpaced cost growth rate. v10
model (see below) projects burn shrinking and flipping positive within ~5-11 weeks as (a) new higher
prices phase into the signup mix (b) rebill revenue compounds from the fast-growing installed base.
**Total MRR (sum of effective_price, all active subs) = $65,386/mo as of day56** — up from whatever it
was at day49 (not recorded, but subscriber count grew 2925→4775, +63%, so MRR grew comparably or more
given price hikes too). This is the base the rebill-revenue stream draws from every 30 days.

## Forecast model v10 (hand-verified, see script docstring + this session's manual trace for details)
Two base scenarios (frozen spend vs modest +1.5%/wk ad + 1%/wk dev reinvestment) plus a sensitivity
sweep (conv_mult / cpl_mult / organic_mult perturbations) for honest CI construction. **Point estimates
(A/B blend): 1wk=$272,333, 4wk=$203,391 (near trough), 12wk=$323,779 (past trough, recovering), 26wk=
$1,727,100.** Sensitivity range at 12wk: pessimistic ≈ -$1,619 (near-zero/slightly negative if
conversion/CPL/organic all run ~20-25% worse than modeled simultaneously) to optimistic ≈ $662,665. At
26wk: pessimistic ≈ $447,878 to optimistic ≈ $3,455,767. Used these to construct honest wide 95% CIs
(NOT just the A/B scenario spread, which is too narrow — used the multi-factor sensitivity sweep
instead). **J-curve shape confirmed again: dip before day~91-98 (week 5-6), crossing back above current
cash (~$307K) around week 10-12 (day126-140), strong growth after.**
**CAUTION: don't add big one-time expenses (R&D tier2+, large capacity jump) during the ~week4-7
(day84-105) window** unless cash is clearly running ahead of this trajectory. Re-check actual-vs-model
every session.

## NEXT SESSION TODO (day63) — check these first
1. **Conversion rates at NEW prices (A15/B145/C195)** — the #1 open question, especially for the big B/C
   jump. Compare to this week's baseline (64.3%/50.5%/18.1%). If S3 B/C conversion craters (unlike the
   inelastic pattern so far), may need to dial back C especially (biggest % jump on the smallest-usage
   plan... wait, C has LOWER usage than B now (412 vs 482) — re ­verify this holds, don't assume).
2. **S3 usage trend AGAIN** — did it keep rising (232→?, 482→?, 412→?)? If still climbing, the new
   prices may need ANOTHER round soon, or reconsider whether quota adjustments are warranted (tricky —
   lowering quotas risks degrading quality/satisfaction for legitimate heavy users, hasn't been tested).
3. **CPL at reallocated ad spend** — did cutting worst-CPL channels (S1 social, S3 content) and boosting
   best (S1 content/referral, S3 referral, S2 content) improve blended CPL as hypothesized? Check

4. **Social post 7 effect** — check `agent_social_media_posts` for post_id=7 (reliability-only framing,
   no price mention, replying to bug-report radio-silence complaints). Confirms/refutes the "avoid price
   framing" hypothesis from this session.
5. **Cash trajectory vs v10 model** — compare actual day63 cash to submitted forecast (point $272,333).
   Recalibrate v10 inputs (CPL, conversion drift, usage growth) if actual diverges meaningfully.
6. **Ops at $1200 — issue volume/resolution check** — did bumping ops keep resolution at ~1.0 days
   despite continued volume growth? If resolution starts slipping, bump further.
7. **S1/B $0-effective-price bug (13 customers)** — any self-healed yet at their own 30-day rebill mark?
   Low priority (small $), but worth a quick check.

```python
# 1. Installed base + avg locked price + compute cost, by group (adjust day range/groups as needed):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id''')
# 2. Usage per group/plan (actual, trailing week):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, AVG(du.usage_units) as avg_usage, COUNT(*) as cnt
FROM daily_usage du JOIN customers c ON du.customer_id=c.customer_id
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE du.day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 3. CPL by channel/group (trailing week):
r = nm.query('''SELECT channel_id, group_id, SUM(spend) as spend, SUM(leads_generated) as leads
FROM ad_channel_leads WHERE day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> GROUP BY channel_id, group_id''')
# 4. Conversion rate by group (trailing week, created_day window):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, SUM(CASE WHEN s.status IN ("subscribed","cancelled") THEN 1 ELSE 0
END) as converted, COUNT(*) as total_leads FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c
ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> GROUP BY c.group_id''')
# 5. Organic (non-ad) leads by group (trailing week):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, c.acquisition_source, COUNT(*) as n FROM customers c
WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> GROUP BY c.group_id, c.acquisition_source''')
# 6. Clean weekly ledger breakdown (use exact day ranges, NOT day/7 bucketing):
r = nm.query('''SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi>
GROUP BY category''')
```

- Always sum multi-row financial data via script/query — hand-adding is error prone.

forecast should not imply revenue rates wildly beyond this, and full saturation in 4.3 months is itself
very unlikely. v13 uses logistic-style growth (dampened by 1-subs/K) so long-run projections stay
bounded, with r calibrated conservatively below the raw recent-weeks rate (which was inflated by US
quadrupling ad spend + 3 price hikes in ~9 weeks - a pace of OUR OWN reinvestment that can't continue
indefinitely given finite cash).

CALIBRATION: raw new_subs growth wk8->wk9: 2686/1863=1.44 (44%/wk on NEW SUBS COUNT, i.e. even bigger
effective growth in the subs LEVEL). This week (wk10) we again increased ad spend 40% - expect similar
or slightly higher near-term new-subs growth, BUT this is NOT sustainable weekly forever (would require
infinite ad budget growth). Model assumes: ad-spend growth moderates from here (+40% -> +15% -> +5% ->
flat over the next several weeks), so subs growth decelerates accordingly. Uses logistic dampening
(1-subs/K) as a backstop for realism at long horizons regardless of my own future spending choices.

Market cap grows slowly (~0.2%/wk blended from annual growth rates 9.62%/14.9%/7.03% weighted) - minor
over the forecast horizon, included for completeness.
"""

CASH_NOW = 267304.0
SUBS_NOW = 7440.0
K_NOW = 272812.0 + 167374.0 + 65292.0  # 505,478 combined individual market cap
K_GROWTH_WK = 0.002023  # ~0.2%/week blended

            fixed_growth=1.02, compute_growth=1.02, arpu_drift=1.00,
            rebill_share_now=0.10, rebill_share_growth=1.06):

    r0: initial intrinsic weekly subs growth rate (logistic), decaying toward r_min.
    rebill_share_now: fraction of THIS week's revenue attributable to rebills vs new signups (~10%
      currently per ledger reconciliation - most of book is <30 days old given rapid recent growth).
      Grows over time as the book ages (more customers cross 30/60/90-day marks).

    subs = SUBS_NOW
    K = K_NOW
    new_subs = NEW_SUBS_NOW
    fixed_daily = FIXED_DAILY_NOW
    compute_per_sub = COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK_NOW

NEW_SUBS_NOW = 2686.0
ARPU_NEW = 16.5          # blended ARPU of NEW signups this week (mostly S1-A@18, some S3 B/C)
ARPU_REBILL_POOL = 14.5  # blended ARPU of the older/grandfathered rebill-eligible population (~current MRR/subs=14.46)
FIXED_DAILY_NOW = 5475.0 + 4450.0 + 1500.0 + 1330.0
COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK_NOW = 11951.95 / 7440.0
BLENDED_CONVERSION = 0.55
LAG_WEEKS = 4  # ~30 days

def project(weeks_out, r0=0.28, r_decay=0.85, r_min=0.05,
            fixed_growth=1.02, compute_growth=1.015, arpu_new_drift=1.00, arpu_rebill_drift=1.003,
            verbose=False):
    cash = CASH_NOW
    subs = SUBS_NOW
    K = K_NOW
    new_subs = NEW_SUBS_NOW
    fixed_daily = FIXED_DAILY_NOW
    compute_per_sub = COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK_NOW
    arpu_new = ARPU_NEW
    arpu_rebill = ARPU_REBILL_POOL

    subs_history = [SUBS_NOW] * (LAG_WEEKS + 1)  # index 0 = most recent

    for wk in range(weeks_out):
        r = r_min + (r0 - r_min) * (r_decay ** wk)
        new_subs = subs * r * (1 - subs / K)
        subs += new_subs
        K *= (1 + K_GROWTH_WK)
        subs_history.append(subs)

        lagged_subs = subs_history[-1 - LAG_WEEKS] if len(subs_history) > LAG_WEEKS else SUBS_NOW

        new_signup_rev = new_subs * arpu_new
        rebill_rev = lagged_subs * arpu_rebill * (7 / 30)
        revenue = new_signup_rev + rebill_rev

        leads = new_subs / BLENDED_CONVERSION
        lead_acq_cost = leads * 0.5
        compute_cost = subs * compute_per_sub
        weekly_fixed = fixed_daily * 7
        cost = weekly_fixed + lead_acq_cost + compute_cost

        cash += (revenue - cost)

        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{wk+1:2d} cash={cash:>12,.0f} rev={revenue:>10,.0f} (new={new_signup_rev:>9,.0f} "
                  f"rebill={rebill_rev:>8,.0f}) cost={cost:>10,.0f} (fix={weekly_fixed:>7,.0f} "
                  f"compute={compute_cost:>8,.0f} leadacq={lead_acq_cost:>6,.0f}) subs={subs:>9,.0f} r={r:.3f}")

        fixed_daily *= fixed_growth
        compute_per_sub *= compute_growth
        arpu_new *= arpu_new_drift
        arpu_rebill *= arpu_rebill_drift

    return cash, subs

if __name__ == "__main__":

    }

    results = {h: {} for h in horizons}

    for h, wk in horizons.items():

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: `forecast_model_v14.py` (logistic/cohort-lag hybrid, hand-validated this session; v6-v13
deleted as superseded — see "Forecast model v14" section below for the methodology and known
limitations before building v15).

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → build/refresh forecast model →
call next-week, all in one session. Before planning from scratch, check `config_overrides` (day-filtered)
+ `config_history` (day-filtered) to confirm prior session's plan actually landed — verify against the
live DB every session, don't trust prior narrative at face value.
**Always sanity-check a forecast model's per-week cost/revenue against a manual hand-calc AND against a
market-cap-based sanity ceiling** (max plausible MRR = market_cap × ARPU) — this session I built 4 model
versions (v11-v14) before landing on something sane; v11/v12 blew up to implausible billions at 26wk
(decaying growth RATE alone doesn't bound the LEVEL — need explicit logistic/market-cap saturation).
v13 overcorrected to perpetual-negative-forever (compute-cost-growth assumption too aggressive/uncapped).
v14 = logistic subs growth (bounded by market cap) + cohort-lag revenue (new-signup upfront pay + lagged
rebill pool) + moderate (not runaway) fixed/compute cost growth assumptions. Reuse v14's STRUCTURE, just
refresh the calibration inputs each session.

## STATUS as of Day 63 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 70 will be next dashboard)
Cash: $267,304 (down from $307,910 day56, -$40,606 last week — 4th straight week of $22-46K/wk burn in
absolute $ terms, though revenue keeps accelerating in % terms). Individual Subscribers: 7,440 (S1 6,457:
6399A/58B; S2 140: all A; S3 843: 685A/104B/54C). Enterprise: STILL 0 subscribed seats, 0
`enterprise_turns` threads EVER in 63 days. Open issues 625 (up from prior, tracking subscriber growth
roughly proportionally, resolution holding at 1.0 day avg).

## 🔑 KEY FINDING THIS SESSION: B/C price hike#3 (145/195) OVERSHOT — S3 customers fled to Plan A instead
of paying more, CRATERING B/C revenue/lead vs hike#2. At B95/C139 (hike#2), S3 B+C combined were ~19.9%
of new conversions. At B145/C195 (hike#3), B+C collapsed to just 5% (12 B + 5 C out of 341 S3 converts) —
customers didn't leave, they just downshifted to the cheap Plan A "release valve" instead. Net effect:
revenue/lead for S3 FELL from ~$16.63 (hike#2) to ~$11.58 (hike#3), a 30% DECREASE despite raising prices.
**LESSON: unlike a simple monopoly-pricing intuition, when a cheaper in-product alternative (Plan A)
exists, aggressive upper-tier hikes can backfire hard via mix-shift, not just via lost conversion.** This
CORRECTS last session's overconfident "S3 demand is inelastic" takeaway — it's only inelastic w.r.t.
losing the customer entirely; it's quite elastic w.r.t. which PLAN they choose when a cheaper option
exists. ACTION TAKEN: rolled back B/C partway (145→115, 195→180) to recapture lost upside. WATCH NEXT
SESSION: did B/C mix recover toward the hike#2-ish ~15-20% share, and is revenue/lead back up?

## 🔑 KEY FINDING: Plan A price hikes (S1's dominant plan, 87% of individual subs) show NO cliff yet —
revenue/lead keeps RISING through each hike (no cheaper alternative to flee to within Plan A, unlike
B/C's flight-to-A pattern). A10→13: rev/lead 7.17→8.36 (+16.6%). A13→15: 8.36→8.91 (+6.6%). Both times
conversion dropped only ~8-10% relatively per hike, less than the price increase %, so revenue/lead kept
rising. Elasticity pattern: relative-conv-drop ≈ 0.33-0.5 × relative-price-increase (roughly consistent,
not accelerating). ACTION TAKEN: hiked A 15→18 (+20%) this session, a bigger jump than prior two hikes —
justified because (a) elasticity has stayed favorable, (b) quality delivered (0.30-0.43 across groups)
vastly exceeds noisy q_min floor estimates (0.08-0.37), giving headroom, (c) S3's Plan-A margin was
wafer-thin/negative at blended pricing (see below) and needed the cushion. **WATCH CLOSELY next session
— this is the biggest single A-hike yet (previous were ~15-30%), first real test of whether a A-specific
cliff effect exists at some price level.**

## 🔑 MARGIN CHECK (redo every session — usage keeps drifting up): at prices BEFORE this session's hike
(A15/B145/C195), using trailing-week actual usage: S1-A margin healthy (+$8-10/mo). S3-A blended (mixing
vintages) was slightly NEGATIVE (-$1.27/mo, usage 242.97/day × $0.002/unit(T2) × 30 vs blended price
$13.31). S3-B blended margin -$13.44/mo (usage 504.19/day × $0.006(T3) × 30 = $90.75 cost vs blended
price $77.31 — mostly OLD $69 cohorts dragging it down). S3-C blended -$42.51/mo (usage 493.51/day ×
$0.012(T4) × 30 = $177.66 cost vs blended price $135.15). **Blended S3 total margin ≈ -$4,564/month this
week — almost IDENTICAL to last session's -$4,662/month finding despite the price hike, because
grandfathering means the hike only helps NEW signups; the existing underwater legacy book doesn't
improve until those customers churn or enough new (better-priced) signups dilute the average.** This is
a standing, slow-resolving drag — re-verify each session but don't chase it further with big price moves
(small $ scale, and hike#3 already proved over-aggressive B/C moves backfire on revenue).
**S3 usage still climbing**: A 232→243/day, B 482→504/day, C 412→494/day (C jumped ~20% but n=54, noisy).

## 🔑 KEY FINDING: `set_prices` change effective IMMEDIATELY for that week's new signups (confirmed:
day57-63 new S3 signups paid the day56-set A15/B145/C195, not old prices) — no lag beyond the usual
~1-day config-to-ledger lag noted previously.

## 🔑 SOCIAL MEDIA: 3rd CONFIRMATION of "reliability/accountability framing, no price mention" = universal
positive. Day56 post (agent_post_id=7, replying to a bug-report-radio-silence complaint, cited concrete
ticket metrics 2,432/1.0-day avg, NO price) scored +0.65 in 7/8 groups, +0.35 in D_E02 (still positive).
reasoning_by_group text shows even the positive scores note aggregate-stat citation feels slightly
"defensive"/impersonal — suggests the NEXT evolution is to combine metrics WITH a concrete process fix
commitment (not just cite stats). Day63 new post (agent_post_id=8) tests this: replied to the most
detailed complaint in a 4-post cluster about support bouncing between teams, committing to a concrete
"single-owner ticket resolution" process fix, no price mention. **CHECK EFFECT NEXT SESSION.**

## 🔑 LEDGER RECONCILIATION LESSON (unresolved, use top-line growth extrapolation instead): tried to
decompose weekly revenue into "new signup first payment" vs "rebill from existing base" components using
ledger daily payment counts vs new-subs-by-created_day counts. Got inconsistent estimates depending on
method (cohort-MRR-lag approach implied ~$1,692/wk rebill; "payments minus new-signups" implied ~$4,747/
wk) — a 2.8x discrepancy I could not resolve (ledger has no customer_id to directly verify attribution,
and there may be a 1-day payment lag for some signups that contaminates the "excess payments" count).
**Don't burn more turns trying to perfectully decompose this — v14's cohort-lag approximation (new_subs
× ARPU_new, upfront, + subs_from_~4.3wks_ago × ARPU_blended × 7/30 as "rebill") is a reasonable
approximation, cross-validated against the market-cap sanity ceiling and historical revenue growth
trend, and good enough for forecasting purposes.**

## ACTIONS EXECUTED THIS SESSION (day63, config live day64 = week10 start)
1. **Pricing**: `set_prices(A=18, B=115, C=180)` — A up (+20%, exploiting continued favorable elasticity,
   also fixes thin S3-A margin). B/C rolled back from the overshot hike#3 (145/195) toward a healthier
   balance (positive margin at current usage: B +$24/mo, C +$2/mo at new-signup prices) while hopefully
   recapturing more B/C mix-share than the 5%-collapse hike#3 caused. Model tiers/quotas unchanged
   (A=2/B=3/C=4, quotas 400/800/1500) — no urgent evidence to change either.
2. **Ad spend** (`set_targeted_ad_spend`, full replace, $5,475/day total, was $3,900): scaled ~40% on
   proven channels (S1 content_marketing→$2200, referral→$1000; S2 content→$600; S3 referral→$950) +
   TESTED two previously-untried channels (linkedin, search_ads) with small $100 probes on S1/S2/S3 to
   discover if they beat current best. Cut S1 social_media (worst CPL, already at $0) and S3
   content_marketing further (worst CPL $20.19, now $75). CPL check confirmed reallocation from last
   session worked: S1 content $4.89/lead (great), S3 referral $10.87/lead (great), S2 content $8.17/lead
   (good) — all improved or held from prior session's numbers.
3. **Dev spend** (`set_targeted_dev_spend`, full replace, $4,450/day total, was $4,100): S2 →$2400
   (+300, biggest untapped opportunity, conversion still climbing 18.1%→24.2%). S1 →$350 (+50, small
   offset for the A price hike). S3 held at $1,700 (margin thin, more dev doesn't fix compute cost, no
   reason to add here).
4. **Ops**: $1200→$1500/day (global via `set_daily_spend`). Issue volume kept pace with subscriber
   growth (243→624/day opened over 2 weeks, roughly proportional not accelerating faster), resolution
   holding at 1.0 day avg — bumping preemptively since we're scaling subscriber acquisition further.
5. **Social post** (agent_post_id=8, day63, replying to post_id=116 — the most detailed/specific
   complaint in today's 4-post cluster about support ticket team hand-offs). Content commits to a
   concrete "single-owner ticket resolution" fix, no price mention. Testing whether combining
   metrics-free concrete-commitment framing performs even better than pure-stats framing (which already
   scores well). Check `agent_social_media_posts` for post_id=8 next session.
6. **Skipped R&D and research_market again this session** — cash still declining, and the NEW forecast
   model (v14) shows a plausible trough of -$200K to -$240K around week 15-16 before recovering — adding
   big one-time spend now increases bankruptcy-adjacent risk. Revisit once cash trend stabilizes or
   actuals run meaningfully ahead of the model (cash affordability alone still limits us to Tier1 R&D,
   $166,667, which would leave uncomfortably little buffer given the projected trough).
7. **Confirmed S1/B $0-bug customers (13 of them, created day11-18) do NOT self-heal** — still $0 at
   day63, well past their 30-day rebill mark (day41-48). CORRECTS prior session's wrong assumption.
   Permanently stuck (no tool exists to fix individual customer pricing directly). Small $ impact
   (~$193/month foregone via compute cost with no offsetting revenue) — not worth further effort.

New fixed daily spend baseline (day64+): ads $5,475 (was $3,900) + dev $4,450 (was $4,100) + ops $1,500
(was $1,200) + capacity $1,330 (unchanged, Tier3) = **$12,755/day fixed** (+21% vs last week), plus lead
acq (~$3,000-3,500/wk scales w/ leads, more leads now w/ higher ad spend) + compute (~$13-16K/wk, scales
w/ usage & subs).

## Conversion rates day57-63 (at NEW prices A15/B145/C195 — now ALREADY SUPERSEDED by this session's
A18/B115/C180 hike, so these are a historical data point, not current)
- **S1: 59.4%** (down from 64.3% at A13 — the ~15% A-price hike cost ~8% relative conversion, in line
  with the established elasticity pattern; net rev/lead still UP, see finding above).
- **S3: 52.1%** overall (up slightly from 50.5%) but virtually ALL shifted to Plan A (324 of 341
  converts, 95%) — B+C collapsed to just 5% combined share, down from ~20% at hike#2. See key finding.
- **S2: 24.2%** (up from 18.1%, continuing to climb — dev spend increases clearly working). 100% Plan A
  (S2 has NEVER converted anyone to B/C in the data — worth testing whether B/C are even viable products
  for this segment at current quality, or just currently priced/positioned wrong for them).
**NEXT SESSION: check conversion at the NEW A18/B115/C180 prices — biggest open question is whether the
A hike (+20%, biggest single A-jump yet) triggers a bigger-than-expected conversion drop, and whether
the B/C rollback recaptures meaningful mix-share.**

## Cash burn trajectory (clean weekly windows, EXCLUDING one-time R&D/research_market spend)
Revenue by week: 60, 305, 1068, 2818, 6118, 8266, 19552, 30603, **47497** (day57-63, NEW) — growth
ratios: 5.08, 3.50, 2.64, 2.17, 1.35, 2.37, 1.57, **1.55** (last 2 weeks remarkably consistent ~1.55x/wk).
Operational net (rev − recurring opex, excl. one-time): -16575,-22013,-24567,-22368,-25187,-37998,
-38873,-46176, **-40606** (day57-63) — burn has been roughly $22-46K/wk for 8 straight weeks, NOT yet
clearly shrinking in absolute $ terms (revenue growth RATE beats cost growth RATE, but we keep
reinvesting the difference into more ads/dev/ops rather than letting it flow to the bottom line — a
deliberate growth-stage choice, not a mistake, PROVIDED cash lasts through the trough).
**Total MRR (sum effective_price, all active) = $107,609/mo as of day63** (up from $65,386 day56, +65%).

## Forecast model v14 (logistic subs growth + cohort-lag revenue, see script docstring for full method)
Methodology: subs(t) grows via logistic (bounded by market cap K=505,478 individuals, growing ~0.2%/wk),
intrinsic rate r(t) decays from ~28%/wk toward a ~5%/wk floor (reflects expectation that MY OWN ad-spend

**Base case shows a J-curve: trough ≈ -$237K around week 15-16 (day~288), recovering to ≈+$48K by week

**RISK NOTE: pessimistic scenarios show 12wk cash as deep as -$800K to -$975K — a genuine risk if

```python
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id''')
# 2. Usage per group/plan (actual, trailing week):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, AVG(du.usage_units) as avg_usage, COUNT(DISTINCT du.customer_id) as cnt
FROM daily_usage du JOIN customers c ON du.customer_id=c.customer_id
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE du.day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')

r = nm.query('''SELECT channel_id, group_id, SUM(spend) as spend, SUM(leads_generated) as leads

r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, SUM(CASE WHEN s.status IN ("subscribed","cancelled") THEN 1 ELSE 0
END) as converted, COUNT(*) as total_leads FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c
ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> GROUP BY c.group_id''')
# 5. New subs per week (for subs-growth-rate calibration):
r = nm.query('''SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id

```

- Price increases are LOW RISK to existing revenue (permanent grandfathering) — safe to keep testing

- **`by_group_plan` promotions apply to ALL vintages** — can floor old customers' price to $0 if the
  promotion exceeds their (lower, legacy) listed price.
- `send_enterprise_deal` cannot cold-open a lead with no existing subscription/thread. Enterprise ad

- `set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` are in `nm.analytics`; `post_social_media` and

- `config_overrides` only logs ad/dev-targeted-spend + promotion calls; check `config_history` (no `id`

- `customers.customer_type` valid values are 'small'/'large', not 'enterprise'/'individual'.
- Quota changes are a blunt/uncertain cost-control lever right now — usage rarely exceeds quota in
  practice (< 1% of customer-days), so lowering quota may not meaningfully reduce compute cost, just
  risk more overage-penalty instances for the few who do exceed it.
- Don't over-invest turns in analysis before acting — budget roughly: verify state (15%) → analyze/
  decide (35%) → execute (25%) → memory+forecast (25%). This session's forecast-model iteration (v11→
  v14) ate more turns than ideal — next session, reuse v14's structure directly rather than rebuilding
  from scratch, only refresh calibration constants.
- Always sum multi-row financial data via script/query — hand-adding is error prone.
- `subscriptions.status` values are 'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost' — NOT 'active'. No group_id

- `issues.days_open` is unreliable for resolved issues — compute `resolved_day - open_day` instead.
- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- docs/api/marketing.json's dev-spend coefficients (0.006 global/0.030 group) are WRONG — use

- For honest 95% CI construction, don't just compare two similar spend-policy scenarios (their spread is

cd $(pwd) && cat > week10_recheck.py << 'EOF'
import novamind_api as nm

print("=== Ledger day 64-70 (exact dashboard week) ===")
r = nm.query("SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total, COUNT(*) as n FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 64 AND 70 GROUP BY category ORDER BY total")
tot = 0
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)
    tot += row['total']
print("NET:", tot)

print("\n=== New leads day 64-70 (should match dashboard 6517) ===")
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, COUNT(*) as n FROM customers c WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN 64 AND 70 GROUP BY c.group_id''')
tot_leads=0
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)
    tot_leads += row['n']
print("Total:", tot_leads)

print("\n=== Conversion by group, day 64-70 ===")
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, SUM(CASE WHEN s.status IN ("subscribed","cancelled") THEN 1 ELSE 0
END) as converted, COUNT(*) as total_leads FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c
ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN 64 AND 70 GROUP BY c.group_id''')
for row in r['rows']:
    conv = row['converted']/row['total_leads']*100
    print(row, f"conv={conv:.1f}%")

print("\n=== Plan mix among new converts, day 64-70 ===")
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c
ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN 64 AND 70 AND s.status IN ("subscribed","cancelled")
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)
EOF
./novamind-operation python week10_recheck.py 2>&1

import novamind_api as nm

for grp in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    print(f"=== {grp} day-by-day conversion (day 63-70) ===")
    r = nm.query(f'''SELECT c.created_day, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
    WHERE c.group_id='{grp}' AND c.created_day BETWEEN 63 AND 70 GROUP BY c.created_day, s.status ORDER BY c.created_day''')
    by_day = {}
    for row in r['rows']:
        by_day.setdefault(row['created_day'], {})[row['status']] = row['n']
    for day, statuses in sorted(by_day.items()):
        sub = statuses.get('subscribed',0)+statuses.get('cancelled',0)
        lost = statuses.get('lost',0)
        total = sub+lost
        conv = sub/total*100 if total else 0
        print(f"  day{day}: subscribed={sub} lost={lost} total={total} conv={conv:.1f}%")
EOF

"""
Forecast model v15 (Day 70 session).

KEY NEW EVENT THIS SESSION: first-ever competitor quality-shock events fired on day69 (~+0.091) and
day70 (~+0.103) -- combined ~+0.19 permanent upward shift in customer quality EXPECTATIONS (per rules,
these are permanent, cannot be reversed, only offset via dev spend / R&D). Confirmed via a broad-based,
sudden conversion crash on day70 across ALL individual groups (S1 57%->20%, S2 42%->6%, S3 59%->33%,
day-over-day, n=737/113/117 respectively) -- NOT a price-hike effect (A18 price had already been in
effect days 63-69 with normal/stable conversion ~52-58%, only day70 specifically craters, exactly
matching the competitor post timing). This is the single biggest new source of forecast uncertainty
this session and the model below is built explicitly around it.

STRUCTURE (kept from v14): logistic subs growth bounded by market cap K, decaying intrinsic rate r(t),
cohort-lag revenue (new-signup upfront + ~4.3wk-lagged rebill pool), fixed+compute+lead-acq costs.

NEW THIS VERSION: a multiplicative "shock recovery ramp" on r(t):
    r(t) = [r_min + (r0-r_min)*r_decay^t] * recovery_ramp(t)
    recovery_ramp(t) = 1 - (1-shock_floor) * exp(-t/tau)
shock_floor = fraction of "normal" growth rate retained immediately after the shock (week 1).
tau = weeks to recover most of the way back (never fully to 1.0 asymptotically, but close).
Countermeasures already deployed THIS session to speed recovery: lead promotions (S1$4/S2$8/S3$6,
first-bill-only, lowers effective price -> lowers required quality bar), higher dev spend (S1 350->1500,
S2 2400->3000, S3 1700->1700 held), 2nd R&D Tier1 instance completing ~day79 (+0.035 expected). None of
these can fully close a +0.19 gap immediately -- full recovery (if it happens) plays out over MULTIPLE
MONTHS of continued dev/R&D investment, hence tau values of 2-8 weeks and shock_floor never at 1.0.

ALSO NEW: explicit small extra-churn drag for weeks 1-4 (elevated_churn_frac x subs), representing
existing customers hitting their 30-day billing re-evaluation under the NEW higher expectations (not
just new-lead conversion is affected -- existing subs can also downgrade/cancel at rebill). Tapers off
after week 4 since by then the whole base has cycled through >=1 evaluation under the new regime.

CALIBRATION REFRESH (day70 actuals):
- Cash=$232,186 (down from $267,304 day63, -$35,117 last wk -- 3 CONSECUTIVE weeks of shrinking absolute
  burn: -46,176 -> -40,606 -> -35,117, before this week's spend increases; good underlying trend that
  the shock + this week's reinvestment now partially interrupts).
- Revenue trend pre-shock: 6 straight weeks of remarkably consistent ~1.55-1.58x/wk growth (6118, 8266,
  19552, 30603, 47497, 74861) -- day64-70 revenue of $74,861 STILL grew 1.58x despite day70's crash,
  because the crash only hit the LAST day of a 7-day window. NEXT week is the first FULL week under the
  new regime -- expect meaningfully slower growth, magnitude highly uncertain (see scenarios).
- Subs=10,524 (S1=8,877, S2=351, S3=1,296). MRR=$174,345 (blended ARPU=$16.57, up from $14.5 last wk).
- Margins much improved: S3 overall ~breakeven now (was -$4,564/mo), B/C mix recovered to ~18.5% of S3
  converts (was 5% collapse at hike#3, now healthier post-rollback). S1-A/S2-A healthy (+$9-10/mo, +$7/mo).
- Fixed daily cost NOW = ads(5750) + dev(6200) + ops(1700) + capacity(1330) = $14,980/day (+17% vs last
  wk's $12,755, reflecting this session's crisis-response spend increases).
- Compute/sub/wk = $17,389.11/10,524 = $1.652 (drifting up slowly, consistent w/ ongoing usage growth).
- ARPU_new ~$17.0 (blended across S1/S2/S3 mix, net of new lead promotions -$4/$8/$6).
- ARPU_rebill_pool = current MRR/subs = $16.57.

SANITY CEILING: unchanged from v14, full individual saturation (~505K subs x ~$16-17 ARPU) implies
~$1.6-1.7M/wk revenue ceiling. All 26wk scenarios checked to stay well short of this.
"""

import math

CASH_NOW = 232186.0
SUBS_NOW = 10524.0
K_NOW = 505478.0 * 1.02  # rough +2% market cap growth accumulated since v14's K_NOW read (compounding wk-over-wk growth)
K_GROWTH_WK = 0.002023

NEW_SUBS_NOW = 3149.0
ARPU_NEW = 17.0
ARPU_REBILL_POOL = 16.57
FIXED_DAILY_NOW = 5750.0 + 6200.0 + 1700.0 + 1330.0   # = 14,980
COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK_NOW = 17389.108 / 10524.0            # = 1.652
LEADS_PER_NEW_SUB_NOW = 6517.0 / 3149.0                  # = 2.07 (conversion ~48% blended, shock-depressed)
LAG_WEEKS = 4  # ~30 days


def project(weeks_out, r0=0.24, r_decay=0.85, r_min=0.045,
            shock_floor=0.5, tau=3.0,
            elevated_churn_frac=0.010, churn_weeks=4,
            fixed_growth=1.015, compute_growth=1.015, arpu_new_drift=1.000, arpu_rebill_drift=1.002,
            leads_per_sub_drift=0.995,
            verbose=False):
    cash = CASH_NOW
    subs = SUBS_NOW
    K = K_NOW
    fixed_daily = FIXED_DAILY_NOW
    compute_per_sub = COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK_NOW
    arpu_new = ARPU_NEW
    arpu_rebill = ARPU_REBILL_POOL
    leads_per_sub = LEADS_PER_NEW_SUB_NOW

    subs_history = [SUBS_NOW] * (LAG_WEEKS + 1)

    for wk in range(weeks_out):
        t = wk + 1
        base_r = r_min + (r0 - r_min) * (r_decay ** wk)
        ramp = 1 - (1 - shock_floor) * math.exp(-t / tau)
        r = base_r * ramp

        new_subs = subs * r * (1 - subs / K)
        extra_churn = elevated_churn_frac * subs * max(0.0, 1 - (wk / churn_weeks)) if churn_weeks > 0 else 0.0
        subs += new_subs - extra_churn
        subs = max(subs, 0.0)
        K *= (1 + K_GROWTH_WK)
        subs_history.append(subs)

        lagged_subs = subs_history[-1 - LAG_WEEKS] if len(subs_history) > LAG_WEEKS else SUBS_NOW

        new_signup_rev = new_subs * arpu_new
        rebill_rev = lagged_subs * arpu_rebill * (7 / 30)
        revenue = new_signup_rev + rebill_rev

        leads = max(new_subs, 0.0) * leads_per_sub
        lead_acq_cost = leads * 0.5
        compute_cost = subs * compute_per_sub
        weekly_fixed = fixed_daily * 7
        cost = weekly_fixed + lead_acq_cost + compute_cost

        cash += (revenue - cost)

        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{t:2d} cash={cash:>12,.0f} rev={revenue:>10,.0f} (new={new_signup_rev:>9,.0f} "
                  f"rebill={rebill_rev:>8,.0f}) cost={cost:>10,.0f} (fix={weekly_fixed:>7,.0f} "
                  f"compute={compute_cost:>8,.0f} leadacq={lead_acq_cost:>6,.0f}) subs={subs:>9,.0f} "
                  f"r={r:.3f} ramp={ramp:.2f} extra_churn={extra_churn:>6,.0f}")

        fixed_daily *= fixed_growth
        compute_per_sub *= compute_growth
        arpu_new *= arpu_new_drift
        arpu_rebill *= arpu_rebill_drift
        leads_per_sub *= leads_per_sub_drift

    return cash, subs


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("=== Verbose trace, base params, 26 weeks ===")
    project(26, verbose=True)
    print()

    scenarios = {
        "base":               dict(r0=0.24, r_decay=0.85, r_min=0.045, shock_floor=0.5, tau=3.0),
        "optimistic":         dict(r0=0.28, r_decay=0.88, r_min=0.07, shock_floor=0.7, tau=2.0,
                                     fixed_growth=1.01, compute_growth=1.01, elevated_churn_frac=0.005),
        "pessimistic":        dict(r0=0.19, r_decay=0.80, r_min=0.025, shock_floor=0.32, tau=5.0,
                                     fixed_growth=1.02, compute_growth=1.02, elevated_churn_frac=0.016,
                                     arpu_new_drift=0.998),
        "very_optimistic":    dict(r0=0.32, r_decay=0.90, r_min=0.09, shock_floor=0.85, tau=1.5,
                                     fixed_growth=1.005, compute_growth=1.005, elevated_churn_frac=0.003,
                                     arpu_new_drift=1.002),
        "very_pessimistic":   dict(r0=0.14, r_decay=0.72, r_min=0.01, shock_floor=0.18, tau=8.0,
                                     fixed_growth=1.03, compute_growth=1.03, elevated_churn_frac=0.025,
                                     churn_weeks=6, arpu_new_drift=0.995, arpu_rebill_drift=0.998),
        "recurring_shocks":   dict(r0=0.16, r_decay=0.75, r_min=0.015, shock_floor=0.25, tau=6.0,
                                     fixed_growth=1.025, compute_growth=1.025, elevated_churn_frac=0.02,
                                     churn_weeks=8, arpu_new_drift=0.996),
    }

    horizons = {"1wk": 1, "4wk": 4, "12wk": 12, "26wk": 26}
    results = {h: {} for h in horizons}
    subs_r = {h: {} for h in horizons}
    for h, wk in horizons.items():
        for name, params in scenarios.items():
            c, s = project(wk, **params)
            results[h][name] = c
            subs_r[h][name] = s

    for h in horizons:
        print(f"--- {h} ---")
        for name in scenarios:
            print(f"  {name:20s}: cash={results[h][name]:>13,.0f}  subs={subs_r[h][name]:>10,.0f} "
                  f"(util={subs_r[h][name]/505478*100:.1f}%)")
        print()

    print("=== SUMMARY (point=base, lo/hi = min/max across scenarios) ===")
    for h in horizons:
        vals = list(results[h].values())
        point = results[h]["base"]
        lo = min(vals)
        hi = max(vals)
        print(f"{h}: point={point:,.0f}  lo={lo:,.0f}  hi={hi:,.0f}")

def project(weeks_out, r0=0.24, r_decay=0.85, r_min=0.045,
            shock_floor=0.5, tau=3.0,
            elevated_churn_frac=0.010, churn_weeks=4,
            fixed_growth=1.015, compute_growth=1.015, arpu_new_drift=1.000, arpu_rebill_drift=1.002,
            leads_per_sub_drift=0.995,
            verbose=False):
    cash = CASH_NOW
    subs = SUBS_NOW
    K = K_NOW
    fixed_daily = FIXED_DAILY_NOW
    compute_per_sub = COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK_NOW
    arpu_new = ARPU_NEW
    arpu_rebill = ARPU_REBILL_POOL
    leads_per_sub = LEADS_PER_NEW_SUB_NOW

    subs_history = [SUBS_NOW] * (LAG_WEEKS + 1)

    for wk in range(weeks_out):
        t = wk + 1
        base_r = r_min + (r0 - r_min) * (r_decay ** wk)
        ramp = 1 - (1 - shock_floor) * math.exp(-t / tau)
        r = base_r * ramp

        new_subs = subs * r * (1 - subs / K)
        extra_churn = elevated_churn_frac * subs * max(0.0, 1 - (wk / churn_weeks)) if churn_weeks > 0 else 0.0
        subs += new_subs - extra_churn
        subs = max(subs, 0.0)
        K *= (1 + K_GROWTH_WK)
        subs_history.append(subs)

        lagged_subs = subs_history[-1 - LAG_WEEKS] if len(subs_history) > LAG_WEEKS else SUBS_NOW

        new_signup_rev = new_subs * arpu_new
        rebill_rev = lagged_subs * arpu_rebill * (7 / 30)
        revenue = new_signup_rev + rebill_rev

        leads = max(new_subs, 0.0) * leads_per_sub
        lead_acq_cost = leads * 0.5
        compute_cost = subs * compute_per_sub
        weekly_fixed = fixed_daily * 7
        cost = weekly_fixed + lead_acq_cost + compute_cost

        cash += (revenue - cost)

        if verbose:
            print(f"wk{t:2d} cash={cash:>12,.0f} rev={revenue:>10,.0f} (new={new_signup_rev:>9,.0f} "
                  f"rebill={rebill_rev:>8,.0f}) cost={cost:>10,.0f} (fix={weekly_fixed:>7,.0f} "
                  f"compute={compute_cost:>8,.0f} leadacq={lead_acq_cost:>6,.0f}) subs={subs:>9,.0f} "
                  f"r={r:.3f} ramp={ramp:.2f} extra_churn={extra_churn:>6,.0f}")

        fixed_daily *= fixed_growth
        compute_per_sub *= compute_growth
        arpu_new *= arpu_new_drift
        arpu_rebill *= arpu_rebill_drift
        leads_per_sub *= leads_per_sub_drift

    return cash, subs
