## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **NEW (day84): applying a single blended compute-per-sub (or other unit-economic) rate across ALL
  segments badly misrepresents forward costs/benefits when growth is concentrated in ONE segment with
  different unit economics.** Always split the model by segment when their economics genuinely differ
  (confirmed materially wrong this session: S1 costs ~$1.05/wk/sub vs S2+S3 blended ~$6.74/wk/sub —
  6.4x difference — and applying the blended rate to S1-concentrated growth wrongly showed cash
  spiraling to zero from organic growth ALONE, before any new ad spend was even added).
- **NEW (day84): a spend-level sweep must check the MINIMUM cash over the whole trajectory across ALL
  scenarios, not just the point-estimate endpoint.** A spend level's "base scenario" cash at week 26 can
  look fine while the trough at week 10-14 (or a worse scenario entirely) is dangerously low or even
  negative. Pick operating points with a comfortable worst-case trough (rule of thumb >40-50% of
  current cash preserved), especially this early in the game (week 12 of 72) when cash cushion is thin.
- **NEW (day84): ops-spend cuts can cause a SUDDEN resolution-capacity ceiling, not a gradual
  slowdown** — going from $1700→$700/day collapsed resolved/opened ratio from ~0.95 to ~0.40 almost
  immediately (not a multi-week gradual decline). Empirical relationship: capacity_per_day ≈ 0.6 ×
  ops_spend. Don't treat ops spend as a "free" cost-cutting lever without checking this ceiling effect.
- **NEW (day84): social-media "process-fix" framing that scores well for most groups can still
  backfire for a SPECIFIC group** (S1: -0.65 on "burst headroom"/"scale" language, day77 post) even
  when 7/8 groups liked it — check `effect_by_group` per-group, not just an aggregate "did it work"
  read, and adapt phrasing (avoid enterprise/scale language) if S1 is a likely reader of the reply.
- **Weekly cash COLLECTED can diverge substantially from the MRR trend** due to 30-day billing-cycle
  lumpiness (this session: collected fell 26% while MRR actually grew 4.6%) — always verify MRR via
  direct query, don't infer MRR direction from a single week's collected-cash figure.
- **At depressed conversion + low new-signup ARPU, heavy ad/dev spend can be cash-NEGATIVE in
  aggregate over a 26-week horizon** even when unit-level LTV/CAC looks positive in isolation — this
  was true during the day70-77 crisis (conversion ~27-35%, price $18). It became FALSE again once
  conversion recovered to ~37% post price-cut and ad elasticity was confirmed near-linear — always
  re-test this conclusion when conversion/pricing/elasticity assumptions change, don't treat a prior
  session's conclusion as permanent.
- **Competitor quality-shock events can recur DAILY for an extended stretch (12 straight days, 69-80),
  then stop** — check `social_media_posts` for 'quality boost' mentions every session; don't assume a
  taper is permanent until confirmed over multiple sessions.
- **Lead promotions (first-bill-only discounts) can create a "second-month cliff"** — reserve for
  smaller supplementary nudges; a genuine list-price cut is more durable for a structural
  conversion/quality-gap fix.
- **B/C-tier price hikes can backfire via mix-shift to a cheaper in-product plan**, not just via lost
  conversion — check plan-mix-among-converts, not just overall conversion%, after any pricing change.
- **A-tier price changes are GLOBAL (no per-group override)** — a cut that helps a low-usage group
  (S1) can push a higher-usage group on the same plan letter (S3-A) into thin/negative margin. Usually
  a small-dollar, acceptable trade-off if the benefiting group is much bigger, but check the math.
- **`subscriptions.plan` field updates in place — no history.** Can't reconstruct past plan assignments.
- **Ledger has no customer_id — can't cleanly decompose "new signup" vs "rebill" revenue.**
- **Ad spend self-funding same-week/short-term ≠ cash-safe at scale, especially post-conversion-shock.**
  Re-verify CPL *and* the resulting cash-flow-adjusted payback period AND a full trough-aware sweep
  (see above), not just CPL alone, before scaling ad spend.
- **Re-verify per-plan-per-group margins EVERY session using ACTUAL usage** — usage drifts up over
  time, and a global price change can flip a segment's margin sign.
- **`set_prices`/`set_model_tiers`/`set_usage_quotas` have NO per-group override** — one global price per
  plan letter across all groups sharing that plan.
- **Social posts emphasizing low price/affordability backfire for quality-focused & enterprise
  segments** (confirmed 1x strongly). Default to reliability/uptime/support-metric or concrete-process-
  fix framing instead, BUT avoid "scale"/"teams"/enterprise-flavored language if S1 is a likely reader
  (see new nuance above) — use generic ticket-escalation-commitment style instead.
- Price increases/decreases are LOW RISK to existing revenue (permanent grandfathering) — safe to keep
  adjusting new-signup prices as margin/conversion analysis supports, but watch for mix-shift effects
  AND confounding with competitor shocks (check day-by-day, not just before/after weekly averages).
- **`by_group_plan` promotions apply to ALL vintages** — can floor old customers' price to $0 if the
  promotion exceeds their (lower, legacy) listed price. `set_lead_promotion` is safer for NEW-lead-only
  discounts but has its own "second-month cliff" risk (see above).
- `send_enterprise_deal` cannot cold-open a lead with no existing subscription/thread. Enterprise ad
  spend generates ~$0 attributed leads.
- `set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` are in `nm.analytics`; `post_social_media`,
  `set_targeted_ad_spend`, and `set_lead_promotion` are in `nm.marketing`; `set_promotion` in `nm.pricing`.
- `config_overrides` only logs ad/dev-targeted-spend + promotion + lead-promotion calls; check
  `config_history` (no `id` column, filter by `day=N`) for prices/tiers/quotas/capacity/global daily
  spend. `config_history`'s ad_spend_* columns read 0 even when targeted ad spend is active (known
  quirk, cross-check ledger `advertising` category instead).
- `customers.customer_type` valid values are 'small'/'large', not 'enterprise'/'individual'.
- `research_projects` has no `completed_day` column — use `status`/`expected_completion_day`/
  `quality_boost_applied` instead.
- Quota changes are a blunt/uncertain cost-control lever — usage rarely exceeds quota in practice.
- Don't over-invest turns in analysis before acting — budget roughly: verify state (15%) → analyze/
  decide (35%) → execute (25%) → memory+forecast (25%). Reuse the existing forecast model's structure
  directly rather than rebuilding from scratch each session — only refresh calibration constants
  (though DO fix real structural bugs when found, like the blended-compute-rate issue this session).
- Always sum multi-row financial data via script/query — hand-adding is error prone.
- `subscriptions.status` values are 'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost' — NOT 'active'. No group_id
  column on subscriptions — must JOIN customers.
- `get_social_posts()` returns a DICT `{'posts': [...], 'total': N}` — iterate `result['posts']`, or
  query `social_media_posts` table directly (gives post_id + source_group_id together, more useful).
- `issues.days_open` is unreliable for resolved issues — compute `resolved_day - open_day` instead.
- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- docs/api/marketing.json's dev-spend coefficients (0.006 global/0.030 group) are WRONG — use
  0.0045/0.0225, empirically confirmed exact multiple times across sessions.
- For honest 95% CI construction: run a scenario sweep with genuinely varied assumptions (conversion
  path, churn multiplier, elasticity), take min/max across scenarios AND across the full 26-week
  trajectory (not just endpoints), widen further judgmentally for model-structure risk, and sanity-
  check against a manual hand-calc AND (for cost projections) a segment-split model, not a blended one.

"""
Forecast model v18 (Day 84 session, REVISION) -- fixes a material flaw found in v17.

CRITICAL FIX: v17 applied a single BLENDED compute-cost-per-sub rate to the ENTIRE subscriber base,
including all future growth. But growth is ~100% concentrated in S1 (all ad spend is S1-only; ~83% of
organic leads are S1 too), and S1's true compute cost (~$1.07/wk/sub, i.e. ~$4.58/mo, confirmed via
usage-table join: S1-A usage 76.4/day * $0.002/unit * 30 = $4.58/mo) is MUCH lower than the blended
average across the whole book (~$1.96/wk/sub = ~$8.4/mo), which is skewed way up by the small
(~2,076 subs, 16% of base) but usage-heavy S2/S3 cohort (S3-B/C especially). Applying the blended rate
to fast-growing S1 subs overstated future compute cost enormously -- e.g. v17 showed cash going
negative by week 18-19 even at UNCHANGED ad spend (700/d) just from the ops increase (1500/d) and
organic-only compounding, which didn't square with a manual sanity check of S1 unit economics
(+$8.42/mo margin per new S1 sub at $13 price). v18 splits the subscriber base into S1 vs
"Other" (S2+S3) and tracks compute cost, MRR, leads, and conversion SEPARATELY for each, since their
economics are fundamentally different (S1 = cheap-to-serve/price-sensitive/high-growth-potential;
Other = expensive-to-serve/quality-sensitive/slow-growth-under-current-settings).

Calibration (day84, all confirmed via query):
  S1: subs=10,786, MRR=$157,951, compute=$11,374/wk ($1.054/wk/sub), ad_leads_wk=924 @ $4,900/wk spend
      (elasticity 0.98, measured), organic_leads_wk=1,110, conversion=37.2% (this week actual)
  Other (S2+S3): subs=2,076, MRR=$65,939, compute=$13,982/wk ($6.736/wk/sub), organic_leads_wk=219
      (no ad spend), conversion=17.4% blended (S2 14.3%, S3 18.6%, small samples/noisy)
  (validation: 11374+13982=25356 vs actual ledger compute $25,176/wk -- within 1%, good fit)

RE-USE NEXT SESSION: refresh all calibration constants from fresh queries (S1 vs Other split for subs/
MRR/compute/leads/conversion). Re-measure ad elasticity if S1 ad spend level changes again. This
segment-split structure should be kept going forward -- it's a materially better fit than a single
blended compute rate given how concentrated growth is in S1.
"""
import math

CASH_NOW = 135639.90

# S1 (cheap-to-serve, price-sensitive, ad+organic growth)
S1_SUBS_NOW = 10786.0
S1_MRR_NOW = 157951.0
S1_COMPUTE_WK_NOW = 11374.0
S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = S1_COMPUTE_WK_NOW / S1_SUBS_NOW
S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW = 924.0
S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW = 4900.0
S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1110.0
S1_ARPU_NEW = 11.0
S1_BASE_CONVERSION = 0.372

# Other = S2+S3 (expensive-to-serve, quality-sensitive, organic-only under current settings)
OTH_SUBS_NOW = 2076.0
OTH_MRR_NOW = 65939.0
OTH_COMPUTE_WK_NOW = 13982.0
OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = OTH_COMPUTE_WK_NOW / OTH_SUBS_NOW
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 219.0
OTH_ARPU_NEW = 10.0
OTH_BASE_CONVERSION = 0.174

AD_ELASTICITY = 0.98
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
CAPACITY_WK = 1330.0*7

def simulate(weeks, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_wk, s1_conv_path, oth_conv_path=lambda w: OTH_BASE_CONVERSION,
             churn_mult=1.0, s1_usage_growth0=0.010, oth_usage_growth0=0.020):
    cash = CASH_NOW
    s1_subs, s1_mrr = S1_SUBS_NOW, S1_MRR_NOW
    oth_subs, oth_mrr = OTH_SUBS_NOW, OTH_MRR_NOW
    s1_cpsw, oth_cpsw = S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK, OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK
    s1_ug, oth_ug = s1_usage_growth0, oth_usage_growth0

        s1_org_leads = S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (s1_subs/S1_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        s1_leads = s1_ad_leads+s1_org_leads

        oth_new = oth_leads*oth_conv

        churn_oth = 0.011*churn_mult + (0.004*churn_mult if w<4 else 0)

"""
Forecast model v19 (Day 91 session, REVISION over v18).

WHY v19: v18 assumed weekly churn ~0.9-1.3% (flat, small "new cohort" bump for first 4 weeks).
Day91 data revealed this was badly wrong -- actual weekly churn THIS WEEK was S1=3.20% (345/10786),
Other=2.84% (59/2076), roughly 2.5-3x the v18 assumption. Root cause (confirmed via cohort tenure
analysis): billing evaluations happen EVERY 30 days per customer, and customer expected-quality drifts
up continuously (organic drift + competitor shocks) -- so EVERY successive 30-day evaluation is harder
to pass than the last, for old AND new cohorts alike. Direct evidence: same S1 cohort (created day25-31)
had 4.1% churn at their FIRST eval (tenure30) vs 8.9% at their SECOND eval (tenure60) -- churn-per-eval
roughly DOUBLED for the identical cohort. Separately, unresolved issues are strongly correlated with
churn-at-eval: cohort members with an open issue churned at 21.9% vs 9.7% for those without (2.3x) --
this component IS controllable via ops spend (issue backlog was exploding after the day77 ops cut,
partially fixed day84 ops-to-1100, backlog still net +150-250/day at that level -> raising further
this session, see MEMORY.md).

Also NEW this session: competitor quality-shocks, which had gone quiet day81-88 (8 days, previously
mis-read as "tapering to zero" -- WRONG, confirmed wrong this session), RESUMED day89-91 with 3 shock
events (~0.03-0.04 magnitude each, larger than the tail-end of the prior cluster). Do not assume any
quiet period is permanent -- re-check every session, no exceptions.

Approach: model an "effective weekly churn rate" per segment that starts at the freshly-calibrated
elevated level and follows a SCENARIO-DEPENDENT path (taper down if ops fix works & shocks stay quiet;
stay elevated or worsen if shocks keep recurring / backlog doesn't clear). This is a coarser
approximation than truly modeling the 30-day-eval-per-customer mechanic, but far more honest than v18's
flat-low-churn assumption. Re-calibrate the starting churn rate AND re-derive the scenario paths fresh
every session from actual cohort-tenure queries (see MEMORY.md query templates) -- don't reuse these
numbers blindly once more weeks of data exist.

Calibration (day91, all confirmed via query):
  S1: subs=11,550, MRR=$167,419, compute=$12,219/wk ($1.068/wk/sub), ad_leads_wk=1,692 @ $8,400/wk
      spend (elasticity ~0.90-0.98), organic_leads_wk=1,346, conversion ad~35.6%/organic~37.7%
      (blended 36.5%). Weekly churn THIS WEEK = 3.20% (elevated, see above).
  Other (S2+S3): subs=2,076, MRR=$69,228, compute=$14,409/wk ($6.95/wk/sub), organic_leads_wk=284,
      conversion S2 11.0%/S3 24.8% (blended 20.8%, small samples/noisy). Weekly churn = 2.84%.
  (validation: 12219+14409=26628 vs actual ledger compute $26,303/wk -- within 1.2%, good fit)

Decision this session: ops 1100->2000/day (targets resolution capacity ~1200/day vs opened ~840-900/
day, so backlog SHRINKS ~300-350/day instead of growing -- addresses the ops/issue component of churn
directly, which is the ONE part of this problem we can reliably control this week). Dev S1 300->800/day,
S3 100->150/day (moderate increase, NOT an aggressive extrapolation -- see MEMORY.md for why I'm wary
of extrapolating the linear-accumulation dev-spend formula too far out on a long horizon without more
data). Ad spend held FLAT this week to isolate the ops-effect measurement.

RE-USE NEXT SESSION: refresh ALL calibration constants. Specifically check: (1) did backlog actually
start shrinking at ops=2000/day (resolved/day should approach ~1200)? (2) did churn-at-eval improve for
the NEXT at-risk cohort (created day62-68, evaluating day92-98)? (3) any new competitor shocks day92-98?
Update the churn scenario paths based on what actually happened, don't just reuse these numbers.
"""
import math

CASH_NOW = 133105.72

# S1 (cheap-to-serve, price-sensitive, ad+organic growth)
S1_SUBS_NOW = 11550.0
S1_MRR_NOW = 167419.0
S1_COMPUTE_WK_NOW = 12219.0
S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = S1_COMPUTE_WK_NOW / S1_SUBS_NOW
S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1692.0
S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW = 8400.0
S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1346.0
S1_ARPU_NEW = 11.0
S1_BASE_CONVERSION = 0.365
S1_CHURN_WK_NOW = 0.0320

# Other = S2+S3 (expensive-to-serve, quality-sensitive, organic-only under current settings)
OTH_SUBS_NOW = 2076.0
OTH_MRR_NOW = 69228.0
OTH_COMPUTE_WK_NOW = 14409.0
OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = OTH_COMPUTE_WK_NOW / OTH_SUBS_NOW
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 284.0
OTH_ARPU_NEW = 10.0
OTH_BASE_CONVERSION = 0.208
OTH_CHURN_WK_NOW = 0.0284

AD_ELASTICITY = 0.92
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
CAPACITY_WK = 1330.0*7

def simulate(weeks, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_wk, s1_conv_path, oth_conv_path=lambda w: OTH_BASE_CONVERSION,
             s1_churn_path=None, oth_churn_path=None,
             s1_usage_growth0=0.010, oth_usage_growth0=0.020):
    cash = CASH_NOW
    s1_subs, s1_mrr = S1_SUBS_NOW, S1_MRR_NOW
    oth_subs, oth_mrr = OTH_SUBS_NOW, OTH_MRR_NOW
    s1_cpsw, oth_cpsw = S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK, OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK
    s1_ug, oth_ug = s1_usage_growth0, oth_usage_growth0
    trace = []
    for w in range(weeks):
        s1_conv = s1_conv_path(w)
        oth_conv = oth_conv_path(w)
        s1_ad_leads = S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW * (ad_wk/S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW)**AD_ELASTICITY if ad_wk>0 else 0.0
        s1_org_leads = S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (s1_subs/S1_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        s1_leads = s1_ad_leads+s1_org_leads
        s1_new = s1_leads*s1_conv
        oth_leads = OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (oth_subs/OTH_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        oth_new = oth_leads*oth_conv

        churn_s1 = s1_churn_path(w)
        churn_oth = oth_churn_path(w)

        mrr_start = s1_mrr+oth_mrr
        s1_mrr = s1_mrr*(1-churn_s1) + s1_new*S1_ARPU_NEW
        oth_mrr = oth_mrr*(1-churn_oth) + oth_new*OTH_ARPU_NEW
        s1_subs = s1_subs*(1-churn_s1) + s1_new
        oth_subs = oth_subs*(1-churn_oth) + oth_new
        mrr_end = s1_mrr+oth_mrr
        revenue = (mrr_start+mrr_end)/2*7/30*0.93

        s1_cpsw *= (1+s1_ug); s1_ug *= 0.85
        oth_cpsw *= (1+oth_ug); oth_ug *= 0.85
        compute_cost = s1_subs*s1_cpsw + oth_subs*oth_cpsw
        lead_acq_cost = LEAD_ACQ_COST*(s1_leads+oth_leads)
        costs = dev_wk+ad_wk+ops_wk+CAPACITY_WK+compute_cost+lead_acq_cost
        cash += revenue-costs
        trace.append(dict(week=w+1, cash=cash, subs=s1_subs+oth_subs, mrr=mrr_end,
                           revenue=revenue, costs=costs, compute=compute_cost))
    return trace

def s1_conv_base(w): return S1_BASE_CONVERSION
def oth_conv_base(w): return OTH_BASE_CONVERSION

# --- churn scenario paths ---
def churn_taper_fast(base):   # ops fix works well, shocks stay quiet -> taper to ~1.5% over 6wk
    def f(w): return max(0.015, base - (base-0.015)*min(1.0, w/6.0))
    return f
def churn_taper_slow(base):   # partial improvement, taper to ~2.2% over 10wk
    def f(w): return max(0.022, base - (base-0.022)*min(1.0, w/10.0))
    return f
def churn_flat(base):         # stays at current elevated level indefinitely
    def f(w): return base
    return f
def churn_worsen(base, cap):  # shocks keep recurring, backlog doesn't clear -> keeps climbing
    def f(w): return min(cap, base + 0.0015*w)
    return f

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("=== SWEEP: (ops_daily, s1_dev_daily) at ad=8400/wk fixed, base conv, TAPER_SLOW churn ===")
    for ops_d, s1_dev_d in [(1100,300),(1500,300),(1500,800),(2000,300),(2000,800),(2000,1500),
                             (2500,800),(2500,1500),(1700,800)]:
        dev_wk = (s1_dev_d+150)*7
        t = simulate(26, 8400, dev_wk, ops_d*7, s1_conv_base, oth_conv_base,
                     churn_taper_slow(S1_CHURN_WK_NOW), churn_taper_slow(OTH_CHURN_WK_NOW))
        vals = [round(t[h-1]['cash']) for h in [1,4,12,26]]
        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in t)); minweek=min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: t[h-1]['cash'])
        print(f"ops={ops_d:>5} s1_dev={s1_dev_d:>5}  wk[1,4,12,26]={vals}  MIN={mincash}@wk{minweek}")

    print()
    print("=== scenario table for CHOSEN op point (ops=2000, s1_dev=800, oth_dev=150, ad=8400/wk) ===")
    ops_wk = 2000*7; dev_wk = (800+150)*7; ad_wk = 8400
    scenarios = {
        "optimistic_taper_fast":   dict(s1_churn_path=churn_taper_fast(S1_CHURN_WK_NOW), oth_churn_path=churn_taper_fast(OTH_CHURN_WK_NOW)),
        "base_taper_slow":         dict(s1_churn_path=churn_taper_slow(S1_CHURN_WK_NOW), oth_churn_path=churn_taper_slow(OTH_CHURN_WK_NOW)),
        "flat_elevated":           dict(s1_churn_path=churn_flat(S1_CHURN_WK_NOW), oth_churn_path=churn_flat(OTH_CHURN_WK_NOW)),
        "worsen_recurring_shocks": dict(s1_churn_path=churn_worsen(S1_CHURN_WK_NOW,0.06), oth_churn_path=churn_worsen(OTH_CHURN_WK_NOW,0.06)),
    }
    results = {}
    for name,p in scenarios.items():
        results[name] = simulate(26, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_wk, s1_conv_base, oth_conv_base, **p)
    for name,trace in results.items():
        vals=[trace[h-1]['cash'] for h in [1,4,12,26]]
        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in trace)); minweek=min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: trace[h-1]['cash'])
        print(f"{name:26s}" + "".join(f"{v:12,.0f}" for v in vals) + f"   MIN={mincash:>12,.0f}@wk{minweek}")

    print()
    print("=== forecast (point=base_taper_slow, lower/upper=min/max across scenarios, widened) ===")
    for h in [1,4,12,26]:
        vals = [results[n][h-1]['cash'] for n in scenarios]
        point = results['base_taper_slow'][h-1]['cash']
        lo,hi = min(vals),max(vals)
        span = hi-lo
        widen = 0.15 if h<=4 else 0.30
        print(f"wk{h:>3}: point={point:>12,.0f} lower={lo-widen*span:>12,.0f} upper={hi+widen*span:>12,.0f}")

"""
Forecast model v20 (Day 91 session) -- adds explicit backlog-linked churn dynamics on top of v19,
since v19's generic "taper" scenario functions couldn't show the BENEFIT of ops spend (only the cost),
making every spend increase look cash-negative. v20 fixes this by modeling:

  weekly_churn(w) = organic_trend(w) + backlog_penalty(w)
  backlog_penalty  = K_BACKLOG * (backlog / total_subs)          [issue-backlog-driven component]
  organic_trend(w) = drift-only component, rising over time independent of backlog

Calibration (all from actual weekly cancellation-rate history, day35-91, queried this session):
  Weekly churn rate (cancelled/base_at_week_start) history: day35-41=0.00%, 42-48=0.20%, 49-55=0.38%,
  56-62=0.40%, 63-69=0.81%, 70-76=1.11%, 77-83=1.50%, 84-90=2.68%. Open backlog history (end of week):
  day35=60,42=121,49=267,56=418,63=628,70=949,77=1260,84=5207,91=6421.
  Backlog was small/organically-growing through day77 (1260) -- the day77-83 churn rate (1.50%) with
  that backlog is used as the "organic-only" reference point. The day77-cut-induced backlog explosion
  (1260->5207->6421) coincided with churn jumping 1.50%->2.68%(->~3.2% my day85-91 measurement, slightly
  different window). K_BACKLOG calibrated so that backlog_fraction=5207/12862=0.405 (day84 state) adds
  ~1.0-1.2pp over the 1.50% organic-only baseline -> K_BACKLOG ~= 2.5 (pp churn per unit backlog
  fraction, i.e. churn += 2.5*backlog/subs). organic_trend(w) continues the pre-crisis rise (~+0.2-0.3pp
  /wk, observed 0%->1.5% over ~7 weeks non-linearly accelerating) -- THIS PART IS THE BIG UNKNOWN: no
  evidence yet on whether it plateaus. Model 3 organic-drift scenarios (decay/continue/accelerate) --
  do NOT assume it just stops; equally do NOT assume it explodes without bound; widen forecast CIs
  accordingly, especially at 12wk/26wk horizons.

Backlog itself evolves mechanically: opened_per_day ~870 (day85-91 actual avg, scales slowly with sub
count), resolved_per_day = 0.6*ops_daily_spend (empirically confirmed multiple sessions, clean fit).

Decision framing this session: v19 showed that jumping straight to ops=2000+dev=950 is NOT cash-safe
if elevated churn persists (drives cash negative by ~week9-10 and it doesn't recover within 26wk). This
v20 model lets us see the BACKLOG-CLEARING BENEFIT explicitly, so we can find a more moderate ops level
that clears backlog meaningfully within a reasonable timeframe (6-10 weeks) without an unsustainable
fixed-cost jump. See bottom of file for the sweep output and final chosen operating point.
"""
import math

CASH_NOW = 133105.72

S1_SUBS_NOW = 11550.0
S1_MRR_NOW = 167419.0
S1_COMPUTE_WK_NOW = 12219.0
S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = S1_COMPUTE_WK_NOW / S1_SUBS_NOW
S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1692.0
S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW = 8400.0
S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1346.0
S1_ARPU_NEW = 11.0
S1_BASE_CONVERSION = 0.365

OTH_SUBS_NOW = 2076.0
OTH_MRR_NOW = 69228.0
OTH_COMPUTE_WK_NOW = 14409.0
OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = OTH_COMPUTE_WK_NOW / OTH_SUBS_NOW
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 284.0
OTH_ARPU_NEW = 10.0
OTH_BASE_CONVERSION = 0.208

AD_ELASTICITY = 0.92
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
CAPACITY_WK = 1330.0*7

BACKLOG_NOW = 6421.0
OPENED_PER_DAY_NOW = 870.0
K_BACKLOG = 2.5          # pp churn (as fraction, e.g. 0.025) per unit backlog/subs fraction... see below
ORGANIC_CHURN_NOW = 0.015  # day77-83 reference (pre-explosion), both segments start here

def organic_trend(w, weekly_slope, cap):
    return min(cap, ORGANIC_CHURN_NOW + weekly_slope*w)

def simulate(weeks, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_daily, s1_conv_path, oth_conv_path,
             organic_slope=0.0015, organic_cap=0.05,
             s1_usage_growth0=0.010, oth_usage_growth0=0.020, opened_growth_wk=0.01):
    cash = CASH_NOW
    s1_subs, s1_mrr = S1_SUBS_NOW, S1_MRR_NOW
    oth_subs, oth_mrr = OTH_SUBS_NOW, OTH_MRR_NOW
    s1_cpsw, oth_cpsw = S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK, OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK
    s1_ug, oth_ug = s1_usage_growth0, oth_usage_growth0
    backlog = BACKLOG_NOW
    opened_per_day = OPENED_PER_DAY_NOW
    trace = []
    for w in range(weeks):
        s1_conv = s1_conv_path(w)
        oth_conv = oth_conv_path(w)
        s1_ad_leads = S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW * (ad_wk/S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW)**AD_ELASTICITY if ad_wk>0 else 0.0
        s1_org_leads = S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (s1_subs/S1_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        s1_leads = s1_ad_leads+s1_org_leads
        s1_new = s1_leads*s1_conv
        oth_leads = OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (oth_subs/OTH_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        oth_new = oth_leads*oth_conv

        total_subs = s1_subs+oth_subs
        backlog_frac = backlog/total_subs if total_subs>0 else 0
        org = organic_trend(w, organic_slope, organic_cap)
        churn_s1 = min(0.5, org + K_BACKLOG*backlog_frac*0.01)   # *0.01 since K_BACKLOG in "pp per unit frac"->fraction
        churn_oth = min(0.5, org + K_BACKLOG*backlog_frac*0.01)

        mrr_start = s1_mrr+oth_mrr
        s1_mrr = s1_mrr*(1-churn_s1) + s1_new*S1_ARPU_NEW
        oth_mrr = oth_mrr*(1-churn_oth) + oth_new*OTH_ARPU_NEW
        s1_subs = s1_subs*(1-churn_s1) + s1_new
        oth_subs = oth_subs*(1-churn_oth) + oth_new
        mrr_end = s1_mrr+oth_mrr
        revenue = (mrr_start+mrr_end)/2*7/30*0.90

        s1_cpsw *= (1+s1_ug); s1_ug *= 0.85
        oth_cpsw *= (1+oth_ug); oth_ug *= 0.85
        compute_cost = s1_subs*s1_cpsw + oth_subs*oth_cpsw
        lead_acq_cost = LEAD_ACQ_COST*(s1_leads+oth_leads)
        ops_wk = ops_daily*7
        costs = dev_wk+ad_wk+ops_wk+CAPACITY_WK+compute_cost+lead_acq_cost
        cash += revenue-costs

        # backlog dynamics
        opened_per_day *= (1+opened_growth_wk/7)
        resolved_per_day = 0.6*ops_daily
        backlog = max(0.0, backlog + (opened_per_day-resolved_per_day)*7)

        trace.append(dict(week=w+1, cash=cash, subs=s1_subs+oth_subs, mrr=mrr_end,
                           revenue=revenue, costs=costs, compute=compute_cost,
                           backlog=backlog, churn=churn_s1))
    return trace

def s1_conv_base(w): return S1_BASE_CONVERSION
def oth_conv_base(w): return OTH_BASE_CONVERSION

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("=== SWEEP: ops_daily (dev held at S1=500/S3=150=650/day=4550/wk, ad=8400/wk), organic_slope=0.0015 base ===")
    for ops_d in [1100,1300,1500,1700,1900,2100,2300]:
        t = simulate(26, 8400, 650*7, ops_d, s1_conv_base, oth_conv_base, organic_slope=0.0015)
        vals = [round(t[h-1]['cash']) for h in [1,4,12,26]]
        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in t)); minweek=min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: t[h-1]['cash'])
        backlog26 = round(t[25]['backlog']); churn26=t[25]['churn']
        print(f"ops={ops_d:>5} wk[1,4,12,26]={vals} MIN={mincash:>10}@wk{minweek}  backlog_wk26={backlog26:>7} churn_wk26={churn26:.3f}")

    print()
    print("=== chosen op point ops=1700, dev S1=500/S3=150, ad=8400/wk -- scenario table across organic-drift assumptions ===")
    ops_d = 1700; dev_wk = 650*7; ad_wk=8400
    scenarios = {
        "slope_decays_fast (opt)":  dict(organic_slope=0.0006, organic_cap=0.03),
        "slope_continues (base)":   dict(organic_slope=0.0015, organic_cap=0.05),
        "slope_accelerates (pess)": dict(organic_slope=0.0028, organic_cap=0.09),
    }
    results={}
    for name,p in scenarios.items():
        results[name]=simulate(26, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_d, s1_conv_base, oth_conv_base, **p)
    for name,trace in results.items():

        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in trace)); minweek=min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: trace[h-1]['cash'])

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 91 = end of week 13. 59 weeks still remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: `forecast_model_v20.py` (segment-split, backlog-linked-churn scenario sim — see its
docstring). This is a MAJOR revision from v18/v19 — read the docstring in full before reusing.

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → refresh forecast model → call
next-week. Verify prior session's plan actually landed via `config_overrides`/`config_history`
(day-filtered) against the live DB — don't trust prior narrative at face value.
**v20 model structure (reuse, refresh calibration every session):** splits S1 vs Other=S2+S3 (different
unit economics, see v18/v19 history for why), AND now separately models an explicit **backlog** state
(opened/day ≈870, resolved/day ≈0.6×ops_spend, confirmed clean multiple sessions) that feeds a
**churn_penalty = K_BACKLOG × backlog/total_subs** on top of an **organic_trend(w)** that drifts up over
time independent of backlog (see "BIG FINDING" below). Always re-derive: S1/Other subs+MRR+compute+
leads+conversion (query templates near bottom), current backlog level + opened/resolved rates, and
recent weekly churn-rate HISTORY (not just this week) to re-estimate organic_trend's slope/plateau.
**Before finalizing any spend decision, sweep AND check MINIMUM cash across the FULL 26-week trajectory
under >=3 genuinely-different scenarios** (not just one "base" case) — this week's sweep showed even a
"do-nothing" spend plan can look fine short-term while a specific driver (churn) craters it by week 20+,
and conversely an over-aggressive spend increase (my first-draft plan: ops$2000+dev$950/day) looked
cash-catastrophic (negative by week 9, unrecovered by week26) versus a more moderate version of the
exact same qualitative decision (ops$1500+dev$600) that stayed sustainable — MAGNITUDE matters a lot,
not just direction. Always sanity-check model week-1 output against a manual hand-calc using last
week's ACTUAL ledger numbers (confirmed this session: model's revenue formula (mrr_avg×7/30×haircut)
matches actual collected cash almost exactly when haircut≈0.93; using 0.90 understated by ~$3-4K/wk —
use 0.93 as the calibrated haircut going forward, revisit if actual/MRR-implied ratio drifts).

## 🚨 BIG FINDING THIS SESSION (day91): churn is structurally rising, NOT just a one-off backlog blip
Weekly cancellation RATE (cancelled/base-at-week-start) history, queried directly day35→91:
0%, 0.20%, 0.38%, 0.40%, 0.81%, 1.11%, 1.50%, **2.68%** (day84-90). This is a CONTINUOUS rise that
PRE-DATES the day77 ops-cut/backlog crisis (already climbing 0%→1.5% over day35-83) — i.e. there are
TWO separate, additive drivers, confirmed via cohort-tenure analysis:
1. **"Organic" drift** (independent of backlog): customer expected-quality drifts up continuously
   (base drift + competitor shocks), and billing re-evaluation happens EVERY 30 days per customer, so
   EVERY successive eval is harder to pass than the last — confirmed directly: the SAME S1 cohort
   (created day25-31) had 4.1% churn at their FIRST eval (tenure30) vs 8.9% at their SECOND eval
   (tenure60) — churn-per-eval odds roughly DOUBLED for the identical customers. This is NOT a
   transient cohort echo — it's evidence the expectation-vs-quality gap widens with tenure/calendar
   time, structurally, for everyone. **R&D is likely the only real lever for this component long-run
   (dev spend log-saturates per the docs) — but dev spend increases DO help some (see below) and are
   cheap, so still worth doing while R&D remains unaffordable.**
2. **Issue-backlog-driven component** (controllable): cohort members with a currently-open unresolved
   issue churned at 21.9% vs 9.7% for those without (2.3x) at their eval — clean, strong signal. The
   day77 ops cut (1700→700/day) caused backlog to explode 1260→5207→6421 (day77→84→91), and this
   directly explains most of the JUMP from the ~1.5% organic trend line to the actual 2.68-3.2% observed
   day84-91. **This component IS fixable via ops spend** — raised ops 1100→1500/day this session
   (targets resolution capacity ~900/day vs opened ~840-900/day; should stabilize then slowly shrink
   backlog — CHECK THIS DIRECTLY next session via opened-vs-resolved-by-day, don't assume it worked).
3. Competitor shocks: **quiet day81-88 (8 days, 0 events) was WRONGLY read last session as "tapering
   confirmed" — it was NOT permanent.** 3 NEW shock events fired day89-91 (magnitudes 0.0305, 0.0433,
   0.0421 — LARGER than the tail of the prior cluster). **Lesson reinforced AGAIN: never assume a quiet
   period means shocks have stopped. Check `social_media_posts` for 'quality boost'/'quality bump'
   mentions EVERY session, no exceptions, indefinitely.**

### What this means for strategy (read before making any spend decision)
A full scenario sweep (forecast_model_v20.py) shows: under a "churn keeps rising at recently-observed
pace" assumption, cash trends toward zero/negative by week 12-26 **regardless of ad/ops/dev spend
levels** (even a "cut everything to zero" test still went negative by week26) — because at CURRENT
subscriber count, gross margin (revenue-compute ≈$27K/wk) barely covers semi-fixed costs (ops+dev+ads+
capacity+lead_acq ≈$30K/wk), so the business is only marginally self-sustaining even before rising
churn. Under a "churn reverts back toward the pre-crisis ~1.2-1.5% trend" assumption (plausible if the
ops fix works AND shocks stay quiet again), cash stays comfortably positive throughout and even a
moderate spend increase pays for itself. **These two scenarios diverge by ~$150-200K by week 26 — this
is the single biggest source of forecast uncertainty right now, wider than anything in prior sessions.
Reflect this honestly with WIDE 12wk/26wk CIs until resolved.**

## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **NEW (day91): NEVER assume a quiet period (in competitor shocks, OR any other adverse dynamic) is
  permanent just because it lasted a week or two.** Day81-88's shock silence was explicitly called
  "confirmed" last session after just 4 days of evidence — it reversed within days. Require MUCH longer
  confirmation windows (3-4+ weeks) before updating a "this has stopped" belief, and even then keep
  re-checking every single session indefinitely.
- **NEW (day91): weekly churn/cancellation rate should be tracked as a LONG HISTORICAL TREND (multiple
  weeks back), not just a single-week snapshot** — a single week's rate can be dominated by one specific
  cohort's bad-luck timing; the multi-week trend (0%→0.2%→...→1.5%→2.68% over 8 weeks) revealed a
  structural, continuously-worsening pattern invisible from any single week's number alone.
- **NEW (day91): billing/quality re-evaluation is EXACTLY periodic (every 30 days per customer) and the
  failure probability at each successive evaluation can RISE over time for the same customers** (4.1%→
  8.9% for one cohort, first eval vs second). Model this as a structural trend, not a fixed per-customer
  risk. Use direct cohort-tenure queries (created_day windows) to measure this precisely each session.
- **NEW (day91): a spend-increase decision needs to be checked at the RIGHT MAGNITUDE, not just the
  right DIRECTION.** My first-draft plan this session (ops $1100→$2000, dev $400→$950/day) was
  qualitatively "correct" (fix the backlog, hedge quality gap) but quantitatively too aggressive —
  modeled cash-negative by week 9, unrecovered by week 26. A more moderate version of the SAME
  qualitative decision (ops→$1500, dev→$600) was much safer. Always sweep MULTIPLE magnitudes, not just
  test one number and accept/reject the whole direction.
- **NEW (day91): more ad spend does not automatically make a spend-scenario sweep look better, even
  when unit-level CAC/LTV math looks favorable in isolation** — if churn is elevated (shortening
  realized customer lifetime) and the forecast HORIZON is short relative to the CAC payback period, MORE
  acquisition spend can show up as cash-negative purely from timing (CAC paid upfront every week,
  revenue trickles in slowly) even though it would eventually pay off over a longer horizon. Always test
  a spend-level sweep (including zero/reduced spend) explicitly rather than assuming "positive unit
  economics = more spend is always better" over any GIVEN forecast window.
- **Applying a single blended compute-per-sub (or other unit-economic) rate across ALL segments badly
  misrepresents forward costs/benefits when growth/economics genuinely differ by segment** (S1 ~$1.07/wk
  vs Other ~$6.95/wk compute, confirmed again this session — always split).
- **A spend-level sweep must check the MINIMUM cash over the whole trajectory across ALL scenarios, not
  just the point-estimate endpoint.**
- **Ops-spend cuts can cause a SUDDEN resolution-capacity ceiling, not a gradual slowdown** — capacity
  ≈0.6×ops_spend, confirmed cleanly across 3+ sessions now at different spend levels.
- **Social-media effect_by_group can flip sign for a specific group even with a similar-style post as a
  prior success** — check `effect_by_group` per-group every time; my "avoid scale language" theory from
  last session was falsified this session by new data (see SOCIAL MEDIA section) — hypotheses about
  this mechanic should be held loosely and re-tested, not treated as settled rules.
- **Weekly cash COLLECTED can diverge substantially from the MRR trend** due to 30-day billing-cycle
  lumpiness — always verify MRR via direct query. The collected/MRR-implied ratio itself is NOISY
  week-to-week (~0.67 to ~1.0 observed across sessions) — use ~0.93 as a central estimate, not a fixed
  constant, and widen forecast CIs to account for this noise.
- **At depressed conversion + low new-signup ARPU, heavy ad/dev spend can be cash-NEGATIVE in aggregate
  over a 26-week horizon** even when unit-level LTV/CAC looks positive in isolation — re-test this
  conclusion whenever conversion/pricing/elasticity/CHURN assumptions change materially (churn is the
  new variable this session that flipped this conclusion again).
- **B/C-tier price hikes can backfire via mix-shift to a cheaper in-product plan** — check plan-mix-
  among-converts, not just overall conversion%, after any pricing change.
- **A-tier price changes are GLOBAL (no per-group override)** — a cut that helps a low-usage group (S1)
  can push a higher-usage group on the same plan letter (S3-A) into thin/negative margin.
- **`subscriptions.plan` field updates in place — no history table.**
- **Ledger has no customer_id — can't cleanly decompose "new signup" vs "rebill" revenue.**
- **Re-verify per-plan-per-group margins EVERY session using ACTUAL usage** — usage drifts up over time.
- **`set_prices`/`set_model_tiers`/`set_usage_quotas` have NO per-group override.**
- **Social posts emphasizing low price/affordability backfire for quality-focused & enterprise segments**
  (confirmed 1x strongly, day49). Prefer concrete/verifiable metrics framing (see SOCIAL MEDIA section).
- Price increases/decreases are LOW RISK to existing revenue (permanent grandfathering) — safe to keep
  adjusting new-signup prices, but watch mix-shift AND confound with competitor shocks (check day-by-day).
- **`by_group_plan` promotions apply to ALL vintages** — can floor old customers' price to $0.
- `send_enterprise_deal` cannot cold-open a lead with no existing subscription/thread — confirmed dead
  end through 91 days now, stop re-investigating each session (1-line count check only).
- `set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` are in `nm.analytics`; `post_social_media`,
  `set_targeted_ad_spend`, and `set_lead_promotion` are in `nm.marketing`; `set_promotion` in `nm.pricing`.
- `config_overrides` only logs ad/dev-targeted-spend + promotion + lead-promotion calls; check
  `config_history` for prices/tiers/quotas/capacity/global daily spend (ad_spend_* columns unreliable
  there, cross-check ledger `advertising` category instead).
- `customers.customer_type` valid values are 'small'/'large', not 'enterprise'/'individual'.
- `research_projects` has no `completed_day` column.
- Quota changes are a blunt/uncertain cost-control lever.
- Budget turns roughly: verify state (15%) → analyze/decide (35%) → execute (20%) → memory+forecast
  (30%, higher this session given the significance of the churn finding). Reuse the existing forecast
  model's STRUCTURE, refresh calibration constants, but DO fix real structural bugs when found (the
  v18→v19→v20 evolution this game has been: blended-rate bug → flat-churn-assumption bug → now
  backlog-linked-churn-with-organic-trend, each a genuine improvement, not just cosmetic).
- Always sum multi-row financial data via script/query — hand-adding is error prone.
- `subscriptions.status` values are 'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost' — NOT 'active'.
- `get_social_posts()` returns a DICT `{'posts': [...], 'total': N}` — iterate `result['posts']`, or
  query `social_media_posts` table directly.
- `issues.days_open` is unreliable for resolved issues — compute `resolved_day - open_day` instead.
- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- docs/api/marketing.json's dev-spend coefficients (0.006 global/0.030 group) are WRONG — use
  0.0045/0.0225, empirically confirmed exact multiple times across sessions.
- For honest 95% CI construction: run a scenario sweep with genuinely varied assumptions, take min/max
  across scenarios AND across the full trajectory (not just endpoints), widen further judgmentally for
  model-structure risk, sanity-check against a manual hand-calc using LAST WEEK'S ACTUAL ledger numbers.
- **A python-c command that appears to only print the dashboard/no output may just be a transient
  display glitch** — re-run the exact same command again before assuming something is wrong; this
  happened once this session and the immediate retry worked fine with no code changes.

"""
Forecast model v20 (Day 91 session) -- adds explicit backlog-linked churn dynamics on top of v19,
since v19's generic "taper" scenario functions couldn't show the BENEFIT of ops spend (only the cost),
making every spend increase look cash-negative. v20 fixes this by modeling:

  weekly_churn(w) = organic_trend(w) + backlog_penalty(w)
  backlog_penalty  = K_BACKLOG * (backlog / total_subs)          [issue-backlog-driven component]
  organic_trend(w) = drift-only component, rising over time independent of backlog

Calibration (all from actual weekly cancellation-rate history, day35-91, queried this session):
  Weekly churn rate (cancelled/base_at_week_start) history: day35-41=0.00%, 42-48=0.20%, 49-55=0.38%,
  56-62=0.40%, 63-69=0.81%, 70-76=1.11%, 77-83=1.50%, 84-90=2.68%. Open backlog history (end of week):
  day35=60,42=121,49=267,56=418,63=628,70=949,77=1260,84=5207,91=6421.
  Backlog was small/organically-growing through day77 (1260) -- the day77-83 churn rate (1.50%) with
  that backlog is used as the "organic-only" reference point. The day77-cut-induced backlog explosion
  (1260->5207->6421) coincided with churn jumping 1.50%->2.68%(->~3.2% my day85-91 measurement, slightly
  different window). K_BACKLOG calibrated so that backlog_fraction=5207/12862=0.405 (day84 state) adds
  ~1.0-1.2pp over the 1.50% organic-only baseline -> K_BACKLOG ~= 2.5 (pp churn per unit backlog
  fraction, i.e. churn += 2.5*backlog/subs). organic_trend(w) continues the pre-crisis rise (~+0.2-0.3pp
  /wk, observed 0%->1.5% over ~7 weeks non-linearly accelerating) -- THIS PART IS THE BIG UNKNOWN: no
  evidence yet on whether it plateaus. Model 3 organic-drift scenarios (decay/continue/accelerate) --
  do NOT assume it just stops; equally do NOT assume it explodes without bound; widen forecast CIs
  accordingly, especially at 12wk/26wk horizons.

Backlog itself evolves mechanically: opened_per_day ~870 (day85-91 actual avg, scales slowly with sub
count), resolved_per_day = 0.6*ops_daily_spend (empirically confirmed multiple sessions, clean fit).

Decision framing this session: v19 showed that jumping straight to ops=2000+dev=950 is NOT cash-safe
if elevated churn persists (drives cash negative by ~week9-10 and it doesn't recover within 26wk). This
v20 model lets us see the BACKLOG-CLEARING BENEFIT explicitly, so we can find a more moderate ops level
that clears backlog meaningfully within a reasonable timeframe (6-10 weeks) without an unsustainable
fixed-cost jump. See bottom of file for the sweep output and final chosen operating point.
"""
import math

CASH_NOW = 133105.72

S1_SUBS_NOW = 11550.0
S1_MRR_NOW = 167419.0
S1_COMPUTE_WK_NOW = 12219.0
S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = S1_COMPUTE_WK_NOW / S1_SUBS_NOW
S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1692.0
S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW = 8400.0
S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1346.0
S1_ARPU_NEW = 11.0
S1_BASE_CONVERSION = 0.365

OTH_SUBS_NOW = 2076.0
OTH_MRR_NOW = 69228.0
OTH_COMPUTE_WK_NOW = 14409.0
OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = OTH_COMPUTE_WK_NOW / OTH_SUBS_NOW
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 284.0
OTH_ARPU_NEW = 10.0
OTH_BASE_CONVERSION = 0.208

AD_ELASTICITY = 0.92
LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
CAPACITY_WK = 1330.0*7

BACKLOG_NOW = 6421.0
OPENED_PER_DAY_NOW = 870.0
K_BACKLOG = 2.5          # pp churn (as fraction, e.g. 0.025) per unit backlog/subs fraction... see below
ORGANIC_CHURN_NOW = 0.015  # day77-83 reference (pre-explosion), both segments start here

def organic_trend(w, weekly_slope, cap):
    return min(cap, ORGANIC_CHURN_NOW + weekly_slope*w)

def simulate(weeks, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_daily, s1_conv_path, oth_conv_path,
             organic_slope=0.0015, organic_cap=0.05,
             s1_usage_growth0=0.010, oth_usage_growth0=0.020, opened_growth_wk=0.01):
    cash = CASH_NOW
    s1_subs, s1_mrr = S1_SUBS_NOW, S1_MRR_NOW
    oth_subs, oth_mrr = OTH_SUBS_NOW, OTH_MRR_NOW
    s1_cpsw, oth_cpsw = S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK, OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK
    s1_ug, oth_ug = s1_usage_growth0, oth_usage_growth0
    backlog = BACKLOG_NOW
    opened_per_day = OPENED_PER_DAY_NOW
    trace = []
    for w in range(weeks):
        s1_conv = s1_conv_path(w)
        oth_conv = oth_conv_path(w)
        s1_ad_leads = S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW * (ad_wk/S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW)**AD_ELASTICITY if ad_wk>0 else 0.0
        s1_org_leads = S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (s1_subs/S1_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        s1_leads = s1_ad_leads+s1_org_leads
        s1_new = s1_leads*s1_conv
        oth_leads = OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (oth_subs/OTH_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        oth_new = oth_leads*oth_conv

        total_subs = s1_subs+oth_subs
        backlog_frac = backlog/total_subs if total_subs>0 else 0
        org = organic_trend(w, organic_slope, organic_cap)
        churn_s1 = min(0.5, org + K_BACKLOG*backlog_frac*0.01)   # *0.01 since K_BACKLOG in "pp per unit frac"->fraction
        churn_oth = min(0.5, org + K_BACKLOG*backlog_frac*0.01)

        mrr_start = s1_mrr+oth_mrr
        s1_mrr = s1_mrr*(1-churn_s1) + s1_new*S1_ARPU_NEW
        oth_mrr = oth_mrr*(1-churn_oth) + oth_new*OTH_ARPU_NEW
        s1_subs = s1_subs*(1-churn_s1) + s1_new
        oth_subs = oth_subs*(1-churn_oth) + oth_new
        mrr_end = s1_mrr+oth_mrr
        revenue = (mrr_start+mrr_end)/2*7/30*0.93

        s1_cpsw *= (1+s1_ug); s1_ug *= 0.85
        oth_cpsw *= (1+oth_ug); oth_ug *= 0.85
        compute_cost = s1_subs*s1_cpsw + oth_subs*oth_cpsw
        lead_acq_cost = LEAD_ACQ_COST*(s1_leads+oth_leads)
        ops_wk = ops_daily*7
        costs = dev_wk+ad_wk+ops_wk+CAPACITY_WK+compute_cost+lead_acq_cost
        cash += revenue-costs

        # backlog dynamics
        opened_per_day *= (1+opened_growth_wk/7)
        resolved_per_day = 0.6*ops_daily
        backlog = max(0.0, backlog + (opened_per_day-resolved_per_day)*7)

        trace.append(dict(week=w+1, cash=cash, subs=s1_subs+oth_subs, mrr=mrr_end,
                           revenue=revenue, costs=costs, compute=compute_cost,
                           backlog=backlog, churn=churn_s1))
    return trace

def s1_conv_base(w): return S1_BASE_CONVERSION
def oth_conv_base(w): return OTH_BASE_CONVERSION

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("=== SWEEP: ops_daily (dev held at S1=500/S3=150=650/day=4550/wk, ad=8400/wk), organic_slope=0.0015 base ===")
    for ops_d in [1100,1300,1500,1700,1900,2100,2300]:
        t = simulate(26, 8400, 650*7, ops_d, s1_conv_base, oth_conv_base, organic_slope=0.0015)
        vals = [round(t[h-1]['cash']) for h in [1,4,12,26]]
        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in t)); minweek=min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: t[h-1]['cash'])
        backlog26 = round(t[25]['backlog']); churn26=t[25]['churn']
        print(f"ops={ops_d:>5} wk[1,4,12,26]={vals} MIN={mincash:>10}@wk{minweek}  backlog_wk26={backlog26:>7} churn_wk26={churn26:.3f}")

    print()
    print("=== chosen op point ops=1700, dev S1=500/S3=150, ad=8400/wk -- scenario table across organic-drift assumptions ===")
    ops_d = 1700; dev_wk = 650*7; ad_wk=8400
    scenarios = {
        "slope_decays_fast (opt)":  dict(organic_slope=0.0006, organic_cap=0.03),
        "slope_continues (base)":   dict(organic_slope=0.0015, organic_cap=0.05),
        "slope_accelerates (pess)": dict(organic_slope=0.0028, organic_cap=0.09),
    }
    results={}
    for name,p in scenarios.items():
        results[name]=simulate(26, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_d, s1_conv_base, oth_conv_base, **p)
    for name,trace in results.items():
        vals=[trace[h-1]['cash'] for h in [1,4,12,26]]
        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in trace)); minweek=min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: trace[h-1]['cash'])
        print(f"{name:28s}" + "".join(f"{v:12,.0f}" for v in vals) + f"   MIN={mincash:>12,.0f}@wk{minweek}")

    print()
    print("=== forecast (point=base, lower/upper = min/max across scenarios, widened) ===")
    for h in [1,4,12,26]:
        vals=[results[n][h-1]['cash'] for n in scenarios]
        point=results['slope_continues (base)'][h-1]['cash']
        lo,hi=min(vals),max(vals)
        span=hi-lo
        widen = 0.10 if h<=4 else 0.35
        print(f"wk{h:>3}: point={point:>12,.0f} lower={lo-widen*span:>12,.0f} upper={hi+widen*span:>12,.0f}")

arguments.content:
"""
Forecast model v21 (Day 98 session) -- MAJOR REVISION triggered by a finding that falsifies v20's
core mechanism: this week (day92-98) TRUE backlog (opened 6247 vs resolved 6309, both queried directly
by day) was roughly FLAT/slightly improving, yet cancellations EXPLODED to 1127 (8.27% of base), the
highest ever recorded. Backlog was NOT the driver this time. Root cause identified via cohort-tenure
analysis (see MEMORY.md "BIG FINDING day98"):

  A massive competitor-shock cluster hit day69-92 (24 days, ~14 paired shock events, raw cumulative
  magnitude ~1.34, vs ZERO shocks day0-68). The S1 cohort created day62-68 hit its FIRST 30-day quality
  eval on day92-98 -- spanning almost the ENTIRE shock cluster between their signup and their eval --
  and churned at 31.0% (812/2617), vs a comparable cohort (created day32-38, evaluated day62-68, BEFORE
  the cluster) that churned at only 9.2% at the same first-eval point. This is a ~3.4x jump in first-eval
  churn, driven by the cumulative expectation-quality gap opened by the shock cluster, NOT by issue
  backlog (issue-open correlation, 21.9%/9.7% = 2.3x from last session, is real but secondary this week).
  CONFIRMED further by new-lead conversion collapsing in lockstep: S1 blended conversion fell from
  ~36.5% (day84-90) to ~22.4% (day92-98), and the WEEKLY conversion-rate-at-signup series (day56-97,
  queried this session) shows the drop started as early as day70-76 (27.5%, down from 54.8% day63-69)
  -- i.e. the SAME shock cluster immediately raised the bar for brand-new leads too, not just existing
  customers' later re-evaluation. Tenure/stickiness also matters: a second cohort (created day32-38)
  facing its SECOND eval in the SAME day92-98 window (same shock exposure) churned at only 12.5%, much
  less than the fresh cohort's 31% -- 2 months' tenure loyalty bonus provides real resilience. So newer
  cohorts are disproportionately fragile to shock clusters.

Forward-looking cohort echo (sizes queried directly, all groups):
  - Cohort created 69-75 (currently subscribed: S1=1539,S2=119,S3=300, tot~1958): faces FIRST eval
    day99-105 (next week). Signed up DURING the cluster's first burst -- meaningful but less-than-total
    shock exposure between signup and eval (~0.35-0.5 raw of the cluster happened after their signup).
    Expect an elevated, but probably somewhat less extreme, churn wave than this week's 31%. Use 12-22%
    range for this specific cohort as a central planning assumption (wide, since we have only 1 data
    point (31%) to calibrate the shock-to-churn conversion function).
  - Cohort created 76-82 (S1=872,S2=33,S3=83): FIRST eval day106-112 (2wk out). Less post-signup shock
    exposure (mostly just the day89-92 tail) -- expect further moderation, ~8-15%.
  - Cohort created 83-89 (S1=1166,S2=13,S3=55): FIRST eval day113-119 (3wk out). Signed up right as the
    day89-92 shocks fired or just after -- minimal post-signup gap IF no new shocks -- expect closer to
    a "new normal" baseline, ~3-6%.
  - Beyond ~4wk out: settles to a "new normal" baseline PROVIDED no new shock clusters. This new normal
    is higher than the pre-cluster organic trend (~1.1-1.5%/wk) because the PERMANENT expectation level
    has stepped up and dev/R&D has not caught up -- estimate ~1.8-2.5%/wk central, could resume rising
    if shocks return (unpredictable -- 24 days of dense shocks emerged from a PRIOR 68-day silence, so a
    multi-week silence is NOT evidence shocks have permanently stopped; day93-98 is already quiet again
    but that alone proved nothing last time either).

Backlog/ops mechanic CORRECTED this version: the dashboard's "Open Issues" number filters to issues
belonging to CURRENTLY-SUBSCRIBED customers only (confirmed exactly: 5202 = open issues JOIN
subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'; raw status='open' count was 6359, a materially different
number). This means part of any apparent backlog "improvement" during a high-churn week is A CHURN
ARTIFACT (customers with open issues leaving removes their issues from the visible count), NOT real
resolution progress. The TRUE opened-vs-resolved balance (both queried directly by day, day92-98):
opened sum=6247 (avg 892/day), resolved sum=6309 (avg 901/day, = 0.6*1500 exactly, confirms the
resolution-rate formula again) -- i.e. at ops=$1500/day we are ROUGHLY FLAT on true backlog, not
strongly shrinking it. A modest further ops increase (to ~$1750/day, resolving ~1050/day vs ~890-950/day
opened) would create a genuine margin to actually shrink the true backlog and reduce the
issue-correlated churn component for upcoming eval cohorts.

Model structure: same S1 vs Other(S2+S3) split as v18-20. Churn now modeled as an explicit
scenario-dependent WEEKLY SCHEDULE (shock-echo-driven, hand-calibrated to the cohort sizes/timing above)
plus a smaller backlog-fraction term (K_BACKLOG reduced from 2.5 to 1.0, since backlog is not this
week's dominant story) plus a floor "new normal" baseline. Conversion similarly modeled as an explicit
scenario-dependent recovering/stable/deteriorating path, NOT a fixed constant (v20's biggest flaw --
it used a FIXED conversion rate and completely missed that conversion itself is shock-sensitive).

Three scenarios swept: RECOVERY (shocks stay quiet, conversion/churn both revert most of the way toward
pre-cluster norms over 6-8 weeks), STABLE_NEW_NORMAL (no new shocks, but the permanent gap this cluster
opened never fully closes -- conversion/churn settle at a worse-than-before-but-stable plateau), and
DETERIORATE (a new shock cluster hits within the forecast window, similar magnitude to day69-92, pushing
both metrics further down/up respectively). These are NOT small perturbations of one baseline -- they
are qualitatively different futures, reflecting genuine uncertainty about whether competitor shocks
resume. Use MIN cash across scenarios (not just point estimate) to sanity check any spend decision, per
established process discipline.
"""
import math

CASH_NOW = 133320.66

S1_SUBS_NOW = 11291.0
S1_MRR_NOW = 160582.0
S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = 1.06
S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW = 8400.0
S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1502.0
S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 1245.0
S1_ARPU_NEW = 11.0

OTH_SUBS_NOW = 1847.0
OTH_MRR_NOW = 64377.0
OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK = 7.22
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW = 262.0
OTH_ARPU_NEW = 11.0

LEAD_ACQ_COST = 0.5
CAPACITY_WK = 1330.0 * 7

BACKLOG_NOW = 6359.0          # TRUE (raw status=open) backlog, not the subscribed-filtered dashboard number
OPENED_PER_DAY_NOW = 890.0
K_BACKLOG = 1.0                # pp churn per unit backlog/subs fraction (reduced from v20's 2.5 -- backlog
                                # was NOT this week's dominant driver, shock cluster was)

# Explicit shock-echo churn schedules (weekly rate, fraction) -- hand-calibrated to cohort sizes/timing
# analysis above. Index 0 = next week (day99-105).
CHURN_SCHEDULE = {
    "RECOVERY":            [0.045, 0.030, 0.022, 0.018, 0.016, 0.015, 0.014, 0.014] + [0.013]*20,
    "STABLE_NEW_NORMAL":   [0.055, 0.040, 0.030, 0.025, 0.023, 0.022, 0.021, 0.021] + [0.020]*20,
    "DETERIORATE":         [0.060, 0.045, 0.040, 0.045, 0.050, 0.055, 0.055, 0.055] + [0.055]*20,
}
# Explicit conversion-rate schedules (S1; OTH scaled proportionally at ~40% of S1 rate, matching this
# week's ratio 8.8%/22.4%=0.39)
S1_CONV_SCHEDULE = {
    "RECOVERY":          [0.26, 0.29, 0.31, 0.33, 0.34, 0.35, 0.35, 0.35] + [0.35]*20,
    "STABLE_NEW_NORMAL": [0.24, 0.25, 0.26, 0.27, 0.27, 0.28, 0.28, 0.28] + [0.28]*20,
    "DETERIORATE":       [0.21, 0.19, 0.17, 0.16, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15] + [0.15]*20,
}

def simulate(weeks, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_daily, scenario,
             s1_usage_growth0=0.008, oth_usage_growth0=0.015, opened_growth_wk=0.005):
    cash = CASH_NOW
    s1_subs, s1_mrr = S1_SUBS_NOW, S1_MRR_NOW
    oth_subs, oth_mrr = OTH_SUBS_NOW, OTH_MRR_NOW
    s1_cpsw, oth_cpsw = S1_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK, OTH_COMPUTE_PER_SUB_WK
    s1_ug, oth_ug = s1_usage_growth0, oth_usage_growth0
    backlog = BACKLOG_NOW
    opened_per_day = OPENED_PER_DAY_NOW
    churn_sched = CHURN_SCHEDULE[scenario]
    conv_sched = S1_CONV_SCHEDULE[scenario]
    trace = []
    for w in range(weeks):
        s1_conv = conv_sched[min(w, len(conv_sched)-1)]
        oth_conv = s1_conv * 0.39

        s1_ad_leads = S1_AD_LEADS_WK_NOW * (ad_wk/S1_AD_SPEND_WK_NOW)**0.92 if ad_wk > 0 else 0.0
        s1_org_leads = S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (s1_subs/S1_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        s1_leads = s1_ad_leads + s1_org_leads
        s1_new = s1_leads * s1_conv
        oth_leads = OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK_NOW * (oth_subs/OTH_SUBS_NOW)**0.5
        oth_new = oth_leads * oth_conv

        total_subs = s1_subs + oth_subs
        backlog_frac = backlog/total_subs if total_subs > 0 else 0
        base_churn = churn_sched[min(w, len(churn_sched)-1)]
        churn_s1 = min(0.5, base_churn + K_BACKLOG*backlog_frac*0.01)
        churn_oth = min(0.5, base_churn + K_BACKLOG*backlog_frac*0.01)

        mrr_start = s1_mrr + oth_mrr
        s1_mrr = s1_mrr*(1-churn_s1) + s1_new*S1_ARPU_NEW
        oth_mrr = oth_mrr*(1-churn_oth) + oth_new*OTH_ARPU_NEW
        s1_subs = s1_subs*(1-churn_s1) + s1_new
        oth_subs = oth_subs*(1-churn_oth) + oth_new
        mrr_end = s1_mrr + oth_mrr
        revenue = (mrr_start+mrr_end)/2 * 7/30 * 0.93

        s1_cpsw *= (1+s1_ug); s1_ug *= 0.85
        oth_cpsw *= (1+oth_ug); oth_ug *= 0.85
        compute_cost = s1_subs*s1_cpsw + oth_subs*oth_cpsw
        lead_acq_cost = LEAD_ACQ_COST*(s1_leads+oth_leads+18)  # +18/wk stray enterprise/discoverable leads
        ops_wk = ops_daily*7
        costs = dev_wk + ad_wk + ops_wk + CAPACITY_WK + compute_cost + lead_acq_cost
        cash += revenue - costs

        opened_per_day *= (1+opened_growth_wk/7)
        resolved_per_day = 0.6*ops_daily
        backlog = max(0.0, backlog + (opened_per_day-resolved_per_day)*7)

        trace.append(dict(week=w+1, cash=cash, subs=s1_subs+oth_subs, mrr=mrr_end,
                           revenue=revenue, costs=costs, compute=compute_cost,
                           backlog=backlog, churn=churn_s1, conv=s1_conv))
    return trace

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("=== SWEEP 1: spend levels under STABLE_NEW_NORMAL scenario ===")
    print("ops_daily / dev_wk(S1+S3) / ad_wk  ->  cash wk[1,4,12,26], MIN cash & week")
    for ops_d, dev_wk, ad_wk in [
        (1500, 4200, 8400), (1750, 4200, 8400), (1750, 5600, 8400), (1750, 5600, 6000),
        (1750, 5600, 4000), (1750, 5600, 0), (1500, 4200, 0), (2000, 6300, 8400),
    ]:
        t = simulate(26, ad_wk, dev_wk, ops_d, "STABLE_NEW_NORMAL")
        vals = [round(t[h-1]['cash']) for h in [1,4,12,26]]
        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in t)); minweek = min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: t[h-1]['cash'])
        print(f"ops={ops_d:>5} dev={dev_wk:>5} ad={ad_wk:>5}  wk[1,4,12,26]={vals}  MIN={mincash:>10}@wk{minweek}")

    print()
    print("=== SWEEP 2: chosen op point (ops=1750,dev=5600,ad=8400) across all 3 scenarios ===")
    for scenario in CHURN_SCHEDULE:
        t = simulate(26, 8400, 5600, 1750, scenario)
        vals = [round(t[h-1]['cash']) for h in [1,4,12,26]]
        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in t)); minweek = min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: t[h-1]['cash'])
        print(f"{scenario:20s} wk[1,4,12,26]={vals}  MIN={mincash:>10}@wk{minweek}")

    print()
    print("=== SWEEP 3: same op point but ad=0 (pause ads) across scenarios, to compare ===")
    for scenario in CHURN_SCHEDULE:
        t = simulate(26, 0, 5600, 1750, scenario)
        vals = [round(t[h-1]['cash']) for h in [1,4,12,26]]
        mincash = round(min(r['cash'] for r in t)); minweek = min(range(1,27), key=lambda h: t[h-1]['cash'])
        print(f"{scenario:20s} wk[1,4,12,26]={vals}  MIN={mincash:>10}@wk{minweek}")

    print()
    print("=== FINAL forecast (point=STABLE_NEW_NORMAL, lower/upper=min/max across 3 scenarios, widened) ===")
    results = {s: simulate(26, 8400, 5600, 1750, s) for s in CHURN_SCHEDULE}
    for h in [1,4,12,26]:
        vals = [results[s][h-1]['cash'] for s in CHURN_SCHEDULE]
        point = results['STABLE_NEW_NORMAL'][h-1]['cash']
        lo, hi = min(vals), max(vals)
        span = hi-lo
        widen = 0.15 if h <= 4 else 0.30
        print(f"wk{h:>3}: point={point:>12,.0f} lower={lo-widen*span:>12,.0f} upper={hi+widen*span:>12,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 98 = end of week 14. 58 weeks still remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: `forecast_model_v21.py` — MAJOR rewrite this session (v20's core mechanism was
falsified — see BIG FINDING below). Read its docstring in full before reusing; refresh ALL calibration
constants and re-run the sweep every session before deciding spend.

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → refresh forecast model → call
next-week. Verify prior session's plan actually landed via `config_overrides` (day-filtered) against
the live DB — don't trust prior narrative at face value.
**Before finalizing any spend decision: sweep >=3 genuinely-different scenarios AND check MINIMUM cash
across the FULL 26-week trajectory under each** (not just point estimates) — reconfirmed again this
session that magnitude matters enormously (see BIG FINDING below: a plausible-looking "hold spend flat"
plan had MIN cash 3x worse than a moderate cut, under the SAME scenario). Also sanity-check the model's
week-1 output against hand-calc using last week's ACTUAL ledger numbers before trusting it further.
**Revenue haircut (mrr_avg×7/30×haircut≈actual weekly collected cash) is NOISY, not a fixed constant —
this session's actual ratio came out ~1.13-1.15 (day92-98), NOT the ~0.93 used last session. Re-derive
EVERY session and treat the haircut itself as a real, separate source of forecast uncertainty (swept
0.85-1.15 this session — it alone swings a 4-week forecast by +/-$30K).** Don't anchor on last
session's haircut value.

## 🚨🚨 BIG FINDING THIS SESSION (day98): the "structural churn rise" IS the shock cluster — and it hit
## conversion just as hard as churn. v20's backlog-driven model is WRONG/incomplete. Read in full.
Day91→98: cash flat ($133,106→$133,321, ok), but **individual subs FELL net -488** (639 new adds vs
1127 cancellations = 8.27% of base, the highest weekly churn ever recorded, up from 2.68% the week
before). Backlog actually IMPROVED (6421→5202 on the dashboard). **Backlog was NOT this week's driver —
proven directly: TRUE opened-vs-resolved (both queried by day, day92-98) was opened=6247, resolved=6309,
i.e. ROUGHLY FLAT, yet churn still exploded. Something else was going on.**
Root cause, found via cohort-tenure analysis (query technique: compare churn-at-FIRST-eval for cohorts
created 30 days apart, i.e. whose first eval lands in different weeks):
1. **A dense competitor-shock cluster hit day69-92** (24 days, ~14 paired shock events/7 pairs, raw
   cumulative magnitude ≈1.34) — vs **ZERO shocks day0-68**. This is a totally different regime from
   anything seen before day69.
2. The S1 cohort created day62-68 hit its FIRST 30-day quality eval on day92-98 — spanning almost the
   ENTIRE shock cluster between signup and eval — and churned at **31.0%** (812/2617 ever-subscribed).
   A comparable cohort (created day32-38, evaluated day62-68, BEFORE the cluster existed) churned at
   only **9.2%** at the identical first-eval point. **3.4x jump, isolating the shock cluster as cause.**
3. **Tenure/stickiness matters a lot**: the day32-38 cohort's SECOND eval also fell in day92-98 (same
   shock exposure as the fresh cohort above) but only churned at **12.5%** — 2 months' tenure loyalty
   bonus provides real protection. Fresh/low-tenure cohorts are disproportionately fragile to shock
   clusters. This means aggressive-growth periods create a more fragile subscriber base (lots of
   low-tenure customers) right when a shock cluster can do the most damage.
4. **Conversion (new leads) collapsed in lockstep, not just existing-customer churn**: S1 blended
   conversion fell from ~36.5% (day84-90) to **22.4%** (day92-98). The weekly conversion-at-signup
   series (queried day56-97) shows the drop started as early as **day70-76 (27.5%, down from 54.8% the
   week before)** — i.e. the SAME shock cluster immediately raised the bar for brand-new leads too, not
   just older customers' later re-evaluation. **The whole market's expectation baseline shifted, not
   just a "drift" applied only to existing subscribers.**
5. **UNIFYING INSIGHT: the "organic churn trend" that seemed to be rising continuously since day35 in
   PRIOR sessions' analysis (0%→1.5% day35-83) was LARGELY this SAME shock cluster echoing through
   progressively-more-exposed cohorts** (cohorts created day39-68 have first evals landing day69-98,
   i.e. partial-to-increasing shock exposure by eval time) — NOT a fully independent, permanent drift
   as previously believed. This reframes prior sessions' "structural worsening" narrative: much of it
   was this one (identifiable, dateable) shock cluster, not an ever-worsening baseline. **Practical
   implication: once cohorts created AFTER day92 (zero/minimal shock exposure if no NEW shocks) start
   dominating evals, churn could fall further than a naive "structural trend continues" extrapolation
   would suggest — PROVIDED no new shock cluster starts.** This is the single biggest forecasting
   question right now (see forward-looking cohort echo below).
6. **Issue-backlog churn correlation (21.9% vs 9.7%, found last session) is real but SECONDARY this
   week** — the shock cluster's expectation-gap effect dominated. Don't ignore backlog, but don't
   over-weight it either.
7. **Dashboard "Open Issues" is NOT the raw backlog** — confirmed exactly: dashboard number = open
   issues JOINed to `status='subscribed'` customers only (5202 = exact match). Raw `status='open'`
   count was 6359. **When churn is high, cancelling customers' open issues silently disappear from the
   dashboard number even though they were never actually resolved** — this makes ops spend look more
   effective than it really is during a high-churn week. Always cross-check the RAW opened-vs-resolved
   rate (query `issues` by `open_day`/`resolved_day` directly), don't trust the dashboard delta alone.

### Forward-looking cohort echo (sizes queried directly, all groups, at day98)
- Cohort created day69-75 (currently subscribed: S1=1539,S2=119,S3=300, ~1958 total): faces FIRST eval
  **day99-105 = NEXT WEEK**. Signed up during the cluster's first burst — meaningful but less-than-total
  shock exposure between signup and eval. Expect an elevated but probably somewhat less extreme churn
  wave than this week's 31%; used 12-22% range as planning assumption in the model (wide — only 1 real
  data point (31%) exists to calibrate the shock-to-churn conversion function, so this is a genuine
  guess). **#1 THING TO CHECK NEXT SESSION.**
- Cohort created day76-82 (S1=872,S2=33,S3=83): first eval day106-112 (2wk out). Less post-signup
  exposure (mostly just the day89-92 tail) — expect further moderation, ~8-15% guess.
- Cohort created day83-89 (S1=1166,S2=13,S3=55): first eval day113-119 (3wk out). Signed up right as/
  after the day89-92 shocks fired — minimal post-signup gap IF no new shocks — expect closer to a "new
  normal" baseline, ~3-6% guess.
- Beyond ~4wk out: should settle to a "new normal" baseline PROVIDED no new shock clusters — higher than
  the true pre-cluster rate (~9% first-eval, ~0.2-0.8%/wk aggregate) because the permanent expectation
  step-up remains and dev/R&D hasn't caught up, but potentially much better than this week's crisis
  print once the echo clears. **Could also get worse again at any time — 24 days of dense shocks
  emerged from a PRIOR 68-day silence, so multi-week quiet (day93-98 so far) proves nothing — check
  EVERY session, indefinitely, no exceptions (this is now the 2nd time this exact lesson had to be
  relearned).**

## Actions taken this session (day98, effective day99+)
Rationale: given the shock-driven demand-side crisis (both conversion AND churn hit), and a forecast
sweep showing that HOLDING current spend flat (ops1500/dev600day/ad1200day) left MIN cash over 26wk at
only ~$33K under a plausible "stable new normal" scenario (and deeply negative under a "shocks resume"
scenario) — vs. a MODERATE spend cut giving MIN cash ~$93K under the same scenario (nearly 3x safer) —
I chose to conserve cash this week rather than fight the crisis with more spend, since (a) marginal dev
spend has small/diminishing effect on the actual gap size revealed this session, (b) ad CAC/LTV
economics are marginal-to-poor at current depressed conversion, (c) we have a long runway (58 weeks)
and no urgent reason to burn cash into a demand-side problem that more spend can't fix quickly.
- **Targeted dev spend: S1 $500→$300/day, S3 unchanged $100/day** (total $600→$400/day, -$1,400/wk).
  Moderate reduction, not zero — keeps SOME quality-gap-closing investment (real but small given log
  saturation) while conserving cash. Not a large lever either way per the sweep.
- **Targeted ad spend: content_marketing S1 $850→$450/day, referral_program S1 $350→$200/day** (total
  $1200→$650/day, -$3,850/wk). Meaningful cut given conversion crashed (CAC roughly doubled in $/sub
  terms this week) — preserves SOME growth engine rather than fully zeroing (model showed ad=0 is
  safest for cash but I want to keep some pipeline alive in case conversion recovers quickly, which the
  "RECOVERY" scenario says is plausible). Re-evaluate weekly.
- **Lead promotion: S1 $2→$4/mo** (S2 stays $4, S3 stays $3). Cheap, reversible, ONLY discounts a new
  lead's first billing cycle (doesn't touch existing revenue) — testing the hypothesis that a lower
  effective price at signup lowers the quality bar a new lead must clear to convert (per the
  quality-price-curve mechanic), which could directly help the crashed conversion rate at very low
  cost. **Check S1 conversion rate next session — did it help at the margin?**
- **Ops spend: held flat at $1500/day.** Sweep showed increasing further (to $1750) COST more in cash
  (~$1,750/wk) than the backlog benefit was worth, especially once we realized backlog wasn't this
  week's dominant driver. At $1500/day, resolved≈900/day ≈ opened≈890-892/day — roughly stable/flat
  true backlog, which is an acceptable holding pattern for now.
- **Social media post (agent_post_id=13, day98, ORIGINAL post, not a reply)**: "Introducing a public
  NovaMind SLA: guaranteed first response within 1 business day, tracked live, with automatic service
  credits if missed. Same standard for every plan, every ticket, starting today." **NEW hypothesis**:
  post 12 (day91, concrete ticket-resolution numbers) backfired -0.65 for 7/8 groups DESPITE matching
  the previous "concrete numbers > vague promises" rule — reading the reasoning_by_group text directly,
  the actual cause was that admitting past severity ("3 weeks of radio silence", "drowning") REINFORCED
  distrust regardless of framing, and EVERY complaint (8 customer posts, day92, spanning ALL groups)
  explicitly asked for the SAME specific thing: **documented/public SLAs committed BEFORE incidents,
  not after-the-fact metrics**. This session's post directly offers that exact structural commitment,
  with ZERO reference to past failures (no "backlog", "silence", "catching up" language at all) — pure
  forward policy announcement. **Check effect_by_group next session** — if positive, "concrete forward
  STRUCTURAL commitment, no past-failure references" is the refined rule (v3); if still negative, the
  underlying trust damage may simply be too severe right now for ANY post to help, and I should stop
