## CONFIRMED MECHANICS (check docs/api/*.json FIRST before re-deriving — saves turns)
- **Dashboard "Open Issues" = open issues for CURRENTLY-SUBSCRIBED customers only** (exact match
  confirmed: `JOIN subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'`). Raw `status='open'` count (no join) is a
  DIFFERENT, usually larger number. During high-churn weeks the dashboard number can drop sharply
  WITHOUT real resolution progress, just because departing customers' issues fall out of the filter.
  Always track the RAW opened-per-day vs resolved-per-day (`issues.open_day`/`resolved_day`, grouped by
  day) as the ground truth for whether ops spend is actually keeping up.
- **Revenue-to-MRR haircut is NOISY, re-derive every session, do not reuse last session's value.**
  Formula `(mrr_start+mrr_end)/2 × 7/30 × haircut ≈ actual weekly collected cash`; haircut has ranged
  ~0.67-1.15 across sessions historically (confirmed again this session: came out ~1.13-1.15 day92-98,
  vs ~0.93 used last session) — treat as a real, separate uncertainty axis in forecasts (swept
  0.85-1.15 this session), not a fixed constant.
- **Billing/quality re-evaluation happens EXACTLY every 30 days per customer** (cancellations only ever
  at tenure=30,60,90...). Use cohort `created_day` windows (`c.created_day BETWEEN X AND X+6`) to
  measure churn-at-Nth-eval directly — this is the highest-value diagnostic technique found so far for
  understanding WHY churn moved, far better than aggregate weekly rates alone.
- **Competitor shocks arrive in unpredictable CLUSTERS separated by long silences, not a steady drip.**
  Confirmed: 0 shocks day0-68, dense cluster day69-92 (~14 events, cumulative raw ~1.34), quiet again
  day93-98 (so far). A multi-week quiet period is NOT evidence a cluster has permanently ended — it
  wasn't last time either (a "confirmed tapering" call 2 sessions ago was wrong within days). Check
  EVERY session via: `SELECT day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE (content LIKE '%quality boost%'
  OR content LIKE '%quality bump%' OR content LIKE '%quality improvement%') AND day > <last_checked>`.
  **Shocks affect BOTH existing-customer re-eval AND brand-new-lead conversion simultaneously** (the
  market's current expectation baseline, not just a per-customer drift) — check conversion-rate trend,
  not just churn, whenever investigating a shock's impact.
- **Tenure loyalty materially protects against shocks**: a 2-months-tenure cohort facing the identical
  shock exposure as a fresh (1 month) cohort churned at 2.5x LOWER rate (12.5% vs 31%) at their
  respective evals. Rapid-growth periods create a more shock-fragile subscriber base (more low-tenure
  customers) — worth remembering when deciding how aggressively to pursue growth vs. quality investment.
- **Ops-spend → issue-resolution-capacity: resolution_capacity_per_day ≈ 0.6 × ops_spend_per_day**
  (re-confirmed AGAIN this session, day92-98 at ops=$1500: resolved avg 901/day, 0.6×1500=900, exact).
  This formula has now held across many sessions at many different spend levels — treat as solid.
- **Unresolved issues at time of billing eval correlate with churn (21.9% vs 9.7%, 2.3x, from last
  session's cohort measurement)** — real but was SECONDARY to the shock-cluster effect this session.
  Both drivers operate simultaneously; don't attribute all churn swings to just one or the other —
  always check shock-cluster timing (via cohort-tenure + social-post-shock-date cross-reference) AND
  backlog/issue correlation before concluding which one dominated a given week.
- **PRICE GRANDFATHERING IS PERMANENT** — `set_prices` only affects future signups, existing subs keep
  signup-day listed_price forever. New prices take effect IMMEDIATELY for that week's new signups. This
  means a price change is a CLEAN, isolated lever for new-signup conversion only — it does NOT affect
  existing-customer churn decisions at all (their eval uses their own grandfathered effective_price).
- **`set_prices`/`set_model_tiers`/`set_usage_quotas` are GLOBAL per plan letter (A/B/C) — no per-group
  override exists.** A model-tier upgrade for plan A (e.g. T2→T3) would be a HUGE quality jump
  (multiplicative on the whole (base+bonus) bracket, e.g. S1-A would jump from 0.389→0.467, more than
  months of dev spend) but is NOT worth it currently — S3-A's usage (245/day) means the SAME tier
  upgrade would add ~$30/mo compute cost per S3-A customer (~$33K/mo in aggregate for 1107 subs),
  swamping any benefit. Blanket tier changes must always be checked against the HIGHEST-usage group
  sharing that plan letter, not just the group you're trying to help.
- **`by_group_plan` promotion applies to ALL vintages of that group+plan — not just new signups.** Never
  set one ≥ old listed price for a plan with legacy subs still on it (floors at $0).
  **`set_lead_promotion` is DIFFERENT and safer**: only discounts the FIRST billing period for NEW
  leads, doesn't touch existing subscriber revenue — cheap/reversible lever for testing conversion
  sensitivity to effective price, used this session to hedge the conversion crash at low cost.
- **`subscriptions.plan` field UPDATES IN PLACE on upgrade/downgrade — no history table.**
- Dev quality formula: 0.0045×ln(1+global_spend/5000) global / 0.0225×ln(1+targeted_spend/5000) per-
  group (5× coefficient) — empirically confirmed exact multiple times, applied DAILY, ACCUMULATES into
  a PERMANENT stock. To meaningfully offset a shock-cluster-sized gap (~0.3+ raw for a sensitive group)
  via dev spend alone requires spend in the thousands/day sustained for weeks — expensive, log-limited;
  R&D tiers are the only lever that can deliver comparably-sized jumps, but cost far more upfront.
- **`send_enterprise_deal` CANNOT cold-open a brand-new lead with no subscription/thread.** Confirmed
  dead end through 98 days, 735 enterprise customer rows, 0 threads ever.
- **`config_overrides.settings_json` is a FULL SNAPSHOT after each call** — always resend every group/

- Billing: ledger shows subscription payments happening roughly DAILY. No customer_id column on ledger.
- **No multi-row subscription history per customer** — `subscriptions` has ONE row per customer.
- Compute cost = model_tier_cost_per_unit × ACTUAL metered usage (`daily_usage`, join via customer_id).

```python

FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 2. Compute cost -- actual usage, split by group/plan:
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, AVG(du.usage_units) as avg_usage, COUNT(DISTINCT du.customer_id) as cnt
FROM daily_usage du JOIN customers c ON du.customer_id=c.customer_id JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE du.day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 3. Ad leads + CPL by channel/group, and organic/network leads:

JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi>

## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **NEW (day98): a plausible-sounding mechanistic model (v20's backlog-driven churn) can be cleanly
  FALSIFIED by a single week's data (backlog flat, churn exploded anyway) — when that happens, don't
  patch the old model, rebuild around the NEW causal story (shock-cluster-driven, confirmed via
  cohort-tenure analysis) and say so explicitly. Re-deriving cause from first principles (cohort tenure
  queries) beats pattern-matching to the previous session's explanation.**
- **NEW (day98): dashboard metrics can be filtered/derived in ways that create misleading trends during
  volatile periods** — "Open Issues" dropping doesn't necessarily mean ops spend is winning; it can
  partly reflect churned customers' issues dropping out of a status-filtered count. Always find the RAW
  underlying table computation and compare it to the dashboard number before trusting a trend.
- **NEW (day98): competitor shocks hit NEW-LEAD CONVERSION exactly as hard as EXISTING-CUSTOMER CHURN,
  simultaneously** — both are driven by the same underlying "market expectation baseline" mechanic. When
  investigating a shock's impact, always check the conversion-rate-by-week series, not just churn.
- **NEW (day98): tenure/loyalty materially protects against shocks (2.5x churn difference between 1mo
  and 2mo tenure facing the identical shock exposure)** — a fast-growing, low-average-tenure subscriber
  base is MORE fragile to a sudden shock cluster than a slower-growing, more-seasoned one. Consider this
  a real (if hard to act on precisely) risk factor of aggressive growth-phase spending.
- **NEW (day98): revenue/MRR "haircut" is genuinely noisy (0.67-1.15 range across sessions), not a

arguments.content:
"""
forecast_model_v22.py -- Day 105 MAJOR rewrite.

BIG FINDING THIS SESSION (day105): A NEW, EVEN LARGER competitor shock cluster hit day99-104
(cumulative raw magnitude ~1.07 in <1 WEEK, vs 1.34 over 24 days for the previous cluster).
Two of the events were enormous (0.24, 0.2401, 0.2381, 0.2381 -- roughly 4x the previous cluster's
typical increment size).

Direct evidence (cohort created_day69-75, S1, exact-day breakdown of churn-at-1st-eval):
  day69->39%, day70->44%, day71->49%, day72->80%, day73->88%, day74->88%, day75->92%
This is a clean, monotonic escalation as eval date moves from day99 (before the day103-104 mega
shock) to day105 (after it) -- CONFIRMS expectations update DAILY and are applied at the exact
moment of each customer's eval (not batched weekly). S2/S3 show the SAME pattern, even worse
(S3 hits 100% for day74-75 signups).

CRITICAL MITIGATING FINDING: TENURE PROTECTION IS HUGE.
Cohort created day39-45 (S1), isolated 2nd-eval-only churn (backed out 1st-eval cancellations
separately via tenure=(end_day-created_day) query): 214 cancelled / 800 entering 2nd eval = 26.75%.
Vs the SAME-WEEK fresh (1st-eval, 30-day tenure) cohort's 67.4% blended (up to 92% for the most
shock-exposed days). S3: 2nd-eval churn 31.7% vs fresh cohort 78%. This ~2.5x protection ratio
matches the ~2.5x found last session (day98) for a smaller shock -- CONSISTENT, treat as a real,
reusable calibration constant.

This means the picture is NOT "the entire base is about to churn 90%" -- it's much more nuanced:
- Fresh (pre-1st-eval) cohorts facing this shock: ~70-92% churn at eval (very bad)
- 2nd-eval cohorts: ~27-32% churn (bad, ~3x worse than original ~9% baseline, but survivable)
- 3rd+/4th+-eval (more tenure): no direct data yet, EXTRAPOLATED lower still (guess, not measured)

Current S1 age-bucket composition of the SUBSCRIBED base (day105), critical for blending:
  0-30d (pre-1st-eval):  3102 (30.1%)
  31-60d (survived 1st): 5827 (56.5%)  <- majority of base is in this "2nd eval ~27-32%" bucket
  61-90d (survived 2nd): 1354 (13.1%)
  91-120d (survived 3rd):   26 (0.25%)
Other(S2+S3) buckets: b0=220, b1=1168, b2=116, b3=0

=> Because the majority of the base sits in the 31-60d bucket (lower churn on next eval), the
BLENDED weekly base-wide churn is NOT 90% -- naive hand-calc gives ~10%/week of TOTAL base from
evals alone under a "no new shocks" assumption. Still much worse than history, but not near-total
collapse in weeks. HOWEVER large uncertainty remains on whether MORE shocks hit (this is now the
3rd cluster event of the game) -- previous "quiet period = over" calls were wrong twice already.

Model: weekly-cohort-aging bucket simulation (b0/b1/b2/b3 per segment), each week 7/30 of each
bucket reaches its next eval and churns at a (scenario+time-varying) rate, survivors advance to
the next bucket, new signups enter b0. b3 is a terminal (4th+ eval, steady-state) bucket.

Revenue haircut THIS week (day99-105) came out extremely low: actual subscription_payment $24,478
vs avg-MRR-implied $49,083 (avg of start/end MRR *7/30) = 0.499 haircut. This is because many
customers due to bill this week CANCELLED instead of paying (eval-churn wave). Expect haircut to
STAY LOW (0.40-0.75) while eval churn remains elevated -- swept explicitly below.

Run this, sanity check week-1 output against hand calc, then use the sweep's min/max (across
scenario AND haircut) for forecast CI bounds.
"""
import numpy as np

CASH0 = 104861.46
DAY0 = 105

# ---- Segment starting state (day105 actuals) ----
# S1
S1_MRR = 143268.0
S1_N = 10309
S1_PRICE = S1_MRR / S1_N          # $/mo avg (grandfathered blend)
S1_COMPUTE_WK_PER_SUB = 11005.05 / S1_N   # $/wk/sub at current usage/tier2

# Other = S2+S3 combined
OTH_MRR = 5613.0 + 46874.0
OTH_N = 334 + 1170
OTH_PRICE = OTH_MRR / OTH_N
OTH_COMPUTE_WK_PER_SUB = (759.08 + 28.75 + 3068.8 + 4098.5 + 2942.3) / OTH_N

# calibration multiplier: my per-sub*avg_usage compute estimate (21902.5) vs actual ledger
# compute this week (24502.70) -- usage is trending up, apply a multiplier to stay realistic.
COMPUTE_CAL = 24502.70 / 21902.5   # ~1.119

# age buckets (0-30d, 31-60d, 61-90d, 91-120d+/terminal), current composition:
S1_BUCKETS0 = dict(b0=3102, b1=5827, b2=1354, b3=26)
OTH_BUCKETS0 = dict(b0=220, b1=1168, b2=116, b3=0)

# organic (network) leads/week at present (ads being cut to $0 this week):
S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK = 1292.0
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK = 82.0 + 137.0

LEAD_COST = 0.5

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
                  (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000)]

S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY = 76.227          # tier2, $0.002/unit
OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY = (163.31 * 332 + 342.21 * 2 + 243.85 * 899 + 473.78 * 206 + 538.90 * 65) / OTH_N
# blended $/unit for Other (mix of tier2 A and tier3/4 B/C) -- derive effective $/unit from compute/usage:
OTH_COST_PER_UNIT = (OTH_COMPUTE_WK_PER_SUB / 7) / OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY   # $/unit blended
S1_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.002


def capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_per_day):
    # keep ~25% headroom before choosing a tier (avoid overload risk); pick cheapest sufficient tier
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.80:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]


def run_scenario(name, churn_sched, conv_sched, haircut, ops_mode="hold_then_taper", weeks=26,
                  new_shock_weeks=None, new_shock_penalty=0.0):
    """
    churn_sched(week) -> (c1,c2,c3,c4) churn rates for bucket transitions b0->1,b1->2,b2->3,b3->3
    conv_sched(week) -> (S1_conv, OTH_conv) conversion rate on organic leads
    new_shock_weeks: set of week indices where an ADDITIONAL shock temporarily spikes c1/c2 (stress test)
    """
    s1 = dict(S1_BUCKETS0)
    oth = dict(OTH_BUCKETS0)
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    mrr_prev = S1_MRR + OTH_MRR
    for w in range(1, weeks + 1):
        c1, c2, c3, c4 = churn_sched(w)
        if new_shock_weeks and w in new_shock_weeks:
            c1 = min(0.97, c1 + new_shock_penalty)
            c2 = min(0.85, c2 + new_shock_penalty * 0.6)
            c3 = min(0.7, c3 + new_shock_penalty * 0.4)
            c4 = min(0.6, c4 + new_shock_penalty * 0.3)

        s1_conv, oth_conv = conv_sched(w)

        def step(buckets, churns, organic_leads_wk, base_n, conv):
            c1_, c2_, c3_, c4_ = churns
            grad0 = buckets['b0'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv0 = grad0 * (1 - c1_)
            grad1 = buckets['b1'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv1 = grad1 * (1 - c2_)
            grad2 = buckets['b2'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv2 = grad2 * (1 - c3_)
            grad3 = buckets['b3'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv3 = grad3 * (1 - c4_)

            cur_total = buckets['b0'] + buckets['b1'] + buckets['b2'] + buckets['b3']
            leads = organic_leads_wk * (cur_total / base_n) if base_n > 0 else 0.0
            new_signups = leads * conv

            new_b0 = buckets['b0'] - grad0 + new_signups
            new_b1 = buckets['b1'] - grad1 + surv0
            new_b2 = buckets['b2'] - grad2 + surv1
            new_b3 = buckets['b3'] - grad3 + surv2 + surv3
            return dict(b0=new_b0, b1=new_b1, b2=new_b2, b3=new_b3), leads, new_signups

        s1, s1_leads, s1_new = step(s1, (c1, c2, c3, c4), S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK, S1_N, s1_conv)
        oth, oth_leads, oth_new = step(oth, (c1 * 1.05, c2 * 1.05, c3 * 1.05, c4 * 1.05), OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK, OTH_N, oth_conv)
        # Other churns slightly worse than S1 throughout (observed: S2/S3 eval churn > S1 eval churn consistently)

        s1_total = s1['b0'] + s1['b1'] + s1['b2'] + s1['b3']
        oth_total = oth['b0'] + oth['b1'] + oth['b2'] + oth['b3']

        s1_mrr = s1_total * S1_PRICE
        oth_mrr = oth_total * OTH_PRICE
        mrr_now = s1_mrr + oth_mrr

        revenue = (mrr_prev + mrr_now) / 2 * 7 / 30 * haircut
        mrr_prev = mrr_now

        total_leads = s1_leads + oth_leads
        lead_cost = total_leads * LEAD_COST

        usage_day = s1_total * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY + oth_total * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY
        compute_cost = (s1_total * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY * S1_COST_PER_UNIT +
                         oth_total * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY * OTH_COST_PER_UNIT) * 7 * COMPUTE_CAL

        cap_cost = capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_day) * 7

        total_subs = s1_total + oth_total
        base_subs = S1_N + OTH_N
        if ops_mode == "hold_then_taper":
            # hold $1500/day for first 3 weeks (fresh SLA commitment), then taper proportionally to
            # subscriber count, floor $250/day
            if w <= 3:
                ops_daily = 1500.0
            else:
                ops_daily = max(250.0, 1500.0 * (total_subs / base_subs))
        else:
            ops_daily = 1500.0
        ops_cost = ops_daily * 7

        dev_cost = 0.0
        ad_cost = 0.0

        total_cost = lead_cost + compute_cost + cap_cost + ops_cost + dev_cost + ad_cost
        cash += revenue - total_cost

        trace.append(dict(week=w, day=DAY0 + w * 7, cash=cash, s1_subs=s1_total, oth_subs=oth_total,
                           total_subs=total_subs, revenue=revenue, cost=total_cost,
                           compute_cost=compute_cost, cap_cost=cap_cost, ops_cost=ops_cost,
                           lead_cost=lead_cost, mrr=mrr_now))
    return trace


# ---------------- Scenarios ----------------
def severe_continuing_churn(w):
    if w <= 4:
        return (0.80, 0.30, 0.18, 0.12)
    elif w <= 12:
        return (0.70, 0.35, 0.22, 0.15)
    else:
        return (0.65, 0.40, 0.25, 0.18)


def moderating_churn(w):
    if w <= 2:
        return (0.80, 0.28, 0.18, 0.12)
    elif w <= 6:
        return (0.55, 0.24, 0.15, 0.11)
    elif w <= 12:
        return (0.40, 0.18, 0.12, 0.10)
    else:
        return (0.30, 0.15, 0.10, 0.09)


def catastrophic_churn(w):
    if w <= 4:
        return (0.88, 0.35, 0.22, 0.15)
    elif w <= 12:
        return (0.88, 0.45, 0.30, 0.22)
    else:
        return (0.90, 0.55, 0.40, 0.30)


def severe_conv(w):
    return (0.10, 0.05)


def moderating_conv(w):
    if w <= 4:
        return (0.11, 0.05)
    elif w <= 12:
        return (0.15, 0.07)
    else:
        return (0.18, 0.09)


def catastrophic_conv(w):
    if w <= 8:
        return (0.07, 0.03)
    else:
        return (0.04, 0.02)


SCENARIOS = {
    "SEVERE_CONTINUING": (severe_continuing_churn, severe_conv, None, 0.0),
    "MODERATING_NO_NEW_SHOCK": (moderating_churn, moderating_conv, None, 0.0),
    "CATASTROPHIC": (catastrophic_churn, catastrophic_conv, None, 0.0),
    # stress test: moderating scenario but ANOTHER shock cluster hits in week 6-7 (historical pattern:
    # clusters recur every ~10-14 weeks after a lull)
    "MODERATING_BUT_NEW_SHOCK_WK6": (moderating_churn, moderating_conv, {6, 7}, 0.35),
}

HAIRCUTS = [0.40, 0.50, 0.65, 0.80]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"{'scenario':32s} {'haircut':8s} {'wk1_cash':>12s} {'wk4_cash':>12s} {'wk12_cash':>12s} {'wk26_cash':>12s} {'min_cash_26wk':>14s} {'wk26_subs':>10s}")
    all_results = {}
    for sname, (churn_f, conv_f, shock_wks, shock_pen) in SCENARIOS.items():
        for hc in HAIRCUTS:
            trace = run_scenario(sname, churn_f, conv_f, hc, new_shock_weeks=shock_wks, new_shock_penalty=shock_pen)
            wk1 = trace[0]['cash']
            wk4 = trace[3]['cash']
            wk12 = trace[11]['cash']
            wk26 = trace[25]['cash']
            min_cash = min(t['cash'] for t in trace)
            wk26_subs = trace[25]['total_subs']
            all_results[(sname, hc)] = trace
            print(f"{sname:32s} {hc:<8.2f} {wk1:12,.0f} {wk4:12,.0f} {wk12:12,.0f} {wk26:12,.0f} {min_cash:14,.0f} {wk26_subs:10,.0f}")

    print()
    print("=== Hand-calc sanity check: week 1 (SEVERE_CONTINUING, haircut=0.50) ===")
    tr = run_scenario("chk", severe_continuing_churn, severe_conv, 0.50)
    w1 = tr[0]
    print(w1)
    print(f"S1 subs after wk1: {tr[0]['s1_subs']:.0f} (started {S1_N})")
    print(f"Other subs after wk1: {tr[0]['oth_subs']:.0f} (started {OTH_N})")

    print()
    print("=== Extract overall min/max across ALL scenarios+haircuts, per horizon ===")
    for idx, label in [(0, "1wk"), (3, "4wk"), (11, "12wk"), (25, "26wk")]:
        vals = [tr[idx]['cash'] for tr in all_results.values()]
        print(f"{label}: min={min(vals):,.0f} max={max(vals):,.0f} median={np.median(vals):,.0f}")

"""
forecast_model_v23.py -- Day105. MAJOR FIX to v22's revenue formula (v22 double-counted churn via
an inappropriately-low haircut sweep 0.40-0.80 reused from a churn-crisis week -- that haircut
NUMBER *already reflects* the churn effect that the bucket model separately/explicitly applies,
so multiplying by both was double-penalizing revenue).

VALIDATED FORMULA (matches actual day98->105 data to within 1.04% error -- see validation below):
    revenue_week = MRR_start_of_week * (7/30) * (1 - blended_churn_rate_among_THIS_WEEKS_evaluators) * noise

Why: only ~7/30=23.3% of the base reaches its billing/eval date in any given week (30-day cycles).
Of THOSE, (1-churn_rate) actually pay; the other 76.7% of the base isn't billed this week at all
(they bill on their own offset week). This is why "haircut" seemed so wildly variable across
sessions (0.40 to 1.15) -- it was almost ENTIRELY explained by that week's specific evaluator
churn rate, not real independent noise. Validation:
    MRR_start(day98)=224959, evaluators this week (t30 cohort ever-sub=1958 + t60 cohort
    ever-sub~1010)=2973, actual cancellations=1601 (blended churn=53.9%), implied revenue =
    224959*7/30*(1-0.539) = $24,224 vs actual $24,478 (-1.04% error). Excellent fit.

Residual noise (unexplained variance beyond the churn-adjusted formula) should be MUCH narrower
now, ~0.90-1.10, not 0.40-1.15 -- most of the historical "haircut" swings ARE the churn effect.

BIG FINDING THIS SESSION: new competitor shock cluster day99-104, BIGGER than the previous one
(cumulative ~1.07 in <1wk vs 1.34/24days prior). Direct evidence (S1 day69-75 cohort, exact-day
breakdown of 1st-eval churn): day69->39%,70->44%,71->49%,72->80%,73->88%,74->88%,75->92%. Clean
escalation as eval date crosses from before to after the day103-104 mega-shock -- CONFIRMS
expectations update daily, applied at the exact moment of eval.

MITIGATING FINDING: tenure protection is large and consistent. Isolated 2nd-eval-only churn (day39-45
cohort, backed out 1st-eval cancellations via tenure=(end_day-created_day)): S1 214/800=26.75%,
S3 32/101=31.7% -- vs the SAME-WEEK fresh 1st-eval cohort's 67-78% blended (up to 92-100% for the
most shock-exposed days). ~2.5x protection ratio, consistent with last session's smaller-shock
finding. Current S1 base age-mix: 0-30d=3102(30%), 31-60d=5827(56%, majority!), 61-90d=1354(13%),
91-120d=26(0.25%). Because the majority of the base sits in the LOWER-churn 31-60d bucket, blended
base-wide weekly churn is NOT 90% -- more like 10-20%/wk under a "no new shocks" assumption.

Model: weekly-cohort-aging bucket simulation (b0=pre-1st-eval,b1=survived1st,b2=survived2nd,
b3=survived3rd+/terminal) per segment (S1, Other=S2+S3). Each week 7/30 of each bucket reaches
its next eval; survivors advance; new organic signups enter b0. Revenue via the validated formula
above (computed directly from the model's own evaluator/survivor counts, no separate haircut
double-count). Ops taper + capacity-tier auto-downgrade as usage falls modeled explicitly.
"""
import numpy as np

CASH0 = 104861.46
DAY0 = 105

S1_MRR = 143268.0
S1_N = 10309
S1_PRICE = S1_MRR / S1_N
S1_COMPUTE_WK_PER_SUB = 11005.05 / S1_N

OTH_MRR = 5613.0 + 46874.0
OTH_N = 334 + 1170
OTH_PRICE = OTH_MRR / OTH_N
OTH_COMPUTE_WK_PER_SUB = (759.08 + 28.75 + 3068.8 + 4098.5 + 2942.3) / OTH_N

COMPUTE_CAL = 24502.70 / 21902.5  # calibration vs actual ledger this week (~1.119)

S1_BUCKETS0 = dict(b0=3102.0, b1=5827.0, b2=1354.0, b3=26.0)
OTH_BUCKETS0 = dict(b0=220.0, b1=1168.0, b2=116.0, b3=0.0)

S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK = 1292.0
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK = 82.0 + 137.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
                  (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000)]

S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY = 76.227
OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY = (163.31 * 332 + 342.21 * 2 + 243.85 * 899 + 473.78 * 206 + 538.90 * 65) / OTH_N
OTH_COST_PER_UNIT = (OTH_COMPUTE_WK_PER_SUB / 7) / OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY
S1_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.002


def capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.80:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]


def run_scenario(churn_sched, conv_sched, noise, ops_mode="hold_then_taper", weeks=26,
                  new_shock_weeks=None, new_shock_penalty=0.0):
    s1 = dict(S1_BUCKETS0)
    oth = dict(OTH_BUCKETS0)
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    for w in range(1, weeks + 1):
        c1, c2, c3, c4 = churn_sched(w)
        if new_shock_weeks and w in new_shock_weeks:
            c1 = min(0.97, c1 + new_shock_penalty)
            c2 = min(0.85, c2 + new_shock_penalty * 0.6)
            c3 = min(0.7, c3 + new_shock_penalty * 0.4)
            c4 = min(0.6, c4 + new_shock_penalty * 0.3)
        s1_conv, oth_conv = conv_sched(w)

        mrr_start = s1['b0'] * S1_PRICE + s1['b1'] * S1_PRICE + s1['b2'] * S1_PRICE + s1['b3'] * S1_PRICE \
            + oth['b0'] * OTH_PRICE + oth['b1'] * OTH_PRICE + oth['b2'] * OTH_PRICE + oth['b3'] * OTH_PRICE

        def step(buckets, churns, organic_leads_wk, base_n, conv):
            c1_, c2_, c3_, c4_ = churns
            grad0 = buckets['b0'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv0 = grad0 * (1 - c1_)
            grad1 = buckets['b1'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv1 = grad1 * (1 - c2_)
            grad2 = buckets['b2'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv2 = grad2 * (1 - c3_)
            grad3 = buckets['b3'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv3 = grad3 * (1 - c4_)

            cur_total = buckets['b0'] + buckets['b1'] + buckets['b2'] + buckets['b3']
            leads = organic_leads_wk * (cur_total / base_n) if base_n > 0 else 0.0
            new_signups = leads * conv

            new_buckets = dict(
                b0=buckets['b0'] - grad0 + new_signups,
                b1=buckets['b1'] - grad1 + surv0,
                b2=buckets['b2'] - grad2 + surv1,
                b3=buckets['b3'] - grad3 + surv2 + surv3,
            )
            total_eval = grad0 + grad1 + grad2 + grad3
            total_surv = surv0 + surv1 + surv2 + surv3
            return new_buckets, leads, new_signups, total_eval, total_surv

        s1_new, s1_leads, s1_newsub, s1_eval, s1_surv = step(s1, (c1, c2, c3, c4), S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK, S1_N, s1_conv)
        oth_new, oth_leads, oth_newsub, oth_eval, oth_surv = step(
            oth, (min(0.97, c1 * 1.05), min(0.9, c2 * 1.05), min(0.8, c3 * 1.05), min(0.7, c4 * 1.05)),
            OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK, OTH_N, oth_conv)

        total_eval = s1_eval + oth_eval
        total_surv = s1_surv + oth_surv
        blended_churn_evaluators = 1 - (total_surv / total_eval) if total_eval > 0 else 0.0

        revenue = mrr_start * 7 / 30 * (1 - blended_churn_evaluators) * noise

        s1, oth = s1_new, oth_new
        s1_total = s1['b0'] + s1['b1'] + s1['b2'] + s1['b3']
        oth_total = oth['b0'] + oth['b1'] + oth['b2'] + oth['b3']
        total_subs = s1_total + oth_total
        base_subs = S1_N + OTH_N

        total_leads = s1_leads + oth_leads
        lead_cost = total_leads * LEAD_COST

        usage_day = s1_total * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY + oth_total * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY
        compute_cost = (s1_total * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY * S1_COST_PER_UNIT +
                         oth_total * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY * OTH_COST_PER_UNIT) * 7 * COMPUTE_CAL
        cap_cost = capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_day) * 7

        if ops_mode == "hold_then_taper":
            if w <= 3:
                ops_daily = 1500.0
            else:
                ops_daily = max(250.0, 1500.0 * (total_subs / base_subs))
        elif ops_mode == "hold":
            ops_daily = 1500.0
        else:
            ops_daily = 750.0
        ops_cost = ops_daily * 7

        total_cost = lead_cost + compute_cost + cap_cost + ops_cost
        cash += revenue - total_cost

        trace.append(dict(week=w, day=DAY0 + w * 7, cash=cash, s1_subs=s1_total, oth_subs=oth_total,
                           total_subs=total_subs, revenue=revenue, cost=total_cost,
                           compute_cost=compute_cost, cap_cost=cap_cost, ops_cost=ops_cost,
                           lead_cost=lead_cost, mrr_start=mrr_start, blended_churn=blended_churn_evaluators))
    return trace


def severe_continuing_churn(w):
    if w <= 4:
        return (0.80, 0.30, 0.18, 0.12)
    elif w <= 12:
        return (0.70, 0.35, 0.22, 0.15)
    else:
        return (0.65, 0.40, 0.25, 0.18)


def moderating_churn(w):
    if w <= 2:
        return (0.80, 0.28, 0.18, 0.12)
    elif w <= 6:
        return (0.55, 0.24, 0.15, 0.11)
    elif w <= 12:
        return (0.40, 0.18, 0.12, 0.10)
    else:
        return (0.30, 0.15, 0.10, 0.09)


def catastrophic_churn(w):
    if w <= 4:
        return (0.88, 0.35, 0.22, 0.15)
    elif w <= 12:
        return (0.88, 0.45, 0.30, 0.22)
    else:
        return (0.90, 0.55, 0.40, 0.30)


def severe_conv(w):
    return (0.10, 0.05)


def moderating_conv(w):
    if w <= 4:
        return (0.11, 0.05)
    elif w <= 12:
        return (0.15, 0.07)
    else:
        return (0.18, 0.09)


def catastrophic_conv(w):
    if w <= 8:
        return (0.07, 0.03)
    else:
        return (0.04, 0.02)


SCENARIOS = {
    "SEVERE_CONTINUING": (severe_continuing_churn, severe_conv, None, 0.0),
    "MODERATING_NO_NEW_SHOCK": (moderating_churn, moderating_conv, None, 0.0),
    "CATASTROPHIC": (catastrophic_churn, catastrophic_conv, None, 0.0),
    "MODERATING_BUT_NEW_SHOCK_WK6": (moderating_churn, moderating_conv, {6, 7}, 0.35),
    "MODERATING_BUT_NEW_SHOCK_WK15": (moderating_churn, moderating_conv, {15, 16}, 0.35),
}

NOISE_RANGE = [0.90, 1.0, 1.10]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("=== VALIDATION: reproduce actual day98->105 week using observed churn ===")
    # observed: mrr_start=224959, blended churn among evaluators=53.9% (t30+t60 cohorts)
    mrr_start_actual = 224959.0
    blended_actual = 0.539
    rev_check = mrr_start_actual * 7 / 30 * (1 - blended_actual)
    print(f"formula revenue={rev_check:,.0f} vs actual $24,478 (error {(rev_check-24478)/24478*100:.2f}%)")
    print()

    print(f"{'scenario':32s} {'noise':6s} {'wk1_cash':>12s} {'wk4_cash':>12s} {'wk12_cash':>12s} {'wk26_cash':>12s} {'min_cash':>12s} {'wk26_subs':>10s}")
    all_results = {}
    for sname, (churn_f, conv_f, shock_wks, shock_pen) in SCENARIOS.items():
        for noise in NOISE_RANGE:
            trace = run_scenario(churn_f, conv_f, noise, new_shock_weeks=shock_wks, new_shock_penalty=shock_pen)
            wk1, wk4, wk12, wk26 = trace[0]['cash'], trace[3]['cash'], trace[11]['cash'], trace[25]['cash']
            min_cash = min(t['cash'] for t in trace)
            all_results[(sname, noise)] = trace
            print(f"{sname:32s} {noise:<6.2f} {wk1:12,.0f} {wk4:12,.0f} {wk12:12,.0f} {wk26:12,.0f} {min_cash:12,.0f} {trace[25]['total_subs']:10,.0f}")

    print()
    print("=== Week1 detail (MODERATING, noise=1.0) sanity check ===")
    tr = run_scenario(moderating_churn, moderating_conv, 1.0)
    for k, v in tr[0].items():
        print(f"  {k}: {v:,.2f}" if isinstance(v, float) else f"  {k}: {v}")

    print()
    print("=== Overall min/max across ALL scenarios+noise, per horizon (for CI construction) ===")
    for idx, label in [(0, "1wk"), (3, "4wk"), (11, "12wk"), (25, "26wk")]:
        vals = [tr[idx]['cash'] for tr in all_results.values()]
        print(f"{label}: min={min(vals):,.0f} max={max(vals):,.0f} median={np.median(vals):,.0f} mean={np.mean(vals):,.0f}")

"""
forecast_model_v24.py -- Day105. Adds TIER DOWNGRADE lever on top of v23's validated revenue formula.

NEW LEVER DISCOVERED THIS SESSION: v23's trace showed cash going negative ~week11-12 in ALL
scenarios even with ads=$0, dev=$0, ops tapering -- because capacity ($1330/day, STUCK at Tier3
since usage/sub is too high to downgrade for many weeks) + compute (~$21-24K/wk, >half of total
cost) overwhelm the shrinking revenue base. Capacity tier can't drop (usage still > tier2 cap in
most scenarios for a long time), so the only large remaining lever is MODEL TIER (per-plan-letter,
GLOBAL, applies to A/B/C independent of group).

Quantified savings (current usage, current subs, held flat for comparison):
  Plan A (T2->T1, mult 0.75->0.60): affects S1(10309)+S2-A(332)+S3-A(899). Savings $12,605/wk.
    S1-A margin/mo: $9.33 -> $13.21 (+42%). Delivered quality drops 0.3965->0.3172 (-0.079 abs,
    SMALL relative to the >1.0 raw shock that just hit -- expect modest incremental churn, unproven).
  Plan B (T3->T2, mult 0.90->0.75): affects S2-B(2)+S3-B(206, currently healthy +$24/mo margin).
    Savings $2,752/wk.
  Plan C (T4->T3, mult 1.00->0.90): affects S3-C(65, CURRENTLY NEGATIVE margin -$23/mo). Savings
    $1,471/wk -- and FLIPS this segment's margin to +$73.89/mo. Clear win, small blast radius.
  TOTAL: $16,828/wk savings if all three downgraded -- larger than our current total ops+cap fixed
  cost combined ($19,810/wk). Potentially flips the whole trajectory from cash-negative to
  cash-positive.

RISK: quality multiplier cut adds to the ALREADY-catastrophic expectation gap (this session's mega
shock). Modeled here as an extra CHURN PENALTY sensitivity (added uniformly to all bucket-churn
rates) so we can see if the trade is STILL favorable even under a pessimistic assumption about
incremental churn. REVERSIBLE -- tier is just a config setting, can revert within a week if the
next eval-cohort data (compare like-for-like bucket, e.g. 31-60d bucket churn) shows a clear,
large incremental deterioration beyond what the ongoing shock alone would predict.

DECISION TAKEN: downgrade all three (A T2->T1, B T3->T2, C T4->T3) this week. Monitor closely.
"""
import numpy as np

CASH0 = 104861.46
DAY0 = 105

S1_MRR = 143268.0
S1_N = 10309
S1_PRICE = S1_MRR / S1_N

OTH_MRR = 5613.0 + 46874.0
OTH_N = 334 + 1170
OTH_PRICE = OTH_MRR / OTH_N

S1_BUCKETS0 = dict(b0=3102.0, b1=5827.0, b2=1354.0, b3=26.0)
OTH_BUCKETS0 = dict(b0=220.0, b1=1168.0, b2=116.0, b3=0.0)

S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK = 1292.0
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK = 82.0 + 137.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
                  (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000)]

S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY = 76.227
OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY = (163.31 * 332 + 342.21 * 2 + 243.85 * 899 + 473.78 * 206 + 538.90 * 65) / OTH_N

# post-downgrade blended $/unit for "Other" (S2-A/S3-A now T1=0.0003; S2-B/S3-B now T2=0.002; S3-C now T3=0.006)
OTH_UNITS_WK = dict(s2a=163.31 * 332, s2b=342.21 * 2, s3a=243.85 * 899, s3b=473.78 * 206, s3c=538.90 * 65)
OTH_COST_PER_UNIT_NEW = (OTH_UNITS_WK['s2a'] * 0.0003 + OTH_UNITS_WK['s2b'] * 0.002 +
                         OTH_UNITS_WK['s3a'] * 0.0003 + OTH_UNITS_WK['s3b'] * 0.002 +
                         OTH_UNITS_WK['s3c'] * 0.006) / sum(OTH_UNITS_WK.values())
OTH_COST_PER_UNIT_OLD = (OTH_UNITS_WK['s2a'] * 0.002 + OTH_UNITS_WK['s2b'] * 0.006 +
                         OTH_UNITS_WK['s3a'] * 0.002 + OTH_UNITS_WK['s3b'] * 0.006 +
                         OTH_UNITS_WK['s3c'] * 0.012) / sum(OTH_UNITS_WK.values())
S1_COST_PER_UNIT_NEW = 0.0003
S1_COST_PER_UNIT_OLD = 0.002


def capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.85:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]


def run_scenario(churn_sched, conv_sched, noise, tier_downgrade=True, extra_churn_penalty=0.0,
                  ops_daily_base=1500.0, ops_taper=True, weeks=26, new_shock_weeks=None, new_shock_penalty=0.0):
    s1 = dict(S1_BUCKETS0)
    oth = dict(OTH_BUCKETS0)
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    s1_cpu = S1_COST_PER_UNIT_NEW if tier_downgrade else S1_COST_PER_UNIT_OLD
    oth_cpu = OTH_COST_PER_UNIT_NEW if tier_downgrade else OTH_COST_PER_UNIT_OLD

    for w in range(1, weeks + 1):
        c1, c2, c3, c4 = churn_sched(w)
        c1, c2, c3, c4 = (min(0.98, c1 + extra_churn_penalty), min(0.95, c2 + extra_churn_penalty),
                          min(0.9, c3 + extra_churn_penalty), min(0.85, c4 + extra_churn_penalty))
        if new_shock_weeks and w in new_shock_weeks:
            c1 = min(0.98, c1 + new_shock_penalty)
            c2 = min(0.9, c2 + new_shock_penalty * 0.6)
            c3 = min(0.8, c3 + new_shock_penalty * 0.4)
            c4 = min(0.7, c4 + new_shock_penalty * 0.3)
        s1_conv, oth_conv = conv_sched(w)

        mrr_start = (s1['b0'] + s1['b1'] + s1['b2'] + s1['b3']) * S1_PRICE + \
                    (oth['b0'] + oth['b1'] + oth['b2'] + oth['b3']) * OTH_PRICE

        def step(buckets, churns, organic_leads_wk, base_n, conv):
            c1_, c2_, c3_, c4_ = churns
            grad0 = buckets['b0'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv0 = grad0 * (1 - c1_)
            grad1 = buckets['b1'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv1 = grad1 * (1 - c2_)
            grad2 = buckets['b2'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv2 = grad2 * (1 - c3_)
            grad3 = buckets['b3'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv3 = grad3 * (1 - c4_)
            cur_total = buckets['b0'] + buckets['b1'] + buckets['b2'] + buckets['b3']
            leads = organic_leads_wk * (cur_total / base_n) if base_n > 0 else 0.0
            new_signups = leads * conv
            new_buckets = dict(b0=buckets['b0'] - grad0 + new_signups, b1=buckets['b1'] - grad1 + surv0,
                               b2=buckets['b2'] - grad2 + surv1, b3=buckets['b3'] - grad3 + surv2 + surv3)
            total_eval = grad0 + grad1 + grad2 + grad3
            total_surv = surv0 + surv1 + surv2 + surv3
            return new_buckets, leads, new_signups, total_eval, total_surv

        s1_new, s1_leads, _, s1_eval, s1_surv = step(s1, (c1, c2, c3, c4), S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK, S1_N, s1_conv)
        oth_new, oth_leads, _, oth_eval, oth_surv = step(
            oth, (min(0.98, c1 * 1.05), min(0.92, c2 * 1.05), min(0.85, c3 * 1.05), min(0.78, c4 * 1.05)),
            OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK, OTH_N, oth_conv)

        total_eval = s1_eval + oth_eval
        total_surv = s1_surv + oth_surv
        blended_churn = 1 - (total_surv / total_eval) if total_eval > 0 else 0.0
        revenue = mrr_start * 7 / 30 * (1 - blended_churn) * noise

        s1, oth = s1_new, oth_new
        s1_total = s1['b0'] + s1['b1'] + s1['b2'] + s1['b3']
        oth_total = oth['b0'] + oth['b1'] + oth['b2'] + oth['b3']
        total_subs = s1_total + oth_total
        base_subs = S1_N + OTH_N

        lead_cost = (s1_leads + oth_leads) * LEAD_COST
        usage_day = s1_total * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY + oth_total * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY
        compute_cost = (s1_total * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY * s1_cpu + oth_total * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB_DAY * oth_cpu) * 7
        cap_cost = capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_day) * 7

        if ops_taper:
            ops_daily = ops_daily_base if w <= 3 else max(250.0, ops_daily_base * (total_subs / base_subs))
        else:
            ops_daily = ops_daily_base
        ops_cost = ops_daily * 7

        total_cost = lead_cost + compute_cost + cap_cost + ops_cost
        cash += revenue - total_cost
        trace.append(dict(week=w, day=DAY0 + w * 7, cash=cash, total_subs=total_subs, revenue=revenue,
                           cost=total_cost, compute_cost=compute_cost, cap_cost=cap_cost, ops_cost=ops_cost,
                           blended_churn=blended_churn))
    return trace


def severe_continuing_churn(w):
    return (0.80, 0.30, 0.18, 0.12) if w <= 4 else (0.70, 0.35, 0.22, 0.15) if w <= 12 else (0.65, 0.40, 0.25, 0.18)


def moderating_churn(w):
    if w <= 2: return (0.80, 0.28, 0.18, 0.12)
    elif w <= 6: return (0.55, 0.24, 0.15, 0.11)
    elif w <= 12: return (0.40, 0.18, 0.12, 0.10)
    else: return (0.30, 0.15, 0.10, 0.09)


def catastrophic_churn(w):
    return (0.88, 0.35, 0.22, 0.15) if w <= 4 else (0.88, 0.45, 0.30, 0.22) if w <= 12 else (0.90, 0.55, 0.40, 0.30)


def severe_conv(w): return (0.10, 0.05)


def moderating_conv(w):
    if w <= 4: return (0.11, 0.05)
    elif w <= 12: return (0.15, 0.07)
    else: return (0.18, 0.09)


def catastrophic_conv(w): return (0.07, 0.03) if w <= 8 else (0.04, 0.02)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"OTH_COST_PER_UNIT_NEW={OTH_COST_PER_UNIT_NEW:.6f} OLD={OTH_COST_PER_UNIT_OLD:.6f}")
    print()
    print("=== Compare WITH vs WITHOUT tier downgrade, across churn-penalty sensitivity (MODERATING scenario, noise=1.0) ===")
    for downgrade in [False, True]:
        for penalty in [0.0, 0.08, 0.15]:
            trace = run_scenario(moderating_churn, moderating_conv, 1.0, tier_downgrade=downgrade, extra_churn_penalty=(penalty if downgrade else 0.0))
            wk1, wk4, wk12, wk26 = trace[0]['cash'], trace[3]['cash'], trace[11]['cash'], trace[25]['cash']
            minc = min(t['cash'] for t in trace)
            print(f"downgrade={downgrade!s:5} penalty={penalty:.2f}  wk1={wk1:>10,.0f} wk4={wk4:>10,.0f} wk12={wk12:>10,.0f} wk26={wk26:>10,.0f} min={minc:>10,.0f} end_subs={trace[25]['total_subs']:>8,.0f}")

    print()
    print("=== Full scenario x noise x penalty sweep WITH tier downgrade ===")
    SCEN = {"SEVERE_CONTINUING": (severe_continuing_churn, severe_conv), "MODERATING": (moderating_churn, moderating_conv),
            "CATASTROPHIC": (catastrophic_churn, catastrophic_conv)}
    all_results = {}
    for sname, (cf, vf) in SCEN.items():
        for noise in [0.90, 1.0, 1.10]:
            for penalty in [0.0, 0.10]:
                trace = run_scenario(cf, vf, noise, tier_downgrade=True, extra_churn_penalty=penalty)
                all_results[(sname, noise, penalty)] = trace
    for idx, label in [(0, "1wk"), (3, "4wk"), (11, "12wk"), (25, "26wk")]:
        vals = [tr[idx]['cash'] for tr in all_results.values()]
        print(f"{label}: min={min(vals):,.0f} max={max(vals):,.0f} median={np.median(vals):,.0f}")
    print()
    for k, tr in all_results.items():
        print(k, f"wk1={tr[0]['cash']:,.0f} wk4={tr[3]['cash']:,.0f} wk12={tr[11]['cash']:,.0f} wk26={tr[25]['cash']:,.0f} min={min(t['cash'] for t in tr):,.0f}")

arguments.content:
# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 105 = end of week 15. 57 weeks remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: `forecast_model_v24.py` (latest; v22/v23/v18-21 are superseded intermediate steps,
kept on disk for reference only). Read its docstring in full before reusing. **Refresh ALL
calibration constants (subs/MRR/compute per group, bucket-age composition, churn schedules) every
session — don't reuse stale hand-tuned numbers verbatim.**

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → refresh forecast model →
call next-week. Verify prior session's plan actually landed via `config_overrides` (day-filtered)
against the live DB. **Before finalizing any spend/pricing decision: sweep >=3 genuinely-different
scenarios AND check MINIMUM cash across the FULL 26-week trajectory under each.** Sanity-check the
model's week-1 output against a hand-calc using last week's ACTUAL ledger numbers before trusting it.

## 🚨 THIS SESSION'S MAJOR FINDINGS (Day105) — read in full, this changes everything

### 1. A SECOND, EVEN BIGGER competitor shock cluster hit day99-104
Cumulative raw magnitude ~1.07 in under a week (two pairs of enormous 0.24/0.238 events — roughly
10-15x the typical increment size), vs 1.34 spread over 24 days for the previous (day69-92)
cluster. This is now the SECOND confirmed cluster of the game; clusters seem to recur after
"quiet" periods of unpredictable length (previously wrongly called "over" twice already —
NEVER assume a quiet streak under ~4 weeks means it's done).

### 2. SOLVED: expectations update DAILY, applied at the exact moment of each customer's own eval
Direct proof: S1 cohort created day69-75 (all evaluate 30 days later, i.e. day99-105), broken out
by EXACT created_day: day69→39%,70→44%,71→49%,72→80%,73→88%,74→88%,75→92% churn. Clean monotonic
escalation exactly tracking eval-date crossing from before to after the day103-104 mega-shock.
S2/S3 show the same pattern (S3 hits 100% for day74-75). **Use exact-created_day breakdowns (not
just weekly cohort aggregates) whenever isolating a shock's timing effect — much higher resolution.**

### 3. TENURE PROTECTION IS LARGE AND CONSISTENT (~2.5x, replicated twice now)
Isolated SECOND-eval-only churn (cohort created day39-45, backed out 1st-eval cancellations via
`tenure=(end_day-created_day)` grouping): S1 214/800=26.75%, S3 32/101=31.7% — vs the SAME-WEEK
FRESH (1st-eval) cohort's 67-78% blended (up to 92-100% for peak-exposure days). This ~2.5x ratio
matches last session's finding for the smaller first cluster — treat as a solid, reusable constant.
**Technique**: query `(s.end_day - c.created_day) as tenure` grouped, for a cohort's cancellations,
to split 1st-eval vs 2nd-eval(+) churn cleanly, then divide by the correct survivor-entering-that-
eval denominator (total_ever_subscribed MINUS those who already left at the prior eval).

Current base age-mix matters hugely for blended impact (query every session, composition shifts):
S1 (day105): 0-30d=3102(30%,pre-1st-eval), 31-60d=5827(56%!,survived 1st), 61-90d=1354(13%,survived
2nd), 91-120d=26(0.25%). Because the MAJORITY sits in the lower-churn 31-60d bucket, blended
base-wide weekly churn is nowhere near the scary 90% fresh-cohort number — more like 10-20%/wk
under a "no new shocks" assumption. **Always build a bucket-aged (not flat-rate) churn model.**

### 4. SOLVED the revenue-haircut mystery (validated to -1.04% error against actual data)
```
revenue_week = MRR_start_of_week * (7/30) * (1 - blended_churn_rate_among_THIS_WEEKS_evaluators) * noise(~0.9-1.1)
```
Only ~7/30=23.3% of the base reaches its billing/eval date in any given week (30-day cycles); of
those, (1-churn) actually pay, the other 76.7% aren't billed at all that week. The wildly-variable
"haircut" (0.40 to 1.15 across past sessions) was almost ENTIRELY this effect, not independent
noise — a bad week's low haircut IS that week's high evaluator churn, already explainable, not a
mystery constant. **Validated**: day98→105, MRR_start=224959, evaluators(t30+t60 cohorts)=2973,
actual cancellations=1601 (blended churn 53.9%), formula→$24,224 vs actual $24,478 (-1.04%).
**Do NOT apply an independent haircut sweep of 0.4-0.8 on top of an explicit churn-bucket model —
that DOUBLE-COUNTS churn** (this was a real bug in my first attempt this session, v22; fixed in v23/v24).
Residual noise beyond the formula should be narrow (~0.90-1.10), not wide.

### 5. NEW LEVER FOUND: MODEL TIER DOWNGRADE — huge, reversible, high-value (ACTED ON THIS SESSION)
Compute cost is `usage × tier_cost_per_unit`; tiers are GLOBAL per plan letter (A/B/C), independent
of group. Quantified savings at current usage (all 3 plans downgraded one tier):
  Plan A (T2→T1, mult 0.75→0.60): -$12,605/wk. Affects S1(10309)+S2-A(332)+S3-A(899).
    S1-A margin/mo: $9.33→$13.21 (+42%). Delivered quality 0.3965→0.3172 (-0.079 abs — SMALL next
    to the >1.0 raw shock that just hit).
  Plan B (T3→T2, mult 0.90→0.75): -$2,752/wk. Affects S2-B(2)+S3-B(206, was healthy +$24/mo).
  Plan C (T4→T3, mult 1.00→0.90): -$1,471/wk. Affects S3-C(65) — **flips margin -$23→+$74/mo.**
  TOTAL: -$16,828/wk, bigger than our entire ops+capacity fixed cost combined ($19,810/wk).
Modeled with an explicit extra-churn-penalty sensitivity (uniform additive to all bucket-churn
rates, representing the uncertain quality-degradation risk): **even at +30pp additive churn
penalty stacked with the CATASTROPHIC scenario (shocks continue+worsen forever), 26wk cash only
fell to -$9,227 (vs -$434,468 in the pre-downgrade model under milder assumptions)**. Strongly
positive-EV. **REVERSIBLE — tier is just a config value, can revert within a week.**
**ACTION TAKEN: downgraded A:2→1, B:3→2, C:4→3 this session (day105).** #1 THING TO CHECK NEXT
SESSION: does the 31-60d bucket's (largest, ~56% of S1) 2nd-eval churn stay near the ~27-32%
observed baseline, or does it jump markedly (would indicate the tier cut is biting harder than
modeled — if so, consider reverting Plan A specifically, since B/C's blast radius is much smaller
and their economics argument is even cleaner/safer).

### 6. R&D has 20 tiers, NOT 10 (correction to long-standing memory error)

## How to rebuild forecast inputs fresh each session
```python
import novamind_api as nm
# 1. Installed base + MRR, by group AND plan:
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 2. Actual usage by group/plan (last 7 days):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, AVG(du.usage_units) as avg_usage, COUNT(DISTINCT du.customer_id) as cnt
FROM daily_usage du JOIN customers c ON du.customer_id=c.customer_id JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE du.day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 3. Bucket-age composition (CRITICAL for blended churn projection):
r = nm.query('''SELECT CASE WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=30 THEN "0-30" WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=60 THEN "31-60"
WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=90 THEN "61-90" WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=120 THEN "91-120" ELSE "120+" END as bucket,
COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE c.group_id="S1" AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY bucket''')  # repeat per group
# 4. Exact-created_day churn-at-eval breakdown for the cohort evaluating THIS week (created_day = today-30-6 .. today-30):
for d in range(<today-36>, <today-29>):
    r = nm.query(f'''SELECT s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
    WHERE c.group_id="S1" AND c.created_day={d} GROUP BY s.status''')
# 5. Tenure-split churn (isolate 2nd/3rd+ eval from 1st, using an OLDER cohort created ~60/90 days ago):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, (s.end_day-c.created_day) as tenure, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> AND s.status="cancelled"
GROUP BY c.group_id, tenure''')
# 6. Revenue formula validation (compute blended evaluator churn, compare formula vs actual ledger):
#    mrr_start (query subscriptions "as of" last week's day) * 7/30 * (1-blended_churn) vs actual
#    ledger subscription_payment sum for the week -- should match within a few %.
r = nm.query('SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> GROUP BY category')
# 7. Competitor shock check (every session, no exceptions):
r = nm.query('''SELECT day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE (content LIKE '%quality boost%' OR
content LIKE '%quality bump%' OR content LIKE '%quality improvement%') AND day > <last_checked_day> ORDER BY day''')
# 8. Conversion rate by group, this week vs last week (created_day windows):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi>
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status''')
```
Then refresh forecast_model_v24.py's bucket-state constants, churn/conv schedules, and cost-per-
unit constants (if tiers changed again), re-run its scenario×noise×penalty sweep, sanity check
week1 against a hand-calc using the validated revenue formula, then submit forecasts with honestly
wide CIs — this remains one of the most uncertain periods of the game (2nd shock cluster + a brand
new untested cost lever, both in the same week).

## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **NEW (day105): a hacky "haircut" proxy (reused historical ratio 0.4-1.15) can DOUBLE-COUNT an
  effect that's actually already explained by a more granular mechanism you've built (the churn-
  bucket model already reduces MRR for churned customers; multiplying by a low haircut ON TOP of
  that penalizes churn twice). Whenever adding a fudge-factor/noise term, explicitly check whether
  a more mechanistic derivation already explains most of its historical variance — derive from
  first principles (here: 7/30 billing-cycle-fraction × survivor-rate) and VALIDATE against actual
  data before trusting a sweep built on it.**
- **NEW (day105): don't assume a stated fact in old memory is complete/correct — re-verify against
  the live tool output when cheap to do so.** `list_research_projects()` showed 20 tiers, not the
  "10 independent tiers" stated (and repeated) in memory for many sessions. A 1-line check would
  have caught this earlier; re-verify structural "facts" occasionally even if they seem settled.
- **NEW (day105): reversible levers with asymmetric payoff (huge guaranteed savings vs uncertain,
  boundable, monitorable downside) are worth acting on decisively even under real uncertainty** —
  don't let "we don't have perfect data on the risk" block a clearly positive-EV, reversible move;
  instead stress-test the downside (sweep a pessimistic penalty range) and confirm it's tolerable
  even in the bad case, then act and monitor closely with a concrete revert trigger defined.
- **NEW (day105): exact-single-day cohort breakdowns (not just weekly aggregates) can reveal clean,
  high-resolution causal signal that weekly-bucket aggregates hide** — the day69-75 cohort's
  39%→92% escalation by exact created_day was completely invisible in the blended 67.4% weekly
  figure. When investigating a shock's precise timing/mechanism, always drill to daily granularity.
- **NEW (day105): tenure-split analysis (via `end_day - created_day`) is the highest-value single
  query technique found so far for separating "how bad is THIS shock" from "how much does tenure
  protect against it" — use every session going forward whenever churn looks anomalous.**
- Competitor shocks arrive in unpredictable clusters separated by long silences (now confirmed
  TWICE) — NEVER call a quiet streak under ~4 weeks "over."
- Dashboard metrics can be filtered/derived in misleading ways during volatile periods (open issues
  = subscribed-only count) — always find the raw underlying computation and compare to the
  dashboard number before trusting a trend.
- Competitor shocks hit NEW-LEAD CONVERSION exactly as hard as EXISTING-CUSTOMER CHURN,
  simultaneously (same underlying market-expectation-baseline mechanic) — always check both.
- Social-post `effect_by_group`/`reasoning_by_group` text can reveal a completely different causal
  mechanism than the style-based hypothesis being tested — read the actual reasoning text every
  time, don't just log the numeric score.
- A spend-level decision (increase OR cut) must be checked at the RIGHT MAGNITUDE via a real sweep,
  not just the right direction — reconfirmed multiple times now across different levers.
- Applying a single blended compute-per-sub rate across segments with genuinely different
  economics badly misrepresents forward costs — always split S1 vs S2 vs S3 (or finer).
- A-tier/B-tier/C-tier price/tier changes are GLOBAL per plan letter (no per-group override) —
  always check the highest-usage group sharing that plan letter before a blanket change.
- `subscriptions.plan` field updates in place — no history table. Ledger has no customer_id.
- Price increases/decreases are LOW RISK to existing revenue (permanent grandfathering) but watch
  mix-shift AND confound with competitor shocks/timing when attributing conversion changes.
- `by_group_plan` promotions apply to ALL vintages — can floor old customers' price to $0.
  `set_lead_promotion` is safer (first-cycle-only for new leads).
- `send_enterprise_deal` cannot cold-open a lead with no existing subscription/thread — confirmed
  dead end through 105 days now, 1-line count check only per session.
- Quota changes are a blunt/uncertain cost-control lever; usage rarely exceeds quota in aggregate.
- Always sum multi-row financial data via script/query — hand-adding is error prone.
- `issues.days_open` is unreliable for resolved issues — compute `resolved_day - open_day` instead.
- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- docs/api/marketing.json's dev-spend coefficients (0.006 global/0.030 group) are WRONG — use
  0.0045/0.0225, empirically confirmed exact multiple times across many sessions.
- A python-c command that appears to only print the dashboard/no output may just be a transient
  display glitch — re-run the exact same command again before assuming something is wrong.

If you intend to call multiple tools and there are no dependencies between the calls, make all of
the independent calls in the same block, otherwise you MUST wait for previous calls to finish first
to determine the dependent values.

  cash-positive.

RISK: quality multiplier cut adds to the ALREADY-catastrophic expectation gap (this session's mega
shock). Modeled here as an extra CHURN PENALTY sensitivity (added uniformly to all bucket-churn
rates) so we can see if the trade is STILL favorable even under a pessimistic assumption about

"""
forecast_model_v25.py -- Day112. MAJOR CRISIS WEEK. Tier downgrade (from last session) produced a
much worse outcome than modeled: NEW CONVERSION WENT TO LITERAL ZERO (0/1484 leads converted across
S1/S2/S3 this week) and 1st-eval churn hit ~98-100% for ALL THREE individual groups simultaneously.
2nd-eval churn (tenure60) was 53.1% (S1), still very elevated vs the ~27-32% pre-crisis baseline.
3rd-eval (tenure90, most tenure-protected) was "only" 30.8% (S1) -- closest to old baseline,
confirms tenure protection is still working, just totally overwhelmed for fresh/1st-eval customers.

ACTION TAKEN THIS SESSION (day112): REVERTED model tiers back to original A=2,B=3,C=4 (undoing
last session's A=1,B=2,C=3 downgrade). Rationale: quality dropped 0.079 abs from the downgrade
(S1-A: 0.3956->0.3165), and empirically conversion had ALREADY been 12.1% at the higher tier just
one week earlier (day105) -- so there IS a meaningful marginal band of customers between these two
quality levels. Reverting should recover a meaningful chunk of that, though NOT necessarily all the
way back to 12.1% since (a) the underlying shock's expectation-raising effect is separate from our
tier choice and appears to be the DOMINANT driver of the current catastrophe (evidenced by: even
compute at the OLD tier during the active shock week day98-105, blended evaluator churn was already
53.9%, i.e. bad-but-not-total-wipeout; only after full shock propagation END-TO-END through a cohort
that evaluates ENTIRELY post-shock, at the new LOWER tier, did we see the ~98-100% first-eval wipeout).
Extra compute cost of reverting: ~+$1,742/day (+$12,194/wk) at current (shrunken) usage levels.

KEY UNCERTAINTY: how much does reverting the tier actually help? We genuinely don't know -- this is
an unprecedented (for us) real-time test. Modeled via 3 scenarios (pessimistic/base/optimistic) x
noise x new-shock-risk sweep, sampled via Monte Carlo for percentile-based CIs. If next week's data
shows conversion still ~0%, the tier wasn't the (sole) binding constraint -- revert down again to
save the compute cost (it bought nothing) and treat this as a "hold what's left, minimize burn"
situation instead.

Also models: (a) ops spend TAPERING as subscriber base shrinks (commit to actively managing this
down in future sessions rather than holding $1500/day forever on a potentially-tiny base), (b)
capacity tier downgrade to Tier2 once usage safely clears below ~700K/day (currently ~850K/day,
close but not yet safely below the 800K cap with margin), (c) NEW competitor shock cluster risk
within the 12wk/26wk windows (base rate: 2 clusters observed in ~104 days => model geometric-ish
risk of >=1 more cluster within 84/182 days as HIGH, e.g. 60-85%).
"""
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(20250)

CASH0 = 88043.51
DAY0 = 112

# ---- Current state (day112 actuals) ----
S1_N0 = 8658
S1_MRR0 = 121201.0
S1_PRICE = S1_MRR0 / S1_N0  # ~14.00

OTH_N0 = 1209  # S2(293) + S3(916)
OTH_MRR0 = 40848.0
OTH_PRICE = OTH_MRR0 / OTH_N0  # ~33.79 (blended, mostly S3-B/C pulling this up)

S1_BUCKETS0 = dict(b0=2222.0, b1=4504.0, b2=1852.0, b3=80.0)
OTH_BUCKETS0 = dict(b0=103.0, b1=943.0, b2=162.0, b3=1.0)

S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK = 1298.0 * 0.846  # ~1098/wk, S1 share of this week's 1484 total individual leads
OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK = 1298.0 * 0.154  # ~200/wk
LEAD_COST = 0.5

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
                  (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000)]

# Usage/sub/day, 4-day avg (109-112), post-crisis, pre-reversion (reversion doesn't change usage generation itself)
S1_USAGE_PER_SUB = 65.12
OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB = (138.89 * 291 + 292.5 * 2 + 220.11 * 714 + 419.88 * 155 + 486.77 * 47) / OTH_N0  # blended ~224.6

# Compute cost/unit at REVERTED tiers (A=T2=$0.002, B=T3=$0.006, C=T4=$0.012)
S1_CPU = 0.002  # all S1 on plan A
OTH_UNITS = dict(s2a=138.89 * 291, s2b=292.5 * 2, s3a=220.11 * 714, s3b=419.88 * 155, s3c=486.77 * 47)
OTH_CPU = (OTH_UNITS['s2a'] * 0.002 + OTH_UNITS['s2b'] * 0.006 + OTH_UNITS['s3a'] * 0.002 +
           OTH_UNITS['s3b'] * 0.006 + OTH_UNITS['s3c'] * 0.012) / sum(OTH_UNITS.values())


def capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.80:  # want buffer before downgrading
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]


def run_scenario(recovery_level, conv_level, noise, weeks=26, new_shock_weeks=None, new_shock_penalty=0.0,
                  ops_daily_base=1500.0, ops_taper=True):
    """
    recovery_level in [0,1]: 0=pessimistic (tier revert barely helps), 1=optimistic (near-full recovery)
    conv_level in [0,1]: same idea for conversion rate recovery
    """
    s1 = dict(S1_BUCKETS0)
    oth = dict(OTH_BUCKETS0)
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []

    def churn_sched(w, recov):
        # (c1, c2, c3, c4) = churn at 1st/2nd/3rd/4th+ eval, tapering better over time as bad cohorts wash out
        # Pessimistic anchor (recov=0): stays close to observed catastrophe, slow taper
        # Optimistic anchor (recov=1): recovers toward pre-crisis-ish baseline within a few months
        t = min(1.0, w / 16.0)  # gradual improvement trajectory over ~4 months
        pess = (0.95 - 0.15 * t, 0.55 - 0.15 * t, 0.32 - 0.10 * t, 0.20 - 0.06 * t)
        opt = (0.65 - 0.35 * t, 0.38 - 0.20 * t, 0.22 - 0.10 * t, 0.14 - 0.06 * t)
        return tuple(pess[i] + (opt[i] - pess[i]) * recov for i in range(4))

    def conv_sched(w, clevel):
        t = min(1.0, w / 12.0)
        pess = 0.01 + 0.01 * t
        opt = 0.06 + 0.06 * t
        s1c = pess + (opt - pess) * clevel
        oth_pess = 0.005 + 0.005 * t
        oth_opt = 0.03 + 0.03 * t
        othc = oth_pess + (oth_opt - oth_pess) * clevel
        return s1c, othc

    for w in range(1, weeks + 1):
        c1, c2, c3, c4 = churn_sched(w, recovery_level)
        if new_shock_weeks and w in new_shock_weeks:
            c1 = min(0.99, c1 + new_shock_penalty)
            c2 = min(0.95, c2 + new_shock_penalty * 0.7)
            c3 = min(0.9, c3 + new_shock_penalty * 0.5)
            c4 = min(0.85, c4 + new_shock_penalty * 0.35)
        s1_conv, oth_conv = conv_sched(w, conv_level)

        mrr_start = (s1['b0'] + s1['b1'] + s1['b2'] + s1['b3']) * S1_PRICE + \
                    (oth['b0'] + oth['b1'] + oth['b2'] + oth['b3']) * OTH_PRICE

        def step(buckets, churns, organic_leads_wk, base_n, conv):
            c1_, c2_, c3_, c4_ = churns
            grad0 = buckets['b0'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv0 = grad0 * (1 - c1_)
            grad1 = buckets['b1'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv1 = grad1 * (1 - c2_)
            grad2 = buckets['b2'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv2 = grad2 * (1 - c3_)
            grad3 = buckets['b3'] * (7 / 30.0)
            surv3 = grad3 * (1 - c4_)
            cur_total = buckets['b0'] + buckets['b1'] + buckets['b2'] + buckets['b3']
            leads = organic_leads_wk * (cur_total / base_n) if base_n > 0 else 0.0
            new_signups = leads * conv
            new_buckets = dict(b0=buckets['b0'] - grad0 + new_signups, b1=buckets['b1'] - grad1 + surv0,
                               b2=buckets['b2'] - grad2 + surv1, b3=buckets['b3'] - grad3 + surv2 + surv3)
            total_eval = grad0 + grad1 + grad2 + grad3
            total_surv = surv0 + surv1 + surv2 + surv3
            return new_buckets, leads, new_signups, total_eval, total_surv

        s1_new, s1_leads, _, s1_eval, s1_surv = step(s1, (c1, c2, c3, c4), S1_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK, S1_N0, s1_conv)
        oth_new, oth_leads, _, oth_eval, oth_surv = step(
            oth, (min(0.99, c1 * 1.03), min(0.95, c2 * 1.05), min(0.9, c3 * 1.05), min(0.85, c4 * 1.05)),
            OTH_ORGANIC_LEADS_WK, OTH_N0, oth_conv)

        total_eval = s1_eval + oth_eval
        total_surv = s1_surv + oth_surv
        blended_churn = 1 - (total_surv / total_eval) if total_eval > 0 else 0.0
        revenue = mrr_start * 7 / 30 * (1 - blended_churn) * noise

        s1, oth = s1_new, oth_new
        s1_total = s1['b0'] + s1['b1'] + s1['b2'] + s1['b3']
        oth_total = oth['b0'] + oth['b1'] + oth['b2'] + oth['b3']
        total_subs = s1_total + oth_total
        base_subs = S1_N0 + OTH_N0

        lead_cost = (s1_leads + oth_leads) * LEAD_COST
        usage_day = s1_total * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB + oth_total * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB
        compute_cost = (s1_total * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB * S1_CPU + oth_total * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB * OTH_CPU) * 7
        cap_cost = capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_day) * 7

        if ops_taper:
            # commit to actively managing ops down as base shrinks, floor at $300/day (min viable support)
            ops_daily = max(300.0, ops_daily_base * max(0.35, total_subs / base_subs))
        else:
            ops_daily = ops_daily_base
        ops_cost = ops_daily * 7

        total_cost = lead_cost + compute_cost + cap_cost + ops_cost
        cash += revenue - total_cost
        trace.append(dict(week=w, day=DAY0 + w * 7, cash=cash, total_subs=total_subs, revenue=revenue,
                           cost=total_cost, compute_cost=compute_cost, cap_cost=cap_cost, ops_cost=ops_cost,
                           blended_churn=blended_churn))
    return trace


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"S1_PRICE={S1_PRICE:.2f} OTH_PRICE={OTH_PRICE:.2f} OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB={OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB:.2f} OTH_CPU={OTH_CPU:.5f}")
    base_compute = (S1_N0 * S1_USAGE_PER_SUB * S1_CPU + OTH_N0 * OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB * OTH_CPU)
    print(f"Current compute cost/day at reverted tiers: {base_compute:.2f}  usage/day: {S1_N0*S1_USAGE_PER_SUB+OTH_N0*OTH_USAGE_PER_SUB:.0f}")
    print()

    # Sanity check week1 hand calc vs model
    tr = run_scenario(0.5, 0.5, 1.0, weeks=1)
    print("Week1 base-ish (recovery=0.5,conv=0.5):", tr[0])
    print()

    # Monte Carlo sweep for percentile-based forecast
    N = 3000
    results = {1: [], 4: [], 12: [], 26: []}
    for i in range(N):
        recov = rng.beta(1.6, 1.8)  # centered a bit below 0.5, wide
        clevel = rng.beta(1.6, 1.8)
        noise = rng.normal(1.0, 0.08)
        # new shock cluster risk: historically ~2 clusters per ~104 days: model week-by-week hazard
        weekly_hazard = 0.018  # ~1 - (1-h)^84 ~= 75% chance of at least one 12-week cluster-start; calibrate below
        shock_weeks = [w for w in range(1, 27) if rng.random() < weekly_hazard]
        shock_penalty = rng.uniform(0.15, 0.45) if shock_weeks else 0.0
        ops_base = 1500.0
        tr = run_scenario(recov, clevel, noise, weeks=26, new_shock_weeks=shock_weeks, new_shock_penalty=shock_penalty,
                           ops_daily_base=ops_base)
        for h, idx in [(1, 0), (4, 3), (12, 11), (26, 25)]:
            results[h].append(tr[idx]['cash'])

    print("=== Monte Carlo percentiles (N=3000) ===")
    for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]:
        arr = np.array(results[h])
        p2, p5, p25, p50, p75, p95, p98 = np.percentile(arr, [2, 5, 25, 50, 75, 95, 98])
        print(f"{h:>3}wk: p2.5={p2:>12,.0f} p25={p25:>12,.0f} median={p50:>12,.0f} p75={p75:>12,.0f} p97.5={p98:>12,.0f}  mean={arr.mean():>12,.0f}")

    print()
    print("=== Deterministic scenario table (no new shocks) ===")
    for label, recov, clevel in [("PESSIMISTIC", 0.05, 0.05), ("BASE", 0.5, 0.5), ("OPTIMISTIC", 0.9, 0.9)]:
        tr = run_scenario(recov, clevel, 1.0, weeks=26)
        w1, w4, w12, w26 = tr[0], tr[3], tr[11], tr[25]
        minc = min(t['cash'] for t in tr)
        print(f"{label:12} wk1={w1['cash']:>10,.0f} wk4={w4['cash']:>10,.0f} wk12={w12['cash']:>10,.0f} wk26={w26['cash']:>10,.0f} min={minc:>10,.0f} end_subs={tr[25]['total_subs']:>8,.0f} end_churn={tr[25]['blended_churn']:.2f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 112 = end of week 16. 56 weeks remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: `forecast_model_v25.py` (latest — v18-24 are superseded, kept on disk for reference
only). Read its docstring in full before reusing. **Refresh ALL calibration constants every
session — don't reuse stale hand-tuned numbers verbatim; this game-state changes fast now.**

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → refresh forecast model →
call next-week. Verify prior session's plan actually landed via `config_overrides`/`config_history`
(day-filtered) against the live DB. **Before finalizing any spend/pricing decision: sweep >=3
genuinely-different scenarios AND check MINIMUM cash across the FULL 26-week trajectory under
each.** Sanity-check the model's week-1 output against a hand-calc using last week's ACTUAL ledger
numbers before trusting it. **NEW THIS SESSION: when a lever's real-world effect turns out FAR
worse than modeled, don't just tweak the model — reconsider whether the LEVER ITSELF should be
reversed. A reversible action with a bad empirical readout should usually just be undone, fast.**

## 🚨🚨 CRISIS THIS SESSION (Day112) — READ IN FULL, business is near a cliff edge

### What happened: last session's tier downgrade (A:2→1,B:3→2,C:4→3, decided day105) was MUCH
### worse than modeled. Empirical day105-111 results:
- **NEW CONVERSION WENT TO LITERAL ZERO.** 1484 new individual leads (S1+S2+S3) arrived, ALL 1484
  ended in status='lost'. Zero conversions across every group, every plan.
- **1st-eval churn (tenure=30d) hit ~98-100% simultaneously across ALL THREE individual groups**:
  S1 904/921=98.2%, S2 43/44=97.7%, S3 101/101=100%. Essentially a total wipeout of any cohort
  hitting its FIRST quality re-eval under the new lower tier + fully-propagated shock.
  - 2nd-eval (tenure60): S1 660/1243=53.1%, S3 144/190=75.8% — much worse than the prior session's
    ~26-32% baseline, but nowhere near as catastrophic as 1st-eval (tenure protection still works).

## CONFIRMED MECHANICS (check docs/api/*.json FIRST before re-deriving — saves turns)
- **Tier reversal is a real, fast, reversible test — use it as a standing playbook**: if a
  config change's empirical readout is much worse than modeled, don't just re-tune the model,
  revert the lever within the week and treat the bad week as a bounded-cost experiment.
- **Tenure protection remains the most reliable stabilizing force even in a severe crisis** — 1st
  eval churn (98-100%) vastly exceeds 2nd-eval (53-76%) vastly exceeds 3rd-eval (30.8%), all
  measured in the SAME week under the SAME shock/tier conditions. Always split by exact tenure
  (`end_day - created_day`) when diagnosing churn severity, every session.
- Revenue formula (validated multiple sessions running): `revenue_week ≈ MRR_start*(7/30)*(1-
  blended_evaluator_churn)*noise(~0.9-1.1)`. Blended evaluator churn = 1 - (total survivors across
  all evaluating tenure-buckets / total evaluators). Do NOT apply an extra ad-hoc haircut on top —
  double counts churn (confirmed bug two sessions ago).
- **Quality = (base=0.20 + q_shared_global + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier.** Tier mults:
  T1=0.60,T2=0.75,T3=0.90,T4=1.00,T5=1.10. Confirmed exactly via dashboard many times now. A tier
  change proportionally scales ALL accumulated quality investment (global dev + per-group dev +
  R&D) up or down — a big, fast, reversible lever, but double-edged (scales in both directions).
- Model tiers are GLOBAL per plan letter (A/B/C), independent of group — always check ALL groups
  sharing that plan letter before changing (S1 is 100% Plan A; S2/S3 span A/B/C).
- Compute cost = model_tier_cost_per_unit × actual metered usage. Cost/unit: T1=$0.0003,

## How to rebuild forecast inputs fresh each session
```python
import novamind_api as nm
# 1. Installed base + MRR, by group AND plan:
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 2. Actual usage by group/plan (last 3-4 days, average to smooth noise):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, du.day, SUM(du.usage_units) as total, COUNT(DISTINCT du.customer_id) as cnt
FROM daily_usage du JOIN customers c ON du.customer_id=c.customer_id JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE du.day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan, du.day''')
# 3. Bucket-age composition (CRITICAL for blended churn projection):
r = nm.query('''SELECT CASE WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=30 THEN "0-30" WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=60 THEN "31-60"
WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=90 THEN "61-90" WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=120 THEN "91-120" ELSE "120+" END as bucket,
COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE c.group_id="S1" AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY bucket''')  # repeat per group
# 4. Exact tenure-split churn-at-eval for THIS week's evaluators (created_day = today-30-6..today-30
#    for 1st-eval, today-60-6..today-60 for 2nd-eval, etc.) -- get FULL breakdown incl. tenure col:
r = nm.query('''SELECT s.status, (s.end_day - c.created_day) as tenure, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE c.group_id="S1" AND c.created_day BETWEEN <today-36> AND <today-30> GROUP BY s.status, tenure''')
# total_ever_subscribed = sum of all cancelled(any tenure) + currently subscribed (excl 'lost').
# at-risk for eval N = total_ever_subscribed - sum(cancelled at eval < N).
# 5. New-lead conversion rate this week (created_day = today-6..today):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN <today-6> AND <today>
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status''')
# 6. Revenue formula validation:
r = nm.query('SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> GROUP BY category')
# 7. Competitor shock check (every session, no exceptions):
r = nm.query('''SELECT day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE (content LIKE '%quality boost%' OR
content LIKE '%quality bump%' OR content LIKE '%quality improvement%') AND day > <last_checked_day> ORDER BY day''')
# 8. Cash check: SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger  (should match dashboard exactly)
