## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **NEW (day112): a reversible lever (tier change) can have a MUCH worse real-world effect than
  even a carefully-stress-tested model predicted (modeled "even at +30pp churn penalty" scenarios;
  actual effect was closer to +50-70pp AND a full conversion cliff to zero, a qualitatively
  different failure mode the model didn't capture — a discrete THRESHOLD/cliff effect, not a smooth
  marginal one). When you see a result far outside your modeled range, the right response is fast
  reversal + data-driven re-test, not just re-fitting the model parameters after the fact.**
- **NEW (day112): threshold/cliff effects are real in this simulator** — going from 12.1% to 0%
  conversion off a ~0.08 absolute quality change (not a huge % move) suggests the customer
  expectation distribution can have a lot of mass bunched right around the current quality level,
  making small quality moves have outsized conversion effects near a threshold. Don't assume
  smooth/linear responses to spend or tier changes — verify empirically after any change, quickly.
- **NEW (day112): combining two levers in the same week (tier + lead promo) trades a clean causal
  read for faster crisis response** — justified here given existential stakes and bounded downside
  of the second lever, but remember it confounds next week's diagnosis; plan a follow-up
  single-lever test once the immediate crisis is stabilized.
- **NEW (day112): don't keep repeating the same public reassurance/promise (e.g., "we fixed
  support") if the underlying problem visibly hasn't resolved (customers still posting the same
  complaint weeks later)** — pivot the social post topic to something concretely true and NEW
  instead of eroding credibility with a broken-record promise.
- A hacky "haircut" proxy that double-counts an effect already captured by a more granular model
  (churn-bucket simulation) is a bug — derive from first principles and validate against data.
- Don't assume a stated fact in old memory is complete/correct — re-verify against live tool output
  when cheap to do so (R&D "10 tiers" was actually wrong for many sessions; it's 20).
- Exact-single-day/tenure cohort breakdowns reveal high-resolution causal signal that weekly-
  bucket aggregates hide — always drill to daily/exact-tenure granularity when diagnosing a shock.
- Competitor shocks arrive in unpredictable clusters separated by long silences (confirmed twice) —
  NEVER call a quiet streak under ~4-6 weeks "over."
- Dashboard metrics can be filtered/derived in misleading ways during volatile periods (open issues
  = subscribed-only count, raw count often much higher) — compare both every session.
- Competitor shocks hit NEW-LEAD CONVERSION and EXISTING-CUSTOMER CHURN equally hard, simultaneously
  (same underlying market-expectation-baseline mechanic) — always check both, every session.
- Social-post `effect_by_group`/`reasoning_by_group` text can reveal a completely different causal
  mechanism than the style-based hypothesis being tested — read the actual reasoning text, not just
  the numeric score.
- Applying a single blended compute-per-sub rate across segments with genuinely different
  economics badly misrepresents forward costs — always split S1 vs S2 vs S3 (or finer) by plan.
- A-tier/B-tier/C-tier price/tier changes are GLOBAL per plan letter (no per-group override) —
  always check the highest-usage group sharing that plan letter before a blanket change.
- `subscriptions.plan` field updates in place — no history table. Ledger has no customer_id.
- `by_group_plan` promotions (nm.pricing.set_promotion) apply to ALL vintages — can floor old
  customers' price to $0 if set carelessly. `set_lead_promotion` is safer (first-cycle-only, new
  leads only) — use this one for testing price-side conversion levers with low downside.
- `send_enterprise_deal` cannot cold-open a lead with no existing subscription/thread — confirmed

"""

   promo active the whole time (S1 effectively FREE first month: global $5 + S1 $8 = $13 credit on

   gap is so large that even $0 effective price fails to convert anyone. New-customer acquisition for
   individual segments (S1/S2/S3) is DEAD until a large quality jump (R&D) closes the gap. No more
   money should be spent chasing NEW conversion via price or ads.

   - 1st-eval (created d83-89, evaluating this week, under REVERTED/high tier): S1 94.1% churn
     (n=1166), S2 100%(n=13, tiny), S3 100%(n=55). Compare to last session's low-tier baseline
     (S1 98.2%, S2 97.7%, S3 100%) -- S1 improved ~4pp, others flat/tiny-sample.
   - 2nd-eval (created d53-59): S1 45.3%(n=1856), S2 34.2%(n=76), S3 64.1%(n=256). vs last session's
     low-tier baseline (S1 53.1%, S3 75.8%) -- ~8-12pp improvement, best signal we have.
   - 3rd-eval (created d23-29): S1 34.4%(n=259), S3 63.6%(n=11,tiny). vs last session's low-tier
     30.8% -- actually SLIGHTLY WORSE despite higher tier! (likely just noise/continued drift,
     different week/cohort, not a clean tier-only comparison).
   Net: retention "benefit" of the tier reversion is small (~4-12pp in the two better-sampled reads)
   and inconsistent (3rd-eval went the WRONG way). Extra compute cost of staying at the reverted
   (high) tier was running ~$13-14k/week. NOT a good trade -- REVERTED TIER BACK DOWN AGAIN this

   better retention and did nothing at all for conversion.

   compute spend at the higher tier wasn't paying for itself). Compute cost from ~$16.5k/wk down to
   an estimated ~$2.5-3k/wk at current (shrinking) subscriber counts -- huge structural saving.

   live social posts (day112-119) still complain about multi-day/multi-team ticket delays (this is

   resolution, which the docs say has an outsized effect below/above a ~2-day resolution threshold).
   Bounded, reversible bet -- watch backlog + sentiment next week, revert if no visible improvement.

   cap) is CLOSE but last week saw single-day spikes to 1.15-1.17M even as subs were already

   given continued subscriber attrition will keep pushing usage down.

   change-set to ONE clean, well-evidenced move (tier) plus one bounded bet (ops) this week, rather
   than piling on more untested levers. Did NOT add a NEW ongoing promotion (set_promotion) this
   week despite it being untested -- the $0-price new-lead-conversion failure is a fairly strong
   signal price relief has limited power against the current expectation gap even for existing
   customers (who already get a tenure-bonus quality boost and STILL churn 34-100%), so the
   expected value of adding yet another live experiment this week was low vs. the value of a clean
   read on the SECOND tier reversal's isolated effect next week.
5. SKIPPED social media post this week. Multiple posts as recently as day119 show the SAME
   "ticket bounced between teams" / "waited a week, radio silence" complaints that TWO prior posts
   (day98, day105) already promised to fix. A third repetition of that promise without visible
   delivered improvement risks reading as insincere. Better to let the ops-spend increase actually
   clear backlog for 1-2 weeks, then post with concrete BEFORE/AFTER numbers if it worked.
6. R&D: still unaffordable ($72,450 cash vs $166,667 Tier-1 min). Enterprise: reconfirmed dead
   (0 threads ever, 0 seats, 917 rows). research_market(): still paused, cash too precious.

KEY STRUCTURAL INSIGHT THIS SESSION: the business is now in a NO-REPLENISHMENT DEATH SPIRAL for
the individual segment -- conversion is 0%, so the entire S1/S2/S3 base is pure run-off: each
cohort ages through its 30/60/90/120-day evals and mostly cancels, with ZERO new adds to backfill.
Every week that passes without an R&D breakthrough, the subscriber base and MRR mechanically shrink
via this run-off process, converging toward some small tenure-protected core (or zero) over the
medium term. The ONLY paths back to growth are (a) an R&D quality jump big enough to close the
expectation gap (currently unaffordable, revisit once cash > ~$250-300k) or (b) the expectation
gap somehow stops widening / the market cools (outside our control, no evidence of this happening
-- expectations only drift up, never down, per the mechanics doc).
GIVEN THIS: the objective for the foreseeable future is COST MINIMIZATION + MAXIMIZING RUNWAY,
harvesting whatever revenue the shrinking tenure-protected base still generates, while
accumulating cash toward an eventual R&D bet IF the runway holds up long enough to get there.

rng = np.random.default_rng(20260119)

    """Model: once modeled usage is safely (<80%) under tier2 cap AND we've held for >=1wk, downgrade."""
    if downgraded:
        for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
            if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.75:
                return cost
        return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]
    return current_tier_cost


def run_scenario(churn_drift_per_wk, conv_recovery_prob_per_wk, ops_helps, new_shock_prob_per_wk,
                  rnd_trigger_cash, weeks=26, noise_scale=1.0):
    """
    churn_drift_per_wk: additive drift to all churn rates per week (expectations only get worse
        over time absent R&D) -- small positive number, e.g. 0.001-0.004/wk
    conv_recovery_prob_per_wk: tiny chance conversion un-sticks partially (e.g. if a competitor
        stumbles, or market cools) -- modeled as a rare stochastic event
    ops_helps: bool/float multiplier on how much the ops-spend bump actually reduces churn (0=no
        effect at all, 1=full modeled effect of ~3-5pp improvement)
    new_shock_prob_per_wk: probability of a NEW competitor shock cluster hitting in a given week,
        which further raises expectations (permanent additional churn-rate step-up)
    rnd_trigger_cash: cash threshold at which we commit to R&D tier 1 (one-shot, if reached)
    """
    state = {g: dict(buckets=dict(d['buckets']), n=d['n'], mrr=d['mrr'], avg_price=d['avg_price'],
                      usage_per_sub=d['usage_per_sub'], cpu_blend=d['cpu_blend'])
              for g, d in GROUPS.items()}
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    capacity_cost = 1330.0  # Tier3 currently
    downgraded_capacity = False
    ops_daily = OPS_DAILY
    rnd_active = None  # (weeks_remaining, quality_boost) once triggered
    quality_multiplier_boost = 0.0  # cumulative effective churn-reduction from a landed R&D boost

    # base churn schedule (this week's fresh empirical read, by eval-bucket index 0..3)
    base_churn = {
        'S1': [0.941, 0.453, 0.344, 0.30],
        'S2': [0.97, 0.342, 0.35, 0.30],
        'S3': [0.98, 0.641, 0.55, 0.35],

        week_lead_cost = 0.0
        total_usage_day = 0.0

        shock_now = rng.random() < new_shock_prob_per_wk
        shock_bump = 0.0

            shock_bump = max(0.0, shock_bump)

        # R&D trigger check (one-shot bet once cash comfortably clears threshold)
        if rnd_active is None and cash > rnd_trigger_cash:
            cost = rng.choice([166667.0, 250000.0])  # tier1-ish cost range
            if cash - cost > 40000:  # don't blow ourselves down to near-zero doing it
                cash -= cost
                dur = max(20, rng.normal(45, 20))
                boost = max(0.02, rng.normal(0.08, 0.04))  # modest tier1-ish quality boost, noisy

            rnd_active[0] -= 7
            if rnd_active[0] <= 0:
                quality_multiplier_boost += rnd_active[1]
                rnd_active = None

        drift = churn_drift_per_wk * w  # cumulative drift, worse over time
        drift -= quality_multiplier_boost * 1.2  # R&D boost offsets drift materially if landed
        ops_relief = 0.04 * ops_helps  # modest flat churn-rate improvement if ops bump is working
        conv_unstuck = rng.random() < conv_recovery_prob_per_wk
        conv_rate = 0.0 if not conv_unstuck else rng.uniform(0.01, 0.05)

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 119 = end of week 17. 55 weeks remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: `forecast_model_v26.py` (latest — v18-25 superseded, kept on disk for reference
only). Read its docstring in full before reusing. **Refresh ALL calibration constants every
session — don't reuse stale hand-tuned numbers verbatim; this game-state changes fast.**

## ⚠️ PROCESS DISCIPLINE (read this first every session)
Budget turns: gather data → decide → ACT (tool calls) → update memory → refresh forecast model →
call next-week. Verify prior session's plan actually landed via direct tool-call return values
and/or `config_history`/`config_overrides` (day-filtered) against the live DB.
**Before finalizing any spend/pricing decision: sweep >=3 genuinely-different scenarios AND check
MINIMUM cash across the FULL 26-week trajectory under each.** Sanity-check the model's week-1
output against a hand-calc using last week's ACTUAL ledger numbers before trusting it.
**When a lever's real-world effect turns out FAR worse (or weaker) than modeled, don't just tweak
the model — reconsider whether the LEVER ITSELF should be reversed.** A reversible action with a
bad empirical readout should usually just be undone, fast (confirmed working playbook 2 sessions
running now — see below).
**NEW THIS SESSION: it's OK to flip-flop WITHIN a session if new analysis changes your mind before
you advance the week** (I bumped ops to $2000 then reverted to $1500 same session after building
the forecast model and realizing the cash-runway risk outweighed the uncertain retention benefit —
zero cost to doing this since only the FINAL config state before `next-week` matters).
**Widen forecast CIs beyond the raw Monte Carlo output** — repeated experience shows actual outcomes
land outside naively-modeled ranges (cliff effects, shock clusters). Treat the model's raw
percentiles as a floor for width, not the final answer; manually widen, especially at 12wk/26wk.

## 🚨 STRUCTURAL DIAGNOSIS (as of Day119) — read this first, it reframes the whole strategy

**Individual-segment new-customer acquisition is CONFIRMED STRUCTURALLY DEAD.** Two consecutive
weeks (day105-112, day112-119) at literally 0% new-lead conversion across S1+S2+S3 (0/1484, then
0/1242 — 100% status='lost' both weeks), tested at BOTH a low model tier (A1/B2/C3, low quality)
AND the reverted-up tier (A2/B3/C4, quality back near pre-crisis ~0.39-0.53), AND with an
aggressive lead promotion active making S1's effective first-month price ~$0 (global $5 + S1 $8 =
$13 credit on a $13 price). **Zero conversions at effectively-free price proves PRICE is not the
binding constraint for new leads — the quality/expectation gap is now so wide that ~the entire
sampled lead distribution fails to clear it, regardless of price.** New-customer acquisition via
price cuts, ads, or promotions is pure waste right now — do not spend on it. The ONLY thing that
could fix this is a large R&D quality jump (unaffordable for now, see below).

**Retention (tier reversion effect) is mixed/modest, NOT worth big compute spend.** Comparing the
low-tier week (day105-111) to the reverted-tier week (day112-119) for the SAME eval-stage:
- 1st-eval (tenure~30d): S1 98.2%→94.1% churn (~4pp better), S2 97.7%→100%(tiny n), S3 100%→100%.
- 2nd-eval (tenure~60d): S1 53.1%→45.3% (~8pp better), S3 75.8%→64.1% (~12pp better) — best signal.
- 3rd-eval (tenure~90d): S1 30.8%→34.4% — actually SLIGHTLY WORSE despite higher tier (likely
  noise/continued drift/different cohort, not a clean tier-only effect).
Net: at most ~4-12pp retention improvement from paying full price for the high tier, costing an
extra ~$13-14k/week in compute. NOT a good trade. **Reverted tier back DOWN AGAIN this session**
(A=2→1, B=3→2, C=4→3) to bank the compute savings — this is the SECOND reversal of this lever;
treat it as settled for now (don't flip back up again without a genuinely new reason/evidence).

**Conclusion: this is now a NO-REPLENISHMENT DEATH SPIRAL for the individual segment.** Zero new
conversions means the entire S1/S2/S3 base is pure run-off — each cohort ages through its
30/60/90/120-day evals and mostly cancels (34-100% depending on tenure-bucket), with nothing
backfilling the funnel. Absent an R&D breakthrough, subscriber count and MRR mechanically shrink
toward some small tenure-protected core (or zero) over the coming months. **Strategy has shifted
from "fight the crisis" to "minimize cost / maximize runway / harvest declining revenue while
accumulating cash toward a possible future R&D bet."**

## ACTIONS TAKEN THIS SESSION (day119, ~1-day lag to ledger)
1. **Reverted model tiers back DOWN: A=2→1, B=3→2, C=4→3** (undoing last session's reversion-up).

   failure is decent evidence price has limited power against the current gap even accounting for

5. **Skipped social media post this week.** Multiple posts as recent as day119 show the SAME

6. **R&D**: still unaffordable ($72,450 cash vs $166,667 Tier-1 min cost). **Enterprise**: reconfirmed
   dead (0 threads ever, 0 seats, 917 `customer_type='large'` rows) — 1-line check only, as usual.
   **research_market()**: still paused, cash too precious to spend $25k on a 30%-odds discovery now.
7. **No new competitor shock found day105-119** (checked `social_media_posts` for shock-language,
   none since day105) — still a quiet streak, but per standing lesson, NEVER assume a cluster is over.

## STATUS as of Day 119 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 126 will be next dashboard)
Cash: $72,449.60 (down from $88,044, -$15,594/wk — but this reflects LAST week's OLD high-tier
compute cost + $1500 ops; this session's changes should roughly halve that burn rate going forward,

### Ledger ground-truth, last 7 days (day113-119), USE THIS not hand-waving estimates:
compute -$16,521 | operations -$10,500 | capacity -$9,310 | lead_acquisition -$573 | development $0

**Key stress signal: fixed costs alone (ops+capacity=$19,810/wk) almost equal ALL revenue collected

## How to rebuild forecast inputs fresh each session
```python
import novamind_api as nm
# 1. Installed base + MRR, by group AND plan:
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 2. Actual usage by group/plan (last 4 days, average to smooth noise):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, du.day, SUM(du.usage_units) as total, COUNT(DISTINCT du.customer_id) as cnt
FROM daily_usage du JOIN customers c ON du.customer_id=c.customer_id JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE du.day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan, du.day''')
# 3. Bucket-age composition (CRITICAL for blended churn projection):
r = nm.query('''SELECT CASE WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=30 THEN "0-30" WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=60 THEN "31-60"
WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=90 THEN "61-90" WHEN (<today>-c.created_day)<=120 THEN "91-120" ELSE "120+" END as bucket,
COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE c.group_id="S1" AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY bucket''')  # repeat per group
# 4. Exact tenure-split churn-at-eval for THIS week's evaluators (created_day = today-30-6..today-30
#    for 1st-eval, today-60-6..today-60 for 2nd-eval, etc.) -- get FULL breakdown incl. tenure col:
r = nm.query('''SELECT s.status, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE c.group_id="S1" AND c.created_day BETWEEN <today-36> AND <today-30> GROUP BY s.status''')
# denominator = cancelled+subscribed (excl 'lost'). churn% = cancelled/(cancelled+subscribed).
# 5. New-lead conversion rate this week (created_day = today-6..today):
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN <today-6> AND <today>
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status''')
# 6. Revenue formula validation:
r = nm.query('SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN <lo> AND <hi> GROUP BY category')
# 7. Competitor shock check (every session, no exceptions):
r = nm.query('''SELECT day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE (content LIKE '%quality boost%' OR
content LIKE '%quality bump%' OR content LIKE '%quality improvement%') AND day > <last_checked_day> ORDER BY day''')
# 8. Cash check: SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger  (should match dashboard exactly)
# 9. Config sanity check: re-issue set_* calls and read the RETURN VALUE directly (immediate,
#    reliable) rather than relying on config_history (has ~1-session lag before it updates).
```

## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **NEW (day119): a lever that seemed well-evidenced (tier reversion UP for retention) turned out
  to deliver only a small, inconsistent benefit (4-12pp on 2/3 measured buckets, WORSE on the 3rd)
  once actually measured against its true cost (~$13-14k/wk compute) — re-reverted it back down.
  Second confirmation that this simulator's quality/tier levers can have much weaker real effects
  than they first appear; always compute $-cost-vs-benefit explicitly before keeping a change.**
- **NEW (day119): don't assume a spend increase is good just because it addresses a visible pain
  point (support complaints) — I initially bumped ops to $2000, then caught myself and reverted
  after modeling the cash-runway impact. The lesson: model the FULL cash trajectory BEFORE locking
  in a spend increase, not after; a plausible-sounding qualitative story (docs describe a mechanism)
  isn't the same as evidence the mechanism is large enough to matter here.**
- **NEW (day119): `get_group_insights` quality-floor estimates can be wildly wrong/stale relative to
  actual empirical conversion behavior** (0.081 estimated floor vs 0% conversion at 0.39 delivered
  quality) — always trust empirical data over these noisy model-estimate fields.
- **NEW (day119): when nearly all the base's revenue is consumed by FIXED costs alone (ops+capacity
  ≈ weekly revenue collected), that's a five-alarm signal to cut fixed costs immediately** — compute
  this ratio explicitly every session (`SUM(ops+capacity ledger)` vs `SUM(subscription_payment
  ledger)` for the same week) as a standing crisis-detection check.
- **NEW (day119): confirmed conversion is 0% at BOTH a low tier AND a high tier, AND at ~$0 price —
  this is strong triangulating evidence that quality/expectation gap, not price or (modest) tier
  differences, is now the sole binding constraint on new-customer acquisition.** Stop spending on
  ads/promotions/price cuts to chase new individual conversions until/unless a big R&D quality jump
  happens; it is confirmed wasted money right now.
- A hacky "haircut" proxy that double-counts an effect already captured by a more granular model
  (churn-bucket simulation) is a bug — derive from first principles and validate against data.
- Don't assume a stated fact in old memory is complete/correct — re-verify against live tool output
  when cheap to do so (R&D "10 tiers" was actually wrong for many sessions; it's 20).
- Exact-single-day/tenure cohort breakdowns reveal high-resolution causal signal that weekly-
  bucket aggregates hide — always drill to daily/exact-tenure granularity when diagnosing a shock.
- Competitor shocks arrive in unpredictable clusters separated by long silences (confirmed twice) —
  NEVER call a quiet streak under ~4-6 weeks "over."
- Dashboard metrics can be filtered/derived in misleading ways during volatile periods (open issues
  = subscribed-only count, raw count often much higher) — compare both every session.
- Competitor shocks hit NEW-LEAD CONVERSION and EXISTING-CUSTOMER CHURN equally hard, simultaneously
  (same underlying market-expectation-baseline mechanic) — always check both, every session.
- Social-post `effect_by_group`/`reasoning_by_group` text can reveal a completely different causal
  mechanism than the style-based hypothesis being tested — read the actual reasoning text, not just
  the numeric score. Also: good social sentiment scores do NOT necessarily translate into actual
  conversion/retention movement — the hard quality-price gate seems to operate somewhat independently.
- Applying a single blended compute-per-sub rate across segments with genuinely different
  economics badly misrepresents forward costs — always split S1 vs S2 vs S3 (or finer) by plan.
- A-tier/B-tier/C-tier price/tier changes are GLOBAL per plan letter (no per-group override) —
  always check the highest-usage group sharing that plan letter before a blanket change. (Though
  note: a plan letter with FEW customers, e.g. Plan C at 39 total, is a cheap/contained place to
  experiment with a tier change without much blast radius — see candidate idea #9 above.)
- `subscriptions.plan` field updates in place — no history table. Ledger has no customer_id.
- `by_group_plan`/`by_group` promotions (nm.pricing.set_promotion) apply to ALL vintages — can floor
  old customers' price if set carelessly, but this is also exactly what makes it useful for
  defending existing-customer retention (unlike set_lead_promotion which only hits new signups).
- `send_enterprise_deal` cannot cold-open a lead with no existing subscription/thread — confirmed
  dead end through 119 days now, 1-line count check only per session.
- Quota changes are a blunt/uncertain cost-control lever; usage rarely exceeds quota in aggregate.
- Always sum multi-row financial data via script/query — hand-adding is error prone.
- `issues.days_open` is unreliable for resolved issues — compute `resolved_day - open_day` instead.
- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- docs/api/marketing.json's dev-spend coefficients (0.006 global/0.030 group) are WRONG — use
  0.0045/0.0225, empirically confirmed exact multiple times across many sessions.
- A python-c command that appears to only print the dashboard/no output may just be a transient
  display glitch — re-run the exact same command again before assuming something is wrong.

"""

(day119) + THIS session's new moves (capacity downgrade, ops cut, S1 promo test, quota raise).

WHAT HAPPENED DAY119-126 (ground truth from ledger + queries, see MEMORY.md for full detail):
- Compute cost confirmed collapsed to $2,838/wk (vs ~$16,521/wk at the higher tier) -- the tier-
  down decision's cost benefit is fully validated, exactly as estimated. This is now SETTLED,
  don't re-litigate without major new evidence.
- Conversion: STILL 0% (896 new leads, 100% lost). Third consecutive week at 0%. Structural.
- Churn got WORSE across the board vs last week, even though tier was HELD CONSTANT (same A1/B2/
  C3 as day105-112's baseline): S1 1st/2nd/3rd-eval = 99.8%/61.6%/56.9% (vs day112-119's
  94.1%/45.3%/34.4% at the HIGHER tier, and vs day105-112's 98.2%/53.1%/30.8% at this SAME tier).
  S3 2nd-eval jumped especially hard: 64.1% -> 90.2%. This strongly suggests continued/accelerating
  quality-expectation DRIFT is the dominant force (not tier per se) -- churn worsened even at
  matched tier, comparing across just ~2 calendar weeks. Drift rate implied by the matched-tier
  comparison (53.1%->61.6% over ~2 weeks with a confound in between) is far larger than v26 assumed
  (v26 used 0.0005-0.004/wk additive; implied here is roughly 0.01-0.02/wk) -- WIDENED drift range
  substantially this version to reflect this, while acknowledging high uncertainty (small-n,
  confounded comparison, could easily be partly cohort noise not pure drift).
- No shock-language posts found day119-126, but posts DO show a new complaint theme: usage
  rate-limiting frustration ("burned through cap in 3 weeks", "rate limits mid-project", "switched
  to Claude API") on TOP of the pre-existing support-ticket-speed complaints. Also new quality
  complaints ("hallucinates more than Claude", "half-baked ideas") -- consistent with our OWN tier
  cuts lowering delivered quality, not necessarily a new competitor shock.

ACTIONS THIS SESSION (day126):
1. Capacity Tier3->Tier2 (confirmed via tool return: 800K cap, $530/day, saves $800/day=$5600/wk).
   Justified by fresh usage recalc: per-current-subscriber cyclical usage pattern (clean 7-day cycle,
   confirmed stable across 29 days of history, day98-126, no anomalous spikes beyond the cycle)
   peaks at ~677K/day at TODAY's subscriber mix -- 15%+ headroom under 800K cap, and base will keep
   shrinking (no replenishment) so headroom should only grow. Prior sessions' "spike to 1.15-1.17M"
   concern was just the SAME cyclical peak at a LARGER historical subscriber base, not an anomaly --
   resolved that uncertainty this session with a full 29-day per-customer-rate history check.
2. Ops $1500->$1000/day (saves $500/day=$3500/wk). Resolution capacity formula (0.6x spend) gives
   ~600/day=4200/wk vs this week's opened-issue rate 5428/wk -- a bit short, backlog may tick up
   modestly for a few weeks, but backlog is currently low (1103 open, subscribed-only) and opened-
   rate should keep falling as the base shrinks further. Outage-prevention saturates well below this
   spend per docs; ops's marginal value here is backlog-clearing speed only, a secondary churn lever.
3. Ongoing promotion test (NEW, first use of this lever): set_promotion(by_group={'S1': 5.0}). $5/mo
   flat deduction on ALL S1 vintages (avg price $14.06 -> effective ~$9.06, ~36% off), applied at
   each customer's NEXT billing eval (gradual full rollout over ~4-5wks as each customer's own
   anniversary passes). Rationale: existing customers have a tenure-loyalty quality cushion (up to
   +0.13 at 12mo) that NEW leads (tested at $0 effective price, still 0% conversion) don't have --
   so price relief might tip marginal EXISTING customers into "quality sufficient" territory even
   though it didn't for brand-new leads. Genuinely untested -- modeled as a wide sweep parameter.
4. Usage quotas raised A=400->600, B=800->1200, C=1500->2500. Justified by direct query: 142/343
   (41%!) of S3 Plan-A customers were within 20 units of their OLD quota cap, 17/69 S3-B, 1 S3-C
   customer sitting at EXACTLY 1500 (hard-capped). This is a real, quota-BOUND constraint for a
   meaningful chunk of our highest-value segment (S3, quality-focused, highest price/quality) and
   directly matches this week's social-media rate-limit complaints. Realistic added-usage estimate
   (only quota-bound customers moving, not the whole group maxing the new cap) is small (~20K/day),
   safely within the new Tier2 cap's headroom.
5. Posted social media reply (agent_post_id=16) to the rate-limit complaint post, announcing the
   quota increase -- honest, concrete, addresses a CURRENT unresolved complaint (unlike the last two
   sessions' support-ticket promises which were already made and not clearly delivered on).
6. R&D still unaffordable ($70,680 cash vs $166,667 Tier1 min). Enterprise reconfirmed dead (0
   threads, 0 seats). Tiers/dev/ad-spend/lead-promo held unchanged (all previously-settled decisions).

KEY UNCERTAINTY THIS VERSION: is the accelerating churn a genuine faster drift-rate (bad, means
harvest-mode runway is shorter than v26 assumed) or partly noise/small-n/confounded-comparison
artifacts (in which case v26-like slower drift may resume)? Sweep BOTH possibilities widely.
Also new and fully untested: does the S1 promotion help retention at all? Sweep 0 (no effect) to
a meaningfully optimistic case. Manually widen CIs further beyond raw Monte Carlo per standing process.
"""
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(20260126)

CASH0 = 70679.717
DAY0 = 126

# ---- Current state (day126 actuals, freshly queried) ----
# usage_per_sub = clean 7-day-cycle average (day117-123), stable across 29 days of history.
# cpu_blend = $/unit blended across plans within the group at CURRENT (low) tier costs
#   (A=T1=$0.0003/unit, B=T2=$0.002/unit, C=T3=$0.006/unit).
GROUPS = {
    'S1': dict(n=5225.0, mrr=73489.0, avg_price=73489.0 / 5225,
               buckets=dict(b0=413.0, b1=1204.0, b2=3195.0, b3=413.0),  # +1 from 120+ folded into b3
               usage_per_sub=75.66, cpu_blend=0.0003, has_promo=True),
    'S2': dict(n=201.0, mrr=3407.0, avg_price=3407.0 / 201,
               buckets=dict(b0=4.0, b1=88.0, b2=109.0, b3=0.0),
               usage_per_sub=(153.80 * 200 + 283.14 * 1) / 201,
               cpu_blend=(153.80 * 200 * 0.0003 + 283.14 * 1 * 0.002) / (153.80 * 200 + 283.14 * 1),
               has_promo=False),
    'S3': dict(n=434.0, mrr=16312.0, avg_price=16312.0 / 434,
               buckets=dict(b0=8.0, b1=154.0, b2=260.0, b3=12.0),
               usage_per_sub=(247.49 * 343 + 469.11 * 69 + 557.71 * 22) / 434,
               cpu_blend=(247.49 * 343 * 0.0003 + 469.11 * 69 * 0.002 + 557.71 * 22 * 0.006) / (
                           247.49 * 343 + 469.11 * 69 + 557.71 * 22),
               has_promo=False),
}

# Leads scale with current subscriber base (2 data points: 1242@7882=0.1576, 896@5860=0.1529/sub --
# fairly consistent organic/referral-driven ratio). 0% conversion baseline, confirmed 3 weeks running.
LEAD_RATE_PER_SUB = 0.153
LEAD_COST = 0.5

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
                  (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000)]

OPS_DAILY0 = 1000.0  # cut this session from 1500
BASE_N0 = sum(d['n'] for d in GROUPS.values())  # 5860

RND_TIER1_COST = 166667.0


def capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_per_day):
    """Pick the cheapest tier that safely (<=90%) covers usage_per_day; used for reactive upgrade
    if modeled usage unexpectedly grows past Tier2 (defensive -- we don't expect this to trigger)."""
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.90:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]


def run_scenario(churn_drift_per_wk, conv_recovery_prob_per_wk, new_shock_prob_per_wk,
                  rnd_trigger_cash, promo_benefit_pp, quota_usage_bump, weeks=26, noise_scale=1.0):
    state = {g: dict(buckets=dict(d['buckets']), n=d['n'], mrr=d['mrr'], avg_price=d['avg_price'],
                      usage_per_sub=d['usage_per_sub'] * (1 + quota_usage_bump if g == 'S3' else 1 + quota_usage_bump * 0.3),
                      cpu_blend=d['cpu_blend'], has_promo=d['has_promo'])
             for g, d in GROUPS.items()}
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    ops_daily = OPS_DAILY0
    rnd_active = None
    quality_boost_landed = 0.0

    base_churn = {
        'S1': [0.998, 0.616, 0.569, 0.55],
        'S2': [1.00, 0.575, 0.55, 0.55],
        'S3': [1.00, 0.902, 0.656, 0.55],
    }

    cluster_weeks_remaining = 0
    cumulative_shock_level = 0.0

    for w in range(1, weeks + 1):
        week_revenue = 0.0
        week_compute_cost = 0.0
        week_lead_cost = 0.0
        total_usage_day = 0.0

        if cluster_weeks_remaining <= 0 and rng.random() < new_shock_prob_per_wk:
            cluster_weeks_remaining = rng.integers(2, 7)
        if cluster_weeks_remaining > 0:
            step = max(0.0, rng.normal(0.045, 0.025) * noise_scale)
            cumulative_shock_level += step
            cluster_weeks_remaining -= 1
        shock_bump = cumulative_shock_level

        if rnd_active is None and cash > rnd_trigger_cash:
            cost = rng.choice([166667.0, 250000.0])
            if cash - cost > 40000:
                cash -= cost
                dur = max(20, rng.normal(45, 20))
                boost = max(0.02, rng.normal(0.08, 0.04))
                rnd_active = [dur, boost]

        if rnd_active is not None:
            rnd_active[0] -= 7
            if rnd_active[0] <= 0:
                quality_boost_landed += rnd_active[1]
                rnd_active = None

        drift = churn_drift_per_wk * w
        drift -= quality_boost_landed * 1.2
        conv_unstuck = rng.random() < conv_recovery_prob_per_wk
        conv_rate = 0.0 if not conv_unstuck else rng.uniform(0.01, 0.05)

        total_n_start = sum(d['n'] for d in state.values())

        for g, d in state.items():
            churn_sched = base_churn[g]
            promo_relief = promo_benefit_pp if d['has_promo'] else 0.0
            b = d['buckets']
            new_b = dict(b0=0.0, b1=0.0, b2=0.0, b3=0.0)
            evaluators_total = 0.0
            survivors_total = 0.0

            frac_eval = 7.0 / 30.0
            for i, key in enumerate(['b0', 'b1', 'b2', 'b3']):
                bucket_n = b[key]
                evaluating = bucket_n * frac_eval
                staying_in_bucket = bucket_n - evaluating
                cr = churn_sched[i] + drift + shock_bump - promo_relief
                cr = min(0.995, max(0.03, cr + rng.normal(0, 0.035) * noise_scale))
                survivors = evaluating * (1 - cr)
                evaluators_total += evaluating
                survivors_total += survivors
                if key != 'b3':
                    nxt = ['b1', 'b2', 'b3'][i]
                    new_b[nxt] += survivors
                else:
                    new_b['b3'] += survivors
                new_b[key] += staying_in_bucket

            leads_this_wk = total_n_start * LEAD_RATE_PER_SUB * rng.uniform(0.85, 1.15)
            week_lead_cost += leads_this_wk * LEAD_COST
            new_converts = leads_this_wk * conv_rate
            new_b['b0'] += new_converts

            d['buckets'] = new_b
            d['n'] = sum(new_b.values())

            eff_price = d['avg_price'] - (5.0 if d['has_promo'] else 0.0)
            eff_price = max(eff_price, 0.5)
            week_revenue += survivors_total * eff_price * rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1)

            usage_day = d['n'] * d['usage_per_sub']
            total_usage_day += usage_day
            week_compute_cost += usage_day * 7 * d['cpu_blend']

        capacity_cost = capacity_cost_for_usage(total_usage_day)

        total_n = sum(d['n'] for d in state.values())
        ops_daily = max(250.0, OPS_DAILY0 * (total_n / BASE_N0))

        week_costs = week_compute_cost + ops_daily * 7 + capacity_cost * 7 + week_lead_cost
        cash += week_revenue - week_costs
        trace.append(dict(week=w, cash=cash, n=total_n, revenue=week_revenue, costs=week_costs,
                           usage=total_usage_day))

    return cash, trace


def summarize(cash_samples):
    arr = np.array(cash_samples)
    return dict(mean=arr.mean(), p2_5=np.percentile(arr, 2.5), p25=np.percentile(arr, 25),
                p50=np.percentile(arr, 50), p75=np.percentile(arr, 75), p97_5=np.percentile(arr, 97.5))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    N = 4000
    horizons = {'1wk': 1, '4wk': 4, '12wk': 12, '26wk': 26}
    results = {h: [] for h in horizons}
    min_cash_traces = []

    for i in range(N):
        # WIDENED drift range this version -- matched-tier week-over-week comparison implied much
        # faster drift (~0.01-0.02/wk) than v26 assumed (0.0005-0.004/wk). Sweep BOTH regimes since
        # true cause (pure drift vs cohort noise/confound) is genuinely uncertain.
        churn_drift = rng.uniform(0.0005, 0.018)
        conv_recovery_p = rng.uniform(0.0, 0.03)
        shock_p = rng.uniform(0.02, 0.09)
        rnd_trigger = rng.uniform(180000, 260000)
        promo_benefit_pp = rng.uniform(0.0, 0.18)  # fully untested -- wide sweep, 0=no effect
        quota_bump = rng.uniform(0.0, 0.15)  # modest realistic usage uptick from quota raise
        noise = rng.uniform(0.7, 1.5)

        cash_final, trace = run_scenario(churn_drift, conv_recovery_p, shock_p, rnd_trigger,
                                          promo_benefit_pp, quota_bump, weeks=26, noise_scale=noise)
        tw = {t['week']: t['cash'] for t in trace}
        min_cash_traces.append(min(t['cash'] for t in trace))
        for hname, hweeks in horizons.items():
            results[hname].append(tw[hweeks])

    for hname in horizons:
        s = summarize(results[hname])
        print(hname, {k: round(v, 0) for k, v in s.items()})

    print('min-cash-over-26wk-trajectory distribution:',
          {k: round(v, 0) for k, v in summarize(min_cash_traces).items()})
    frac_negative = np.mean(np.array(min_cash_traces) < 0)
    print('fraction of scenarios ever going negative over 26wk:', round(frac_negative, 3))

"""
forecast_model_v28.py -- Day126 (Week18). MAJOR STRUCTURAL FIX vs v26/v27: replaces the crude
"4-bucket, 7/30-of-bucket-evaluates-uniformly" approximation with an EXACT per-day tenure
histogram simulation. This matters a lot -- discovered this session that the bucket-uniform
assumption was significantly WRONG because historical signups came in clumps (past ad campaigns /
promotions ran for specific weeks, not continuously), so the tenure distribution is lumpy, not
smooth. Concretely: next week (day127-133), EXACT tenure data shows 1866/5225 (35.7%!) of S1 will
hit an eval boundary (413 at the 30d mark, 920 at 60d, 511 at 90d, 22 at 120d) -- vs the old bucket
model's uniform estimate of only ~1219 (23.3% flat). The old model was UNDERSTATING near-term
churn volume by ~53%. This version fixes that by simulating each exact tenure value day-by-day.

METHOD: for each group, maintain a numpy array indexed by exact tenure (days). Each simulated day:
shift everyone's tenure +1, then for anyone landing EXACTLY on a multiple of 30 (their eval day),
apply that eval-number's churn rate (1st/2nd/3rd/4th eval empirical, 5th+ uses a fallback), removing
churned customers and letting survivors continue. New leads (currently ~0% convert) enter at
tenure=0. This is exact/mechanistic, not a bucket approximation, and matches the real per-customer
30-day billing-cycle mechanic described in the sim docs precisely.

BASE DATA (day126 exact tenure histograms saved to tenure_histogram_day126.json this session):
S1 n=5225 (100% Plan A), S2 n=201 (200A+1B), S3 n=434 (343A+69B+22C).
MRR: S1=$73,489 (avg $14.06), S2=$3,407 (avg $16.95), S3=$16,312 (avg $37.59).

FRESH CHURN-AT-EVAL (day119-126 evaluators, see MEMORY.md for full derivation) -- WORSE than 2
weeks ago at the SAME tier (A1/B2/C3), suggesting continued/accelerating expectation drift is the
dominant force, not tier: S1=[.998,.616,.569,.55*] S2=[1.0,.575,.55*,.55*] S3=[1.0,.902,.656,.55*]
(*=fallback, insufficient/no sample this week for that eval stage).

SESSION DECISIONS (all confirmed via tool return values):
1. Capacity Tier3->Tier2 (800K cap, $530/day, saves $5,600/wk). Fresh usage recalc (29-day clean
   per-customer cyclical pattern, no anomalous spikes ever found) shows ~15%+ headroom at peak
   under Tier2 even before further shrinkage. Also raised quotas (#3 below) which adds modest usage
   -- realistic (not worst-case) added-usage estimate still leaves comfortable headroom.
2. Ops $1500->$1000/day (saves $3,500/wk). Resolution capacity (~0.6x spend) roughly tracks this
   week's opened-issue rate; backlog (1103, subscribed-only) is low and should keep shrinking as
   base shrinks. Ops's marginal effect on churn is unproven/secondary per docs (outage-prevention
   saturates far below this spend level) -- treating this purely as a bounded backlog-management cost.
3. Usage quotas raised A=400->600,B=800->1200,C=1500->2500 -- 41% of S3-Plan-A customers were
   within 20 units of the OLD cap (one dead-on at exactly 1500), directly matching this week's
   social-media rate-limit complaints. Cheap (only quota-bound customers actually use more).
4. Posted social reply (id16) re: the quota increase -- honest, addresses a live, current complaint.
5. TESTED THEN REVERSED an S1 ongoing promotion ($5/mo) WITHIN this same session, before advancing.
   Built 3-way Monte Carlo comparison (promo-swept-benefit vs promo-cost-only vs no-promo) and found
   "no promo" clearly dominated (mean 26wk cash -$8,153 vs -$18,573 vs -$20,783) -- the certain ~36%
   revenue cut is large & immediate, the retention benefit is pure speculation, and the new-lead
   $0-price test (0% conversion even at zero price) argues price relief has limited power against a
   quality-gap-driven problem. Reversed back to $0 before calling next-week (config is free/instant
   to change; confirmed via tool return). Live game state = promo never happened.
6. R&D unaffordable ($70,680 cash vs $166,667 Tier1). Enterprise reconfirmed dead (0 threads ever).

HEADLINE FINDING THIS VERSION (even with the more precise engine): the individual segment, under
a naive "current rates persist + drift" extrapolation, implies a severe multi-month decline (0%
conversion + 55-100% churn per eval compounds fast: e.g. steady 55%/cycle churn over 6 cycles =>
~0.8% of the ORIGINAL cohort survives). This is a genuine structural risk, not a modeling artifact
-- but treat the FAR-out (12wk/26wk) magnitude with real skepticism (heterogeneity within cohorts,
i.e. survivors increasingly being a self-selected "hard core" with probably-lower true ongoing
churn than the population-average rate we're extrapolating, is NOT captured by this model and would
make reality less severe than shown here) -- hence still manually widen CIs upward beyond the raw
Monte Carlo, especially at 12wk/26wk, on TOP of the wide sweep already built in.

import numpy as np
import json

rng = np.random.default_rng(20260126)

CASH0 = 70679.717
DAY0 = 126
MAX_TENURE = 500  # headroom for 26wk = 182 days beyond current max observed tenure (~122)

with open('tenure_histogram_day126.json') as f:
    _hist = json.load(f)

GROUP_META = {
    'S1': dict(avg_price=73489.0 / 5225, usage_per_sub=75.66, cpu_blend=0.0003, s3_like=False),
    'S2': dict(avg_price=3407.0 / 201,
               usage_per_sub=(153.80 * 200 + 283.14 * 1) / 201,
               cpu_blend=(153.80 * 200 * 0.0003 + 283.14 * 1 * 0.002) / (153.80 * 200 + 283.14 * 1),
               s3_like=False),
    'S3': dict(avg_price=16312.0 / 434,
               usage_per_sub=(247.49 * 343 + 469.11 * 69 + 557.71 * 22) / 434,
               cpu_blend=(247.49 * 343 * 0.0003 + 469.11 * 69 * 0.002 + 557.71 * 22 * 0.006) / (
                           247.49 * 343 + 469.11 * 69 + 557.71 * 22),
               s3_like=True),
}

BASE_CHURN = {
    'S1': [0.998, 0.616, 0.569, 0.55],
    'S2': [1.00, 0.575, 0.55, 0.55],
    'S3': [1.00, 0.902, 0.656, 0.55],
}

LEAD_RATE_PER_SUB = 0.153  # leads/week per existing sub (organic/referral, consistent across 2 data pts)
LEAD_COST = 0.5

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
                  (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000)]

OPS_DAILY0 = 1000.0
BASE_N0 = 5225 + 201 + 434
RND_TIER1_COST = 166667.0


def make_initial_arrays():
    arrs = {}
    for g, h in _hist.items():
        a = np.zeros(MAX_TENURE + 10)
        for t_str, n in h.items():
            t = int(t_str)
            if t < len(a):
                a[t] = n
        arrs[g] = a
    return arrs


def capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.90:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]


def eval_rate(g, mult_index, drift, shock_bump):
    """mult_index: 1=30d eval, 2=60d, 3=90d, 4=120d, 5+=fallback (uses last available)."""
    sched = BASE_CHURN[g]
    base = sched[min(mult_index - 1, len(sched) - 1)]
    cr = base + drift + shock_bump
    return min(0.995, max(0.02, cr))


def run_scenario(churn_drift_per_wk, conv_recovery_prob_per_wk, new_shock_prob_per_wk,
                  rnd_trigger_cash, quota_usage_bump, weeks=26, noise_scale=1.0):

    cash = CASH0
    trace = []

    quality_boost_landed = 0.0

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

kept on disk for reference only, do NOT reuse their churn engine, see below). Read its docstring in
full before reusing. **Refresh ALL calibration constants every session.**

## 🚨🚨 MODELING BREAKTHROUGH THIS SESSION (Day126) — read this before building any forecast

**The old "4-bucket, uniform 7/30-of-bucket-evaluates-per-week" churn model (v18-v27) was
STRUCTURALLY WRONG and significantly overstated long-run decline.** Discovered by pulling the
EXACT per-day tenure histogram (`SELECT (today - created_day) as tenure, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY
tenure`) and finding it is NOT uniformly spread — it's lumpy/clumped because historical signups
happened in campaign-driven bursts, not continuously. Example (day126, S1): tenure 25-29 has 413
people (100% of the "0-30" bucket!) all clustered right at the edge of their 30-day eval, about to
ALL evaluate within the next 5 days — not a smooth 23.3%/week trickle. Next-week eval load for S1
was 1866/5225 (35.7%!) vs the old bucket model's flat assumption of ~1219 (23.3%).
**Why this mattered so much for the FORECAST (not just precision):** the old bucket model, by
sampling a flat 7/30 of each bucket EVERY week forever, kept re-exposing a large population to the
harshest rate (1st-eval, ~99.8% churn) indefinitely, because the bucket only geometrically decayed
(23.3%/wk outflow) rather than actually emptying out. In reality, that population is a ONE-TIME
historical cohort that evaluates in a concentrated burst and then is GONE (no replenishment at
tenure=0 since conversion is 0%) — the 99.8% rate only really bites ONCE (this concentrated wave),
not smoothly re-applied to a phantom "still 76.7%-full" bucket for months. Net effect: the bucket
model showed cash going NEGATIVE by ~week 20-26 (median ~-$7,800 at 26wk); the corrected EXACT
model shows cash staying POSITIVE throughout 26wk (median ~$22,900, 0% chance of going negative in
the model's own scenarios — though I still manually widened the lower tail for real-world model risk).
**NEW METHOD (use every session going forward):**
```python
import novamind_api as nm, json
out = {}
for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    r = nm.query(f'SELECT ({{today}} - c.created_day) as tenure, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s '
                 f'JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.group_id="{{g}}" AND '
                 f's.status="subscribed" GROUP BY tenure ORDER BY tenure')
    out[g] = {{row['tenure']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}}
json.dump(out, open('tenure_histogram_dayNNN.json','w'))
```
Then simulate forward with a numpy array indexed by EXACT tenure day (size ~500), shifting +1/day,
applying the appropriate eval-stage churn rate whenever tenure hits an exact multiple of 30 (1st
eval=30d, 2nd=60d, 3rd=90d, 4th=120d, 5th+=fallback rate), letting survivors continue, adding new
leads at tenure=0 (currently ~0 given 0% conversion). This is MECHANISTICALLY exact (matches the
sim's real 30-day billing-cycle-per-customer mechanic) rather than a smoothing approximation.
Runs fast (numpy day-by-day loop, ~2500 draws x 26wk in ~12s). See `forecast_model_v28.py` in full.
**ALWAYS use this exact-tenure method going forward, never revert to the old bucket approximation.**

# 1. Installed base + MRR, by group AND plan:
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 2. EXACT tenure histogram (THE critical input now, replaces bucket table):
out = {}
for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    r = nm.query(f'SELECT ({today} - c.created_day) as tenure, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s '
                 f'JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.group_id="{g}" AND '
                 f's.status="subscribed" GROUP BY tenure ORDER BY tenure')
    out[g] = {row['tenure']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
json.dump(out, open(f'tenure_histogram_day{today}.json','w'))
# 2b. Next-week eval load sanity check (how many evaluate in each of the next 7 days):
for g,h in out.items():

    print(g, sum(v for t,v in h.items() for mult in [30,60,90,120,150] if mult-7<=t<=mult-1))
# 3. Actual usage by group/plan (last 7-10 days, to capture the full weekly cycle):
r = nm.query(f'''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, du.day, SUM(du.usage_units) as total, COUNT(DISTINCT du.customer_id) as cnt
FROM daily_usage du JOIN customers c ON du.customer_id=c.customer_id JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE du.day BETWEEN {today-9} AND {today} AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan, du.day''')
# 4. Exact eval-stage churn for THIS week's evaluators (created_day = today-30-6..today-30 for 1st
#    eval, today-60-6..today-60 for 2nd, etc.) -- get full status breakdown:
for lo,hi in [(today-36,today-30),(today-66,today-60),(today-96,today-90),(today-126,today-120)]:
    r = nm.query(f'''SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN {lo} AND {hi}
    GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status''')
# denominator = cancelled+subscribed (excl 'lost'). churn% = cancelled/(cancelled+subscribed).
# 5. New-lead conversion rate this week:
r = nm.query(f'''SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today}
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status''')
# 6. Revenue/cost formula validation:
r = nm.query(f'SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today} GROUP BY category')
# 7. Competitor shock check (every session, no exceptions) -- keyword search AND read full posts:
r = nm.query(f'''SELECT day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE day > {today-14} ORDER BY day''')
# 8. Cash check: SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger  (should match dashboard exactly)
# 9. Config sanity check: re-issue set_* calls and read the RETURN VALUE directly (immediate,
#    reliable) rather than relying on config_history (has ~1-session lag before it updates).
# 10. R&D affordability + enterprise dead-check (1-line each):
print(nm.research.list_research_projects()['tiers'][0])  # cost/status of tier1

- **NEW (day126, BIG ONE): the bucket-based churn model (7/30-of-bucket-evaluates-uniformly) was
  structurally wrong because real signup history is lumpy/clumped, not uniform — it artificially
  prolongs exposure to harsh early-eval churn rates for months instead of one concentrated wave,
  making long-run forecasts far too pessimistic. Always pull the EXACT tenure histogram and
  simulate off real 30-day eval boundaries. This was a forecast-accuracy issue, not a decision
  error, but a big one — probably the single highest-value modeling fix of the game so far.**
- **NEW (day126): modeled a speculative promo BEFORE committing and reversed within the session
  when the Monte Carlo comparison showed it was negative-EV** — confirms the "flip-flop within a
  session is free and good practice" lesson from last session generalizes well; do this for ANY
  new lever whose cost is certain/large and whose benefit is speculative, especially when cash is
  tight. Don't rely on "plausible mechanism" stories (tenure-loyalty cushion) without modeling the
  actual $ trade-off against the certain cost.
- **NEW (day126): checked per-CUSTOMER max usage (not just group averages) and found a meaningful
  quota-bound subset (41% of S3-A) even though the group's blended average usage was well under
  quota** — always check distributional/tail behavior, not just averages, before concluding a lever
  (like quotas) doesn't matter.
- Churn getting WORSE at a matched/held-constant tier (day105-112 vs day119-126, same A1/B2/C3)
  is strong evidence that continuous expectation DRIFT, not tier, is now the dominant force —
  don't keep re-attributing observed churn changes to whichever lever was most recently touched;
  always check for a same-tier/same-lever comparison across time before attributing causally.
- A hacky "haircut" proxy that double-counts an effect already captured by a more granular model
  is a bug — derive from first principles and validate against data (this cost us dearly with the
  bucket model — always sanity check a model's mechanism against exact underlying data, not just
  its aggregate outputs looking "reasonable").
- Don't assume a stated fact in old memory is complete/correct — re-verify against live tool output
  when cheap (R&D tier count was wrong for many sessions; assumed-uniform tenure distribution was
  wrong this session — both cost real accuracy before being caught).
- Exact-day/tenure cohort breakdowns reveal high-resolution causal signal that weekly-bucket
  aggregates hide — ALWAYS drill to exact-day granularity, not just 30-day buckets, when the
  population's history might be non-uniform (which it usually is, given campaigns/promotions ran
  for specific historical windows).
- Competitor shocks arrive in unpredictable clusters separated by long silences — NEVER call a
  quiet streak (even 21+ days now) "over"; also read full post CONTENT each session, not just
  keyword-matched subsets, since new complaint themes (rate-limiting) emerged that keyword search
  for "quality boost/competitor/launch" completely missed.
- Social-post `reasoning_by_group` text can reveal a different causal mechanism than the hypothesis
  being tested — read the actual text. Good sentiment scores do NOT reliably predict conversion/
  retention movement — the hard quality-price gate operates somewhat independently of sentiment.
- Applying a single blended compute-per-sub rate across segments with different economics badly
  misrepresents forward costs — always split by group AND plan.
- A/B/C-tier price/tier changes are GLOBAL per plan letter (no per-group override) — always check
  the highest-usage group sharing that plan letter before a blanket change.
- `subscriptions.plan` field updates in place — no history table. Ledger has no customer_id.
- `send_enterprise_deal` cannot cold-open a lead with no existing subscription/thread — confirmed
  dead end through 126 days now, 1-line count check only per session.
- Quota changes are a genuinely useful, CHEAP lever when a real quota-bound subset exists — check
  per-customer max usage, don't dismiss quotas as "blunt" without checking distributional data.
- Always sum multi-row financial data via script/query — hand-adding is error prone.
- `issues.days_open` is unreliable for resolved issues — compute `resolved_day - open_day` instead.
- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- docs/api/marketing.json's dev-spend coefficients (0.006 global/0.030 group) are WRONG — use
  0.0045/0.0225, empirically confirmed exact multiple times across many sessions.
- A python-c command that appears to only print the dashboard/no output may be a transient display

METHOD: for each group, maintain a numpy array indexed by exact tenure (days). Each simulated day:
shift everyone's tenure +1, then for anyone landing EXACTLY on a multiple of 30 (their eval day),
apply that eval-number's churn rate (1st/2nd/3rd/4th eval empirical, 5th+ uses a fallback), removing
churned customers and letting survivors continue. New leads (currently ~0% convert) enter at
tenure=0. This is exact/mechanistic, not a bucket approximation, and matches the real per-customer
30-day billing-cycle mechanic described in the sim docs precisely.

BASE DATA (day126 exact tenure histograms saved to tenure_histogram_day126.json this session):
S1 n=5225 (100% Plan A), S2 n=201 (200A+1B), S3 n=434 (343A+69B+22C).
MRR: S1=$73,489 (avg $14.06), S2=$3,407 (avg $16.95), S3=$16,312 (avg $37.59).

dominant force, not tier: S1=[.998,.616,.569,.55*] S2=[1.0,.575,.55*,.55*] S3=[1.0,.902,.656,.55*]
(*=fallback, insufficient/no sample this week for that eval stage).

1. Capacity Tier3->Tier2 (800K cap, $530/day, saves $5,600/wk). Fresh usage recalc (29-day clean
   per-customer cyclical pattern, no anomalous spikes ever found) shows ~15%+ headroom at peak
   under Tier2 even before further shrinkage. Also raised quotas (#3 below) which adds modest usage
   -- realistic (not worst-case) added-usage estimate still leaves comfortable headroom.
2. Ops $1500->$1000/day (saves $3,500/wk). Resolution capacity (~0.6x spend) roughly tracks this

   $0-price test (0% conversion even at zero price) argues price relief has limited power against a
   quality-gap-driven problem. Reversed back to $0 before calling next-week (config is free/instant
   to change; confirmed via tool return). Live game state = promo never happened.
6. R&D unaffordable ($70,680 cash vs $166,667 Tier1). Enterprise reconfirmed dead (0 threads ever).

HEADLINE FINDING THIS VERSION (even with the more precise engine): the individual segment, under
a naive "current rates persist + drift" extrapolation, implies a severe multi-month decline (0%
conversion + 55-100% churn per eval compounds fast: e.g. steady 55%/cycle churn over 6 cycles =>
~0.8% of the ORIGINAL cohort survives). This is a genuine structural risk, not a modeling artifact
-- but treat the FAR-out (12wk/26wk) magnitude with real skepticism (heterogeneity within cohorts,
i.e. survivors increasingly being a self-selected "hard core" with probably-lower true ongoing
churn than the population-average rate we're extrapolating, is NOT captured by this model and would
make reality less severe than shown here) -- hence still manually widen CIs upward beyond the raw
Monte Carlo, especially at 12wk/26wk, on TOP of the wide sweep already built in.

import numpy as np
import json

rng = np.random.default_rng(20260126)

CASH0 = 70679.717
DAY0 = 126
MAX_TENURE = 500  # headroom for 26wk = 182 days beyond current max observed tenure (~122)

with open('tenure_histogram_day126.json') as f:
    _hist = json.load(f)

GROUP_META = {
    'S1': dict(avg_price=73489.0 / 5225, usage_per_sub=75.66, cpu_blend=0.0003, s3_like=False),
    'S2': dict(avg_price=3407.0 / 201,
               usage_per_sub=(153.80 * 200 + 283.14 * 1) / 201,
               cpu_blend=(153.80 * 200 * 0.0003 + 283.14 * 1 * 0.002) / (153.80 * 200 + 283.14 * 1),
               s3_like=False),
    'S3': dict(avg_price=16312.0 / 434,
               usage_per_sub=(247.49 * 343 + 469.11 * 69 + 557.71 * 22) / 434,
               cpu_blend=(247.49 * 343 * 0.0003 + 469.11 * 69 * 0.002 + 557.71 * 22 * 0.006) / (
                           247.49 * 343 + 469.11 * 69 + 557.71 * 22),
               s3_like=True),
}

BASE_CHURN = {
    'S1': [0.998, 0.616, 0.569, 0.55],
    'S2': [1.00, 0.575, 0.55, 0.55],
    'S3': [1.00, 0.902, 0.656, 0.55],
}

LEAD_RATE_PER_SUB = 0.153  # leads/week per existing sub (organic/referral, consistent across 2 data pts)
LEAD_COST = 0.5

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50000, 85), (200000, 215), (800000, 530), (2500000, 1330),
                  (8000000, 4000), (25000000, 10000), (80000000, 28000), (300000000, 75000)]

OPS_DAILY0 = 1000.0
BASE_N0 = 5225 + 201 + 434
RND_TIER1_COST = 166667.0


def make_initial_arrays():
    arrs = {}
    for g, h in _hist.items():
        a = np.zeros(MAX_TENURE + 10)
        for t_str, n in h.items():
            t = int(t_str)
            if t < len(a):
                a[t] = n
        arrs[g] = a
    return arrs


def capacity_cost_for_usage(usage_per_day):
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if usage_per_day <= cap * 0.90:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]


def eval_rate(g, mult_index, drift, shock_bump):
    """mult_index: 1=30d eval, 2=60d, 3=90d, 4=120d, 5+=fallback (uses last available)."""
    sched = BASE_CHURN[g]
    base = sched[min(mult_index - 1, len(sched) - 1)]
    cr = base + drift + shock_bump
    return min(0.995, max(0.02, cr))


def run_scenario(churn_drift_per_wk, conv_recovery_prob_per_wk, new_shock_prob_per_wk,
                  rnd_trigger_cash, quota_usage_bump, weeks=26, noise_scale=1.0):
    arrs = make_initial_arrays()
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    rnd_active = None
    quality_boost_landed = 0.0
    cluster_weeks_remaining = 0
    cumulative_shock_level = 0.0

    usage_per_sub = {}
    for g, meta in GROUP_META.items():
        bump = quota_usage_bump if meta['s3_like'] else quota_usage_bump * 0.3
        usage_per_sub[g] = meta['usage_per_sub'] * (1 + bump)

    for w in range(1, weeks + 1):
        if cluster_weeks_remaining <= 0 and rng.random() < new_shock_prob_per_wk:
            cluster_weeks_remaining = rng.integers(2, 7)
        if cluster_weeks_remaining > 0:
            step = max(0.0, rng.normal(0.045, 0.025) * noise_scale)
            cumulative_shock_level += step
            cluster_weeks_remaining -= 1
        shock_bump = cumulative_shock_level

        if rnd_active is None and cash > rnd_trigger_cash:
            cost = rng.choice([166667.0, 250000.0])
            if cash - cost > 40000:
                cash -= cost
                dur = max(20, rng.normal(45, 20))
                boost = max(0.02, rng.normal(0.08, 0.04))
                rnd_active = [dur, boost]
        if rnd_active is not None:
            rnd_active[0] -= 7
            if rnd_active[0] <= 0:
                quality_boost_landed += rnd_active[1]
                rnd_active = None

        drift = churn_drift_per_wk * w
        drift -= quality_boost_landed * 1.2
        conv_unstuck = rng.random() < conv_recovery_prob_per_wk
        conv_rate = 0.0 if not conv_unstuck else rng.uniform(0.01, 0.05)

        week_revenue = 0.0
        week_compute_cost = 0.0
        week_lead_cost = 0.0
        total_usage_day_list = []

        for day in range(7):
            day_revenue = 0.0
            for g, arr in arrs.items():
                meta = GROUP_META[g]
                total_n_before = arr.sum()
                # shift tenure +1
                new_arr = np.zeros_like(arr)
                new_arr[1:] = arr[:-1]
                overflow = arr[-1]  # anyone at max tenure just stays lumped (rare/negligible)
                new_arr[-1] += overflow

                # apply churn exactly at multiples of 30
                for mult in range(30, MAX_TENURE, 30):
                    if mult < len(new_arr) and new_arr[mult] > 0:
                        k = mult // 30
                        cr = eval_rate(g, k, drift, shock_bump)
                        cr = min(0.995, max(0.02, cr + rng.normal(0, 0.035) * noise_scale))
                        n_at = new_arr[mult]
                        survivors = n_at * (1 - cr)
                        day_revenue += survivors * meta['avg_price'] * rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1)
                        new_arr[mult] = survivors

                # new leads at tenure 0 (organic, scales with current base; 0% conv baseline)
                leads_today = (total_n_before * LEAD_RATE_PER_SUB / 7.0) * rng.uniform(0.85, 1.15)
                week_lead_cost += leads_today * LEAD_COST
                new_arr[0] += leads_today * conv_rate

                arrs[g] = new_arr

            week_revenue += day_revenue
            total_usage_today = sum(arrs[g].sum() * usage_per_sub[g] for g in arrs)
            total_usage_day_list.append(total_usage_today)
            for g in arrs:
                week_compute_cost += arrs[g].sum() * usage_per_sub[g] * GROUP_META[g]['cpu_blend']

        avg_usage_day = np.mean(total_usage_day_list)
        capacity_cost = capacity_cost_for_usage(max(total_usage_day_list))  # size for the PEAK day, safer

        total_n = sum(arrs[g].sum() for g in arrs)
        ops_daily = max(200.0, OPS_DAILY0 * (total_n / BASE_N0))

        week_costs = week_compute_cost + ops_daily * 7 + capacity_cost * 7 + week_lead_cost
        cash += week_revenue - week_costs
        trace.append(dict(week=w, cash=cash, n=total_n, revenue=week_revenue, costs=week_costs,
                           usage=avg_usage_day))

    return cash, trace


def summarize(cash_samples):
    arr = np.array(cash_samples)
    return dict(mean=arr.mean(), p2_5=np.percentile(arr, 2.5), p25=np.percentile(arr, 25),
                p50=np.percentile(arr, 50), p75=np.percentile(arr, 75), p97_5=np.percentile(arr, 97.5))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    N = 800  # day-level sim is heavier; reduced N for runtime, still plenty for stable percentiles
    horizons = {'1wk': 1, '4wk': 4, '12wk': 12, '26wk': 26}
    results = {h: [] for h in horizons}
    min_cash_traces = []

    for i in range(N):
        churn_drift = rng.uniform(0.0005, 0.018)
        conv_recovery_p = rng.uniform(0.0, 0.03)
        shock_p = rng.uniform(0.02, 0.09)
        rnd_trigger = rng.uniform(180000, 260000)
        quota_bump = rng.uniform(0.0, 0.15)
        noise = rng.uniform(0.7, 1.5)

        cash_final, trace = run_scenario(churn_drift, conv_recovery_p, shock_p, rnd_trigger,
                                          quota_bump, weeks=26, noise_scale=noise)
        tw = {t['week']: t['cash'] for t in trace}
        min_cash_traces.append(min(t['cash'] for t in trace))
        for hname, hweeks in horizons.items():
            results[hname].append(tw[hweeks])

    for hname in horizons:
        s = summarize(results[hname])
        print(hname, {k: round(v, 0) for k, v in s.items()})

    print('min-cash-over-26wk-trajectory distribution:',
          {k: round(v, 0) for k, v in summarize(min_cash_traces).items()})
    frac_negative = np.mean(np.array(min_cash_traces) < 0)
    print('fraction of scenarios ever going negative over 26wk:', round(frac_negative, 3))

FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 2. EXACT tenure histogram (critical input, replaces bucket table):

for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:

                 f'JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.group_id="{g}" AND '
                 f's.status="subscribed" GROUP BY tenure ORDER BY tenure')
    out[g] = {row['tenure']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}

JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE du.day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today} AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
