# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 140 = end of week 20. 52 weeks remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: **`forecast_model_v30.py`** (latest). v18-29 superseded/stale. **v30 has a MAJOR
methodology upgrade over v28/29 — see below. Read its docstring before reusing.**

## 🚨🚨 BIGGEST FINDING THIS SESSION (Day140): churn-at-eval calibration method was OVERSTATING
## true hazard — new clean week-over-week method gives a much more favorable (and validated) schedule

**Old method (used day126→133 sessions):** snapshot a `created_day` cohort's CURRENT status
(cancelled vs subscribed) at various ages. PROBLEM: for cohorts older than 30d, this is
CUMULATIVE survival through MULTIPLE eval passes, not the marginal rate at any single eval — it
compounds and overstates true per-eval hazard, especially at eval#2/3/4.

**New method (adopt permanently):** save `tenure_histogram_dayN.json` every session (already doing
this). Next session, compare `tenure_histogram_day(N-7).json` to the current one: for each tenure
`T` in the old file, check `T+7` in the new file. If a 30-day-multiple boundary falls in `(T, T+7]`,
`marginal_churn = 1 - count_at(T+7) / count_at(T)`. This isolates the churn hazard AT EXACTLY one
eval, cleanly. **Validated by a PERFECT sanity check: cohorts NOT crossing any boundary show
survival = 1.000 exactly** (confirms billing/eval happens ONLY at exact 30-day multiples, zero
attrition in between — matches documented mechanic exactly, gives high confidence in the method).

**Fresh results (2 data points each, day126→133 and day133→140 transitions):**
| Group | eval#1 (30d) | eval#2 (60d) | eval#3 (90d) | eval#4 (120d) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 99.8% (n=413) | 69.7%(n=920)/94.3%(n=35)→~71% | 57.1%(n=511)/50.4%(n=617)→~54% | 22.7%(n=22)/49.0%(n=49)→~41% |
| S2 | 100%(n=4) | 76.9%(n=65)/100%(n=1) | 100%(n=1)/0%(n=2) — all thin/noisy |
| S3 | 100%(n=8) | 89.7%(n=146) | 83.1%(n=59)/92.9%(n=56)→~88% | 100%(n=1, noise) |

**Key insight:** marginal churn DECLINES monotonically & substantially with eval number for S1
(99.8%→71%→54%→41%, best-sampled group) — a much more optimistic shape than the old cumulative
method implied (which read 85-99% at eval#2/3, badly overstated by compounding). This is
mechanistically consistent with tenure-loyalty bonus + survivorship (see prior session's finding,
now on firmer footing). **ALSO: the day127-130 competitor shock cluster does NOT show a clear
jump in this cleaner metric** (S1 eval#3 was STABLE/slightly IMPROVED 57.1%→50.4% straddling the
shock window) — casts real doubt on last session's "shock causes +12-24pt marginal churn jumps"
claim, which was likely a methodological artifact of the flawed cumulative-cohort snapshot, not a
genuine shock signature. Tempered shock frequency/magnitude assumptions back down in v30
accordingly (shocks are still real — visible continuously in social posts, raise expectations per
documented mechanics — just harder to detect a large quantitative bite in any single week's actual
churn data than previously assumed; could still be there but diluted/gradual rather than a sharp spike).
**Action for next session: repeat this week-over-week comparison again (day140→147) to get a 3rd
data point per eval stage and further tighten the calibration — especially eval#2 which is still
noisy (35-920 sample range) and eval#4 (thin, 22-49).**

## STATUS as of Day 140 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 147 will be next dashboard)
Cash: $60,038.94 (down -$6,219 from day133's $66,258 — bigger drop than prior week's -$4,421,
BUT this decline was expected/consistent: bigger eval wave (1085 total S1+S2+S3 vs prior ~700) +
still-elevated churn rates). **Calibration check: LAST session's 1wk forecast was
[56500,63000] pt 59900 — actual $60,039 landed almost exactly on point estimate. Excellent
calibration, validates the exact-tenure-histogram engine.**
Individual Subs: 3845 (S1=3507 all Plan A, S2=145 [144A+1B], S3=193 [164A/24B/5C]). MRR: S1
$49,561 (avg $14.13), S2 $2,427 (avg $16.74), S3 $5,756 (avg $29.82) = $57,744 total (down from
$63,624 at day133). New leads day134-140: 474 (S1 ~410/S2 23/S3 41 lost), **100% lost, ZERO
conversions — 5th week running.** Cancellations this week: 422. Enterprise: still 0 seats, 0
threads ever (reconfirmed).

### Ledger ground-truth, last 7 days (day134-140):
capacity -$3,710 | compute -$1,134 | operations -$4,900 (old $700/day config, ~1-day lag as
usual — this session's NEW $800/day takes effect day140+) | lead_acquisition -$250 | development $0
| subscription_payment +$3,775 | **NET -$6,219**.

### Issue backlog rising — ops bumped 700→800/day this session
Backlog (subscribed-only, properly filtered): 750 (day133) → **1122 (day140), +49%**, even as base
shrank 4267→3845 (-10%). Root cause CONFIRMED precisely: issues opened/day held steady ~420-480
throughout, but **resolved/day fell from ~600-650 (day127-133, at $1000 ops) to ~380-420
(day134-140, at $700 ops)** — exact match to the `resolution_capacity ≈ 0.6×ops_spend` formula
(0.6×1000=600 ✓, 0.6×700=420 ✓, confirmed yet again). Net backlog growth ~+40-80/day at $700 ops.
**Action: bumped ops $700→$800/day this session** (0.6×800=480/day resolved, should slightly
exceed the ~450/day opened rate and start shrinking backlog again). Cost: +$100/day=+$700/wk —
modest, worth it given multiple NEW social posts this week specifically about slow support
("ghosted", "crickets", "support ticket limbo... waiting over a week", 3+ such posts day140).
Note: effect of resolution speed on ACTUAL churn remains structurally unproven (churn seems
dominated by the hard quality-price gate per the eval data), but cost is small and downside-protection
against reputation cascade seems worth it. **Recheck backlog trend next session — if it's
shrinking again at $800, consider tapering further as base keeps shrinking; if still growing,
reconsider a bigger bump.**

## 🆕 PRICE CUT EXPERIMENT LAUNCHED THIS SESSION (Day140) — FREE, zero downside
**Cut prices: A $13→$6, B $115→$55, C $180→$85.** Rationale: `set_prices` ONLY affects NEW
signups going forward — existing 3845 subs keep their grandfathered price forever (confirmed
mechanic, re-verified in docs). Since new-lead conversion has been EXACTLY 0% for 5+ weeks
running, there is **zero downside** to testing a much lower price (existing revenue totally
unaffected) and **some chance of upside** if price (not quality) is the binding constraint for
some segment. Supporting clue: `get_group_insights()` noisy (info_level=1, ±65%) estimates show
S2's `quality_floor_q_min`≈0.37 is CLOSE to our delivered S2-A quality (0.3765) — S2 specifically
might be quality-gated (price cut alone may not help S2 much). S1's floor≈0.081 and S3's≈0.145 are
both well below our delivered quality (0.31/0.42) — puzzling if quality is the true gate for them;
more likely a steep price-dependent component of the curve (which we can't see directly) or
reputation-driven suppression is really binding for S1/S3. **Since eval#1 (30-day) churn is
ROCK-SOLID at ~99-100% across every read so far (multiple weeks, multiple groups, decent S1
sample n=413+), even IF the price cut revives conversion, most new converts will likely churn at
their first 30-day eval regardless — temper expectations, this is more an information-value/
low-cost-optionality play than a likely cash savior.** Also fixed an edge case: S1's lead_promotion
was $8/mo (from before) which would exceed the new $6 price (zero/negative first month) — reduced
S1 lead promo to $3/mo. Current lead promo: global $5, S1 $3, S2 $10, S3 $10.
**Action for next session: check new-lead conversion rate specifically — did ANY leads convert
this week that didn't before? If yes, price was (part of) the answer — consider ad spend to scale.
If still 0%, price is not the binding constraint — quality/reputation is, and this lever is a dead
end; consider reverting prices to reduce any tiny long-tail revenue risk (though probably harmless
either way given no one is converting).**

## R&D CORRECTION: 20 tiers total, not 10 (memory error, fixed this session)
`docs/tables/research_projects.json`: **20 independent tiers** (not 10 as previously written in
memory) — Tiers 1-10 standard R&D ($166,667–$1,666,667, +0.04 to +0.85 mean quality), Tiers 11-20
"frontier moonshots" (higher cost/timeline/variance, e.g. tier 11 $2.5M/+1.1, up to presumably
tier20 much larger — didn't see full tier 18-20 costs this session, check `list_research_projects()`
fully next time if ever relevant). Still totally unaffordable now ($60,039 cash vs $166,667 Tier1
minimum) — not actionable, just correcting the fact for future reference.

## Usage & cost calibration (Day140)
Per-customer usage (7-day avg, current subs): S1-A=75.96/day (flat vs 75.75 last wk), S2-A=159.41
(~flat), S2-B=207.57(n=1), S3-A=277.62 (down slightly from 284.21), S3-B=496.47 (down from
511.45), S3-C=501.03 (down from 583.95) — usage-per-survivor drift has PAUSED/reversed slightly
this week (previously it kept rising every session) — worth rechecking, may just be noise from a
smaller surviving population. Daily usage totals last 14d: ranged 231,717–662,402, highly
volatile. **Capacity: stay Tier2 ($530/day, 800K cap)** — even recent LOW days (~231-285K) are
close to Tier1's 200K cap with little margin, and high days (585-662K) need Tier2 comfortably.
Quota-bound check: S3-A 25/164 (15.2%) near-quota (≥90%), consistent with recent sessions, no
action needed. Compute cost confirmed ≈ usage × tier_unit_cost (T1=$0.0003) — small vs
capacity/ops, not a major lever.

## ACTIONS TAKEN THIS SESSION (Day140)
1. **Price cut (free experiment):** A $13→$6, B $115→$55, C $180→$85. See section above.
2. **Ops $700→$800/day** (+$700/wk) to arrest issue-backlog growth (750→1122 this week). See above.
3. **Fixed S1 lead_promotion** $8→$3 (was about to exceed new $6 price, edge case avoided).
4. **Held unchanged:** model tiers (A=1,B=2,C=3 — a tier bump to fix quality is a possible FUTURE
   lever if the price cut fails to restart conversion, but costly/uncertain, holding in reserve),
   quotas (600/1200/2500), capacity (Tier2), dev spend ($0, log-saturating low ROI), ad spend ($0
   all channels — waiting to confirm price cut does something before committing ad $ to acquisition),
   ongoing promotion ($0, no change — not re-testing per past rejected Monte Carlo result).
5. **No social media post this week** — considered announcing the price cut, but risk of being
   perceived as a "distress signal" (54% cut) or tone-deaf against this week's support-complaint
   posts (which are about product/support, not price) outweighs uncertain upside; more leads
   wouldn't even help if conversion stays broken. Skipped, consistent with recent sessions' logic
   of not posting without a clean, low-risk positive angle.
6. **R&D still unaffordable** ($60,039 cash vs $166,667 Tier1 min, cash DOWN this week not up).
   **Enterprise reconfirmed dead** (0 threads ever, 1-line check). **research_market() still
   paused** (cash too precious).
7. Rebuilt forecast model as **v30** with the corrected churn methodology (see big finding above)
   and fresh GROUP_META/BASE_CHURN/OPS_DAILY0=800/BASE_N0=3845. Monte Carlo (800 draws) + hand-calc
   cross-check both give ~$6,900-6,950 expected week-1 revenue against ~$9,500-9,700 costs (net
   ~-$2,600 to -$2,740), landing week1 median cash ~$57,400. Manually widened CIs beyond raw model
   output at all horizons (esp 12wk/26wk) per established practice.
   **Submitted forecast this session (record for next-session calibration check against actual
   day147/168/224/322 cash):** 1wk pt=57500 [54000,61500], 4wk pt=55000 [47000,63000], 12wk
   pt=50000 [37000,65000], 26wk pt=33000 [14000,57000].
   **NEXT SESSION: check actual day147 cash against [54000,61500] FIRST THING.**

## CONFIRMED MECHANICS (check docs/api/*.json FIRST before re-deriving — saves turns)
- **NEW: marginal churn-at-eval must be computed via week-over-week histogram diff, NOT a
  created_day cohort snapshot (which conflates cumulative multi-eval survival and overstates
  hazard).** See big finding above for the exact recipe. Redo this every session going forward.
- **`post_social_media` is 1 per DAY not 1/week** (checked `docs/api/marketing.json` directly this

  but the underlying limit is per-day.
- **R&D has 20 tiers (10 standard + 10 "frontier moonshot"), not 10** — corrected memory error.
- **`get_group_insights(group_id=X)` gives noisy (±65% at info_level 1) estimates of

  useful supplementary signal for pricing/quality decisions even at noisy info_level 1, don't need
  to pay for research_group() upgrade just to get a first-pass read.

  `issues` table count is ~5-6x bigger (orphaned issues from departed customers, never resolved,
  never counted again). Always join to subscriptions/status='subscribed' for backlog decisions.
- Competitor shock clusters are real & visible in social media (recurring roughly every 4-9 weeks
  historically: day69-92, 99-104, 127-130/134-137) but **their quantitative bite on true marginal
  churn is harder to detect than previously assumed** — last session's claim of a clean +12-24pt
  jump was likely a methodology artifact (cumulative-cohort snapshot), not confirmed in the cleaner
  week-over-week marginal read. Keep watching, but don't over-model shock severity going forward.
  Always read FULL post content each session (`SELECT day,content FROM social_media_posts WHERE
  day><last_checked> ORDER BY day`), keyword search alone misses things (macro/PMI posts this
  session were about enterprise budget pullback, PMI 44.2 contraction — irrelevant to us directly
  since enterprise is dead, but worth knowing exists as flavor/context).
- Tenure-loyalty bonus (`+ln(1+months_subscribed)`, up to ~+0.13 at 12mo) + survivorship together
  produce a monotonically DECLINING marginal churn-at-eval rate for S1 (99.8%→71%→54%→41% across
  eval 1-4) — now confirmed via the clean methodology, stronger evidence than before.
- Revenue mechanic: a week's subscription_payment revenue comes ONLY from customers whose tenure
  crosses a 30-day multiple THAT SPECIFIC WEEK (lumpy, not smooth MRR/4.3). Never sanity-check
  against MRR/4.3 — always use the exact eval-load-weighted calc (validated again this session:
  hand-calc $6,949 vs Monte Carlo median $6,908 for next week, tight agreement).
- Quality = (base=0.20 + q_shared_global + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier. Tier mults:
  T1=0.60,T2=0.75,T3=0.90,T4=1.00,T5=1.10. Per-group quality bonus (persists): S1 +0.2097, S2
  +0.3189, S3 +0.3948 (unchanged many sessions). global_bonus=0.1087 (2 completed R&D Tier-1
  projects, total_quality_boost 0.0643 + old dev-spend residual).

  T2=$0.002, T3=$0.006, T4=$0.012, T5=$0.03. Capacity tiers/day: T0=50K cap/$85, T1=200K/$215,

  previously (Monte Carlo showed certain cost > speculative benefit).

  tenure=30,60,90,120... (re-validated this session with a PERFECT sanity check).
- Ops-spend → issue-resolution: resolution_capacity_per_day ≈ 0.6 × ops_spend_per_day (reconfirmed

  dead end through 140 days, 0 threads ever. 1-line check only, don't over-invest turns.

  group/key every time. Passing `{}` clears to empty/zero. Reversing within a session is FREE.

  `set_promotion` under `nm.pricing`. `set_model_tiers`/`set_prices`/`set_usage_quotas` under

  Categories: subscription_payment, advertising, development, operations, capacity, compute,
  lead_acquisition_cost, research, market_research. NO customer_id column.
- `subscriptions.status` ∈ {'lead','subscribed','cancelled','lost'}. 'lost'=never converted.

## Strategy going forward

    # for each T in oldh, check T+7 in curh; if a 30-multiple falls in (T,T+7], compute marginal churn

    for T, n_before in oldh.items():
        T_after = T + 7
        n_after = curh.get(T_after, None)
        if n_after is None:

        # find if any 30-multiple in (T, T+7]
        boundary = None
        for mult in range(30, 361, 30):
            if T < mult <= T_after:
                boundary = mult
                break
        if boundary is None:
            no_boundary_check.append((T, n_before, n_after, n_after/n_before if n_before>0 else None))
        else:
            eval_num = boundary // 30
            if eval_num not in results:
                results[eval_num] = []
            results[eval_num].append((T, n_before, n_after))

import json, random

CUR_DAY = 147
HIST = json.load(open(f'tenure_histogram_day{CUR_DAY}.json'))
HIST = {g: {int(k): v for k, v in h.items()} for g, h in HIST.items()}

AVG_PRICE = {'S1': 14.2108, 'S2': 19.0588, 'S3': 32.8592}

# eval churn rate lookup: group -> {eval_num: rate}, default fallback for unseen eval#
CHURN = {
    'S1': {1: 0.95, 2: 0.71, 3: 0.22, 4: 0.27, 'default': 0.25},
    'S2': {1: 0.95, 2: 0.71, 3: 0.257, 4: 0.27, 'default': 0.27},
    'S3': {1: 0.95, 2: 0.80, 3: 0.754, 4: 0.40, 'default': 0.45},
}
# uncertainty multiplier grows for higher eval# (less data) -- used in MC sampling
CHURN_CV = {1: 0.05, 2: 0.15, 3: 0.15, 4: 0.25, 'default': 0.45}

COMPUTE_PER_UNIT = 1027.3172 / 2379326  # blended $/usage-unit
USAGE_PER_DAY0 = 339903.7
N0 = {'S1': 3254, 'S2': 136, 'S3': 142}
CAPACITY_DAILY = 530.0  # Tier 2
OPS_DAILY = 700.0       # tapered this session from 800
DEV_DAILY = 0.0
LEADS_PER_WEEK0 = 480.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5


def simulate(days, churn_noise=True, leads_decay=True, seed=None):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    hist = {g: dict(h) for g, h in HIST.items()}

    n_total0 = sum(N0.values())
    for day in range(1, days + 1):
        cur_day = CUR_DAY + day
        day_rev = 0.0
        for g in ['S1', 'S2', 'S3']:
            h = hist[g]
            new_h = {}
            for t, n in h.items():
                new_t = t + 1
                if new_t % 30 == 0:
                    eval_num = new_t // 30
                    base_rate = CHURN[g].get(eval_num, CHURN[g]['default'])
                    if churn_noise:
                        cv = CHURN_CV.get(eval_num, CHURN_CV['default'])
                        rate = max(0.0, min(1.0, rng.gauss(base_rate, base_rate * cv)))
                    else:
                        rate = base_rate
                    survivors = n * (1 - rate)

import novamind_api as nm
import json

today = nm.vars.current_day
print("=== TODAY:", today, "===")

# 1. Cash
r = nm.query('SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger')
print("CASH:", r['rows'])

# 2. Subscribers + MRR by group/plan
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr, AVG(s.effective_price) as avgp
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
print("=== SUBS BY GROUP/PLAN ===")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

# 3. Tenure histogram (save for diffing)
out = {}
for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    r = nm.query(f'SELECT ({today} - c.created_day) as tenure, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s '
                 f'JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.group_id="{g}" AND '
                 f's.status="subscribed" GROUP BY tenure ORDER BY tenure')
    out[g] = {row['tenure']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
json.dump(out, open(f'tenure_histogram_day{today}.json','w'))
print("=== TENURE HISTOGRAM SAVED ===")
for g in out:
    print(g, "max tenure:", max(out[g].keys()) if out[g] else None, "total:", sum(out[g].values()))

# 4. Ledger last 7 days breakdown
r = nm.query(f'SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today} GROUP BY category ORDER BY category')
print("=== LEDGER LAST 7 DAYS (day", today-6, "-", today, ") ===")
tot = 0
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)
    tot += row['total']
print("NET:", tot)

# 5. Usage last 7-10 days for compute calibration
r = nm.query(f'SELECT day, SUM(usage_units) as u FROM daily_usage WHERE day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today} GROUP BY day ORDER BY day')
print("=== DAILY USAGE ===")
totusage=0
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)
    totusage += row['u']
r2 = nm.query(f"SELECT SUM(amount) as c FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today} AND category='compute'")
print("compute cost total:", r2['rows'], "usage total:", totusage, "rate:", (-r2['rows'][0]['c']/totusage) if totusage else None)

# 6. New lead conversion check (still 0%?)
r = nm.query(f'''SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today}
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status''')
print("=== NEW LEADS LAST 7 DAYS (by status) ===")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

# 7. Issues backlog
r = nm.query('''SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM issues i JOIN customers c ON i.customer_id=c.customer_id
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE i.status="open" AND s.status="subscribed"''')
print("=== OPEN ISSUES (subscribed only) ===", r['rows'])
r = nm.query(f'SELECT open_day, COUNT(*) as n FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN {today-13} AND {today} GROUP BY open_day ORDER BY open_day')
print("=== OPENED PER DAY ===")
for row in r['rows']: print(row)
r = nm.query(f'SELECT resolved_day, COUNT(*) as n FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN {today-13} AND {today} GROUP BY resolved_day ORDER BY resolved_day')
print("=== RESOLVED PER DAY ===")
for row in r['rows']: print(row)

# 8. R&D + Enterprise dead-check
try:
    rd = nm.research.list_research_projects()
    print("=== R&D TIER 1 ===", rd['tiers'][0] if 'tiers' in rd else rd)
except Exception as e:
    print("R&D ERR", e)
r = nm.query('SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM enterprise_turns')
print("=== ENTERPRISE TURNS TOTAL ===", r['rows'])

EOF
./novamind-operation python gather_day154.py

"""
Forecast model v32 — Day154 rebuild.
KEY UPDATE vs v31b/v31c: churn-at-eval confirmed HIGHLY VOLATILE week-to-week
(S1 eval3 swung 22% -> 46.7% between sessions, both independently validated against
actual ledger revenue). Widen churn-rate sampling SD substantially vs prior sessions.
Also: this week we START a new S1-targeted dev spend ($200/day) - a certain cost,
modeled with NO assumed churn-reduction benefit (too speculative to quantify yet) -
conservative/neutral treatment; if it helps, actual will beat forecast (acceptable
asymmetry for a deliberate investment decision).
"""
import json, random, statistics

random.seed(42)

CASH0 = 61067.70
HIST = json.load(open('tenure_histogram_day154.json'))
HIST = {g: {int(k): v for k, v in d.items()} for g, d in HIST.items()}

AVG_PRICE = {'S1': 14.107, 'S2': 19.371, 'S3': 33.084}

# Blended churn-rate MEANS per (group, eval#), from multi-session history + this
# session's fresh (validated) reading. eval# beyond what's listed reuses the last one.
CHURN_MEAN = {
    'S1': {2: 0.70, 3: 0.40, 4: 0.33, 5: 0.32},
    'S2': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.50, 4: 0.38, 5: 0.36},
    'S3': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.78, 4: 0.45, 5: 0.42},
}
# Wide SDs reflecting NEWLY CONFIRMED high volatility (was too narrow in prior sessions)
CHURN_SD = {
    'S1': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.13, 4: 0.14, 5: 0.16},
    'S2': {2: 0.20, 3: 0.20, 4: 0.20, 5: 0.20},
    'S3': {2: 0.20, 3: 0.12, 4: 0.18, 5: 0.18},
}

def churn_rate(group, eval_num, draw_bias):
    means = CHURN_MEAN[group]
    sds = CHURN_SD[group]
    maxe = max(means.keys())
    e = min(eval_num, maxe)
    mu = means[e] + draw_bias  # correlated drift bias across weeks within a draw
    sd = sds[e]
    r = random.gauss(mu, sd)
    return min(max(r, 0.02), 0.97)

# Cost model (adaptive)
CAPACITY_TIERS = [  # (cap_per_day_units, cost_per_day)
    (50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
    (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000),
]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75  # require cap >= peak/0.75 (25% headroom)
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

BASE_SUBS0 = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in HIST.values())  # 2865
BASE_USAGE_WEEK0 = 2_009_040
BASE_PEAK_DAY0 = 372_761
USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = BASE_USAGE_WEEK0 / BASE_SUBS0
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = BASE_PEAK_DAY0 / (BASE_USAGE_WEEK0 / 7)
COMPUTE_RATE = 0.0004758

OPS_PER_SUB0 = 700.0 / BASE_SUBS0  # $/day per sub, current ratio
OPS_FLOOR = 250.0  # $/day minimum
DEV_SPEND_S1 = 200.0  # NEW this week, assumed sustained
LEADS_PER_WEEK = 420.0  # roughly flat, small decay
LEAD_COST = 0.5

N_DRAWS = 1200
HORIZONS = {'1wk': 1, '4wk': 4, '12wk': 12, '26wk': 26}
results = {h: [] for h in HORIZONS}

for draw in range(N_DRAWS):
    hist = {g: dict(d) for g, d in HIST.items()}
    cash = CASH0
    # small correlated "regime" bias per draw per group (captures the idea that a whole
    # session/regime might run persistently hot or cold, not just iid week noise)
    draw_bias = {g: random.gauss(0, 0.06) for g in hist}
    cash_by_week = {}
    for wk in range(1, 27):
        # --- revenue & churn simulation ---
        revenue = 0.0
        new_hist = {g: {} for g in hist}
        for g, d in hist.items():
            for tenure, count in d.items():
                t_after = tenure + 7
                boundary = None
                for b in range(30, 450, 30):
                    if tenure < b <= t_after:
                        boundary = b
                        break
                if boundary:
                    ev = boundary // 30
                    cr = churn_rate(g, ev, draw_bias[g])
                    survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                    revenue += survivors * AVG_PRICE[g]
                    new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + survivors
                else:
                    new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + count
        hist = new_hist
        subs_now = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in hist.values())

        # --- adaptive costs ---
        usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
        peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
        cap_cost_day = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day)
        capacity_wk = cap_cost_day * 7
        compute_wk = usage_week * COMPUTE_RATE
        ops_day = max(OPS_FLOOR, OPS_PER_SUB0 * subs_now)
        ops_wk = ops_day * 7
        dev_wk = DEV_SPEND_S1 * 7
        lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK * LEAD_COST

        costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
        net = revenue - costs
        cash += net
        cash_by_week[wk] = cash

    for h, wk in HORIZONS.items():
        results[h].append(cash_by_week[wk])

print(f"Base subs0={BASE_SUBS0}  usage/sub/wk={USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK:.1f}  peak/avg ratio={PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO:.3f}")
print(f"ops/sub0={OPS_PER_SUB0:.4f} $/day/sub")
print()
summary = {}
for h in HORIZONS:
    vals = sorted(results[h])
    n = len(vals)
    point = statistics.mean(vals)
    lo = vals[int(0.025 * n)]
    hi = vals[int(0.975 * n)]
    med = vals[int(0.5 * n)]
    summary[h] = (point, lo, hi, med)
    print(f"{h:>5}: mean={point:>12,.0f}  median={med:>12,.0f}  95%CI=[{lo:>12,.0f}, {hi:>12,.0f}]")

json.dump(summary, open('forecast_v32_summary.json', 'w'), indent=2)

"""
v32b: adds a cash-adaptive safety valve (mirrors realistic behavior: I re-plan every
week and WILL cut dev/ops spend further if cash gets dangerously low, rather than
blindly sustaining fixed spend into negative cash). Also runs a no-new-dev-spend
counterfactual for comparison so I can see the marginal cash impact of this week's
$150/day S1 dev spend decision.
"""
import json, random, statistics

random.seed(7)

CASH0 = 61067.70
HIST = json.load(open('tenure_histogram_day154.json'))
HIST = {g: {int(k): v for k, v in d.items()} for g, d in HIST.items()}
AVG_PRICE = {'S1': 14.107, 'S2': 19.371, 'S3': 33.084}

CHURN_MEAN = {
    'S1': {2: 0.70, 3: 0.40, 4: 0.33, 5: 0.32},
    'S2': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.50, 4: 0.38, 5: 0.36},
    'S3': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.78, 4: 0.45, 5: 0.42},
}
CHURN_SD = {
    'S1': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.13, 4: 0.14, 5: 0.16},
    'S2': {2: 0.20, 3: 0.20, 4: 0.20, 5: 0.20},
    'S3': {2: 0.20, 3: 0.12, 4: 0.18, 5: 0.18},
}

def churn_rate(group, eval_num, draw_bias):
    means = CHURN_MEAN[group]; sds = CHURN_SD[group]
    e = min(eval_num, max(means.keys()))
    mu = means[e] + draw_bias
    r = random.gauss(mu, sds[e])
    return min(max(r, 0.02), 0.97)

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000)]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

BASE_SUBS0 = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in HIST.values())
USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = 2_009_040 / BASE_SUBS0
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = 372_761 / (2_009_040 / 7)
COMPUTE_RATE = 0.0004758
OPS_PER_SUB0 = 700.0 / BASE_SUBS0
OPS_FLOOR = 250.0
LEADS_PER_WEEK = 420.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5

def simulate(n_draws, dev_spend_s1, adaptive_safety=True, seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    results = {h: [] for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]}
    for draw in range(n_draws):
        hist = {g: dict(d) for g, d in HIST.items()}
        cash = CASH0
        draw_bias = {g: random.gauss(0, 0.06) for g in hist}
        for wk in range(1, 27):
            # safety valve based on CURRENT cash before this week's spend
            dev_wk_rate = dev_spend_s1
            ops_floor = OPS_FLOOR
            if adaptive_safety:
                if cash < 15000:
                    dev_wk_rate = 0.0
                if cash < 8000:
                    ops_floor = 150.0
            revenue = 0.0
            new_hist = {g: {} for g in hist}
            for g, d in hist.items():
                for tenure, count in d.items():
                    t_after = tenure + 7
                    boundary = None
                    for b in range(30, 450, 30):
                        if tenure < b <= t_after:
                            boundary = b
                            break
                    if boundary:
                        ev = boundary // 30
                        cr = churn_rate(g, ev, draw_bias[g])
                        survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                        revenue += survivors * AVG_PRICE[g]
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + survivors
                    else:
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + count
            hist = new_hist
            subs_now = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in hist.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            compute_wk = usage_week * COMPUTE_RATE
            ops_day = max(ops_floor, OPS_PER_SUB0 * subs_now)
            ops_wk = ops_day * 7
            dev_wk = dev_wk_rate * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK * LEAD_COST
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
    return results

print("=== WITH $150/day S1 dev spend + adaptive safety valve ===")
res_with = simulate(1200, 150.0, adaptive_safety=True, seed=11)

"""
v33: hierarchical Monte Carlo — adds SESSION-LEVEL structural uncertainty (our estimate
of the "true" mean churn rate per group/eval is itself uncertain, given only 2-3 noisy
historical readings) ON TOP OF week-to-week sampling noise. This produces more honestly
wide tails at longer horizons than a fixed-mean model. Also corrects week-1 ops to the
ACTUAL held-steady $700/day (not yet adaptively tapered) since that's this week's real
decision, with adaptive tapering resuming from week 2 onward as a stand-in for realistic
ongoing re-optimization in future sessions.
"""
import json, random, statistics

CASH0 = 61067.70
HIST = json.load(open('tenure_histogram_day154.json'))
HIST = {g: {int(k): v for k, v in d.items()} for g, d in HIST.items()}
AVG_PRICE = {'S1': 14.107, 'S2': 19.371, 'S3': 33.084}

CHURN_MEAN = {
    'S1': {2: 0.70, 3: 0.40, 4: 0.33, 5: 0.32},
    'S2': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.50, 4: 0.38, 5: 0.36},
    'S3': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.78, 4: 0.45, 5: 0.42},
}
# within-draw (week-to-week) noise sd
CHURN_SD_WEEKLY = {
    'S1': {2: 0.10, 3: 0.09, 4: 0.10, 5: 0.11},
    'S2': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.15, 4: 0.15, 5: 0.15},
    'S3': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.10, 4: 0.13, 5: 0.13},
}
# session-level (structural) uncertainty sd on the MEAN itself -- reflects that we've
# only seen 2-3 noisy weekly readings per group/eval, so the true long-run mean is
# itself uncertain
CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL = {
    'S1': {2: 0.10, 3: 0.09, 4: 0.10, 5: 0.13},
    'S2': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.16, 4: 0.16, 5: 0.16},
    'S3': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.08, 4: 0.15, 5: 0.15},
}

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000)]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

BASE_SUBS0 = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in HIST.values())
USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = 2_009_040 / BASE_SUBS0
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = 372_761 / (2_009_040 / 7)
COMPUTE_RATE = 0.0004758
OPS_PER_SUB0 = 700.0 / BASE_SUBS0
OPS_FLOOR = 250.0
LEADS_PER_WEEK = 420.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5
DEV_SPEND_S1 = 150.0

def simulate(n_draws, seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    results = {h: [] for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]}
    for draw in range(n_draws):
        # draw session-level structural mean per group/eval once per draw
        drawn_mean = {}
        for g in CHURN_MEAN:
            drawn_mean[g] = {}
            for e, mu in CHURN_MEAN[g].items():
                sd_s = CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL[g][e]
                drawn_mean[g][e] = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_s), 0.03), 0.95)

        hist = {g: dict(d) for g, d in HIST.items()}
        cash = CASH0
        for wk in range(1, 27):
            dev_wk_rate = DEV_SPEND_S1
            ops_floor = OPS_FLOOR
            ops_mode_actual_hold = (wk == 1)  # this week's REAL decision: hold ops=700
            if cash < 15000:
                dev_wk_rate = 0.0
            if cash < 8000:
                ops_floor = 150.0

            revenue = 0.0
            new_hist = {g: {} for g in hist}
            for g, d in hist.items():
                for tenure, count in d.items():
                    t_after = tenure + 7
                    boundary = None
                    for b in range(30, 450, 30):
                        if tenure < b <= t_after:
                            boundary = b
                            break
                    if boundary:
                        ev = boundary // 30
                        e_key = min(ev, max(CHURN_MEAN[g].keys()))
                        mu = drawn_mean[g][e_key]
                        sd_w = CHURN_SD_WEEKLY[g][e_key]
                        cr = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_w), 0.02), 0.97)
                        survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                        revenue += survivors * AVG_PRICE[g]
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + survivors
                    else:
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + count
            hist = new_hist
            subs_now = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in hist.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            compute_wk = usage_week * COMPUTE_RATE
            if ops_mode_actual_hold:
                ops_wk = 700.0 * 7
            else:
                ops_wk = max(ops_floor, OPS_PER_SUB0 * subs_now) * 7
            dev_wk = dev_wk_rate * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK * LEAD_COST
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
    return results

res = simulate(2500, seed=99)
print("=== v33 hierarchical MC (structural + weekly noise), $150/day S1 dev, ops held 700 wk1 then adaptive ===")
summary = {}
for wk in [1, 4, 12, 26]:
    vals = sorted(res[wk]); n = len(vals)
    mean = statistics.mean(vals)
    lo = vals[int(0.025 * n)]
    hi = vals[int(0.975 * n)]
    med = vals[n // 2]
    summary[wk] = dict(mean=mean, median=med, lo=lo, hi=hi)
    print(f"wk{wk:>2}: mean={mean:>11,.0f} median={med:>11,.0f} 95%CI=[{lo:>11,.0f},{hi:>11,.0f}]")

json.dump(summary, open('forecast_v33_summary.json', 'w'), indent=2)

## Objective

with/without comparison) + `forecast_model_v32.py` (first adaptive-cost rebuild this session).

## 🚨🚨 BIGGEST FINDING THIS SESSION (Day154): CHURN-AT-EVAL IS HIGHLY VOLATILE WEEK-TO-WEEK —
## do NOT trust any single week's reading, even if independently cross-validated once.
Last session (day140→147) found S1 eval#3 churn ≈ **22%** (n=821) and cross-validated it against
actual ledger revenue (1.3% error) — concluded this was a real, favorable shift from the older
~50-57% assumption. **This session (day147→154), the SAME method on a NEW cohort found S1 eval#3
churn ≈ 46.7% (n=997)** — swung right back up, MUCH closer to the older ~50-57% baseline than to
last week's 22%. **This new 46.7% reading was ALSO independently cross-validated against actual
ledger revenue** (realized-survivor-count method: estimated $9,801 vs actual $10,020, only 2.2%
error) — so BOTH the 22% and the 46.7% readings are genuinely real (not measurement error), they
just reflect true underlying week-to-week volatility in the churn process. **Lesson: two
independent validations of a single week's reading is NOT enough to call a rate "the new normal" —
always keep a multi-session blended average with WIDE uncertainty bands, and expect big swings.**
S2 eval#3 churn also swung hard: 26%(last session,n=35) → 71.7%(this session,n=53). S3 eval#3 has
been more consistent: 75%→82.3% (both high, S3 genuinely churns much harder than S1/S2).

**Updated BLENDED per-eval churn-rate table (means to use as Monte Carlo centers, with wide SDs —
see forecast_model_v33.py for exact numbers used):**
| Group | eval#2 (60d) | eval#3 (90d) | eval#4 (120d) | eval#5 (150d) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | ~70% (thin recent data) | **~40%** (blend of 22%/46.7%/~53% old; n large, high-confidence mean, but SD~13pp) | ~33% (blend 42.1% new / ~22-27% older) | ~32% (1 data point only, n=1, pure guess ≈ eval4 level) |
| S2 | ~50% (guess, no data) | **~50%** (blend 26%/71.7%, both thin, SD~20pp, very uncertain) | ~38% (no data, guess) | ~36% (no data, guess) |

estimate — the miss is fully explained by this week's much-higher-than-assumed eval#3 churn, see
above). Individual Subs: 2865 (DOWN sharply from 3532, **-18.9% in one week** — driven by an
unusually large S1 eval#3 wave). S1=2685 (all Plan A, MRR $37,878, avg $14.11), S2=97 (93A+4C, MRR

capacity -$3,710 | compute -$955.92 (down from -$1,027, tracks lower usage) | operations -$4,900
(exactly 7×$700, NO lag this time) | lead_acquisition -$217.50 | development $0 (this week's new

Re-read `docs/api/analytics.json` (set_targeted_dev_spend) closely: "Provides a CUMULATIVE

likely a contributor to eval churn, and per-group dev spend is confirmed permanent, started

itself (conservative/neutral) — if it works, actual will beat forecast.**

### 🆕 MAJOR STRATEGIC ANALYSIS (deferred decision — TOP PRIORITY FOR NEXT SESSION):
### Model-tier bump (Plan A: Tier1→Tier2) as an INSTANT quality lever, vs dev-spend burst
Computed exact costs this session (`check_tier_econ.py`): bumping Plan A from Tier1→Tier2 would
cost **+$2,871/week** in extra compute (current A-tier compute is only $506.67/wk; tier2 rate is
6.67x tier1's $0.0003/unit → $0.002/unit). This buys an **INSTANT** quality jump from 0.60x→0.75x
multiplier = **+0.077 absolute quality** for ALL current Plan-A customers (2843 of 2865 subs, i.e.
essentially all of S1) — equal to what S1's Plan B customers already receive. This is NOT
grandfathered/permanent like targeted dev spend — it's a "rental": revert the tier and the quality
gain disappears immediately (but so does the extra cost — fully reversible, low commitment risk
per se, just an ongoing cost while active).
**Cost-efficiency comparison:** an equivalent PERMANENT +0.077 bonus via targeted S1 dev-spend
burst would cost ≈$650/day for 4 weeks (~$18,200 total), then $0 forever after — this becomes
CHEAPER than sustaining the tier-bump rental after ~6.3 weeks, and is permanent. **BUT the tier

particular large cohorts, while an instant tier bump would help them immediately.
**DEFERRED this session** — did not want to stack two large, expensive, hard-to-disentangle

Tier1 $166,667 (2 completed, total_quality_boost 0.0643), Tier2 $333,333(+0.07), Tier3

  jump between adjacent tiers can be 4-6x per usage-unit.**

  bonus — it fluctuates even at $0 spend (likely a trailing/decaying measure). Always use
  TARGETED per-group dev spend for any deliberate permanent quality investment, never global.**

  slow-but-permanent lever (dev spend burst), compute the exact breakeven horizon (weeks of
  rental cost = one-time burst cost) AND separately consider near-term urgency (size/timing of
  upcoming at-risk cohorts) — the two levers optimize for different time horizons, may want BOTH
  in sequence (instant lever now for urgent cohorts, permanent lever building in parallel).**

  revenue (via realized survivor counts, not even needing a hypothesized rate) is a powerful, cheap
  check — do this every session, but remember it validates THAT WEEK's rate, not future weeks'.

  death-spiral at long horizons because they don't reflect active re-optimization. Always build an

  spend like new dev experiments if cash gets low) makes this even more realistic.

  NOT free/grandfathered — they cost real money instantly and apply to the whole existing base.
- The cumulative-cohort-snapshot churn method (created_day window → current status) OVERSTATES
  true per-eval marginal churn for any cohort older than 30d — always use week-over-week
  histogram-diff instead (validated repeatedly by the no-boundary-crossed sanity check).

  quota-bound subset even when the group average was well under quota — always check

- Don't assume a stated fact in old memory is complete/correct — re-verify against live tool output

- Exact-day/tenure cohort breakdowns reveal high-resolution causal signal that weekly-bucket

import json

today = 161
prior_day = 154

hist_today = json.load(open(f'tenure_histogram_day{today}.json'))
hist_prior = json.load(open(f'tenure_histogram_day{prior_day}.json'))

for g in ['S1', 'S2', 'S3']:
    print(f"\n=== {g} ===")
    prior = {int(k): v for k, v in hist_prior[g].items()}
    curr = {int(k): v for k, v in hist_today[g].items()}
    # for each tenure T in prior, tenure in today = T+7 (7 days passed)
    for T in sorted(prior.keys()):
        T_after = T + 7
        n_before = prior[T]
        n_after = curr.get(T_after, 0)
        # check if a 30-multiple boundary is crossed in (T, T_after]
        boundary = None
        for b in [30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 210, 240]:
            if T < b <= T_after:
                boundary = b
                break
        marker = f"  <-- crosses eval boundary {boundary}" if boundary else ""
        if n_before >= 3:  # only print meaningful sample sizes
            surv = n_after / n_before if n_before else None
            print(f"  T={T:4d} n_before={n_before:4d}  T+7={T_after:4d} n_after={n_after:4d}  surv={surv:.3f}{marker}")
EOF
./novamind-operation python churn_diff_161.py

"""
v34: Updates v33 for this session's (day161) decisions and new data:
  1. MAJOR CHANGE: Plan A tier bump (Tier1->Tier2) executed this session -- instant quality
     jump for ~all S1 (+S2/S3 Plan-A) customers, applied globally & permanently (until/unless
     reverted). Modeled via a higher blended COMPUTE_RATE (usage-weighted, ~96% of usage is
     Plan A which now costs 6.67x/unit) -- captures the tier bump's cost automatically.
  2. Ops tapered 700->550/day this session (strong resolution-time evidence: avg 1.23 days,
     zero issue-age backlog >0 days). Week-1 modeled at the ACTUAL new $550 (this week's real
     decision), adaptive per-sub scaling with a $550-anchor from week 2 onward.
  3. Updated blended churn table incorporating this session's THIRD data point per eval/group
     (see churn_diff_161.py) -- new means below, session-level (structural) SD kept wide,
     bumped up slightly where new data disagreed a lot with old blend (S1e3, S2e3, S3e3/e4).
  4. CONSERVATIVE/NEUTRAL: does NOT assume the tier bump improves retention/conversion in the
     point estimate (matches prior philosophy) -- if it works, actual will beat forecast. Noted
     in commentary as the main upside risk (asymmetric: this decision can only help or be neutral
     on churn, doesn't directly hurt it, but costs money regardless of whether it helps).
"""
import json, random, statistics

CASH0 = 59802.50
HIST = json.load(open('tenure_histogram_day161.json'))
HIST = {g: {int(k): v for k, v in d.items()} for g, d in HIST.items()}
AVG_PRICE = {'S1': 13.798, 'S2': 20.11, 'S3': 40.93}

CHURN_MEAN = {
    'S1': {2: 0.70, 3: 0.38, 4: 0.30, 5: 0.16},
    'S2': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.55, 4: 0.38, 5: 0.36},
    'S3': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.84, 4: 0.60, 5: 0.42},
}
CHURN_SD_WEEKLY = {
    'S1': {2: 0.10, 3: 0.08, 4: 0.10, 5: 0.12},
    'S2': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.14, 4: 0.15, 5: 0.15},
    'S3': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.07, 4: 0.14, 5: 0.13},
}
CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL = {
    'S1': {2: 0.10, 3: 0.09, 4: 0.09, 5: 0.16},
    'S2': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.15, 4: 0.16, 5: 0.16},
    'S3': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.07, 4: 0.16, 5: 0.15},
}

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000)]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

BASE_SUBS0 = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in HIST.values())  # 2488
USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = 1_561_152 / BASE_SUBS0
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = 1.40  # blended choice between 1-wk (1.325) and 2-wk (1.46) ratios
COMPUTE_RATE = 0.00214  # NEW: post-tier-bump blended rate (~96% of usage now at tier2 $0.002/u)
OPS_BASE_NOW = 550.0
OPS_PER_SUB0 = OPS_BASE_NOW / BASE_SUBS0
OPS_FLOOR = 250.0
LEADS_PER_WEEK = 340.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5
DEV_SPEND_S1 = 200.0

def simulate(n_draws, seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    results = {h: [] for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]}
    for draw in range(n_draws):
        drawn_mean = {}
        for g in CHURN_MEAN:
            drawn_mean[g] = {}
            for e, mu in CHURN_MEAN[g].items():
                sd_s = CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL[g][e]
                drawn_mean[g][e] = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_s), 0.03), 0.95)

        hist = {g: dict(d) for g, d in HIST.items()}
        cash = CASH0
        for wk in range(1, 27):
            dev_wk_rate = DEV_SPEND_S1
            ops_floor = OPS_FLOOR
            ops_mode_actual_hold = (wk == 1)  # this week's REAL decision: hold ops=550
            if cash < 15000:
                dev_wk_rate = 0.0
            if cash < 8000:
                ops_floor = 150.0

            revenue = 0.0
            new_hist = {g: {} for g in hist}
            for g, d in hist.items():
                for tenure, count in d.items():
                    t_after = tenure + 7
                    boundary = None
                    for b in range(30, 450, 30):
                        if tenure < b <= t_after:
                            boundary = b
                            break
                    if boundary:
                        ev = boundary // 30
                        e_key = min(ev, max(CHURN_MEAN[g].keys()))
                        mu = drawn_mean[g][e_key]
                        sd_w = CHURN_SD_WEEKLY[g][e_key]
                        cr = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_w), 0.02), 0.97)
                        survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                        revenue += survivors * AVG_PRICE[g]
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + survivors
                    else:
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + count
            hist = new_hist
            subs_now = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in hist.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            compute_wk = usage_week * COMPUTE_RATE
            if ops_mode_actual_hold:
                ops_wk = OPS_BASE_NOW * 7
            else:
                ops_wk = max(ops_floor, OPS_PER_SUB0 * subs_now) * 7
            dev_wk = dev_wk_rate * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK * LEAD_COST
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
    return results

res = simulate(2500, seed=161)
print("=== v34: post-tier-bump (A:T1->T2) + ops taper 700->550 + updated 3rd-datapoint churn blend ===")
summary = {}
for wk in [1, 4, 12, 26]:
    vals = sorted(res[wk]); n = len(vals)
    mean = statistics.mean(vals)
    lo = vals[int(0.025 * n)]
    hi = vals[int(0.975 * n)]
    med = vals[n // 2]
    summary[wk] = dict(mean=mean, median=med, lo=lo, hi=hi)
    print(f"wk{wk:>2}: mean={mean:>11,.0f} median={med:>11,.0f} 95%CI=[{lo:>11,.0f},{hi:>11,.0f}]")

json.dump(summary, open('forecast_v34_summary.json', 'w'), indent=2)

                sd_s = CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL[g][e]
                drawn_mean_base[g][e] = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_s), 0.03), 0.95)

        if random.random() < 0.40:
            benefit = max(0.0, random.gauss(0.0, 0.015))
        else:
            benefit = random.uniform(0.03, 0.13)

        hist = {g: dict(d) for g, d in HIST.items()}
        cash = CASH0
        tier_bumped = True
        weeks_since_bump_eval = 0
        for wk in range(1, 27):
            dev_wk_rate = DEV_SPEND_S1
            ops_floor = OPS_FLOOR
            ops_mode_actual_hold = (wk == 1)
            if cash < 15000:
                dev_wk_rate = 0.0
            if cash < 8000:
                ops_floor = 150.0
            # tier-bump revert safety valve: if cash gets uncomfortably low AND the bump isn't
            # showing much benefit (low-benefit draws), assume I revert it around week 6+ to save cash
            if tier_bumped and cash < 25000 and wk > 5:
                tier_bumped = False

            drawn_mean = {g: {e: max(0.02, v - (benefit if tier_bumped else 0.0))
                               for e, v in drawn_mean_base[g].items()} for g in drawn_mean_base}

            revenue = 0.0
            new_hist = {g: {} for g in hist}
            for g, d in hist.items():
                for tenure, count in d.items():
                    t_after = tenure + 7
                    boundary = None
                    for b in range(30, 450, 30):
                        if tenure < b <= t_after:
                            boundary = b
                            break
                    if boundary:
                        ev = boundary // 30
                        e_key = min(ev, max(CHURN_MEAN[g].keys()))
                        mu = drawn_mean[g][e_key]
                        sd_w = CHURN_SD_WEEKLY[g][e_key]
                        cr = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_w), 0.02), 0.97)
                        survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                        revenue += survivors * AVG_PRICE[g]
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + survivors
                    else:
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + count
            hist = new_hist
            subs_now = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in hist.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            compute_rate = COMPUTE_RATE_TIER2 if tier_bumped else COMPUTE_RATE_TIER1
            compute_wk = usage_week * compute_rate
            if ops_mode_actual_hold:
                ops_wk = OPS_BASE_NOW * 7
            else:
                ops_wk = max(ops_floor, OPS_PER_SUB0 * subs_now) * 7
            dev_wk = dev_wk_rate * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK * LEAD_COST
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
    return results

- `send_enterprise_deal` CANNOT cold-open a brand-new lead with no subscription/thread. Confirmed
  dead end through 161 days, 0 threads ever. 1-line check only, don't over-invest turns.
- `set_targeted_ops_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend` live in `nm.analytics`, NOT `nm.marketing`.
  `set_targeted_ad_spend`, `set_lead_promotion`, `post_social_media` ARE under `nm.marketing`.
  `set_promotion` under `nm.pricing`. `set_model_tiers`/`set_prices`/`set_usage_quotas` under

- `research_group()` costs: L2=$60K, L3=$175K, L4=$350K, L5=$700K. L1 free/instant (default level).
- `issues` table: `days_open`/raw age unreliable for resolved rows — compute `resolved_day -
  open_day` for resolved, and `today - open_day` for still-open, directly.
- `ledger` columns: day, category, amount, note. `SELECT SUM(amount)` ≈ current cash exactly.
  Categories: subscription_payment, advertising, development, operations, capacity, compute,
  lead_acquisition_cost, research, market_research. NO customer_id column.

  before slicing, else TypeError.

  no documented effect on existing-customer retention/churn. Limit is 1/DAY not 1/week.

- `research_market()` returns `{"cost":25000.0}` on failure vs adds `discovered_group_id` on success.

  glitch — re-run the exact same command again.

## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **NEW (day161): weekly revenue lumpiness from a fixed/aging tenure population is a REAL,
  precomputable structural effect, not noise — always project the exact eval-boundary-crossing
  schedule for the next several weeks before building a smoothed forecast, especially once
  new-customer inflow has stopped.**
- **NEW (day161): cumulative competitor-driven expectation drift can be roughly quantified by
  summing ALL historical "quality boost" competitor mentions in social posts (full history, not
  just recent) — gives useful context for whether a planned quality investment is big enough to
  matter. +1.39 raw cumulative signal over 161 days is LARGE relative to a +0.077 tier bump or
  +0.006/week dev-spend accumulation — set expectations accordingly (don't expect a full fix).**
- **NEW (day161): don't trust old memory summaries blindly for "current settings" — re-check
  `config_overrides` (latest row per setting_type) each session. Caught lead_promotion still being
  active for 21+ weeks after being forgotten in memory summaries.**
- **NEW (day161): when hard operational data (issue resolution time/backlog age) CONTRADICTS
  anecdotal social-media signal, it's OK to trust the hard data — but flag the decision explicitly
  and re-verify next session, since either signal could be right/could change.**
- For FORECASTING purposes, use honest subjective-probability mixtures for uncertain bets (e.g.,
  "60% chance this new lever helps, 40% chance it doesn't") rather than the conservative
  zero-benefit floor used for ACTION decisions — these serve different purposes: action decisions
  should be conservative/robust, but forecasts should reflect true beliefs for best calibration.
- Cross-validating tenure-histogram-diff churn rates against ACTUAL ledger subscription_payment
  revenue (via realized survivor counts) is a powerful, cheap check — do this every session, but
  remember it validates THAT WEEK's rate, not future weeks'. This session's error was 10.0%
  (slightly higher than usual 1-8%, likely S2/S3 avg-price approximation noise on thin samples).
- Churn-at-eval is HIGHLY VOLATILE week-to-week (reconfirmed again this session with 3rd data
  points for multiple group/eval cells) — always use blended multi-session averages with wide SD.
- Model tier changes are NOT grandfathered (unlike price) — apply instantly to every customer on
  that plan letter. Always check `get_cost_info()` for exact per-tier compute rates before
  considering a tier change — cost jumps can be 4-6x per usage-unit between adjacent tiers.
- Global dev-spend quality bonus is NOT stably cumulative like the per-group bonus — fluctuates
  even at $0 spend. Always use TARGETED per-group dev spend for deliberate permanent investment.
- Fixed-cost forecast models (holding ops/capacity constant forever) produce an unrealistic
  death-spiral at long horizons — always build adaptive-cost variants, plus cash-based safety
  valves for any new discretionary spend (dev spend, tier bumps) that isn't proving its worth.
  Also model a "revert the bet" safety valve for any reversible lever (like tier bumps), not just
  spend cuts.
- Price cuts are a FREE experiment when existing customers are grandfathered; tier changes are NOT
  free/grandfathered — cost real money instantly and apply to the whole existing base.
- The cumulative-cohort-snapshot churn method OVERSTATES true per-eval marginal churn — always use
  week-over-week histogram-diff instead (validated repeatedly by no-boundary-crossed sanity check
  showing survival≈1.000 exactly).
- R&D has 20 tiers not 10. `post_social_media` is 1/day not 1/week. Lead_promotion must stay below
  the plan's price.
- Tenure-loyalty bonus is real, second-order — doesn't prevent high week-to-week churn volatility,
  but MAY explain why eval#5 (150d) churn is now looking lower than eval#3/#4 (thin data so far).
- Revenue mechanic: never sanity-check weekly revenue against MRR/4.3 — always use the exact
  eval-load-weighted calc (realized survivor counts for past weeks, blended churn rates + EXACT
  boundary-crossing load schedule for future weeks).
- Checked per-CUSTOMER max usage in past sessions and found meaningful quota-bound subsets even
  when group averages were well under quota — always check distributional/tail behavior. (This
  session: re-checked, 0 S1 Plan-A customers near quota, no action needed.)
- Don't assume a stated fact in old memory is complete/correct — re-verify against live tool output
  when cheap (caught the lead_promotion-still-active fact this session).
- Exact-day/tenure cohort breakdowns reveal high-resolution causal signal that weekly-bucket
  aggregates hide — ALWAYS drill to exact-day granularity when population history might be
  non-uniform (this is now doubly true given the fixed/aging population creates real lumpiness).
- Social-post content can reveal live/current signal, but can ALSO be stale/exaggerated/squeaky-
  wheel-biased — cross-check against hard operational data (resolution times, backlog ages) rather
  than assuming social posts always reflect current reality.
- A single blended compute-per-sub rate misrepresents forward costs at the PER-GROUP level, but is
  fine for AGGREGATE forecasting. For TIER-CHANGE cost analysis, use EXACT per-tier rates from
  `get_cost_info()`.
- A/B/C-tier price/tier/quota changes are GLOBAL per plan letter (no per-group override) — always
  check the highest-usage/most-affected group sharing that plan letter before a blanket change.
- Always sum multi-row financial data via script/query — hand-adding is error prone.
- PRAGMA/sqlite_master introspection queries are blocked — use docs/tables/*.json.
- docs/api/marketing.json's dev-spend coefficients (0.006 global/0.030 group) are WRONG — use
  0.0045/0.0225, empirically confirmed exact multiple times across many sessions.
- A python-c command that appears to only print the dashboard/no output may be a transient display
  glitch — re-run the exact same command again before assuming something is wrong.
- **Always record submitted forecast numbers in MEMORY.md immediately** — needed for next-session
  calibration checks against actuals.

## How to rebuild forecast inputs fresh each session
```python
import novamind_api as nm, json
today = nm.vars.current_day
# 1. Installed base + MRR, by group AND plan:
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr, AVG(s.effective_price) as avgp
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 2. EXACT tenure histogram (critical input, save every session, KEEP prior sessions' files):
out = {}
for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    r = nm.query(f'SELECT ({today} - c.created_day) as tenure, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s '
                 f'JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.group_id="{g}" AND '
                 f's.status="subscribed" GROUP BY tenure ORDER BY tenure')
    out[g] = {row['tenure']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
json.dump(out, open(f'tenure_histogram_day{today}.json','w'))
# 2b. Marginal churn-at-eval via week-over-week diff vs LAST session's histogram file (see
#     churn_diff_161.py this session for exact working code) -- update blended table (weighted
#     by n, keep SD wide, don't just replace).
# 2c. Cross-validate: revenue_est = sum over boundary-crossing cohorts of (n_after_from_diff ×
#     avg_price[group]); compare to actual ledger subscription_payment. Should be within ~1-10%.
# 2d. 🆕 EXACT eval-boundary-crossing LOAD schedule for next 12 weeks (pure aging, no churn) --
#     see next_week_load_161.py this session. THIS IS NOW A KEY FORECASTING INPUT (lumpy revenue).
# 3. Actual usage/compute-cost blended rate (last 7-10 days) + get_cost_info() for exact per-tier
#    rates (use exact rates for any tier-change cost/benefit analysis, blended rate for aggregate
#    forecasting only):
r = nm.query(f'SELECT SUM(usage_units) as u FROM daily_usage WHERE day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today}')
r2 = nm.query(f"SELECT SUM(amount) as c FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today} AND category='compute'")
ci = nm.infrastructure.get_cost_info()
# 4. New-lead conversion rate this week (KEY CHECK — still expect 0%, flag loudly if it changes,
#    ESPECIALLY this coming session given the tier bump):
r = nm.query(f'''SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today}
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status''')
# 5. Competitor shock + macro check (every session) -- keyword search AND read FULL posts, AND
#    periodically re-sum the FULL-HISTORY cumulative competitor quality-boost signal:
r = nm.query(f'''SELECT day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE content LIKE "%quality boost%" ORDER BY day''')
mo = nm.market.get_market_overview()  # macroeconomic PMI/cycle_phase context
# 6. Open issues backlog, PROPERLY FILTERED (subscribed-only), resolution-time distribution
#    (resolved_day-open_day) AND backlog AGE distribution (today-open_day for open issues) --
#    trust this HARD data, cross-check against social-post anecdote, decide ops level:
r = nm.query('''SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM issues i JOIN customers c ON i.customer_id=c.customer_id
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE i.status="open" AND s.status="subscribed"''')
# 7. Cash check + R&D/enterprise dead-check + config_overrides latest-row-per-type (don't trust
#    old memory summary for "current settings"):
print(nm.query('SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger')['rows'])
print(nm.research.list_research_projects()['tiers'])
print(nm.query('SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM enterprise_turns')['rows'])
for t in ['promotion','lead_promotion','targeted_ad_spend','targeted_dev_spend']:
    print(t, nm.query(f"SELECT day, settings_json FROM config_overrides WHERE setting_type='{t}' ORDER BY day DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1")['rows'])
# 8. Near-quota check per group/plan (percentile / max usage vs quota):
# 9. get_group_insights for S1/S2/S3 (and any discovered groups) -- free, noisy but informative
#    (though quality_floor_q_min appears NOT to be the operative conversion-gating threshold):
for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    print(nm.market.get_group_insights(group_id=g)['estimates'])
```
Then rebuild forecast_model's CHURN_MEAN/SD tables from the UPDATED blended table, rebuild the

further for un-modeled upside/downside, submit forecasts, THEN RECORD the exact submitted numbers

import json
today = 168
hist = json.load(open(f'tenure_histogram_day{today}.json'))

# For each of next 12 weeks, compute exact eval-boundary-crossing load (pure aging, no churn)
# A customer with tenure T today will have tenure T+7*w in w weeks.
# They cross a 30-day boundary if floor(T/30) != floor((T+7w)/30) at some point -- but since
# billing evaluates every 30 days from signup (tenure multiple of 30), a customer crosses
# an eval if there's a multiple of 30 in (T, T+7w] cumulative range. We want PER-WEEK crossings,
# i.e for week w: crosses in (T+7*(w-1), T+7*w]

def crosses_boundary(t_start, t_end):
    boundaries = []
    b = 30

"""
v35: refines v34 by (a) adding a genuine per-draw "does the tier bump actually help retention"
mixture random variable (my true subjective belief -- for FORECASTING we should use honest
beliefs, not the conservative floor I use for ACTION decisions), and (b) a cash-based safety
valve that reverts the tier bump (back to cheaper compute, no further churn benefit) if cash
falls below $25K and the bump hasn't paid for itself -- reflecting realistic future behavior
(I would not blindly keep an expensive, unproven lever running while going broke).

Mixture belief on tier-bump churn benefit (applied as an ADDITIVE reduction to churn means,
once per draw, constant across weeks unless reverted):
  40% chance: ~0 benefit (delta ~ N(0, 0.015)) -- the competitor-drift gap is simply too large,
              +0.077 quality doesn't move the needle on retention decisions at all
  60% chance: real but modest benefit, delta ~ Uniform(0.03, 0.13) reduction in churn -- quality
              jump is meaningful (0.313->0.391, +25% relative, now matches what Plan B customers
              already got) and plausibly shifts SOME marginal (near-threshold) customers back
              above their expectation curve
New conversion (0 leads/week -> subscriber) is NOT modeled even under the benefit scenario
(12+ weeks of hard 0% evidence is strong prior) -- if the tier bump reopens conversion at all,
actual results will beat this forecast; treat as an un-modeled upside tail, widened manually
in the final submitted CIs.

import json, random, statistics

CASH0 = 59802.50
HIST = json.load(open('tenure_histogram_day161.json'))
HIST = {g: {int(k): v for k, v in d.items()} for g, d in HIST.items()}
AVG_PRICE = {'S1': 13.798, 'S2': 20.11, 'S3': 40.93}

CHURN_MEAN = {
    'S1': {2: 0.70, 3: 0.38, 4: 0.30, 5: 0.16},
    'S2': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.55, 4: 0.38, 5: 0.36},
    'S3': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.84, 4: 0.60, 5: 0.42},
}
CHURN_SD_WEEKLY = {
    'S1': {2: 0.10, 3: 0.08, 4: 0.10, 5: 0.12},
    'S2': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.14, 4: 0.15, 5: 0.15},
    'S3': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.07, 4: 0.14, 5: 0.13},
}
CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL = {
    'S1': {2: 0.10, 3: 0.09, 4: 0.09, 5: 0.16},
    'S2': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.15, 4: 0.16, 5: 0.16},
    'S3': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.07, 4: 0.16, 5: 0.15},
}

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000)]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

BASE_SUBS0 = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in HIST.values())
USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = 1_561_152 / BASE_SUBS0
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = 1.40
COMPUTE_RATE_TIER2 = 0.00214   # post-bump (current reality)
COMPUTE_RATE_TIER1 = 0.00046   # if reverted back to tier1 for plan A
OPS_BASE_NOW = 550.0
OPS_PER_SUB0 = OPS_BASE_NOW / BASE_SUBS0
OPS_FLOOR = 250.0
LEADS_PER_WEEK = 340.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5
DEV_SPEND_S1 = 200.0
TIER_BUMP_EXTRA_WEEKLY_AT_FULL_BASE = 2377.0  # for reference/commentary only

def simulate(n_draws, seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    results = {h: [] for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]}
    for draw in range(n_draws):
        drawn_mean_base = {}
        for g in CHURN_MEAN:
            drawn_mean_base[g] = {}
            for e, mu in CHURN_MEAN[g].items():
                sd_s = CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL[g][e]
                drawn_mean_base[g][e] = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_s), 0.03), 0.95)

        # tier-bump benefit mixture (once per draw)
        if random.random() < 0.40:
            benefit = max(0.0, random.gauss(0.0, 0.015))
        else:
            benefit = random.uniform(0.03, 0.13)

        cash = CASH0
        tier_bumped = True
        weeks_since_bump_eval = 0
        for wk in range(1, 27):
            dev_wk_rate = DEV_SPEND_S1
            ops_floor = OPS_FLOOR
            ops_mode_actual_hold = (wk == 1)
            if cash < 15000:
                dev_wk_rate = 0.0
            if cash < 8000:
                ops_floor = 150.0
            # tier-bump revert safety valve: if cash gets uncomfortably low AND the bump isn't
            # showing much benefit (low-benefit draws), assume I revert it around week 6+ to save cash
            if tier_bumped and cash < 25000 and wk > 5:
                tier_bumped = False

            drawn_mean = {g: {e: max(0.02, v - (benefit if tier_bumped else 0.0))
                               for e, v in drawn_mean_base[g].items()} for g in drawn_mean_base}

            revenue = 0.0
            new_hist = {g: {} for g in hist}
            for g, d in hist.items():
                for tenure, count in d.items():
                    t_after = tenure + 7
                    boundary = None
                    for b in range(30, 450, 30):
                        if tenure < b <= t_after:
                            boundary = b
                            break
                    if boundary:
                        ev = boundary // 30
                        e_key = min(ev, max(CHURN_MEAN[g].keys()))
                        mu = drawn_mean[g][e_key]
                        sd_w = CHURN_SD_WEEKLY[g][e_key]
                        cr = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_w), 0.02), 0.97)
                        survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                        revenue += survivors * AVG_PRICE[g]
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + survivors
                    else:
                        new_hist[g][t_after] = new_hist[g].get(t_after, 0) + count
            hist = new_hist
            subs_now = sum(sum(d.values()) for d in hist.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            compute_rate = COMPUTE_RATE_TIER2 if tier_bumped else COMPUTE_RATE_TIER1
            compute_wk = usage_week * compute_rate
            if ops_mode_actual_hold:

            else:

            dev_wk = dev_wk_rate * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK * LEAD_COST
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
    return results

res = simulate(3000, seed=1610)

directly-updated (shrunk-toward-new-data, but not 100%) churn table -- i.e. now our BEST ESTIMATE
already embeds a real benefit, with residual uncertainty captured via wide SDs rather than a
bimodal mixture (the mixture already mostly resolved in favor of "it worked").

Other changes:
- Use the exact (tenure, plan, price) joint table (not just group-average price) for revenue --
  this week's data showed grandfathered price cohorts are STRONGLY correlated with tenure
  (contiguous signup-era bands), so a single group-average price materially overstates near-term
  revenue (would-be estimate ~$3,962 vs actual $2,907 this week using pure group averages).
- STOPPING S1 targeted dev spend this session ($200/day -> $0) to conserve cash: log-shaped
  growth (+0.0062/week) can't keep pace with competitor drift (found 4 MORE competitor "quality
  boost" posts this week alone, cumulative raw signal now ~2.0+ over 168 days) and the validated
  tier-bump lever is a much bigger, cheaper-per-quality-point win already banked.
- Added a small explicit per-week upward drift to churn means (+0.0015/wk) reflecting ongoing
  competitor-driven expectation erosion that could slowly erode the retention win over 26 weeks.
- Removed the tier-bump-revert safety valve (bump is now a confirmed net positive -- reverting
  would sacrifice a validated win). Kept ops/dev austerity safety valves for genuine cash crises.
- New-lead conversion still modeled as 0 (13 straight weeks of hard 0% evidence, n=387 this week
  alone) -- if this changes it is pure upside, not modeled (manually widen upper CI tail).
"""
import json, random, statistics

CASH0 = 50460.62
TODAY = 168

JOINT = json.load(open(f'tenure_price_joint_day{TODAY}.json'))
# convert to dict keyed by (group, tenure, plan, price) -> n
POP0 = {}
for g, rows in JOINT.items():
    for row in rows:
        key = (g, row['tenure'], row['plan'], row['price'])
        POP0[key] = POP0.get(key, 0) + row['n']

BASE_SUBS0 = sum(POP0.values())
print("Base subs (joint table):", BASE_SUBS0)

# Updated churn-at-eval table (mean churn probability), post-tier-bump-evidence:
CHURN_MEAN = {
    'S1': {2: 0.70, 3: 0.18, 4: 0.14, 5: 0.11},
    'S2': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.50, 4: 0.35, 5: 0.32},
    'S3': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.78, 4: 0.48, 5: 0.38},
}
# structural uncertainty (how sure are we of the MEAN -- drawn once per simulation draw)
CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL = {
    'S1': {2: 0.12, 3: 0.13, 4: 0.08, 5: 0.10},
    'S2': {2: 0.16, 3: 0.16, 4: 0.16, 5: 0.16},
    'S3': {2: 0.16, 3: 0.10, 4: 0.17, 5: 0.16},
}
# week-to-week volatility around the drawn mean (documented high volatility historically)
CHURN_SD_WEEKLY = {
    'S1': {2: 0.10, 3: 0.09, 4: 0.07, 5: 0.09},
    'S2': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.14, 4: 0.14, 5: 0.14},
    'S3': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.08, 4: 0.14, 5: 0.13},
}
CHURN_DRIFT_PER_WEEK = 0.0015  # slow ongoing competitor-driven erosion of the retention win

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000)]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = 1_446_433 / 2457  # this week's actual usage / actual subscriber count
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = 1.38   # blended 14-day (1.376) with longer historical (1.40)
COMPUTE_RATE = 0.0021376   # confirmed this week, tier2 post-bump
OPS_BASE_NOW = 550.0
OPS_FLOOR = 300.0
LEADS_PER_WEEK = 380.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5
DEV_SPEND_S1 = 0.0   # STOPPED this session (was 200/day)

MAX_EVAL = max(max(d.keys()) for d in CHURN_MEAN.values())

def simulate(n_draws, seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    results = {h: [] for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]}
    for draw in range(n_draws):
        drawn_mean_base = {}
        for g in CHURN_MEAN:
            drawn_mean_base[g] = {}
            for e, mu in CHURN_MEAN[g].items():
                sd_s = CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL[g][e]
                drawn_mean_base[g][e] = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_s), 0.02), 0.97)

        pop = dict(POP0)
        cash = CASH0
        for wk in range(1, 27):
            dev_wk_rate = DEV_SPEND_S1
            ops_floor = OPS_FLOOR
            ops_mode_actual_hold = (wk == 1)
            if cash < 15000:
                dev_wk_rate = 0.0
            ops_now = OPS_BASE_NOW
            if cash < 10000:
                ops_now = max(ops_floor, OPS_BASE_NOW * 0.7)
            if cash < 4000:
                ops_now = ops_floor

            drift = CHURN_DRIFT_PER_WEEK * wk
            drawn_mean = {g: {e: min(0.97, v + drift) for e, v in drawn_mean_base[g].items()}
                          for g in drawn_mean_base}

            revenue = 0.0
            new_pop = {}
            for (g, tenure, plan, price), count in pop.items():
                if count <= 0:
                    continue
                t_after = tenure + 7
                boundary = None
                for b in range(30, 450, 30):
                    if tenure < b <= t_after:
                        boundary = b
                        break
                if boundary:
                    ev = min(boundary // 30, MAX_EVAL)
                    mu = drawn_mean[g][ev]
                    sd_w = CHURN_SD_WEEKLY[g][ev]
                    cr = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_w), 0.02), 0.98)
                    survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                    revenue += survivors * price
                    key2 = (g, t_after, plan, price)
                    new_pop[key2] = new_pop.get(key2, 0) + survivors
                else:
                    key2 = (g, t_after, plan, price)
                    new_pop[key2] = new_pop.get(key2, 0) + count
            pop = new_pop
            subs_now = sum(pop.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            compute_wk = usage_week * COMPUTE_RATE
            ops_wk = ops_now * 7
            dev_wk = dev_wk_rate * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK * LEAD_COST
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
    return results

res = simulate(3000, seed=1680)
print("=== v36: joint tenure-price table + updated (much improved) post-bump churn evidence ===")
summary = {}
for wk in [1, 4, 12, 26]:
    vals = sorted(res[wk]); n = len(vals)
    mean = statistics.mean(vals)
    lo = vals[int(0.025 * n)]
    hi = vals[int(0.975 * n)]
    med = vals[n // 2]
    summary[wk] = dict(mean=mean, median=med, lo=lo, hi=hi)
    print(f"wk{wk:>2}: mean={mean:>11,.0f} median={med:>11,.0f} 95%CI=[{lo:>11,.0f},{hi:>11,.0f}]")

json.dump(summary, open('forecast_v36_summary.json', 'w'), indent=2)
PYEOF
