# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 168 = end of week 24. 48 weeks remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: **`forecast_model_v36.py`** (PRIMARY — uses exact (tenure,plan,price) joint
population table + directly-updated post-tier-bump churn table, reflecting this session's big
retention-improvement finding). v35/v34 SUPERSEDED (kept for methodology reference). v18-v30
DELETED this session (confirmed stale, freed clutter). v31-v33 kept but stale.

## 🎉🎉 STATUS as of Day 168 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 175 next dashboard)
Cash: $50,460.62 (down -$9,341.88 from day161's $59,802.50 — **matches last session's forecast
[48000,53500] point=50700 EXTREMELY well: actual 50,461 vs point 50,700, ~0.5% error, EXCELLENT
calibration, and confirms the "lumpy eval load" prediction was correct**). Individual Subs: 2457
(down from 2488, -31, matches Cancellations:31 exactly). New Individual Leads: 387, **0 converted
— 0% conversion CONFIRMED continuing, now ~13 weeks straight running (387 leads this week, ALL
status='lost', n large enough that true 0% is a strong read, not noise)**. Base by group/plan:
S1=2356 (all A, MRR $32,614, avg $13.84 — but see BIG per-tenure PRICE finding below), S2=63
(59A+4C, MRR $1,267), S3=38 (25A+1B+12C, MRR $1,478). TOTAL MRR $35,359 (still shrinking, 0 new
inflow). Enterprise: still 0 seats, 0 threads ever (168 days). Open issues 329 (subscribed-only),
**all age=0, avg resolution 1.0-1.3 days — CONFIRMED HEALTHY again this session (2nd week in a
row) despite continued "ghosted"/"radio silence" social complaints — the 5,892 OTHER "open" issues
in the raw table belong to CANCELLED customers (orphaned records, not a live backlog)**.

### Ledger ground-truth, last 7 days (day162-168):
operations -$3,850 (7×$550, confirms taper holding) | capacity -$3,710 (7×$530) | compute
-$3,091.88 (**up from -$777.20 pre-bump — confirms tier-bump cost, blended rate now
$0.0021376/unit, matches predicted $0.00214 exactly**) | development -$1,400 (7×$200, S1 targeted,
STOPPED this session going forward) | lead_acquisition -$197.00 (394 leads×$0.5) |
subscription_payment +$2,907.00 (279 payments, avg $10.42/payment) | **NET -$9,341.88** (exact
match to cash delta, confirms methodology). Usage 1,446,433 (avg 206,633/day), 14-day peak/avg
ratio 1.376 (blended-in as 1.38 for forecasting).

## 🎉🎉🎉 MAJOR FINDING: TIER BUMP RETENTION BENEFIT CONFIRMED — LARGE, POSITIVE SIGNAL
Ran tenure-histogram diff day161→day168 (see `churn_diff_168.py`). This week's eval-boundary
crossers are the FIRST cohort whose billing evaluation happened ENTIRELY after the day161 tier
bump (A/B: T1→T2, C: T1→T3) took effect. Results, weighted by sample size:
- **S1 eval#4 (120d): survival 90.7% (n=268!) i.e. CHURN ONLY 9.3%** — vs. prior blended estimate
  of ~30% churn pre-bump. This is a MASSIVE, high-confidence (large n) improvement — churn roughly
  **1/3 of the prior rate**.
- S1 eval#3 (90d): survival 100% (n=10, thin but consistent direction) vs. prior blend 38% churn.
- S1 eval#5 (150d): survival 91.7% (n=24) i.e. churn 8.3%, vs. prior blend ~16% churn — also
  improved, roughly half.
- S3 eval#4 (120d): survival 80% (n=5, thin) vs. prior blend 60% churn — also directionally much
  better, though sample too thin to be confident of magnitude.
- S2: zero crossings this week (no data point).
**Mechanistic interpretation: this is believable, not just noise — quality for S1 Plan A jumped
0.313→0.396 (matches what Plan-B customers already got), closing much of the gap between delivered
quality and customer expectations AT THE MARGIN for existing (tenure-cushioned) customers. The
bump is a genuine, validated win for RETENTION.** New-lead CONVERSION remains 0% (387/387 lost)
— consistent with the hypothesis that brand-new leads face the FULL expectation gap with no
tenure-loyalty cushion, so the same quality jump that saves existing customers at eval doesn't
(yet) clear the bar for someone with zero tenure bonus. **Decision: KEEP the tier bump (A=2,B=2,
C=3) — do NOT revert. This is now a confirmed net positive lever, not a gamble.**
Updated blended CHURN_MEAN table (post-bump, forward-looking best estimate) is in
`forecast_model_v36.py` — S1: eval2~70%(no data)/eval3~18%/eval4~14%/eval5~11%. S2: ~50/50/35/32%.
S3: ~50/78/48/38% (S2/S3 revised down more cautiously — thin/no new data this week for them).

## 🆕 NEW METHODOLOGY: (tenure, plan, PRICE) joint table >> group-average price for forecasting
Checked WHY realized revenue this week ($2,907, avg $10.42/payment) came in below a naive
group-average-price estimate (~$3,962 using S1 avg $13.84). Found: **S1 Plan A has 5 distinct
grandfathered price cohorts ($9 n=148, $10 n=448, $13 n=573, $15 n=671, $18 n=516) that are
STRONGLY correlated with tenure** (customers who signed up in the same historical window share
both similar tenure AND similar price, since price was constant during their signup era). This
week's eval#4 crossers (tenure 113-126) happened to be overwhelmingly the **$10 cohort** (248 of
279 payments = 89%), not the $13.84 group average. **Upgrades/downgrades were 0/0 this week, so
this is NOT a downgrade effect — it's pure price-cohort/tenure correlation.** Built
`tenure_price_joint_day168.json` (full joint table) and rewired `forecast_model_v36.py` to carry
EXACT (group,tenure,plan,price)→count state through the simulation instead of a single group-avg
price — hand-validated: deterministic mean-churn wk+1 revenue calc ($6,466) matches full MC median
almost exactly. **ACTION FOR FUTURE SESSIONS: always rebuild the joint tenure-price table each
session (cheap query, `tenure_price_joint.py` pattern) — it materially changes near-term revenue
precision vs. a group-average price.**

## 🆕 ACTION: STOPPED S1 targeted dev spend ($200/day → $0) this session
Rationale: log-shaped per-group quality growth (+0.0225×ln(1+spend/5000)/day ≈ +0.0062/week at
$200/day) cannot conceivably keep pace with competitor-driven expectation drift — found **4 MORE
competitor "quality boost" social posts this week alone** (days 163-166, summing to ~0.30 raw
signal), on top of the already-large +1.39 cumulative signal found last session (full-history sum
now ~2.0+). The tier bump was a much bigger, cheaper-per-quality-point win (instant +0.077 vs.
months of dev-spend trickle) and is now validated (see above) — no need to also fund the slow
lever. Saves $1,400/week. **The S1 per-group quality bonus (+0.2221) is CUMULATIVE/persists — it
does NOT decay from stopping spend, it just stops growing further.** This is a safe, isolated cost
cut (does not risk reversing the retention win, which is driven by the tier bump, not dev spend).

## Competitor-drift & macro (recheck every session)
4 new competitor "quality boost" events this week (days 163,164,165,166 — ~0.066-0.086 raw signal
each). Cumulative full-history raw signal now roughly **~2.0** (was ~1.39 nine days ago) — drift is
ACCELERATING, not steady. This is the underlying reason new-lead conversion likely stays stuck at
0% even with the tier bump (existing/tenured customers get a cushion; brand-new leads don't).
Macro: still PMI 45.3, contraction/trough, UNCHANGED for many sessions now — no signal of relief.

## R&D: still unaffordable, gap grew slightly smaller in %terms but still far off
Tier1 $166,667 (2 completed, total_quality_boost 0.0643). Cash $50,461 is ~$116,206 short. Given
12wk median forecast is only ~$5-6K and 26wk median is NEGATIVE (~-$30K to -$34K), R&D remains out
of reach for the foreseeable future under current trajectory. Revisit each session, don't force it.

## Capacity: HOLD Tier 2 — usage still exceeds Tier1's 200K/day cap on most days
Daily usage last 14 days ranged 131,490–295,550; most days in the 220K-295K range, comfortably
above Tier1's 200K cap (would overload almost daily). Tier2 (800K cap, $530/day) has huge headroom
(~30-37% utilized at peak) — expensive slack, but necessary given peak-day risk. **As population
keeps shrinking (no new inflow, ongoing even-if-slower churn), usage will keep dropping — recheck
EVERY session whether peak usage has fallen enough to safely downgrade to Tier1 (~$315/day =
$2,205/week savings).** Not yet — hold this week.

## Ops: HOLD $550/day — 2nd consecutive week confirmed healthy
Avg resolution ~1.0-1.3 days, 100% of open issues (for currently-subscribed customers) are age=0.
Social media STILL shows recurring "ghosted"/"radio silence"/"crickets" complaints (Alex Chen,
Sam Rivera, Sophie Anderson posts day168) — 2nd session running where hard data contradicts
anecdote. Continuing to trust hard data (healthy) over anecdote (likely squeaky-wheel/stale/
persona-flavor-text bias baked into the social-post generator, not a live signal). Posted a
reassuring reply this session (`post_social_media`, reply_to_post_id=355, free action) acknowledging
the sentiment while citing the real ~1-day resolution time — no cash cost, might help reputation
at the margin. **Do NOT cut ops further THIS session** (want ≥2 weeks confirmation at current level
before the NEXT taper — already tapered 700→550 last session; consider 550→500 NEXT session if
still healthy, since $500 is a documented reference point (~1.1% daily outage risk) and $550 likely

"""
v37: MAJOR CORRECTION following week-25 (day175) data. Last week's "tier bump fixed retention"
conclusion was based on n=268 in ONE favorable cohort (9.3% churn) -- this week's NEW cohort
crossing the SAME eval boundary (120d) showed 36.1% churn (n=482)! Pooling both weeks:
  - eval@120 (ev4): pooled n=750, churn=26.5%
  - eval@150 (ev5): pooled n=93,  churn=26.9%
This is a much more sober, believable read: the tier bump likely DID help somewhat (26-27% vs.
an old pre-bump blend of ~30-38%), but the effect is MODEST, not the dramatic 9% first thought.
Root cause of the swing: grandfathered PRICE cohorts are strongly tenure-correlated, and
different weekly cohorts crossing the same eval boundary can have very different price (hence
very different quality-price fit) -- the day161->168 cohort was cheaper ($10), day168->175
cohort was $13 (much bigger, much higher churn). Churn-at-eval is inherently COHORT-DEPENDENT
and volatile -- don't over-trust any single week's reading again.

ACTION THIS SESSION: cut Plan A list price 13 -> 9 (matches historically-successful cohort,
still positive gross margin ~$3.7/mo at avg usage). This is FREE for existing (grandfathered)
customers -- only affects new signups. Modeled as a probabilistic "reopening" scenario (uncertain
whether price alone can overcome the apparent quality-expectation deficit that's held new-lead
conversion at 0% for 13 straight weeks -- willingness-to-pay estimates suggest price isn't the
main binding constraint, quality/expectation-drift is more likely -- so we use a modest ~20%
probability of any reopening, not a confident bet).
Also tapered ops 550->500 (2nd+ week confirmed healthy backlog).
"""
import json, random, statistics

CASH0 = 44279.814
TODAY = 175

JOINT = json.load(open(f'tenure_price_joint_day{TODAY}.json'))
POP0 = {}
for g, rows in JOINT.items():
    for row in rows:
        key = (g, row['tenure'], row['plan'], row['price'])
        POP0[key] = POP0.get(key, 0) + row['n']

BASE_SUBS0 = sum(POP0.values())
print("Base subs (joint table):", BASE_SUBS0)

    'S1': {2: 0.60, 3: 0.28, 4: 0.265, 5: 0.269, 6: 0.28},
    'S2': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.45, 4: 0.35,  5: 0.35,  6: 0.36},
    'S3': {2: 0.50, 3: 0.55, 4: 0.42,  5: 0.42,  6: 0.43},
}
CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL = {
    'S1': {2: 0.15, 3: 0.14, 4: 0.09, 5: 0.10, 6: 0.11},
    'S2': {2: 0.18, 3: 0.18, 4: 0.17, 5: 0.17, 6: 0.17},
    'S3': {2: 0.18, 3: 0.15, 4: 0.18, 5: 0.18, 6: 0.18},
}
CHURN_SD_WEEKLY = {
    'S1': {2: 0.12, 3: 0.11, 4: 0.10, 5: 0.10, 6: 0.10},

                                 # since we no longer believe the bump was a dramatic structural fix)
MAX_EVAL_DEFINED = 6  # evals beyond 6 (180d+) reuse the ev=6 rate + drift

                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000)]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = 1_396_782 / 2243   # this week's actual usage / actual subscriber count
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = 1.26   # this week's 14-day peak/avg (255269/203087)
COMPUTE_RATE = 0.0021160  # this week's exact blended rate (2955.804/1396782)

LEAD_COST = 0.5

# New-signup / conversion-reopening scenario (price cut A: 13->9 this session)

    idx = boundary // 30
    return min(idx, MAX_EVAL_DEFINED)

        conv_rate = random.uniform(0.01, 0.09) if reopen else random.uniform(0.0, 0.003)
        reopen_delay_wk = random.randint(1, 3)  # takes a bit for word-of-mouth to catch on

        pop = dict(POP0)
        cash = CASH0
        for wk in range(1, 27):

            dev_wk_rate = DEV_SPEND_S1
            if cash < 15000:

            if cash < 10000:
                ops_now = max(OPS_FLOOR, OPS_BASE_NOW * 0.7)
            if cash < 4000:
                ops_now = OPS_FLOOR

            drift = CHURN_DRIFT_PER_WEEK * wk
            drawn_mean = {g: {e: min(0.97, v + drift) for e, v in drawn_mean_base[g].items()}
                          for g in drawn_mean_base}

            revenue = 0.0
            new_pop = {}

                if count <= 0:
                    continue
                t_after = tenure + 7
                boundary = None
                for b in range(30, 480, 30):
                    if tenure < b <= t_after:
                        boundary = b
                        break
                if boundary:
                    ev = eval_index(boundary)
                    mu = drawn_mean[g][ev]
                    sd_w = CHURN_SD_WEEKLY[g][ev]
                    cr = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_w), 0.02), 0.98)
                    survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                    revenue += survivors * price
                    key2 = (g, t_after, plan, price)
                    new_pop[key2] = new_pop.get(key2, 0) + survivors
                else:
                    key2 = (g, t_after, plan, price)
                    new_pop[key2] = new_pop.get(key2, 0) + count
            pop = new_pop

            # New conversions (if reopened), starting after reopen_delay_wk
            new_subs = 0.0
            if wk >= reopen_delay_wk:
                leads_this_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK_BASE * (sum(pop.values()) / BASE_SUBS0)
                new_subs = leads_this_wk * conv_rate
                # new subs start at tenure=7 (after their first week), price = NEW_PRICE_A, group S1 (dominant)
                key_new = ('S1', 7, 'A', NEW_PRICE_A)
                pop[key_new] = pop.get(key_new, 0) + new_subs
                # they don't pay until their first 30-day eval, so no immediate revenue this week

            subs_now = sum(pop.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            compute_wk = usage_week * COMPUTE_RATE
            ops_wk = ops_now * 7
            dev_wk = dev_wk_rate * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK_BASE * (subs_now / BASE_SUBS0) * LEAD_COST
            onboarding_new = new_subs * LEAD_COST  # already counted in lead_wk approx; skip double count
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
                diag_subs[wk].append(subs_now)
    return results, diag_subs

if __name__ == '__main__':

        print(f"wk{h}: median=${med:,.0f} mean=${mean:,.0f} [{lo:,.0f}, {hi:,.0f}]  subs_median={subs_med:.0f}")

              compute_rate=0.0021160, leads_wk=330.0, usage_per_sub_wk=1_396_782/2243):

            revenue += survivors * price

            churned_total += count - survivors
        else:
            total_pop_after += count
    usage_wk = usage_per_sub_wk * total_pop_after

    cash_delta = revenue - costs

"""
Compare: KEEP Plan A/B at Tier2 (current) vs REVERT to Tier1, given the now-much-more-modest
estimated retention benefit (pooled churn 26.5-26.9% at T2 vs assumed ~30-35% at T1, i.e. only
~3.5-8.5pts worse, NOT the ~20pt swing first believed). Compute savings from T1 are large
(rate 0.0003 vs 0.002/unit, 6.67x cheaper) since Plan A is 99.7% of usage.
"""
import json, random, statistics

CASH0 = 44279.814
JOINT = json.load(open('tenure_price_joint_day175.json'))
POP0 = {}
for g, rows in JOINT.items():
    for row in rows:
        key = (g, row['tenure'], row['plan'], row['price'])
        POP0[key] = POP0.get(key, 0) + row['n']
BASE_SUBS0 = sum(POP0.values())

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000)]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = 1_396_782 / 2243
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = 1.26
OPS_BASE_NOW = 500.0
LEADS_PER_WEEK_BASE = 330.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5

def run(scenario, n_draws=2000, seed=7):
    # scenario: 'T2' (keep, rate .00212 blended incl C@T3) or 'T1' (revert A/B to T1, keep C@T3)
    random.seed(seed)
    if scenario == 'T2':
        rate_A = 0.002
        churn_adj = 0.0
    else:
        rate_A = 0.0003
        churn_adj = 0.06  # assume churn worsens by 6pts (mid of 3.5-8.5pt plausible range) at each eval
    rate_C = 0.006
    CHURN_MEAN = {
        'S1': {1: 0.45, 2: 0.60, 3: 0.28+churn_adj, 4: 0.265+churn_adj, 5: 0.269+churn_adj, 6: 0.28+churn_adj},
        'S2': {1: 0.45, 2: 0.50, 3: 0.45+churn_adj, 4: 0.35+churn_adj,  5: 0.35+churn_adj,  6: 0.36+churn_adj},
        'S3': {1: 0.45, 2: 0.50, 3: 0.55+churn_adj, 4: 0.42+churn_adj,  5: 0.42+churn_adj,  6: 0.43+churn_adj},
    }
    SD_S = 0.13
    results = {h: [] for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]}
    for draw in range(n_draws):
        drawn_mean_base = {g: {e: min(max(random.gauss(mu, SD_S), 0.03), 0.97) for e, mu in CHURN_MEAN[g].items()} for g in CHURN_MEAN}
        pop = dict(POP0)
        cash = CASH0
        for wk in range(1, 27):
            subs_prev = sum(pop.values())
            ops_now = max(150.0, OPS_BASE_NOW * (subs_prev / BASE_SUBS0) ** 0.5)
            drift = 0.0010 * wk
            drawn_mean = {g: {e: min(0.97, v + drift) for e, v in drawn_mean_base[g].items()} for g in drawn_mean_base}
            revenue = 0.0
            new_pop = {}
            for (g, tenure, plan, price), count in pop.items():
                if count <= 0: continue
                t_after = tenure + 7
                boundary = None
                for b in range(30, 480, 30):
                    if tenure < b <= t_after:
                        boundary = b; break
                if boundary:
                    ev = min(max(boundary // 30, 1), 6)
                    mu = drawn_mean[g][ev]
                    cr = min(max(random.gauss(mu, 0.10), 0.02), 0.98)
                    survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                    revenue += survivors * price
                    new_pop[(g, t_after, plan, price)] = new_pop.get((g,t_after,plan,price), 0) + survivors
                else:
                    new_pop[(g, t_after, plan, price)] = new_pop.get((g,t_after,plan,price), 0) + count
            pop = new_pop
            subs_now = sum(pop.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            # split usage proportionally A vs C (99.7% vs 0.3% roughly, hold fixed ratio)
            usage_A = usage_week * (1275120/1396782)
            usage_C = usage_week * (16184/1396782)  # (approx, ignoring tiny group compositional drift)
            compute_wk = usage_A * rate_A + usage_C * rate_C
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            ops_wk = ops_now * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK_BASE * (subs_now / BASE_SUBS0) * LEAD_COST
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
    return results

for scenario in ['T2', 'T1']:
    res = run(scenario)
    print(f"\n=== Scenario: {scenario} ===")
    for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]:
        vals = sorted(res[h])
        n = len(vals)
        med = vals[n//2]
        print(f"  wk{h}: median=${med:,.0f}  [{vals[int(n*0.025)]:,.0f}, {vals[int(n*0.975)]:,.0f}]")

"""
v38: Combines the v37 pooled-churn correction with a DECISIVE cost-cut action this session:
reverting Plan A model tier 2->1. Analysis (tier_revert_comparison.py) showed this is a large,
clear net-positive even under a pessimistic assumption that reverting worsens eval-churn by
+6pts (mid of plausible 3.5-8.5pt range implied by pooled data): wk26 median cash improves from
~-$20,300 (keep T2) to ~+$420 (revert to T1) in a like-for-like comparison. Compute rate at T1 is
0.0003/unit vs 0.002/unit at T2 (6.67x cheaper), and Plan A is 99.7% of usage -- the retention
"benefit" of T2 turned out much smaller than first believed (see v37 notes: pooled churn 26.5-
26.9% at T2 vs assumed ~30-38% pre-bump, only ~3.5-10pt real gap, not the ~20pt first thought from
a single lucky-cohort week). Compute savings vastly exceed the plausible retention cost.

Also modeling this week's Plan A price cut (13->9) as a probabilistic acquisition-reopening
scenario (unchanged from v37: ~20% probability, since willingness-to-pay estimates suggest price
isn't the primary binding constraint -- quality/expectation-drift more likely -- so cutting price
alone may not be sufficient, though it's a free/no-risk test worth running).

Ops tapered 550->500 this session (2nd+ week confirmed healthy backlog), adaptive scaling with
population continues.
"""
import json, random, statistics

CASH0 = 44279.814
TODAY = 175

JOINT = json.load(open(f'tenure_price_joint_day{TODAY}.json'))
POP0 = {}
for g, rows in JOINT.items():
    for row in rows:
        key = (g, row['tenure'], row['plan'], row['price'])
        POP0[key] = POP0.get(key, 0) + row['n']
BASE_SUBS0 = sum(POP0.values())
print("Base subs (joint table):", BASE_SUBS0)

# Churn-adj applied due to the tier revert (A: T2->T1). Central +6pt, with its own uncertainty.
TIER_REVERT_CHURN_ADJ_MEAN = 0.06
TIER_REVERT_CHURN_ADJ_SD = 0.035  # genuine uncertainty on how much the revert costs in retention

CHURN_MEAN_BASE = {
    'S1': {1: 0.45, 2: 0.60, 3: 0.28, 4: 0.265, 5: 0.269, 6: 0.28},
    'S2': {1: 0.45, 2: 0.50, 3: 0.45, 4: 0.35,  5: 0.35,  6: 0.36},
    'S3': {1: 0.45, 2: 0.50, 3: 0.55, 4: 0.42,  5: 0.42,  6: 0.43},
}
CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL = {
    'S1': {1: 0.18, 2: 0.15, 3: 0.14, 4: 0.09, 5: 0.10, 6: 0.11},
    'S2': {1: 0.18, 2: 0.18, 3: 0.18, 4: 0.17, 5: 0.17, 6: 0.17},
    'S3': {1: 0.18, 2: 0.18, 3: 0.15, 4: 0.18, 5: 0.18, 6: 0.18},
}
CHURN_SD_WEEKLY = {
    'S1': {1: 0.15, 2: 0.12, 3: 0.11, 4: 0.10, 5: 0.10, 6: 0.10},
    'S2': {1: 0.15, 2: 0.16, 3: 0.15, 4: 0.15, 5: 0.15, 6: 0.15},
    'S3': {1: 0.15, 2: 0.16, 3: 0.10, 4: 0.15, 5: 0.15, 6: 0.15},
}
CHURN_DRIFT_PER_WEEK = 0.0010
MIN_EVAL_DEFINED, MAX_EVAL_DEFINED = 1, 6

CAPACITY_TIERS = [(50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
                  (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000), (80_000_000, 28000), (300_000_000, 75000)]
def capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day_units):
    safety = peak_day_units / 0.75
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if safety <= cap:
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK = 1_396_782 / 2243
PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO = 1.26
RATE_A_T1 = 0.0003
RATE_C_T3 = 0.006
USAGE_A_FRAC = 1275120 / 1396782
USAGE_C_FRAC = 16184 / 1396782
OPS_BASE_NOW = 500.0
OPS_FLOOR = 150.0
LEADS_PER_WEEK_BASE = 330.0
LEAD_COST = 0.5
DEV_SPEND_S1 = 0.0

P_REOPEN = 0.20
NEW_PRICE_A = 9.0

def eval_index(boundary):
    idx = boundary // 30
    return min(max(idx, MIN_EVAL_DEFINED), MAX_EVAL_DEFINED)

def simulate(n_draws, seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    results = {h: [] for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]}
    diag_subs = {h: [] for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]}
    for draw in range(n_draws):
        churn_adj = min(max(random.gauss(TIER_REVERT_CHURN_ADJ_MEAN, TIER_REVERT_CHURN_ADJ_SD), 0.0), 0.20)
        drawn_mean_base = {}
        for g in CHURN_MEAN_BASE:
            drawn_mean_base[g] = {}
            for e, mu in CHURN_MEAN_BASE[g].items():
                sd_s = CHURN_SD_STRUCTURAL[g][e]
                drawn_mean_base[g][e] = min(max(random.gauss(mu + churn_adj, sd_s), 0.03), 0.97)

        reopen = random.random() < P_REOPEN
        conv_rate = random.uniform(0.01, 0.09) if reopen else random.uniform(0.0, 0.003)
        reopen_delay_wk = random.randint(1, 3)

        pop = dict(POP0)
        cash = CASH0
        for wk in range(1, 27):
            subs_prev = sum(pop.values())
            ops_now = max(150.0, OPS_BASE_NOW * (subs_prev / BASE_SUBS0) ** 0.5)
            dev_wk_rate = DEV_SPEND_S1
            if cash < 15000:
                dev_wk_rate = 0.0
            if cash < 10000:
                ops_now = max(OPS_FLOOR, ops_now * 0.7)
            if cash < 4000:
                ops_now = min(ops_now, OPS_FLOOR)

            drift = CHURN_DRIFT_PER_WEEK * wk
            drawn_mean = {g: {e: min(0.97, v + drift) for e, v in drawn_mean_base[g].items()}
                          for g in drawn_mean_base}

            revenue = 0.0
            new_pop = {}
            for (g, tenure, plan, price), count in pop.items():
                if count <= 0:
                    continue
                t_after = tenure + 7
                boundary = None
                for b in range(30, 480, 30):
                    if tenure < b <= t_after:
                        boundary = b
                        break
                if boundary:
                    ev = eval_index(boundary)
                    mu = drawn_mean[g][ev]
                    sd_w = CHURN_SD_WEEKLY[g][ev]
                    cr = min(max(random.gauss(mu, sd_w), 0.02), 0.98)
                    survivors = count * (1 - cr)
                    revenue += survivors * price
                    key2 = (g, t_after, plan, price)
                    new_pop[key2] = new_pop.get(key2, 0) + survivors
                else:
                    key2 = (g, t_after, plan, price)
                    new_pop[key2] = new_pop.get(key2, 0) + count
            pop = new_pop

            new_subs = 0.0
            if wk >= reopen_delay_wk:
                leads_this_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK_BASE * (sum(pop.values()) / BASE_SUBS0)
                new_subs = leads_this_wk * conv_rate
                key_new = ('S1', 7, 'A', NEW_PRICE_A)
                pop[key_new] = pop.get(key_new, 0) + new_subs

            subs_now = sum(pop.values())
            usage_week = USAGE_PER_SUB_WEEK * subs_now
            usage_A = usage_week * USAGE_A_FRAC
            usage_C = usage_week * USAGE_C_FRAC
            compute_wk = usage_A * RATE_A_T1 + usage_C * RATE_C_T3
            peak_day = (usage_week / 7) * PEAK_TO_AVG_RATIO
            capacity_wk = capacity_cost_for_peak(peak_day) * 7
            ops_wk = ops_now * 7
            dev_wk = dev_wk_rate * 7
            lead_wk = LEADS_PER_WEEK_BASE * (subs_now / BASE_SUBS0) * LEAD_COST
            costs = capacity_wk + compute_wk + ops_wk + dev_wk + lead_wk
            cash += revenue - costs
            if wk in results:
                results[wk].append(cash)
                diag_subs[wk].append(subs_now)
    return results, diag_subs

if __name__ == '__main__':
    results, diag_subs = simulate(4000, seed=42)
    summary = {}
    for h in [1, 4, 12, 26]:
        vals = sorted(results[h])
        n = len(vals)
        med = vals[n//2]
        lo = vals[int(n*0.025)]
        hi = vals[int(n*0.975)]
        mean = statistics.mean(vals)
        subs_med = sorted(diag_subs[h])[n//2]
        summary[h] = {'median': med, 'mean': mean, 'lo95': lo, 'hi95': hi, 'subs_median': subs_med}
        print(f"wk{h}: median=${med:,.0f} mean=${mean:,.0f} [{lo:,.0f}, {hi:,.0f}]  subs_median={subs_med:.0f}")
    json.dump(summary, open('forecast_v38_summary.json', 'w'), indent=1)

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 175 = end of week 25. 43 weeks remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: **`forecast_model_v38.py`** (PRIMARY). v37 kept (intermediate, pooled-churn-only
step). v35/v36 kept for historical reference (SUPERSEDED — v36's "big retention win" conclusion
was WRONG, see below). v18-v34 DELETED (confirmed stale). Many old gather/check scripts from
day126-154 also deleted this session to reduce clutter — keep only ~last 2-3 sessions' worth going
forward.

## 🚨 STATUS as of Day 175 (submitted next-week to advance → Day 182 next dashboard)
Cash: $44,279.81 (down -$6,180.81 from day168's $50,460.62 — smaller drop than day161→168's
-$9,342 mainly because MRR base is smaller now, not because things improved). Individual Subs:
2243 (down from 2457, -214, matches Cancellations:214 exactly — a MUCH bigger cancellation wave
than the prior week's 31). New Individual Leads: 319, **0 converted — 0% conversion CONFIRMED
continuing, now 14 STRAIGHT WEEKS (100% of new leads have acquisition_source='network', i.e.
word-of-mouth/referral — ad spend is $0, so ads aren't the issue)**. MRR dropped to $31,987 (from
$35,359, -9.5% in one week). Base: S1=2157 (all A), S2=60 (56A+4C), S3=26 (23A+3C). Enterprise:
still 0 seats, 0 threads EVER across 175 days (fully, permanently dead — 1-line check only from
now on). Open issues 301 (299/301 age=0, avg resolution 1.05 days — STILL HEALTHY, 3rd+ session
confirmed).

## 🔴🔴🔴 MAJOR CORRECTION: last session's "tier bump fixed retention" conclusion was WRONG/overstated
Last session (day168) found S1 eval@120d survival 90.7% (churn only 9.3%, n=268) and concluded the
day161 tier bump was a large, confirmed retention win. **This week's FRESH cohort crossing the
SAME eval@120d boundary showed only 63.9% survival (36.1% CHURN, n=482)** — a huge reversal!
Root-caused it: grandfathered PRICE is strongly correlated with tenure (customers signed up in
the same window share price+tenure). The day161→168 cohort crossing eval was priced ~$10 (cheap,
easy quality-price fit, low churn). This week's day168→175 cohort was priced $13 (pricier, worse
fit, high churn). **Pooling BOTH weeks' data gives a much more sober, believable estimate:**
- S1 eval@120d (pooled n=750): churn = **26.5%**
- S1 eval@150d (pooled n=93): churn = **26.9%**
These pooled rates ARE modestly better than the old pre-bump blend (~30-38%), so the tier bump
probably DID help a little (~3.5-10pt), just nowhere near the dramatic 9% first thought.
**LESSON: never trust a single week's churn-at-eval reading, even with n~250-300 — cohort
composition (price!) varies week to week and can swing the reading by 3-4x. Always POOL multiple
weeks' diffs for the same eval boundary before updating beliefs.** S2/S3 have thin/no fresh data
this week (S2 n=13 one boundary only, S3 n=8 pooled) — kept close to old pre-bump priors for those
(small population anyway, doesn't move the needle much on total cash).

## 🎉 MAJOR DECISION THIS SESSION: REVERTED Plan A/B model tier 2→1 (huge cost cut)
Given the corrected (modest, ~3.5-10pt) retention benefit of the T2 bump, ran a rigorous
cost-benefit comparison (`tier_revert_comparison.py`) comparing "keep T2" vs "revert to T1"
across a 26-week MC, using a PESSIMISTIC assumption that reverting costs +6pt extra churn (mid of
the plausible 3.5-8.5pt range) at every eval from now on. Result: **T1 wins by a landslide** —
wk26 median cash: T2=-$20,300 vs T1=+$420 (in the matched comparison; full v38 model with all
other updates gives wk26 median ~+$950). Even stress-tested with churn_adj forced to a much WORSE
+20pt (double what we think is realistic): wk26 median only -$1,255, still far better than keeping
T2's -$20,300+. **Why: Plan A is 99.7% of usage, and compute rate differential is HUGE — T1=
$0.0003/unit vs T2=$0.002/unit (6.67x)**. Current usage ~1.275M units/week on Plan A alone; at T2
that's ~$2,550/week compute, at T1 only ~$383/week — saves **~$2,167/week**, dwarfing the modest
retention cost. **ACTION: `set_model_tiers(A=1, B=1, C=3)`** (kept C at tier3 — only 7 customers,
paying $85-103/mo each, small savings (~$92/wk) not worth the risk of losing that MRR for such a
tiny population). Quality for S1/S2/S3 Plan A is now back to ~0.317/0.390/0.447 (was 0.397/0.469/
0.526 at T2). **This does NOT cause immediate churn — churn is a discrete hazard evaluated ONLY at
each customer's own 30-day eval mark (confirmed again this week: ALL 214 cancellations had tenure
EXACTLY 120 or 150, no in-between values) — so the quality drop will only start affecting churn
as customers hit their NEXT scheduled eval over the coming 30 days, not immediately.**
**RISK NOTED (unverified, no data either way): reverting might also reduce satisfaction →
referral-generation (our ONLY lead channel). Checked lead/subscriber ratio trend day168→175 for a
hint (leads fell faster than subs, -17.6% vs -8.7%) — weak evidence AGAINST a strong quality→
referral link (if quality bump had been juicing referrals, we'd expect the ratio to be improving,
not worsening) but NOT conclusive. Watch new-lead COUNT (not just conversion) next session for any
unexpected drop — if leads/week craters (not just stays ~300-330), reconsider.**

## 🧪 EXPERIMENT THIS SESSION: cut Plan A price $13 → $9 (test reopening new-lead conversion)
Rationale: 14 straight weeks of 0% conversion despite S1 already effectively seeing ~$10-13 after
existing lead_promotion ($3 off for S1). `get_group_insights('S1')` shows willingness_to_pay=
$25.87 (noisy ±65%, but WELL above our $9-13 price range) — suggests price is likely NOT the
primary binding constraint; more likely an accumulated quality-vs-expectation gap (competitor
drift has been accelerating per last 2 sessions' findings). This is a FREE test (existing
customers are permanently grandfathered — only NEW signups get $9). **CONFOUND WARNING: the tier
revert (quality DOWN) happened the SAME week — if conversion still doesn't reopen next week(s),
do NOT conclude "price doesn't matter" with full confidence, since quality also just dropped
simultaneously. Would need to retest at a higher quality tier later to fully isolate price's
effect.** Modeled as ~20% probability of "reopening" (modest 1-9% lead conversion rate) in the MC,
delayed 1-3 weeks (word-of-mouth lag). If ANY new subscribers appear next week — even 1-2 — that's
a huge, hugely-actionable signal (would flip the whole death-spiral narrative). **CHECK THIS FIRST
NEXT SESSION: query `SELECT group_id, status, COUNT(*) FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c...
WHERE c.created_day > 175 GROUP BY group_id, status` — any status='subscribed' rows = SUCCESS.**

## Other actions this session
- **Tapered ops $550→$500/day** (saves $350/wk) — 3rd+ session confirmed healthy backlog (299/301
  open issues age=0, avg resolution 1.05 days over 14 days, n=4499 resolved).
- **Held capacity (infrastructure) at Tier 2** — 14-day usage: avg 203,087/day, peak 255,269, peak/
  avg ratio 1.257. Several days still exceed Tier1's 200K cap. Recheck every session as population
  shrinks; downgrade to Tier1 (save $315/day=$2,205/wk) once peak safely clears ~190-200K
  sustained. NOTE: this is DIFFERENT from model tier (just reverted 2→1) — capacity tier is about
  total usage-volume/overload risk, model tier is about per-unit quality/cost. Don't conflate them.
- **Held dev spend at $0** (S1 targeted dev spend stopped last session, bonus persists at +0.2221,
  frozen). Not worth restarting — at T1 the multiplier on dev-spend-driven quality is even lower
  (0.60x vs 0.75x), making it even less cost-effective now.
- **No ad spend** — still 100% organic/network leads; wait for ANY sign conversion is reopening
  before spending real money on paid acquisition.
- **No R&D** — reconfirmed 20 tiers exist (not 10 — the top-level instructions doc's "10 tiers" is
  wrong for this instance, matches memory's earlier correction). Tier1 (cheapest) = $166,667, way
  beyond our ~$44K cash. Tiers 2-20 cost more. Completely unaffordable, don't force it.
- **No enterprise action** — 0 threads, ever, 175 days. Confirmed structurally dead.
- **Posted 1 social media update** (free, 1/day allowed) announcing the $9 price cut, timed to
  try to stimulate referral/word-of-mouth leads (our ONLY channel — 100% of this week's leads were
  acquisition_source='network').
- Left lead_promotion unchanged (global $5, S1 $3, S2 $10, S3 $10 — active since day140).
- Usage is NOT concentrated in power users (checked distribution: only 28/2279 customers use
  >300 units/day out of a 900 quota, top-20 customers = only 5.1% of total daily usage) — quota
  cuts are NOT a viable cost lever, don't bother pursuing this.

## Current config snapshot (day175, after this session's changes)
Prices: A=$9, B=$115, C=$180 (A cut from $13). Model tiers: A=1, B=1, C=3 (A/B reverted from 2).
Quotas: A=900,B=1200,C=2500 (unchanged). Capacity: Tier 2 (infrastructure, unchanged). Daily
spend: Ops=$500 (was $550), Dev=$0 (unchanged). Lead promo: global $5, S1 $3, S2 $10, S3 $10
(unchanged). Ad spend: $0 all channels (unchanged).

## FORECAST METHODOLOGY THIS SESSION (v37 → v38)
v37: corrected churn table (pooled, see above), kept tier at T2 (initial pass before deciding to
revert), added price-cut-reopening mixture (20% prob, 1-9% conversion rate, 1-3wk delay). Also
added POPULATION-ADAPTIVE ops scaling (ops = max($150, $500×(subs/subs0)^0.5)) since a rational
CEO (me) WOULD cut ops spend as the base shrinks — a flat-ops assumption was unrealistic and
overstated long-horizon burn in past models.
v38: same as v37 but with the model-tier revert baked in (compute rate 0.0003 for Plan A/B
instead of 0.002), plus an explicit extra churn_adj (mean +6pt, SD 3.5pt, capped 0-20pt) applied
on top of the pooled base rates to represent the plausible retention cost of the revert.
Validated wk1 with a deterministic hand-calc across a churn-rate sweep (sanity_wk1_175.py) —
MC median $44,459 vs hand-calc ~$44,200-45,100 for churn 0.30-0.35 — good agreement.
Raw MC (5000 draws): wk1 [42,443,46,373] median 44,459 | wk4 [32,984,38,622] median 35,150 |
wk12 [18,153,26,889] median 22,285 | wk26 [-2,497,6,872] median 937.
**Manually widened all bands for submission** beyond raw MC — this is the FIRST week actually
living with the tier-revert decision, real-world could deviate from modeled assumptions in either
direction, plus genuine uncertainty about the price-cut experiment and my own future rebalancing
decisions in weeks I haven't lived through yet.

**Submitted forecast this session (record for next-session calibration check against actual
day182/203/259/357 cash):**
- 1wk (day182): pt=44500 [41000, 47500]
- 4wk (day203): pt=35000 [28000, 42000]
- 12wk (day259): pt=21000 [8000, 34000]
- 26wk (day357): pt=0 [-28000, 38000]
**NEXT SESSION: check actual day182 cash against [41000,47500] FIRST THING.** Also: (a) did ANY
new conversion happen (see experiment note above)? (b) did the tier-revert's assumed +6pt churn
cost show up in the next eval-boundary cohort (won't be visible for 1-4 weeks depending on which
cohort crosses next, since the eval that matters is whoever's NEXT scheduled 30-day mark, and this
week's carryover cohort already had T2 quality baked in when THEY were originally acquired/priced
— the T1-quality effect only bites for evals happening from day175 onward, which is ~all of them
now). (c) did leads/week hold steady ~300-330 (checking the referral-generation risk noted above)?

## Strategy going forward
1. **TOP PRIORITY next session: check for ANY new conversions** (the price-cut experiment) — even
   a tiny nonzero number is a massive signal given 14 straight weeks of hard 0%.
2. **Check actual day182 cash against [41000,47500]** — if wildly off, figure out why immediately
   (outage? competitor shock? conversion surprise? tier-revert effect stronger/weaker than
   modeled?).
3. **Keep rebuilding tenure histogram + (tenure,plan,price) joint table + churn-diff EVERY
   session** — but this session's big lesson: **POOL at least 2 weeks of diffs for the same eval

## CONFIRMED MECHANICS (check docs/api/*.json FIRST before re-deriving — saves turns)
- **Billing/eval happens at EXACTLY 30-day tenure multiples per customer, deterministically** —
  reconfirmed this week: ALL 214 cancellations had tenure exactly 120 or exactly 150 (no
  120-126 spread) even though the "at-risk" population spanned tenure 113-119 the prior week.
  Zero churn happens between 30-day marks. This means churn is a pure discrete-hazard process,
  not continuous — model it that way (already doing this).
- **Weekly revenue ≈ SUM of (price × survivors) for customers crossing a 30-day boundary that
  week** — validated again this week (predicted ~$4,292-4,500 from the exact joint-price-table
  calc vs actual ledger $4,500, close match). This IS the right methodology, keep using it.
- **Grandfathered price is STRONGLY tenure-correlated** (reconfirmed) — different weekly cohorts
  crossing the SAME eval boundary can have very different price/quality fit and hence very
  different churn rates (this week: $13 cohort at eval@120 churned 39% vs $10 cohort at the same
  boundary churned only 8.7%). Always use the exact joint table, and expect volatility week to
  week purely from cohort-composition effects, separate from any true underlying rate change.
- **Model tier ≠ Capacity tier** — two totally separate systems. Model tier (`set_model_tiers`,
  1-5 per plan A/B/C) sets quality multiplier (T1=0.60x...T5=1.10x) AND compute cost/unit
  ($0.0003 to $0.03). Capacity tier (`set_capacity_tier`, 0-7 global) sets total usage-volume
  capacity ($85/day@50K cap ... $75000/day@300M cap) and overload/outage risk. Changing one does
  NOT affect the other.
- **Usage is broad-based, NOT power-user-concentrated** — only ~1.2% of customers (28/2279) use
  >300 of a 900 daily quota; top 20 users = 5.1% of total usage. Quota cuts would NOT meaningfully
  reduce compute cost — don't pursue this lever.

  referral is the entire acquisition engine currently. `post_social_media` (free, 1/day) may help

  top-level SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS doc claim of "10 tiers" is WRONG for this simulator instance,
  trust `list_research_projects()` output over the static docs.
- Targeted per-group dev spend config **persists automatically across sessions once set** (and
  stopping it doesn't reduce the already-accumulated bonus, just freezes further growth).
- Issue resolution remains FAST/healthy (3rd+ consecutive session confirmed): ~1.0-1.3 days avg,

  status='subscribed' — cancelled customers' orphaned issue rows stay "open" forever and wildly

## Lessons / errors log (don't repeat these)
- **NEW (day175): NEVER trust a single week's churn-at-eval reading, even at n~250-300** — cohort
  price/composition varies week to week (strongly tenure-correlated) and can swing the observed
  rate by 3-4x (9.3% one week, 36.1% the very next week, for the SAME eval boundary). Always POOL
  ≥2 weeks of diff data for the same boundary before updating action-relevant beliefs. This
  directly caused an incorrect "large retention win" conclusion last session that this session had
  to correct.
- **NEW (day175): when a "validated" lever turns out to be much weaker than first measured, always
  redo the cost-benefit math from scratch** — the day161 tier bump looked like a no-brainer keep
  at a (wrongly) believed ~20pt retention improvement, but at the TRUE ~3.5-10pt improvement, the
  compute-cost premium (6.67x for T2 vs T1) completely flips the conclusion. Don't anchor on a
  past session's "confirmed win" framing if the underlying data changes.
- **NEW (day175): population-ADAPTIVE cost assumptions matter a lot for long-horizon forecasts** —
  a flat-ops-forever model was unrealistically pessimistic; modeling that a rational CEO (me)
  would taper ops roughly with sqrt(population ratio) meaningfully improved the realism of wk12/
  wk26 forecasts (I would actually do this in real play, so the forecast should assume it).
  Similarly capacity tier should always be modeled adaptively (already was).
- **NEW (day175): usage/cost concentration should be checked before assuming a quota cut would
  help** — checked distribution directly this session, confirmed usage is broad-based (not power-
  user-concentrated), so quota cuts are not a viable lever here. Good to verify empirically rather
  than assume.
- **NEW (day175): a price cut is a genuinely free experiment (grandfathering) but confounding it
  with a SIMULTANEOUS quality change (tier revert) muddies attribution** — acceptable tradeoff
  here given the tier-revert's cost case was overwhelming and time-sensitive, but flag explicitly
  in memory so next session doesn't over-interpret a null result on the price experiment alone.
- (day168): a tier bump's retention benefit CAN be validated within just 1 week via tenure-
  histogram diff — TRUE, but the correct practice is to keep collecting MORE weeks before fully
  trusting the magnitude, per the correction above. Direction can be read fast; magnitude needs
  pooling.
- (day168): grandfathered price is correlated with tenure — always build the joint
  (tenure,plan,price) table for revenue forecasting, not just a group-average price.
- (day168): competitor-driven expectation drift can ACCELERATE — recheck the full-history
  cumulative "quality boost" sum every session.
- (day161): weekly revenue lumpiness from a fixed/aging tenure population is a REAL,
  precomputable structural effect — always project the exact eval-boundary-crossing schedule.
- (day161): don't trust old memory summaries blindly for "current settings" — re-check
  `config_overrides` (latest row per setting_type) each session.
- For FORECASTING purposes, use honest subjective-probability beliefs/updated-means for uncertain
  bets rather than the conservative floor used for ACTION decisions — but ALSO don't let a single
  week's data swing the mean too far (see the pooling lesson above) — balance both.
- Cross-validating tenure-histogram-diff churn rates against ACTUAL ledger subscription_payment
  revenue (via realized survivor counts, WITH exact per-cohort prices) is a powerful, cheap check
  — do this every session.
- Model tier changes are NOT grandfathered (unlike price) — apply instantly to every customer on
  that plan letter, fully reversible, no documented one-time "shock" penalty. Always check
  `get_cost_info()` for exact per-tier compute rates before considering a tier change.
- Global dev-spend quality bonus is NOT stably cumulative like the per-group bonus — fluctuates
  even at $0 spend. Always use TARGETED per-group dev spend for deliberate permanent investment.
- Fixed-cost forecast models (holding ops/capacity constant forever) produce an unrealistic
  death-spiral at long horizons — always build adaptive-cost variants matching what a rational
  CEO would actually do.
- Price cuts are a FREE experiment when existing customers are grandfathered; tier changes are NOT
  free — cost/save real money instantly and apply to the whole existing base (in EITHER direction
  — reverting a tier bump saves money immediately just as raising one costs money immediately).
- The cumulative-cohort-snapshot churn method OVERSTATES true per-eval marginal churn — always use
  week-over-week histogram-diff instead, POOLED across ≥2 weeks per the new lesson above.
- R&D has 20 tiers not 10 (docs' top-level claim is wrong for this instance). `post_social_media`

## How to rebuild forecast inputs fresh each session
```python
import novamind_api as nm, json
today = nm.vars.current_day
# 1. Installed base + MRR, by group AND plan:
r = nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(s.effective_price) as mrr, AVG(s.effective_price) as avgp
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan''')
# 2. EXACT tenure histogram (save every session, KEEP prior 2-3 sessions' files, delete older):
out = {}
for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    r = nm.query(f'SELECT ({today} - c.created_day) as tenure, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s '
                 f'JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.group_id="{g}" AND '
                 f's.status="subscribed" GROUP BY tenure ORDER BY tenure')
    out[g] = {row['tenure']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
json.dump(out, open(f'tenure_histogram_day{today}.json','w'))
# 2b. EXACT (tenure, plan, price) JOINT table (critical -- price cohorts correlate with tenure):
outj = {}
for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    r = nm.query(f'''SELECT ({today} - c.created_day) as tenure, s.plan, s.effective_price as price, COUNT(*) as n
    FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
    WHERE c.group_id="{g}" AND s.status="subscribed" GROUP BY tenure, s.plan, price ORDER BY tenure''')
    outj[g] = [dict(row) for row in r['rows']]
json.dump(outj, open(f'tenure_price_joint_day{today}.json','w'))
# 2c. Marginal churn-at-eval via week-over-week diff vs LAST session's histogram file (see
#     churn_diff_175.py this session for exact working code). *** POOL with the diff from 2
#     sessions ago too (same eval boundary) before updating the forecast churn table -- do NOT
#     act on a single week's diff alone (day175 lesson). ***
# 2d. Cross-validate: revenue_est using the joint table's exact per-cohort prices (NOT group avg);
#     compare to actual ledger subscription_payment. Should be within ~1-10%.
# 2e. EXACT eval-boundary-crossing LOAD schedule for next 12 weeks -- see the "gap to next 30-
#     multiple boundary" bucketing pattern in gather_day175c.py. Key forecasting input.
# 3. Actual usage/compute-cost blended rate (last 7-10 days) + get_cost_info() for exact per-tier
#    rates. ALSO split usage by PLAN (A vs C etc, see check_c_usage.py) if considering any
#    tier-change cost analysis -- a single blended rate hides which plan drives the cost.
r = nm.query(f'SELECT SUM(usage_units) as u FROM daily_usage WHERE day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today}')
r2 = nm.query(f"SELECT SUM(amount) as c FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today} AND category='compute'")
ci = nm.infrastructure.get_cost_info()
# 4. New-lead conversion rate this week (KEY CHECK -- flag LOUDLY if nonzero, huge signal):
r = nm.query(f'''SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN {today-6} AND {today}
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status''')
# 5. Competitor shock + macro check (every session):
r = nm.query(f'''SELECT day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE content LIKE "%quality boost%" ORDER BY day''')
mo = nm.market.get_market_overview()
# 6. Open issues backlog, FILTERED TO subscription status='subscribed':
r = nm.query('''SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM issues i JOIN customers c ON i.customer_id=c.customer_id
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE i.status="open" AND s.status="subscribed"''')
# 7. Cash check + R&D/enterprise dead-check + config_overrides latest-row-per-type:
print(nm.query('SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger')['rows'])
print(nm.research.list_research_projects()['tiers'])
print(nm.query('SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM enterprise_turns')['rows'])
for t in ['promotion','lead_promotion','targeted_ad_spend','targeted_dev_spend']:
    print(t, nm.query(f"SELECT day, settings_json FROM config_overrides WHERE setting_type='{t}' ORDER BY day DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1")['rows'])
# 8. Daily usage peak/avg over 14 days (for capacity-tier decisions):
r = nm.query(f'SELECT day, SUM(usage_units) as u FROM daily_usage WHERE day > {today-14} GROUP BY day ORDER BY day')
# 9. get_group_insights for S1/S2/S3 -- free, noisy (quality_floor_q_min likely decorative, but
#    willingness_to_pay is a useful sanity check on whether price vs quality is the binding
#    constraint for acquisition).
for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
    print(nm.market.get_group_insights(group_id=g)['estimates'])
```
Then rebuild forecast_model's CHURN_MEAN/SD tables from the POOLED (≥2 weeks) blended table, rebuild

"""
Forecast model v39 -- built day182, week26, in response to a MAJOR structural shock:
- 601 cancellations this week (vs 214 prior week) -- churn at eval@120/150 was ~75-80%,
  FAR worse than the pooled ~26.5-36% estimate from prior sessions.
- Plan C (untouched T3 quality, no tier change) ALSO fully wiped out (7->0 customers) at
  its eval this week -- strong evidence the driver is NOT solely the T1/T2 tier choice,
  but a broader force (accelerating competitor-driven expectation drift, confirmed via
  social posts showing near-daily competitor "quality boost" announcements of ~0.015-0.02
  each; possibly compounded by macro PMI turning to contraction (45.9) and a reputation
  hit from our own day175 price-cut announcement, which S2/S3 received NEGATIVELY).
- Actions taken this week (day182): reverted model tier A/B back to 1->2 (quality
  insurance, now cheap given shrunken usage + capacity downgrade offset), downgraded
  capacity tier 2->1 (usage safely under 200K cap, saves $2205/wk), bumped ops 500->700
  (backlog was 598 open vs 301 prior wk, 2 outages this week vs 0 in prior 13 days),
  set an ONGOING promotion (S1 $6, S2/S3 $9) directly targeting the quality-price fit of
  survivors at their NEXT eval (this is a NEW lever not used before -- set_promotion,
  distinct from set_lead_promotion which only affects brand-new leads).
- A HUGE eval wave is scheduled: exact tenure data shows 755 people evaluate in the next
  7 days alone (week+1), dominated by a $18-price cohort (512 people) -- historically the
  highest surviving grandfathered price, likely the MOST vulnerable to quality-price
  mismatch. Promotion cuts their effective price 18->12; tier revert restores T2 quality
  (0.75x mult vs 0.60x). Combined effect on survival is UNCERTAIN -- modeled with a wide
  band. Subsequent waves (week+2..5: 262,327,274,24) are dominated by LOWER historical
  prices ($9,$10,$13) -> lower effective price post-promo -> expected somewhat better
  survival odds per the quality-price curve (modest price = modest quality needed).
- Sum of week+1..+5 waves = 755+262+327+274+24 = 1642 = EXACTLY current population,
  confirming the "~every 30 days, 100% of the base evaluates exactly once" model.
  Beyond week 5, switch to smoothed model: 7/30=23.3%/week of current population
  evaluates each week (steady-state approximation once the lumpy actual-data front is
  exhausted).

METHODOLOGY:
- Weekly-step Monte Carlo, 26-week horizon (182 days), ~4000 trials.
- Per-trial "severity" latent path: severity_0 ~ TruncNormal(0.50,0.13,[0.15,0.85])
  (baseline churn rate at ~$8 effective price, POST our interventions -- anchored between
  the crisis-week 75-80% [pre-intervention, T1, no promo] and the old pre-crisis pooled
  26.5-36% estimate, since interventions provide SOME relief but competitor drift is real
  & ongoing so a full reversion to old rates seems unlikely). Random-walk drift over time
  (mean +0.004/wk, sd 0.006/wk, can go either way) + weekly idiosyncratic noise (sd 0.05).
- Price adjustment: churn_rate = severity_t + 0.025*(effective_price - 8), reflecting the
  quality-price curve (higher price needs higher quality -> more vulnerable). Clipped
  [0.05, 0.97].
- Revenue = sum(effective_price for survivors of THIS WEEK's evaluators only) -- matches
  confirmed discrete-hazard-at-billing mechanic (non-evaluators don't pay this week).
- Costs: capacity adaptive (tier0 if usage<40K, tier1 if <160K, tier2 if <640K...), ops
  adaptive (~700*(pop/pop0)^0.5, floor $150), compute = usage * $0.002/unit (T2 rate,
  assumes we hold T2 throughout -- no further tier changes modeled), lead_acq = leads*$0.5
  (leads/week ~ 0.166*population, i.e. current 272/1642 ratio, organic/referral only).
- Small mixture probability (15%, down from v38's 20% given still-confirmed 0% conversion
  even after BOTH a price cut AND a quality improvement) that conversion reopens at a
  modest 1-7% rate, delayed 1-4 weeks -- long tail upside scenario.
- Manually widen bands further at submission for un-modeled uncertainty -- this is a
  FIRST week living with THREE simultaneous new interventions (tier, capacity, promotion)
  whose combined effect is genuinely unknown, on top of an already highly volatile,
  structurally-declining business.
"""
import json, random, math

random.seed(20182)

TODAY = 182
CASH0 = 39472.202

# Exact eval-wave data for weeks 1-5 (from tenure_price_joint_day182.json bucketing)
# {week_offset: [(price, n), ...]}  -- these are pre-promotion listed/grandfathered prices
WAVES = {
    1: [(18.0, 512), (15.0, 83), (10.0, 138), (9.0, 20), (13.0, 2)],
    2: [(18.0, 32), (10.0, 219), (9.0, 11)],
    3: [(13.0, 218), (10.0, 91), (9.0, 18)],
    4: [(15.0, 133), (13.0, 109), (9.0, 32)],
    5: [(15.0, 22), (9.0, 2)],
}
POP0 = 1642
PROMO_S1 = 6.0  # applies to ~97% of population; use as blended promo assumption for all groups

CAPACITY_TIERS = [  # (max_units_per_day, cost_per_day)
    (50_000, 85), (200_000, 215), (800_000, 530), (2_500_000, 1330),
    (8_000_000, 4000), (25_000_000, 10000),
]

def capacity_cost(daily_usage):
    for cap, cost in CAPACITY_TIERS:
        if daily_usage <= cap * 0.85:  # keep ~15% headroom like a rational operator would
            return cost
    return CAPACITY_TIERS[-1][1]

def trunc_normal(mean, sd, lo, hi):
    for _ in range(50):
        v = random.gauss(mean, sd)
        if lo <= v <= hi:
            return v
    return min(max(mean, lo), hi)

def run_trial(weeks=26):
    cash = CASH0
    pop = POP0
    usage_per_cust = 143476 / 1642  # ~87.4 units/cust/day, observed day182

    severity = trunc_normal(0.50, 0.13, 0.15, 0.85)

    # conversion-reopening mixture
    reopen = random.random() < 0.15
    reopen_week = random.randint(1, 4)
    reopen_rate = random.uniform(0.01, 0.07)

    cash_path = {}
    # remaining "exact" waves (mutate copy)
    remaining_waves = {k: list(v) for k, v in WAVES.items()}

    for wk in range(1, weeks + 1):
        severity += random.gauss(0.004, 0.006)
        severity = min(max(severity, 0.05), 0.95)
        sev_t = min(max(severity + random.gauss(0, 0.05), 0.05), 0.97)

        # --- determine this week's evaluating cohort ---
        if wk in remaining_waves:
            cohort = remaining_waves[wk]
        else:
            # smoothed steady-state: 23.3%/week of current population, at a blended
            # avg effective (pre-promo) price of $12 (rough blend of surviving mix)
            n_eval = pop * (7 / 30)
            cohort = [(12.0, n_eval)]

        revenue = 0.0
        survivors_total = 0.0
        cancels_total = 0.0
        for price, n in cohort:
            eff_price = max(price - PROMO_S1, 0.0)
            churn_rate = sev_t + 0.025 * (eff_price - 8)
            churn_rate = min(max(churn_rate, 0.05), 0.97)
            survive_frac = 1 - churn_rate
            survivors = n * survive_frac
            revenue += survivors * eff_price
            survivors_total += survivors
            cancels_total += n * churn_rate

        pop = max(pop - cancels_total, 0.0)

        # --- new leads / conversion (mostly still 0%, small reopening tail) ---
        leads = 0.166 * pop
        new_subs = 0.0
        if reopen and wk >= reopen_week:

# NovaMind CEO — Running Memory

## Objective
Maximize CASH at day 504 (72 weeks). We are at Day 182 = end of week 26. 42 weeks remain.
Conversation resets every week — this file is my ONLY memory.
Must submit rationale + 12 cash forecasts (point/lo/hi at 1/4/12/26 wk) EVERY next-week call or it 400s.
CLI: `./novamind-operation next-week "<rationale>" c1_pt c1_lo c1_hi c4_pt c4_lo c4_hi c12_pt c12_lo c12_hi c26_pt c26_lo c26_hi`
Forecast script: **`forecast_model_v39.py`** (PRIMARY, this session). v38/v37 kept for reference
(pre-crash models, now largely obsolete assumptions). v35/v36 superseded. Delete v35-v37 next
session if v39 proves reasonable, keep only most recent 2 versions.

## 🔴🔴🔴 CATASTROPHIC EVENT THIS SESSION (Day175→182): mass-churn crash, 601 cancellations
Cash: $39,472.20 (down from $44,279.81, -$4,807.61). Individual Subs: **1642 (down from 2243,
-601!!)** — by far the biggest single-week loss ever seen (prior worst was 214). New Leads: 272,
**0 converted (16th straight week of 0% conversion, now CONFIRMED even after BOTH the $9 price cut
AND — this week — a quality tier increase; price is clearly NOT the binding constraint)**.
MRR cratered: $22,866 (was $31,987, -28.5% in one week). **Plan C (S2/S3 premium plan, was 7
customers) is now FULLY WIPED OUT (0 remaining)** — critical because Plan C's quality (T3) was
NEVER touched by our tier changes, yet it still crashed to ~100% loss at its eval this week. Open
issues 598 (up from 301, nearly doubled) — new-issue creation spiked to 750/day and 614/day on the
2 outage days (day176, day182; normal days are ~200-330/day, resolution capacity is ~280-320/day),
causing backlog buildup. **First outages in 20+ days**: day176 (10min) + day182 (30min) = 40min
total this week, vs ZERO in the prior 13+ days. 5 angry customer social posts on day182 alone
about the outage, several explicitly threatening to churn ("might have to look elsewhere").

## 🔬 ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS: multiple compounding shocks, NOT primarily the T1 tier revert
Exact eval-boundary math (pop at tenure 113-119 vs day175 snapshot, tenure_at_cancel this week):
S1 eval@120 pool ≈644, cancelled≈496 → **~77% churn**. Eval@150 pool≈120, cancelled≈96 → **~80%
churn**. This is FAR worse than the prior pooled estimate of ~26.5-36%. Investigated whether last
session's T2→T1 model-tier revert (day175) was the cause: **traced the largest cancelled cohort's
signup date (day62) — they were on T1 quality their ENTIRE lifetime (T2 window was only day161-175,
brief, and didn't overlap any of their eval dates at day92/122/152/182) — yet they STILL crashed at
their 4th eval after passing 3 prior ones at T1. This proves the T1/T2 flip is NOT the sole/primary
driver.** Stronger evidence: **Plan C (untouched T3 quality) also collapsed ~100% this week.**
The REAL drivers appear to be a confluence of:
1. **Accelerating competitor-driven expectation drift** — social posts now show near-daily
   competitor "quality boost" announcements (~0.015-0.02 each, e.g. QuantumEdge/ApexSaaS, 2-4
   distinct posts across just days180-181) — this is a permanent, cumulative, unstoppable-by-us
   upward pressure on required quality (confirmed structural per docs; we have no R&D budget to
   counter it — cheapest tier still $166,667 vs our ~$39K cash).
2. **Self-inflicted reputation hit**: our day175 social post announcing the $9 price cut was
   received NEGATIVELY by S2 (-0.6) and S3 (-0.6) — quality-conscious segments interpreted a price
   cut as a "cheapening" signal. This likely hurt the whole book's quality-price fit at the margin,
   right before this week's huge eval wave. **LESSON: NEVER frame messaging around price cuts to
   quality-focused segments — reputation/sentiment effects can be worse than the direct mechanical
   effect and hit ALL groups, not just the one the price change applies to.**
3. **Macro turned to contraction**: PMI 45.9 published day181 (measuring conditions ~30d prior) —
   companies/individuals "pulling back on discretionary spend." Could be raising price sensitivity
   / lowering effective willingness-to-pay broadly.
4. Outage-driven issue-spike (598 open, satisfaction damage) — compounds the above, though
   probably a smaller contributor than #1/#2.
**CONCLUSION: this is very likely a structural, largely unstoppable decline given our cash
constraints (no R&D affordable), not a one-off mistake to "undo."** Full population wipeout within
~26 weeks is a plausible base case per this session's MC model (see below) — plan accordingly
(shift weight toward cash preservation, not just retention-fighting).

## 💡 NEW LEVER DISCOVERED: `set_promotion` (ongoing, for EXISTING subscribers)
Distinct from `set_lead_promotion` (only affects brand-new leads' conversion). `set_promotion`
gives an ongoing $/month deduction applied at EVERY billing/eval cycle for CURRENT subscribers —
directly lowers their effective price at the exact moment their quality-price fit is evaluated.
Was sitting at effectively $0 this whole game (only a stray irrelevant S1/B=$0 entry, never used
for S1's actual Plan A). **This is a much more precise/controllable retention lever than the tier
choice** since it directly targets the quality-PRICE curve's price side. Used this session (see
Actions below). Cost: reduces revenue from ALL who evaluate henceforth (not just marginal
cancellers) — a real trade-off, but justified given how catastrophic the alternative looks.

## Actions taken this session (day182)
1. **`set_model_tiers(A=2, B=2, C=3)`** — reverted the day175 T1 revert back UP to T2 for Plan
   A/B. Rationale: given demonstrated outsized importance of quality this week, and given usage
   has shrunk enough that T2's extra compute cost is now modest (~$1,900/wk at current ~1.1M
   units/wk, will keep shrinking), this is now a "cheap enough" insurance bet, ESPECIALLY given a
   huge (755-person) eval wave hits in the next 7 days. NOTE: root-cause analysis above suggests
   tier alone probably isn't the dominant driver (Plan C crashed despite untouched tier) — so don't
   expect this alone to fix things, it's one of several hedges.
2. **`set_capacity_tier(tier=1)`** (from tier2) — usage has fallen to ~90-215K/day (well under
   Tier1's 200K cap most days, day182=143,476), saves $315/day=$2,205/wk. **Net combined with the
   tier revert above: capacity savings ($2,205/wk) ROUGHLY OFFSETS the T1→T2 compute cost increase
   (~$1,900/wk) — this pairing is close to cost-NEUTRAL while buying a real quality improvement.**
   Confirmed via service_day table that "Overload: None" this week despite 2 outages — i.e.
   outages are from the INDEPENDENT random baseline risk (reduced by ops $), NOT from
   overload/capacity-tier choice — so downgrading capacity does NOT increase outage risk as long as
   usage stays under the new cap (it does, with ~28% headroom, and population is shrinking further).
3. **`set_daily_spend(operations=700, development=0)`** (ops up from $500) — backlog nearly
   doubled (598 vs 301) and outages returned (40min, first in 20+ days) this week; modest ops bump
   to accelerate issue resolution and further cut baseline outage risk given how fragile the
   situation is. +$1,400/wk cost.
4. **`set_promotion(by_group={'S1':6.0,'S2':9.0,'S3':9.0})`** — NEW lever (see above). Targets
   the huge upcoming 755-person eval wave, which is dominated by the HIGHEST surviving
   grandfathered price ($18, n=512) — likely the most vulnerable cohort to quality-price mismatch.
   Post-promo their effective price becomes $12 (LOWER than the $13-15 effective prices that just
   catastrophically failed this week with NO promo) — combined with the tier revert's quality
   bump, this is a real, meaningful two-sided intervention for that cohort specifically.
5. **Posted 1 social media reply** (to post_id=387, an outage complaint) — genuine apology +
   mentioned the quality/reliability upgrade, explicitly did NOT mention price this time (lesson
   from the price-cut post backfiring with S2/S3). Low-risk goodwill/reputation repair attempt.
6. Left prices unchanged (A=$9,B=$115,C=$180) — grandfathering means this doesn't affect existing
   at-risk customers; already proved price cut alone doesn't reopen conversion.
7. Left lead_promotion, ad spend ($0), dev spend ($0, beyond the daily_spend call above) unchanged.
8. No R&D (still ~4.2x too expensive), no enterprise action (confirmed dead, 0 threads ever,
   0-cost 1-line check only), no market research (cash too precious).

## 🆕 DISCOVERED: R&D history predates my memory logs — 2x Tier-1 completed on day 0 and day 49
`list_research_projects()` showed Tier 1 "completed: 2, total_quality_boost: 0.0643" — NOT a bug.
Confirmed via ledger: `research_project` category (NOT 'research' — that name errors) shows two
-$166,667 charges on day 0 and day 49 (project ids t1_1, t1_2), both completed, contributing a
permanent +0.0643 quality boost baked into the CURRENT global_bonus baseline already reflected in
all dashboard quality figures. This was from early-game action before my current memory log
history began (day161+) — just context, not a new opportunity (still can't afford new R&D at
$166,667 minimum vs our ~$39K cash). Ledger `category` valid values (confirmed exhaustively this
session via error message): subscription_payment, compute, capacity, advertising, operations,
development, lead_acquisition_cost, initial_funding, market_research, group_research,
research_project.

## 📅 HUGE UPCOMING EVAL SCHEDULE (exact, from tenure data day182) — CHECK THIS FIRST NEXT SESSION
Built exact "days-to-next-eval" bucketing (fixed a mod-30 boundary bug from earlier attempts).
Sum of week+1..+5 waves = 755+262+327+274+24 = **1642 = EXACTLY current population** — confirms
"~every 30 days, 100% of the base evaluates exactly once" model (validates the discrete-hazard
approach). Exact breakdown (pre-promo grandfathered price):
- **week+1 (days 183-189): 755 evaluating — DOMINATED by $18 price (n=512)**, the highest
  surviving grandfathered cohort, historically most vulnerable. Also 83@$15, 138@$10, 20@$9, 2@$13.
  **THIS IS THE FIRST COHORT TO EXPERIENCE THE COMBINED TIER-REVERT + PROMOTION INTERVENTION —
  THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT THING TO CHECK NEXT SESSION.** If survival is still catastrophic
  (churn >65-70%) despite BOTH interventions, that's strong evidence this is unstoppable structural
  decline — PIVOT HARD to pure cost-minimization/wind-down mode (see Strategy below). If survival
  improves meaningfully (churn drops to <50%), the interventions are working — keep them.
- week+2 (190-196): 262 evaluating, mostly $10 (n=219) — lower price, expect better survival.
- week+3 (197-203): 327 evaluating, mostly $13 (n=218).
- week+4 (204-210): 274 evaluating, mostly $15(133)/$13(109).
- week+5 (211-217): 24 evaluating (small tail).
Rebuild this exact schedule every session (see script pattern below) — it's the single highest-
value forecasting input given the discrete, lumpy, deterministic nature of the eval mechanic.

## 🎲 FORECAST MODEL v39 — sobering long-run picture, wide bands submitted
Weekly-step MC (~4000-6000 trials), using EXACT wave data for weeks 1-5, smoothed 23.3%/wk
(=7/30) steady-state thereafter. Per-trial latent "severity" (baseline churn at ~$8 effective
price, post-intervention) ~ TruncNormal(mean=0.50, sd=0.13, [0.15,0.85]) — anchored between the
crisis 75-80% (pre-intervention) and old pre-crisis pooled 26.5-36%, since interventions should
help SOME but competitor drift is real/ongoing so full reversion seems unlikely. Slow upward drift
(+0.004/wk mean) + per-wave noise. Price-adjustment: churn = severity + 0.025×(eff_price-8) (higher
price needs higher quality → more vulnerable, calibrated loosely off this week's data). Adaptive
costs: capacity steps down as usage falls, ops ~700×sqrt(pop/pop0) with floors ($150 normal, $40
if pop<150, $0 if pop<30 — modeling that a rational future-me would wind down spend as the
customer base becomes negligible). **Result: population compounds down FAST even at "moderate"
(not crisis-level) churn — median population by wk26 is only ~58 (range ~14-188 at 10-90%ile) —
i.e. the individual-subscriber business plausibly nears-total-wipeout within 26 weeks under a wide
range of assumptions, simply from the 30-day discrete-hazard compounding (e.g. even a "mild" 45%
per-cycle churn implies ~0.55^6≈2.8% of population survives 6 cycles=~180 days).** Raw MC: wk1
median $35,286 [33,710,36,952 p1-p99] | wk4 $18,457 [17,821,20,566] | wk12 -$16,141
[-29,055,1,410] | wk26 -$45,775 [-92,033,-10,967]. **Manually widened further for submission** —
raw near-term MC bands are too narrow (only reflect my specific model's internal parameter
variance, not genuine model-specification uncertainty or discrete-event risk like another outage);
also shaded 12wk/26wk points LESS negative than raw median since a real future-me would keep
adapting/cutting costs harder if things go worse than modeled (the MC assumes a mostly-static
policy after this week, which likely overstates burn in bad scenarios and understates recovery in
good ones).

**Submitted forecast this session (record for next-session calibration check against actuals):**
- 1wk (day189): pt=35000 [30000, 40000]
- 4wk (day210): pt=19000 [8000, 28000]
- 12wk (day266): pt=-8000 [-40000, 25000]
- 26wk (day364): pt=-15000 [-85000, 45000]

the week+1 (755-person, $18-dominated) cohort's actual survival rate** — this is the key diagnostic
for whether the tier+promotion intervention is working at all.

## Strategy going forward — DECISION RULE for next session
1. **TOP PRIORITY: pull exact cancellation data for the week+1 cohort (tenure crossing to

     intervention has real signal — keep it, consider whether to extend (e.g. bump promotion

   - If churn is STILL catastrophic (>65-70%) despite BOTH a quality bump AND a price-effective

     tools. **PIVOT HARD to pure cash-preservation/wind-down mode**: revert model tier back down
     to T1 (recapture the compute savings since quality clearly isn't the fix), consider dropping
     the promotion (stop giving away margin with no retention benefit), cut ops toward the bare
     floor, downgrade capacity further as population falls, and basically run lean/harvest for
     whatever's left of the individual book while preserving cash for the remaining ~40+ weeks.
2. **Re-examine capacity tier** every session as population keeps shrinking — Tier1 (200K cap)

3. **Re-run the exact eval-schedule bucketing** every session (see script pattern below) — weeks
   2-5 are already known (262, 327, 274, 24) — use this for revenue forecasting regardless of the
   tier/promo decision.
4. Watch for ANY new-lead conversion (still 0% after 16 weeks, price cut AND quality bump both
   tried) — if a 3rd consecutive intervention also fails to move it, treat acquisition as
   permanently closed and stop hoping for a reopening in future forecasts.
5. Watch social posts for further competitor "quality boost" mentions — try to tally cumulative
   magnitude over time to get a better empirical handle on the true expectation-drift rate (this

6. If the pivot-to-wind-down trigger fires: also reconsider whether ANY ops spend is worthwhile

   quality/uptime for a shrinking handful of customers may exceed their remaining LTV.
7. Keep reassessing whether reverting model tier back down (T1) makes sense EVEN IF churn improves
   somewhat — the question is whether the RETENTION benefit (in $ terms) exceeds the compute cost
   delta, which shrinks automatically as usage/population falls (so the case for T2 gets weaker

8. R&D: still unaffordable (cheapest $166,667 vs ~$39K cash). Given the dire cash trajectory, this

   on it as a future lever unless something changes dramatically.
9. Enterprise: confirmed dead, 1-line check only.
10. **Always record the actual submitted forecast numbers in MEMORY.md** for next-session
    calibration checks against actuals — did this again this session.

## Current config snapshot (day182, after this session's changes)
Prices: A=$9, B=$115, C=$180 (unchanged). Model tiers: A=2, B=2, C=3 (A/B reverted UP from 1).
Quotas: A=900,B=1200,C=2500 (unchanged). Capacity: **Tier 1** (down from Tier2). Daily spend:

## CONFIRMED MECHANICS (check docs/api/*.json FIRST before re-deriving — saves turns)
- **`set_promotion` (nm.pricing) = ONGOING discount for EXISTING subscribers, applied at every

  Distinct from `set_lead_promotion` (nm.marketing) which ONLY affects brand-new lead conversion.
  Was undiscovered/unused as a real lever until this session — a major addition to the toolkit.
- **Outages are governed by an INDEPENDENT random baseline probability (reduced by ops $: ~3%/day
  at $0, ~1.1%/day at $500), SEPARATE from overload (usage>capacity).** Confirmed this week:

  downgrading capacity tier (as long as usage stays under the new cap) does NOT by itself increase

- **A single week's realized churn-at-eval rate can swing WILDLY (26-36% historical pooled →
  75-80% this week) due to a confluence of factors, not just one lever** — this week's crash
  happened despite Plan C's quality being completely untouched, proving the T1/T2 tier flip is NOT

  posts, macro, outages/issues) before attributing a churn swing to any single lever change.

  segments (S2/S3 rated our day175 price-cut post -0.6 sentiment each)** — reputation damage from
  messaging can compound with or even exceed the direct mechanical effect of the underlying
  decision. Frame future posts around quality/reliability, not price, when addressing
  quality-focused segments.
- **R&D is 20 tiers, cheapest (Tier 1) $166,667** — confirmed AGAIN this session, and discovered
  tier 1 was actually completed twice already (day0, day49, predating my memory logs), permanently
  contributing +0.0643 quality already baked into current baseline. Still unaffordable at current
  cash (~$39K vs $166,667 needed, ~4.2x short).
- Ledger `category` valid values (confirmed exhaustively via error message this session):
  subscription_payment, compute, capacity, advertising, operations, development,
  lead_acquisition_cost, initial_funding, market_research, group_research, research_project. (NOT

- Model tier ≠ Capacity tier (still true, reconfirmed) — two totally separate systems. Tier
  (`set_model_tiers`) sets quality multiplier + compute $/unit. Capacity (`set_capacity_tier`) sets
  total daily usage-volume cap + baseline overload exposure (but NOT outage risk directly — see
  above).
